car_name: 2027 Rolls-Royce Cullinan Review
overview:
The 2027 Rolls-Royce Cullinan continues to occupy a class almost entirely of its own. Rather than competing on practicality or performance alone, the Cullinan focuses on delivering unmatched craftsmanship, supreme comfort, and an unmistakable sense of occasion. Every journey feels effortlessly luxurious thanks to its whisper-quiet cabin, handcrafted materials, and a twin-turbocharged V-12 engine that delivers immense power with remarkable refinement.

For 2027, Rolls-Royce leaves the Cullinan mechanically unchanged, relying instead on its virtually limitless bespoke customization program to ensure every example remains unique. While its bold exterior styling continues to divide opinions, the Cullinan's extraordinary ride quality, premium materials, and near-endless personalization options reinforce its status as one of the world's most prestigious luxury SUVs.
pricing:
Cullinan: Starting at $434,950
Cullinan Black Badge: Starting at $504,950
drivetrain:
Power comes from a twin-turbocharged 6.7-liter V-12 producing 563 horsepower in the standard Cullinan and 592 horsepower in the Black Badge. Both versions pair the engine with a silky-smooth eight-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive. Despite weighing nearly three tons, the Cullinan accelerates with surprising urgency while maintaining the effortless composure expected from a Rolls-Royce. The adaptive air suspension continuously scans the road ahead using cameras and automatically adjusts damping to absorb imperfections before occupants even notice them. The result is an incredibly smooth, isolated ride that feels closer to gliding than driving. Steering remains light and predictable, prioritizing comfort over outright sportiness while ensuring the SUV remains easy to maneuver despite its imposing dimensions.

The Cullinan delivers EPA-estimated fuel economy ratings of 12 mpg in the city, 19 mpg on the highway, and 14 mpg combined. During real-world highway testing, it achieved approximately 21 mpg, demonstrating respectable long-distance efficiency for a luxury SUV powered by a large twin-turbocharged V-12 engine.
interior: The Cullinan's cabin exemplifies automotive luxury, blending exquisite craftsmanship with modern technology. Buyers can choose from an enormous selection of premium leathers, fine wood veneers, polished metal accents, and sustainable upholstery options, allowing every interior to be uniquely tailored. The front seats offer exceptional comfort with heating, ventilation, and multiple adjustment functions, while rear passengers enjoy limousine-like accommodations with generous legroom, massage functions, reclining seats, and optional individual captain's chairs. Rolls-Royce also offers the distinctive Viewing Suite, which transforms the cargo area into a pair of leather-wrapped seats overlooking the rear, creating an exclusive space for outdoor events. Cargo capacity stands at 21 cubic feet, expanding significantly when the rear seats are folded.
technology: A 10.2-inch touchscreen infotainment system integrates seamlessly into the dashboard and operates through Rolls-Royce's latest Spirit software. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard alongside Bluetooth connectivity, navigation, and access to the exclusive Rolls-Royce Whispers owner application. Rear-seat passengers receive dedicated entertainment displays with independent streaming capability, Bluetooth headphone connectivity, and full access to seat adjustment functions. An 18-speaker premium audio system delivers outstanding sound quality throughout the exceptionally quiet cabin.
safety: The Cullinan is equipped with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance technologies including adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, lane-departure warning, night vision, and numerous electronic safety systems that enhance driver confidence while preserving the effortless driving experience expected from a Rolls-Royce.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / Unlimited miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / Unlimited miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 4 years / Unlimited miles
pros: Supreme ride comfort, extraordinary craftsmanship, and virtually limitless personalization create an unmatched luxury SUV experience.
cons: Extremely expensive and its bold exterior styling may not appeal to every luxury buyer.
mn_take: The 2027 Cullinan remains the definitive ultra-luxury SUV, delivering comfort and exclusivity that few vehicles can rival.

car_name: 2027 Rolls-Royce Spectre Review
overview:
The 2027 Rolls-Royce Spectre continues to redefine what an ultra-luxury electric grand tourer should be. Rather than chasing headline-grabbing acceleration figures or class-leading driving range, Rolls-Royce has focused on delivering an effortless, silent, and exceptionally refined driving experience that stays true to the brand’s century-old philosophy. The Spectre combines handcrafted craftsmanship, cutting-edge electric technology, and unmistakable road presence into a package that feels unlike any other EV currently on sale.

For 2027, Rolls-Royce enhances the Spectre with more powerful electric motors, improved battery efficiency, and an estimated driving range exceeding 300 miles on higher-spec models. Interior refinements, new materials, updated illuminated dashboard elements, and additional personalization options further elevate the ownership experience. Although rivals such as the Lucid Air and Mercedes-Benz EQS offer significantly greater value and longer driving ranges, neither delivers the exclusivity, craftsmanship, and prestige that define the Spectre.
pricing:
Spectre: Starting at approximately $400,000
Spectre Black Badge: Starting at approximately $500,000
drivetrain:
The standard Spectre is powered by dual electric motors producing 592 horsepower, while the performance-focused Black Badge increases output to 670 horsepower. Both models feature an all-wheel-drive system that delivers instant torque with remarkable smoothness. Despite weighing well over three tons, the Spectre accelerates with effortless authority while maintaining the calm and composed demeanor expected from a Rolls-Royce. Rather than emphasizing aggressive handling, the adaptive suspension prioritizes supreme ride comfort, virtually eliminating road imperfections before they reach the cabin. Extensive sound insulation creates one of the quietest passenger compartments available in any production vehicle, allowing occupants to enjoy complete serenity even at highway speeds. The standard Spectre reaches 60 mph in approximately 3.7 seconds, making it remarkably quick while never sacrificing refinement for outright performance.

The Spectre uses a 102.0-kWh battery pack and now offers an estimated driving range of 296 to 326 miles, depending on the selected model. Battery improvements for 2027 have increased efficiency by roughly 18 percent compared to the previous version. DC fast charging comes standard, allowing convenient long-distance travel, although most owners are likely to recharge overnight using premium home charging installations.
interior: Every surface inside the Spectre showcases Rolls-Royce's extraordinary attention to craftsmanship. Premium leather, open-pore wood, polished metal trim, and customizable illuminated panels create an environment that feels more like a luxury lounge than an automobile. The signature Starlight Headliner remains one of the cabin's defining features, while illuminated door panels extend the celestial theme throughout the interior. Rear-hinged coach doors provide graceful entry and exit, emphasizing the ceremonial nature of every journey. Front occupants enjoy exceptionally comfortable bucket seats, while rear passengers benefit from individually sculpted seating, premium amenities, and the quiet atmosphere that has become synonymous with the Rolls-Royce name. Although the trunk offers only around 10 cubic feet of storage, it remains sufficient for luxury weekend travel.
technology: A 10.1-inch touchscreen infotainment system integrates seamlessly into the handcrafted dashboard without disrupting the cabin's elegant design. A fully digital instrument cluster provides essential driving information while maintaining a classic Rolls-Royce aesthetic. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard alongside Bluetooth connectivity, built-in navigation, and a premium 18-speaker Bespoke Audio sound system. The interface emphasizes simplicity and elegance rather than overwhelming drivers with unnecessary complexity.
safety: The Spectre comes equipped with an extensive suite of modern driver assistance technologies, including automated emergency braking, adaptive cruise control with lane-centering capability, lane-keeping assist, and numerous electronic safety systems that enhance confidence without diminishing the effortless driving experience.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / Unlimited miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / Unlimited miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 4 years / Unlimited miles
pros: Exceptional craftsmanship, whisper-quiet electric performance, and unmatched luxury make the Spectre one of the world's finest grand tourers.
cons: Extremely expensive and offers considerably less driving range than far more affordable luxury EVs.
mn_take: The 2027 Rolls-Royce Spectre proves that true luxury is defined by effortless refinement rather than numbers on a specification sheet.

car_name: 2027 Rolls-Royce Phantom Review
overview: The 2027 Rolls-Royce Phantom continues to represent the absolute pinnacle of handcrafted luxury motoring. Rather than chasing lap times or cutting-edge performance figures, the Phantom focuses on delivering an unmatched experience of serenity, prestige, and effortless refinement. Every journey feels ceremonial, whether you're arriving at a luxury hotel or simply commuting through city streets. Its commanding presence, iconic Pantheon grille, and timeless proportions ensure it remains one of the most recognizable automobiles ever built. Inside, the Phantom is less of a luxury sedan and more of a private lounge on wheels. Every surface is meticulously handcrafted using the finest leather, natural wood veneers, polished metal accents, and bespoke materials chosen by the owner. Rolls-Royce's virtually limitless customization program allows buyers to personalize nearly every detail, making each Phantom a one-of-one masterpiece.
pricing:
Phantom: Starting at $555,350
Phantom Extended Wheelbase: Starting at $635,350
MotorNation Recommendation: The Phantom Extended Wheelbase is the ideal choice, offering significantly more rear-seat space and the ultimate chauffeur-driven luxury experience.
drivetrain:
Powering every 2027 Phantom is a magnificent 6.7-liter twin-turbocharged V12 engine producing 563 horsepower, paired with an exceptionally smooth eight-speed automatic transmission that sends power exclusively to the rear wheels. Rather than emphasizing aggressive acceleration, the V12 delivers effortless torque with near-silent operation, allowing the Phantom to gather speed with remarkable grace. Despite its enormous size, the Phantom feels surprisingly composed thanks to rear-wheel steering and an advanced adaptive air suspension. A sophisticated road-scanning camera continuously analyzes the pavement ahead, preparing the suspension for potholes, undulations, and imperfections before the wheels even reach them. The result is a ride quality that feels almost detached from the road surface, creating the famous "magic carpet ride" experience for which Rolls-Royce is renowned. Acceleration remains impressive for a limousine of this size, with the standard Phantom estimated to reach 60 mph in around 4.5 seconds. However, outright performance is secondary to refinement, as every control input is calibrated to prioritize smoothness over sportiness.

Efficiency has never been a priority for a flagship Rolls-Royce, and the Phantom reflects that philosophy. The EPA estimates fuel economy at 12 mpg in the city and 19 mpg on the highway, figures that are expected from a handcrafted luxury limousine powered by a large twin-turbocharged V12 engine. Owners purchasing a Phantom are unlikely to prioritize fuel costs, as the vehicle is designed to deliver effortless performance and uncompromising refinement rather than efficiency. For its intended clientele, the extraordinary comfort and seamless power delivery far outweigh its substantial fuel consumption.
interior: The Phantom's cabin sets the benchmark for automotive luxury. Every component is handcrafted with obsessive attention to detail, from the thick leather upholstery and real wood veneers to the polished metal switchgear and plush carpeting. Rolls-Royce even offers the signature Starlight Headliner, which recreates a night sky using hundreds of individually illuminated fiber-optic lights. Rear-seat passengers receive the greatest attention. The Extended Wheelbase model provides limousine-like legroom, complemented by reclining massaging seats, power-operated coach doors, privacy curtains, refrigerated storage, premium entertainment systems, and virtually endless bespoke customization options. Whether driven personally or chauffeured, occupants experience an atmosphere closer to a private luxury suite than a conventional automobile. Practicality is respectable as well, with a generous 19-cubic-foot trunk capable of accommodating multiple pieces of luggage, including bespoke Rolls-Royce luggage sets designed specifically for the Phantom.
technology: Although craftsmanship remains the Phantom's defining characteristic, its technology is thoroughly modern. A beautifully integrated 10.3-inch infotainment display sits discreetly behind a full-width glass dashboard panel, preserving the cabin's elegant design while providing access to navigation, media, and vehicle settings. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, alongside Bluetooth connectivity, built-in navigation, and Wi-Fi capability. Rear passengers enjoy individual touchscreen displays mounted behind the front seats, allowing independent control of entertainment, navigation, and vehicle functions. The available Bespoke 18-speaker premium audio system delivers exceptional sound quality, transforming the silent cabin into a world-class listening environment while maintaining the Phantom's signature serenity.
safety: The 2027 Phantom combines traditional luxury with a comprehensive suite of modern safety technologies. Standard equipment includes forward collision warning, lane-departure warning, and front and rear parking sensors, helping the driver maneuver the large sedan with confidence. Buyers can also equip the Phantom with adaptive cruise control, night vision assistance, and advanced laser lighting technology for improved visibility during nighttime driving. While Rolls-Royce prioritizes passenger comfort above all else, the Phantom incorporates sophisticated driver-assistance systems that complement its effortless driving experience.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / Unlimited miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / Unlimited miles
Complimentary Scheduled Maintenance: 4 years / Unlimited miles
pros: Outstanding handcrafted luxury, whisper-quiet V12, unmatched ride comfort, limitless personalization, and an exceptional rear-seat experience.
cons: Extremely expensive, poor fuel economy, chauffeur-focused dynamics, and costly bespoke options.
mn_take: The 2027 Rolls-Royce Phantom remains the ultimate expression of handcrafted luxury and effortless prestige.

car_name: 2026 Rolls-Royce Ghost Review
overview:
The 2026 Rolls-Royce Ghost remains one of the finest expressions of modern luxury, combining handcrafted craftsmanship with effortless V-12 power and an almost supernatural ride quality. Sitting below the flagship Phantom in the brand's lineup, the Ghost offers a more understated personality without sacrificing the opulence expected from a Rolls-Royce. Every surface inside is meticulously crafted, from the hand-stitched leather upholstery to the open-pore wood veneers and polished metal accents.

Despite its immense size and weight, the Ghost delivers remarkable composure and refinement. Advanced technologies such as all-wheel steering, GPS-assisted transmission mapping, and a road-scanning suspension system ensure that occupants experience a level of comfort few automobiles can match. Whether driven personally or enjoyed from the rear seat, the Ghost feels less like a conventional luxury sedan and more like a moving sanctuary.
pricing:
Ghost: Starting at $370,750
Ghost Extended Wheelbase: Starting at $420,750
Ghost Black Badge: Starting at $440,750
drivetrain:
Powering the standard Ghost is a twin-turbocharged 6.7-liter V-12 producing 563 horsepower, while the Black Badge variant raises output to 591 horsepower. An eight-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive ensure seamless delivery of power with virtually no drama. Acceleration is effortless rather than aggressive, with Rolls-Royce claiming a 0-60 mph time of around 4.6 seconds. More impressive than outright speed, however, is the Ghost's uncanny smoothness. The adaptive suspension continuously reads the road ahead and adjusts itself before imperfections are even encountered, creating an almost floating sensation. Rear-wheel steering and balanced weight distribution also provide surprising agility for such a large luxury sedan.

Efficiency is understandably not a priority in a hand-built V-12 limousine. EPA estimates stand at 12 mpg in the city and 19 mpg on the highway. While those figures are modest, buyers in this segment are unlikely to prioritize fuel consumption over refinement and exclusivity. The Ghost's effortless power delivery and whisper-quiet cruising character more than compensate for its thirst, making every journey feel exceptionally serene.
interior: The cabin of the Ghost represents automotive craftsmanship at its highest level. Rich leather upholstery, thick carpeting, genuine wood trim, and polished metal accents create an environment that feels more like a luxury suite than a sedan. Optional features such as the Starlight headliner transform nighttime journeys into something truly special. Rear-seat comfort is equally impressive. Passengers enjoy generous legroom, massaging seats, entertainment screens, and exceptional noise isolation. The Extended Wheelbase model further enhances rear-seat accommodation, making it ideal for chauffeur-driven owners. The 17-cubic-foot trunk provides ample luggage space, and Rolls-Royce even offers bespoke luggage sets tailored specifically to fit the compartment perfectly.
technology: A wide glass panel spans the dashboard and houses the digital instrument cluster, infotainment display, and unique illuminated fascia elements. The 10.3-inch touchscreen supports navigation, Bluetooth connectivity, wireless Apple CarPlay, and Android Auto. Rear passengers benefit from a dedicated entertainment system that allows control of media, navigation, and streaming functions. The standard 18-speaker Bespoke audio system delivers 1,400 watts of power, creating a concert-hall experience regardless of seating position. Technology is integrated elegantly rather than aggressively, preserving the timeless atmosphere expected from a Rolls-Royce.
safety: The Ghost comes equipped with an extensive suite of driver-assistance systems designed to enhance safety without intruding on the driving experience. Automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, adaptive cruise control, and lane-keeping assistance are all standard. Although crash-test ratings are unavailable, the Ghost's advanced safety systems and sophisticated engineering provide confidence befitting a flagship luxury sedan.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years, unlimited miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years, unlimited miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 4 years, unlimited miles
pros: Exceptional craftsmanship and unmatched cabin luxury.
cons: Extremely expensive and expensive to personalize.
mn_take: The 2026 Rolls-Royce Ghost remains one of the most refined luxury sedans in the world, delivering effortless V-12 power and extraordinary craftsmanship with unmatched elegance.

car_name: 2026 Rivian R1T
overview:
The 2026 Rivian R1T remains one of the most compelling electric pickups on the market. While competitors have entered the segment with larger dimensions or more traditional truck credentials, the R1T continues to distinguish itself through clever packaging, exceptional ride quality, and supercar-rivaling performance. New for 2026 is an in-house Quad-Motor setup producing an astonishing 1,025 horsepower, further elevating the truck's capabilities both on and off the road.

Despite being closer in size to a midsize pickup, the R1T offers practicality that rivals some full-size trucks thanks to its innovative gear tunnel, spacious front trunk, and impressive towing capacity. Combined with premium appointments and a driving experience that feels more refined than rugged, the R1T continues to set the benchmark for electric pickups.
pricing:
Dual-Motor Standard Pack: Starting at $74,885
Dual-Motor Large Pack: Starting at $81,885
Performance Dual-Motor Large Pack: Starting at $86,885
Dual-Motor Max Pack: Starting at $88,885
Performance Dual-Motor Max Pack: Starting at $93,885
Tri-Motor Max Pack: Starting at $102,885
Quad-Motor Max Pack: Starting at $117,885
Launch Edition Quad-Motor Max Pack: Starting at $121,885
drivetrain:
Rivian offers an impressively broad powertrain lineup. The standard Dual-Motor configuration generates 533 horsepower and 610 lb-ft of torque, while the Performance Dual-Motor increases output to 665 horsepower and 829 lb-ft. Buyers seeking extreme performance can opt for the Tri-Motor variant producing 850 horsepower and 1,103 lb-ft, while the flagship Quad-Motor raises the bar with 1,025 horsepower and 1,198 lb-ft of torque. Acceleration is extraordinary. The Quad-Motor reaches 60 mph in just 2.6 seconds, placing it among the quickest production trucks ever built. Yet the R1T's brilliance lies not only in speed but also in its composure. Steering remains direct, ride comfort is remarkably supple, and the adjustable air suspension gives the truck an impressive blend of luxury and off-road capability. Towing capability reaches 11,000 pounds, while payload capacity stands at 1,764 pounds. However, towing heavy trailers significantly affects real-world range.

Efficiency varies depending on battery pack and motor configuration. EPA estimates range between 71 and 94 MPGe in the city and 63 to 80 MPGe on the highway. The Max battery pack offers the greatest efficiency and longest driving range.

Three battery options are available:

Standard Pack: Up to 258 miles
Large Pack: Up to 292 miles
Max Pack: Up to 420 miles

DC fast charging reaches up to 220 kW, allowing a 10–80 percent recharge in approximately 30 to 41 minutes. For 2026, every R1T adopts the North American Charging Standard (NACS) port, granting access to Tesla Superchargers while including a CCS adapter for broader compatibility.
interior: Inside, the R1T delivers a refined atmosphere that blends premium materials with practical usability. Leather upholstery, open-pore wood trim, and comfortable seating contribute to a sophisticated cabin environment. Visibility is excellent, and generous headroom and legroom ensure comfort for both front and rear passengers. Rear-seat occupants enjoy ample space and premium finishes, making long journeys comfortable. Storage remains one of the truck's strongest attributes. In addition to the cargo bed, the R1T features a spacious front trunk, a lockable gear tunnel positioned between the cabin and bed, and additional in-bed storage compartments. Rivian claims a total of 12 cubic feet of lockable storage, enhancing the truck's versatility.
technology: Dominating the dashboard is a 15.6-inch central touchscreen paired with a digital instrument display. Rivian's interface is clean and responsive, utilizing expandable tiles for easier access to navigation, media, climate settings, and vehicle functions. Connectivity features include over-the-air updates, remote vehicle commands, live navigation, digital key functionality, and the Connect+ service, which adds video streaming and access to thousands of apps. Buyers can choose between a standard 10-speaker audio system and an optional 16-speaker premium system with Dolby Atmos support. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto remain absent, which continues to be one of the few notable shortcomings in an otherwise advanced cabin.
safety:
The 2026 R1T comes equipped with Rivian's enhanced driver-assistance suite featuring 11 cameras, five radars, and multiple redundant sensors designed to improve performance in adverse weather and low-light conditions.

Standard safety features include:

Automatic emergency braking
Adaptive cruise control
Lane-departure warning
Advanced hands-free driver-assistance technology
AI-based predictive safety systems

The extensive sensor network provides a reassuring layer of confidence for highway cruising and daily driving.
warranty:
Rivian offers one of the strongest warranty packages in the electric vehicle segment.

Limited Warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles
Battery and Powertrain Warranty: 8 years or 175,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None

The lengthy battery and drivetrain coverage provides additional peace of mind for long-term ownership.
pros: Exceptional performance and class-leading ride quality.
cons: Lack of Apple CarPlay and Android Auto remains frustrating.
mn_take: The 2026 Rivian R1T remains the benchmark electric pickup by combining luxury, innovation, and breathtaking performance without compromising utility.

car_name: 2026 Rivian R1S Review
overview: The 2026 Rivian R1S continues to refine the formula that made it one of the most compelling electric SUVs on the market. Combining rugged capability, genuine seven-passenger practicality, and impressive performance, the R1S occupies a unique position between luxury SUV and adventure machine. For 2026, Rivian raises the stakes with an all-new Quad-Motor variant producing an astonishing 1,025 horsepower and introducing independent wheel control for enhanced off-road capability and dynamic precision. Despite increasing competition from newcomers such as the Lucid Gravity, Volvo EX90, Hyundai Ioniq 9, and Kia EV9, the R1S remains distinctive thanks to its premium cabin, adjustable air suspension, and remarkable driving range. It is a vehicle equally comfortable exploring remote trails or carrying a family across long distances in quiet luxury.
pricing:
Dual-Motor Standard Pack – $78,885
Dual-Motor Large Pack – $85,885
Performance Dual-Motor Large Pack – $90,885
Dual-Motor Max Pack – $92,885
Performance Dual-Motor Max Pack – $97,885
Tri-Motor Max Pack – $108,885
Quad-Motor Max Pack – $123,885
Launch Edition Quad-Motor Max Pack – $127,885

The Dual-Motor Large Pack represents the sweet spot of the lineup, delivering strong performance and an impressive balance between range and value. Enthusiasts seeking ultimate capability will find the Quad-Motor variants particularly tempting.
drivetrain:
The R1S lineup offers four distinct powertrain configurations. The entry-level Dual-Motor model produces 533 horsepower, while Performance Dual-Motor variants increase output further. The Tri-Motor version delivers 850 horsepower, and the headline-grabbing Quad-Motor model develops a staggering 1,025 horsepower. Rivian's latest "one-wheel, one-motor" philosophy allows each wheel to operate independently, providing exceptional traction and stability. The system even enables innovative off-road functions such as the "Kick Turn" feature, which rotates the vehicle more effectively in challenging terrain. Additional drive modes including Desert Rally and Hill Climb demonstrate Rivian's motorsport-inspired approach to software tuning. A revised suspension calibration improves body control and ride composure, while the standard adjustable air suspension provides up to 15 inches of ground clearance. Performance remains breathtaking, with the Tri-Motor variant reaching 60 mph in just 2.8 seconds. Few three-row SUVs can combine such explosive acceleration with genuine off-road capability.

Efficiency varies according to battery size and powertrain configuration. Dual-Motor models achieve EPA ratings of up to 94 MPGe in city driving and 77 MPGe on the highway, while the high-performance Quad-Motor variants sacrifice some efficiency, returning as low as 71 MPGe city and 63 MPGe highway. Driving range remains one of the R1S's greatest strengths. Depending on configuration, range spans from 258 miles to an impressive 410 miles. Real-world highway testing of the Tri-Motor Max Pack delivered around 250 miles at sustained 75-mph speeds.
interior: The R1S cabin embraces understated luxury rather than excessive flash. Premium materials, tasteful wood accents, and soft-touch surfaces create an elegant and welcoming atmosphere. Heated and ventilated front seats come standard, while the commanding driving position provides excellent outward visibility. Second-row accommodations are comfortable and spacious enough for adults, although the third row is best suited for children or occasional use. Access to the rear-most seats requires sliding the second-row bench forward, which can be somewhat cumbersome. Cargo versatility is exceptional. The front trunk adds useful storage, while folding both rear rows creates a cavernous cargo area capable of accommodating family vacations, camping gear, or bulky equipment. The R1S remains one of the most practical luxury EVs available.
technology: A massive 15.6-inch touchscreen dominates the dashboard and houses nearly every vehicle function. Rivian's software interface is intuitive and highly customizable, with permanent shortcuts for navigation, climate controls, and media. Connectivity features include eight USB ports, dual wireless charging pads, Wi-Fi capability for up to eight devices, and available premium 19-speaker audio with Dolby Atmos support and Apple Spatial Audio compatibility. However, the absence of Apple CarPlay and Android Auto remains one of the R1S's biggest shortcomings. Owners must rely entirely on Rivian's native software ecosystem, which may disappoint users accustomed to smartphone integration.
safety: Every R1S comes equipped with Rivian's advanced Autonomy Platform. Utilizing 11 cameras, five radars, 38 sensors, and AI-powered predictive systems, the SUV offers an extensive suite of safety technologies. Standard features include automated emergency braking, adaptive cruise control, lane-departure warning, and various collision mitigation systems. The sophisticated sensor array is designed to provide enhanced visibility and performance even in adverse weather conditions.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: Five years or 60,000 miles.
Battery and Powertrain Warranty: Eight years or 175,000 miles.
Corrosion Coverage: Included.
Complimentary Scheduled Maintenance: None.

Rivian provides one of the strongest battery and drivetrain warranties in the segment, offering peace of mind for long-term ownership.
pros: Impressive range, luxurious interior, exceptional off-road capability, and supercar-level acceleration in higher trims.
cons: No Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, touchscreen dependency for most controls, and growing competition from less expensive rivals.
mn_take: The 2026 Rivian R1S remains one of the most versatile electric SUVs on sale, blending premium comfort, genuine adventure capability, and remarkable performance into a package that feels uniquely Rivian.

car_name: 2026 Rimac Nevera Review
overview: The 2026 Rimac Nevera occupies a realm where engineering brilliance borders on science fiction. Built in Croatia and limited to just 150 examples worldwide, the electric hypercar combines extraordinary technology with astonishing performance. Its quad-motor powertrain produces levels of acceleration that were once reserved for theoretical discussions rather than production automobiles. Despite possessing over 1,800 horsepower in standard form and more than 2,100 horsepower in the Nevera R, the car is far more than a numbers exercise. The chassis delivers remarkable balance, the steering communicates with surprising delicacy, and the experience remains emotional despite the absence of a traditional combustion engine. The Nevera proves that electrification does not have to come at the expense of character.
pricing:
Nevera – From approximately $2,200,000
Nevera R – From approximately $2,500,000
Nevera R Founder's Edition – From approximately $3,000,000

The standard Nevera already offers unimaginable levels of performance, but the even more powerful Nevera R raises the bar with over 2,100 horsepower and enhanced dynamics. Buyers can extensively personalize materials, colors, and finishes to create truly bespoke examples.
drivetrain:
At the heart of the Nevera lies one of the most sophisticated electric drivetrains ever developed. Four independent motors power all four wheels, allowing Rimac's advanced torque-vectoring system to distribute power with incredible precision. The standard Nevera produces 1,813 horsepower, while the track-focused Nevera R pushes output to an astounding 2,107 horsepower. Such figures enable acceleration that feels almost unreal. Rimac claims the standard model reaches 60 mph in just 1.85 seconds, while the Nevera R cuts that figure to an astonishing 1.74 seconds. Yet raw acceleration is only part of the story. A carbon-fiber monocoque chassis, active aerodynamics, perfectly weighted steering, and immense braking capability give the Nevera the finesse expected of a world-class hypercar. Unlike many ultra-high-performance EVs, the Nevera manages to create a genuine connection between machine and driver.

Efficiency is understandably not the primary mission of a 2,000-horsepower hypercar, but the Nevera delivers respectable figures considering its performance capabilities. The EPA estimates around 50 MPGe in city driving and 51 MPGe on the highway. While those numbers appear impressive, enthusiastic use of the powertrain will naturally have a dramatic effect on range and energy consumption.
interior: The Nevera's cabin blends race-inspired engineering with handcrafted luxury. Exposed carbon fiber, billet aluminum, Alcantara, and premium leather create an environment that feels technical yet elegant. Every example can be tailored to the individual owner's tastes, ensuring no two cars are exactly alike. The seating position is low and purposeful, with supportive sports seats designed to withstand extreme lateral forces. Visibility is surprisingly good for a hypercar, and overall refinement is impressive considering the vehicle's extraordinary performance envelope. Practicality is understandably secondary. Storage space is minimal, with only a tiny compartment beneath the rear glass hatch suitable for a few small bags or luxury essentials.
technology: Three digital displays dominate the cabin and provide access to vehicle information, telemetry, and infotainment functions. The central touchscreen is mounted on machined aluminum hardware robust enough to endure the tremendous g-forces generated by the car. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are included, along with Bluetooth connectivity and wireless smartphone charging. Audio duties are handled by an eight-speaker Focal Utopia M sound system, delivering premium acoustics befitting a multimillion-dollar hypercar. A dedicated passenger display allows occupants to monitor acceleration, speed, and various performance metrics, adding another layer to the Nevera's immersive experience.
safety: The Nevera focuses primarily on performance rather than advanced driver-assistance technologies. Conventional features such as blind-spot monitoring and adaptive cruise control are absent. However, the car's rigid carbon-fiber structure, sophisticated traction management, powerful braking system, and torque-vectoring capabilities contribute significantly to overall safety and stability during high-speed driving.
warranty:
Battery Warranty: Eight years with unlimited mileage.
Limited Warranty: Details not publicly disclosed.
Powertrain Warranty: Details not publicly disclosed.
Complimentary Maintenance: Not announced.

While public information regarding ownership coverage remains limited, the battery warranty provides reassuring long-term protection for such an advanced electric powertrain.
pros: Immense quad-motor power delivers acceleration unlike almost anything else on the planet.
cons: Limited range and an astronomical price restrict ownership to a tiny group of buyers.
mn_take: The 2026 Rimac Nevera transforms electric performance into an emotional experience, proving that the future of hypercars can be just as thrilling as their combustion-powered legends.

car_name: 2027 Ram HD Review
overview: The 2027 Ram HD lineup continues to prove that heavy-duty trucks don't have to sacrifice comfort for capability. Available in 2500 and 3500 forms, Ram's heavy-duty pickups combine immense towing and payload capacities with interiors that rival luxury SUVs. Whether configured as a work-focused Tradesman or a leather-lined Limited, the Ram HD manages to blend brute strength with refinement in a way few competitors can match. For 2027, the biggest development is the arrival of the legendary Cummins diesel engine in the Power Wagon for the first time, giving off-road enthusiasts access to the massive torque and long-range towing capability previously unavailable in Ram's most adventurous heavy-duty model. From hauling equipment and fifth-wheel trailers to crossing rough terrain, the Ram HD remains one of the most versatile trucks in the segment.
pricing:
Tradesman – $50,170
Lone Star – $53,920
Big Horn – $53,920
Black Express – $56,385
Warlock – $59,715
Laramie – $65,625
Rebel – $73,070
Power Wagon – $76,565
Limited – $77,635
Longhorn – $77,635
drivetrain:
Ram offers two powerful engines across the HD lineup. Standard models are powered by a naturally aspirated 6.4-liter HEMI V-8 producing 405 horsepower and 429 pound-feet of torque. Buyers requiring serious pulling power can opt for the legendary 6.7-liter Cummins turbo-diesel inline-six, which delivers 430 horsepower and an astonishing 1,075 pound-feet of torque. Both engines are paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission and are available with rear- or four-wheel drive. The gasoline V-8 provides brisk acceleration and smooth operation, making it ideal for daily driving and lighter-duty tasks. The diesel, meanwhile, shines when heavy trailers enter the equation. Its immense low-end torque makes towing effortless, and recent refinements have improved both responsiveness and noise suppression.

Capability remains extraordinary. The Ram 3500 can tow up to 36,610 pounds when properly equipped, while payload capacity reaches nearly 7,950 pounds. The 2500 model offers up to 20,000 pounds of towing capability, ensuring there is a configuration suitable for nearly every commercial or recreational requirement. Despite their size, Ram HD trucks deliver impressive ride quality. The suspension absorbs imperfections well, and the cabin remains remarkably composed, even over rough roads. The Power Wagon and Rebel trims add genuine off-road capability, while the diesel-equipped Power Wagon introduces a new dimension of torque and range for adventure-minded buyers.

Official EPA ratings are unavailable because heavy-duty pickups exceed the weight classification required for EPA testing. However, real-world results have proven encouraging. In independent highway testing, a Ram 2500 Crew Cab 4x4 equipped with the Cummins diesel returned an impressive 22 mpg at highway speeds. While city consumption remains substantial, the diesel engine's efficiency under load and on long-distance journeys makes it a strong choice for those who regularly tow heavy trailers.
interior: The Ram HD continues to offer arguably the most luxurious interior in the heavy-duty truck segment. Material quality is exceptional, with available leather upholstery, wood trim, and premium finishes giving upper trims an almost SUV-like atmosphere. Front occupants enjoy spacious accommodations and a choice between bucket seats or a traditional bench. Heated and ventilated seats, power adjustments, and lumbar support are available across much of the lineup. Rear-seat comfort depends on cab configuration, but Crew Cab models provide generous room while Mega Cab versions offer class-leading space. The additional rear legroom makes long journeys far more comfortable for passengers. Practicality remains excellent with available 6-foot-4-inch and 8-foot cargo beds, allowing owners to tailor the truck to work or recreational duties.
technology: Ram equips the HD lineup with one of the segment's most advanced infotainment systems. Standard models receive an 8.4-inch touchscreen, while optional 12.0-inch and massive 14.5-inch displays provide a more upscale and modern experience. An available 10.3-inch passenger display further enhances the truck's technology credentials. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, while navigation and Wi-Fi connectivity are available. Multiple USB ports and household-style power outlets ensure tools and devices remain charged throughout the workday. Audiophiles can opt for the premium 17-speaker Harman Kardon audio system, delivering exceptional sound quality and elevating the cabin's luxury credentials.
safety: Ram offers an extensive list of driver-assistance technologies for the HD lineup. Standard safety equipment includes forward-collision warning, automatic emergency braking, and adaptive cruise control. Optional systems add blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, and additional trailer-focused assistance technologies that improve confidence when hauling heavy loads. These features help make the Ram HD easier to maneuver despite its considerable size.
warranty:
Ram backs its heavy-duty trucks with one of the strongest powertrain warranties in the segment.

Limited Warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles.
Powertrain Warranty: 10 years or 100,000 miles.
Complimentary Maintenance: None.

While free scheduled maintenance is absent, the lengthy powertrain coverage exceeds what most rivals provide.
pros: Class-leading interior quality combines with massive towing capability and a refined diesel powertrain.
cons: Huge dimensions make parking and maneuvering challenging, while fuel consumption remains substantial around town.
mn_take: The 2027 Ram HD delivers exceptional capability without compromising comfort, making it one of the most complete heavy-duty pickups money can buy.

car_name: 2027 Ram 1500 REV Review
overview: The 2027 Ram 1500 REV represents a fascinating evolution of the full-size pickup truck. Rather than committing to a conventional battery-electric setup, Ram has developed a sophisticated range-extended electric powertrain that combines electric propulsion with the reassurance of a gasoline engine acting solely as a generator. The result is a truck that promises electric driving for everyday use while eliminating the range anxiety often associated with pure EVs. Despite its advanced powertrain, the REV remains every bit a Ram 1500. It retains the brand's body-on-frame architecture, refined ride quality, and upscale cabin that have made the conventional model one of the most comfortable pickups on the market. With a claimed combined range of up to 690 miles and towing capability reaching 14,000 pounds, the REV aims to bridge the gap between traditional gasoline trucks and the electric future.
pricing:
Tradesman – $60,000 (est.)
Big Horn – $70,000 (est.)
Limited – $80,000 (est.)
Tungsten – $100,000 (est.)
drivetrain:
Unlike conventional hybrids, the Ram 1500 REV's 3.6-liter V-6 engine never directly powers the wheels. Instead, it functions as a generator that supplies electricity to a battery pack, which in turn powers dual electric motors. Combined output stands at an impressive 647 horsepower and 610 pound-feet of torque, with standard all-wheel drive across the range. The electric motors provide instant response and strong acceleration, while the body-on-frame platform preserves the toughness expected from a full-size pickup. Standard air suspension enhances ride quality and features a kneeling function to ease loading and entry. Ram's independent rear suspension continues to give the truck one of the most refined rides in the segment. Capability remains a major highlight. Properly equipped models can tow up to 14,000 pounds and carry payloads of up to 2,625 pounds, putting the REV among the most capable electrified pickups currently available.

Official EPA ratings have yet to be announced, but the REV offers an estimated 145 miles of all-electric driving before the gasoline-powered generator becomes necessary. When the battery and fuel tank are fully utilized, Ram claims a remarkable total driving range of up to 690 miles. Its massive 69.7-kWh battery pack can also be replenished through DC fast charging, with Ram estimating a 20-to-80 percent recharge in approximately 45 minutes. This combination of electric capability and extended range makes the REV particularly attractive for buyers who regularly cover long distances or tow heavy loads.
interior: Inside, the Ram 1500 REV delivers a premium environment that rivals many luxury SUVs. High-quality materials, intricate metallic detailing, and available suede accents give the cabin an upscale atmosphere. Heated and ventilated leather seats are available, along with massage functionality on upper trims. Crew Cab models provide abundant rear-seat space, making long journeys comfortable for passengers. The rear bench folds upward to accommodate larger items inside the cabin, while the standard 5-foot-7-inch bed is complemented by the practical RamBox storage system, providing secure and weather-resistant cargo compartments. Ride comfort remains exceptional thanks to the truck's air suspension and well-controlled chassis. Even on rough surfaces, the REV delivers a refined and composed driving experience that few competitors can match.
technology: Technology plays a major role inside the 1500 REV. A 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster comes standard, while buyers can choose between 12.0-inch and 14.5-inch infotainment touchscreens. An optional 10.3-inch passenger display adds another layer of functionality and entertainment. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, and dual wireless charging pads provide convenient charging for two smartphones simultaneously. Audiophiles can opt for the exclusive 23-speaker Klipsch premium audio system available on the range-topping Tungsten trim. The system's customizable interface allows frequently used functions to remain easily accessible, contributing to a user-friendly experience despite the abundance of technology.
safety: Ram equips the 1500 REV with a broad suite of driver-assistance technologies. Standard equipment includes automated emergency braking, pedestrian detection, and lane-keeping assistance. Available features include adaptive cruise control and additional advanced driver-assistance systems designed to improve long-distance comfort and safety. Combined with the truck's strong structure and extensive safety technology, the REV aims to provide confidence whether commuting or towing heavy loads.
warranty:
Ram backs the 1500 REV with competitive warranty coverage.

Limited Warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles.
Powertrain Warranty: 10 years or 100,000 miles.
Hybrid Component Warranty: 8 years or 100,000 miles.
Complimentary Maintenance: None.

The generous powertrain coverage remains one of the strongest offerings in the full-size pickup segment.
pros: Outstanding 690-mile combined range and impressive towing capability.
cons: Pricing climbs quickly on upper trims and no complimentary maintenance is included.
mn_take: The 2027 Ram 1500 REV successfully blends electric efficiency with traditional truck capability, creating one of the most compelling and versatile pickups in the segment.

overview:
The 2027 Ram 1500 continues to distinguish itself in the fiercely competitive full-size pickup segment by combining truck capability with ride comfort that feels remarkably refined. From work-oriented Tradesman models to the luxurious Tungsten, the Ram lineup offers a broad range of personalities. Buyers can choose from a mild-hybrid V-6, the returning 5.7-liter Hemi V-8, and Ram's twin-turbocharged Hurricane inline-six in two states of tune. For 2027, Ram also expands its performance ambitions with the new Rumble Bee family of street trucks, including the range-topping 777-horsepower Rumble Bee SRT.

Although rivals from Ford and Chevrolet offer higher maximum towing figures, few trucks can match the Ram's combination of smooth ride quality, upscale cabin materials, and everyday comfort.
pricing:
Tradesman — Starting at $45,170
Express — Starting at $47,295
Lone Star — Starting at $50,425
Big Horn — Starting at $50,425
Warlock — Starting at $56,010
Rumble Bee — Starting around $60,000
Back Country — Starting around $63,000
Laramie — Starting at $64,475
Limited — Starting at $79,400
Longhorn — Starting at $79,895
Rumble Bee 392 — Starting around $85,000
Tungsten — Starting at $91,795
Rumble Bee SRT — Starting around $100,000

The Laramie remains the sweet spot in the lineup, offering premium leather upholstery, heated and ventilated seats, power-folding mirrors, and 22-inch wheels. Buyers who appreciate traditional V-8 power can also equip it with the no-cost Hemi option.
drivetrain:
Ram offers an unusually wide range of engines. The standard 3.6-liter V-6 produces 305 horsepower and incorporates a 48-volt mild-hybrid system. The revived 5.7-liter Hemi V-8 delivers 395 horsepower and retains the signature exhaust note that many truck enthusiasts appreciate. Ram's twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter Hurricane inline-six generates either 420 or 540 horsepower and provides exceptional refinement along with effortless acceleration. Off-road buyers can opt for the Rebel, while performance enthusiasts have the new Rumble Bee family. The standard Rumble Bee uses the Hemi V-8, while the Rumble Bee 392 adopts a naturally aspirated 6.4-liter V-8 with 470 horsepower. At the top sits the Rumble Bee SRT, powered by a supercharged 6.2-liter V-8 delivering 777 horsepower. Ram claims a 0-60 mph time of just 3.4 seconds, making it one of the quickest pickup trucks ever built. Every engine pairs with an eight-speed automatic transmission. Rear-wheel drive and four-wheel drive configurations are available, while the Ram's unique rear coil-spring suspension delivers a smoother ride than most competitors. Models equipped with the optional air suspension benefit from adjustable ride height for improved efficiency and off-road capability.

The 2027 Ram 1500 remains highly capable despite not leading the segment outright. Properly equipped models can tow up to 11,610 pounds and carry a maximum payload of 2,360 pounds. Those requiring heavier-duty capabilities may want to consider the Ramcharger or the heavy-duty Ram HD lineup.

Fuel economy varies significantly depending on engine choice. The most efficient configuration is the rear-wheel-drive V-6, rated at up to 20 mpg city and 25 mpg highway. Models powered by the standard-output Hurricane inline-six achieve up to 21 mpg combined, while the high-output 540-horsepower version sacrifices some efficiency in favor of stronger performance. Real-world testing of a 540-horsepower 4x4 model returned 20 mpg during highway driving, while a long-term Big Horn Crew Cab with the 420-horsepower Hurricane averaged 18 mpg on the highway.
interior: The Ram 1500 continues to offer one of the finest interiors in the pickup segment. Crew Cab models provide generous passenger space, excellent outward visibility, and numerous storage compartments. Buyers can choose between front bucket seats or a bench arrangement with a folding center console. Higher trims introduce heated and ventilated seating, panoramic sunroofs, premium leather upholstery, genuine wood trim, and reclining rear seats. The luxurious Tungsten trim raises the bar even further with quilted leather, massaging 24-way power-adjustable seats, and a suede headliner. Both Quad Cab and Crew Cab body styles provide spacious rear accommodations, although the Crew Cab offers noticeably greater comfort. Available bed lengths include five-foot-seven-inch and six-foot-four-inch configurations.
technology: Ram continues to offer one of the best infotainment systems in the class. A 12.0-inch touchscreen is standard, while higher trims receive a massive 14.5-inch display. An optional 10.3-inch passenger screen further enhances the cabin's technology appeal. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, while buyers can choose among several audio systems, including a 23-speaker Klipsch premium setup. Multiple USB ports, household power outlets, and numerous charging solutions make the Ram exceptionally versatile for both work and family use.
safety: The Ram 1500 includes a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies. Standard equipment includes automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert. Optional features include adaptive cruise control with a hands-free driving capability, enhancing convenience during long-distance travel.
warranty:
Limited warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles
Powertrain warranty: 10 years or 100,000 miles
Complimentary scheduled maintenance: None
pros: Class-leading ride comfort and a richly appointed cabin make it one of the most refined full-size pickups available.
cons: Maximum towing capacity trails several key competitors and pricing climbs rapidly on higher trims.
mn_take: The 2027 Ram 1500 blends luxury, comfort, and performance better than any other half-ton pickup, making it an exceptionally well-rounded truck.

car_name: 2026 Porsche Macan Electric
overview: The 2026 Porsche Macan Electric proves that electrification doesn't have to come at the expense of driver engagement. Built on an 800-volt architecture and offered alongside the gasoline-powered Macan, the all-electric model retains the agile, sporty personality that has made the Macan Porsche's best-selling vehicle. Despite its increased weight and EV packaging, the Macan Electric delivers exceptional chassis balance, quick steering, and impressive acceleration, making it one of the most rewarding electric SUVs on the market. For 2026, Porsche introduces a new GTS variant that slots between the 4S and Turbo models. Additional upgrades include a digital key for Apple and Android devices, expanded third-party app support, smarter parking assistance, and an increased towing capacity of up to 5,500 pounds.
pricing:
Base — Starting at $82,650
Macan 4 — Starting at $86,350
Macan 4S — Starting at $92,250
Macan GTS — Starting at $107,650
Macan Turbo — Starting at $115,050

Porsche's vast catalog of options allows extensive customization, but the Macan 4 strikes the best balance between range, performance, and price. The Premium Package, which adds ventilated front seats, heated rear seats, four-zone climate control, and a Bose audio system, is particularly appealing.
drivetrain:
The Macan Electric lineup offers four distinct levels of performance. The base model uses a rear-mounted motor producing 335 horsepower, or 355 hp with Overboost activated. Dual-motor all-wheel-drive versions increase output considerably, with the Macan 4 producing up to 402 horsepower, the 4S reaching 509 hp, the GTS delivering 563 hp, and the Turbo topping the range with a staggering 630 hp. Every model benefits from adaptive air suspension, while higher trims receive additional technologies such as torque vectoring, electronically controlled differentials, and Porsche Active Suspension Management. Rear-wheel steering is optional, enhancing agility at low speeds and stability during high-speed driving. Performance is genuinely sports-car quick. The Turbo reaches 60 mph in just 2.9 seconds, while even the base model completes the sprint in 5.0 seconds. The new GTS combines excellent body control with exceptional cornering precision, making it one of the most engaging electric SUVs currently available.

The Macan Electric uses a 95.0-kWh battery pack and supports DC fast charging at up to 270 kW. During testing, charging from 10 to 90 percent required approximately 33 minutes. EPA estimates vary between 288 and 315 miles depending on the model. The standard rear-wheel-drive version offers the greatest efficiency, while the more powerful variants trade some range for stronger acceleration. Porsche's innovative battery architecture can split into two 400-volt sections when connected to lower-voltage chargers, improving charging flexibility. Maximum towing capacity has increased to 5,500 pounds, giving the Macan Electric a practical advantage over many competitors.
interior: The Macan Electric features a driver-focused cabin that closely resembles Porsche's traditional layout. Supportive seats, ambient lighting, sustainable materials, and leather-free upholstery options contribute to a modern atmosphere. While material quality is excellent, the interior styling lacks some of the visual drama expected in this price category. Front occupants enjoy generous comfort, but rear-seat accommodations are tighter. Two adults fit adequately, although shoulder room and legroom become restrictive for three passengers. Cargo capacity measures 18 cubic feet behind the second row and expands to 47 cubic feet with the seats folded. An additional front storage compartment provides three cubic feet of extra space.
technology: A 12.6-inch digital instrument cluster and a 10.9-inch central touchscreen form the centerpiece of the dashboard. Buyers can also equip a separate 10.9-inch passenger display, allowing video playback while maintaining driver safety. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, while Porsche's voice assistant can be activated with "Hey Porsche." An augmented reality head-up display overlays navigation information onto the windshield, enhancing usability. Audio upgrades include Bose and Burmester premium sound systems with up to 21 speakers.
safety: The Macan Electric comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies. Standard features include automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, lane-departure warning, and lane-keeping assist. Optional adaptive cruise control and more advanced lane-centering functions provide additional convenience for highway travel.
warranty:
Limited warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles
Battery and powertrain coverage: 8 years or 100,000 miles
Complimentary scheduled maintenance: None
pros: Excellent handling and chassis balance make it one of the most engaging electric SUVs available.
cons: Rear-seat space and cargo capacity are less generous than many rivals.
mn_take: The 2026 Porsche Macan Electric successfully preserves the Macan's sports-car DNA while delivering impressive range, rapid charging, and everyday usability.

car_name: 2026 Porsche Cayenne Electric / Cayenne Coupe Electric
overview: The 2026 Porsche Cayenne Electric marks one of the most significant evolutions in the Cayenne's history. Following the Macan's move toward battery power, Porsche's iconic mid-size SUV enters the EV era while preserving the athletic personality that has made the Cayenne one of the benchmark performance SUVs. Available in both conventional SUV and sleeker Coupe body styles, the Cayenne Electric combines immense power, rapid charging capability, and everyday practicality with the refined driving dynamics expected from Stuttgart. Its longer wheelbase, lower roofline, and wide stance give the electric Cayenne a more aggressive appearance than its gasoline-powered counterpart. More importantly, the engineering beneath the skin ensures it drives like a Porsche. From the relatively sensible base model to the astonishing 1,139-horsepower Turbo, the Cayenne Electric delivers an experience that feels every bit worthy of the crest on its hood.
pricing:
Base Cayenne Electric: Starting at $111,350
Base Cayenne Coupe Electric: Starting at $116,150
Cayenne Electric S: Starting at $128,650
Cayenne Coupe Electric S: Starting at $133,550
Cayenne Turbo Electric: Starting at $165,350
Cayenne Turbo Coupe Electric: Starting at $170,350

The base model represents the best value in the lineup. It still delivers exceptional performance and premium features while saving nearly $50,000 compared with the range-topping Turbo. Buyers seeking outright insanity, however, will find the four-digit horsepower Turbo impossible to ignore.
drivetrain:
All Cayenne Electric models feature dual electric motors and standard all-wheel drive. The base version produces 435 horsepower, while the S trim raises output to 657 horsepower. At the top of the range sits the Cayenne Turbo Electric, whose incredible 1,139 horsepower makes it the most powerful production Porsche ever created. The standard chassis employs two-chamber air springs and adaptive dampers, while higher trims can be equipped with Porsche's remarkable Active Ride suspension. During testing, the system delivered exceptional body control while absorbing road imperfections with almost magical smoothness. Rear-axle steering is available throughout the lineup, and the Turbo model receives a torque-vectoring limited-slip differential for even sharper dynamics.

Active aerodynamic elements further distinguish the Turbo. Deployable rear aero blades reduce drag at highway speeds and contribute to improved efficiency. Despite weighing considerably more than the gasoline-powered Cayenne Turbo GT, the electric flagship promises even greater performance. Porsche claims the base model reaches 60 mph in 4.5 seconds, the S does the same sprint in 3.6 seconds, and the Turbo rockets to 60 mph in a staggering 2.4 seconds. Real-world testing suggests it could be quicker still.

Practicality remains a key strength of the Cayenne Electric. Porsche rates the SUV for a maximum towing capacity of 7,716 pounds, matching the capability of the Rivian R1S and comfortably surpassing several luxury EV rivals. That level of capability makes the Cayenne Electric more than just a performance machine, allowing owners to tow boats, trailers, or recreational equipment without compromise.

The Cayenne Electric utilizes a large 108-kWh battery pack and Porsche's advanced 800-volt electrical architecture. Official EPA figures have yet to be finalized, but estimated driving range falls between 330 and 340 miles depending on configuration. Charging performance is expected to set new standards within the Porsche lineup. Peak DC fast-charging speeds reach an impressive 400 kW, making the Cayenne Electric Porsche's quickest-charging EV to date. Under ideal conditions, Porsche claims the battery can recharge from 10 to 80 percent in just 16 minutes. Another important milestone is the inclusion of a standard NACS charging port, allowing seamless access to a growing network of DC fast chargers. A secondary J1772 connector is located on the opposite side of the vehicle for convenient AC charging.
interior: The Cayenne Electric introduces a more futuristic interpretation of Porsche luxury. Although the steering wheel and seating position remain familiar, the dashboard design is dominated by digital displays and advanced technology. Thanks to a wheelbase that stretches almost five inches longer than the gasoline-powered Cayenne, rear passengers enjoy significantly improved legroom. The second-row seats fold electronically at the touch of a button, maximizing cargo flexibility. The standard SUV provides 20 cubic feet of cargo space behind the rear seats and expands to 56 cubic feet when the seats are folded flat. An additional three-cubic-foot front trunk offers enough room for backpacks or charging cables. The Coupe variant sacrifices some luggage space in exchange for a sportier roofline. Overall cabin space remains generous, comfortably accommodating four or five passengers in premium surroundings while maintaining Porsche's driver-focused atmosphere.
technology: Technology takes center stage inside the Cayenne Electric. The dashboard is dominated by Porsche's new "Flow Display," a curved OLED screen design that merges seamlessly into the center console. A 12.3-inch central touchscreen serves as the primary interface, while an optional 14.9-inch passenger display transforms the dashboard into an expansive digital environment. The curved OLED interface offers excellent clarity and responsiveness, giving the cabin a thoroughly modern appearance. Connectivity features are comprehensive, and the system supports advanced multimedia and vehicle functions with ease. Compared with the standard Cayenne, the electric model presents a more futuristic and immersive environment that feels appropriately advanced for Porsche's next-generation SUV.
safety: Porsche equips the Cayenne Electric with a solid suite of standard driver-assistance technologies. Automated emergency braking, adaptive cruise control, and lane-keeping assist are included across the lineup. More sophisticated systems are available as options, including a remote parking assistant and a 360-degree camera system that improves visibility during low-speed maneuvers. These features complement the Cayenne's exceptional chassis and provide reassurance during both urban commuting and long-distance journeys.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: Four years or 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: Four years or 50,000 miles
Battery Warranty: Eight years or 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None
pros: Outstanding performance, ultra-fast charging capability, and impressive passenger space.
cons: Pricing climbs rapidly, base models miss out on Active Ride suspension, and the styling may not appeal to everyone.
mn_take: The 2026 Cayenne Electric successfully brings Porsche's legendary driving character into the EV era, delivering breathtaking performance and genuine luxury without sacrificing practicality.

car_name: 2027 Porsche Cayenne E-Hybrid / Cayenne E-Hybrid Coupe
overview: The 2027 Porsche Cayenne E-Hybrid proves that electrification doesn't have to come at the expense of driver involvement. Despite carrying the additional weight of a plug-in hybrid system, the Cayenne E-Hybrid retains the sharp reflexes and rewarding dynamics that have defined Porsche SUVs for years. It blends strong electric capability with exceptional performance, making it equally comfortable commuting silently through town or attacking winding roads with surprising enthusiasm. Available in traditional SUV and Coupe body styles, the Cayenne E-Hybrid lineup ranges from the 463-horsepower base model to the ferocious Turbo E-Hybrid with 729 horsepower. Regardless of trim, every model delivers the balance of luxury, practicality, and athleticism expected from a Porsche. While rivals may offer greater efficiency or lower prices, few can match the Cayenne E-Hybrid's ability to combine sports-car responses with family-friendly versatility.
pricing:
Base E-Hybrid: Starting at approximately $106,000
Base E-Hybrid Coupe: Starting at approximately $110,000
S E-Hybrid: Starting at approximately $114,000
S E-Hybrid Coupe: Starting at approximately $120,000
Turbo E-Hybrid: Starting at approximately $166,000
Turbo E-Hybrid Coupe: Starting at approximately $172,000

The base E-Hybrid remains the sweet spot of the range. Its 463-hp powertrain provides abundant performance while leaving room in the budget for desirable options. Buyers seeking extreme acceleration and V-8 character will appreciate the Turbo E-Hybrid, but its substantial price premium places it in rarefied territory.
drivetrain:
Three plug-in hybrid powertrains are offered across the lineup. Base E-Hybrid models combine a turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 with an electric motor to produce 463 horsepower. The S E-Hybrid raises output to 512 horsepower using the same engine. At the top of the range, the Turbo E-Hybrid pairs a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 with an electric motor for a remarkable 729 horsepower. Every model uses an eight-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive. Although the transmission occasionally feels slightly hesitant during low-speed operation, overall refinement remains impressive.

The standard adaptive suspension effectively disguises the SUV's substantial curb weight, delivering agility that feels unnatural for something weighing over 5,000 pounds. Switching to Hybrid or Sport mode significantly improves responsiveness by allowing the gasoline engine to engage more readily. Performance is suitably outrageous. The base model reaches 60 mph in 4.6 seconds, while the Turbo E-Hybrid Coupe storms to 60 mph in only 3.1 seconds, placing it among the quickest SUVs currently available. Even more impressive is the confidence and composure the Cayenne exhibits when driven enthusiastically through corners.

Practicality remains one of the Cayenne E-Hybrid's strengths. Properly equipped, the standard E-Hybrid and S E-Hybrid models can tow up to 7,716 pounds. The more powerful Turbo E-Hybrid sacrifices some capacity but still offers a substantial 6,614-pound towing limit. These figures make the Cayenne E-Hybrid a genuine all-rounder, equally suited for family road trips, boats, or recreational trailers.

A 21.8-kWh battery pack powers all models. EPA estimates suggest electric driving ranges of approximately 29 miles for the base E-Hybrid, 27 miles for the S E-Hybrid, and 24 miles for the Turbo E-Hybrid. Real-world performance can exceed those numbers. During testing, the Turbo E-Hybrid Coupe managed an impressive 39 miles of electric-only operation before the gasoline engine engaged. Owners can easily handle daily commuting using electricity alone, while the hybrid system seamlessly provides long-distance flexibility without range anxiety.

Despite its considerable performance, efficiency remains respectable. EPA estimates stand at 21 mpg city, 23 mpg highway, and 22 mpg combined across the lineup. Testing of the previous Turbo E-Hybrid Coupe produced 22 mpg during a 75-mph highway fuel economy evaluation. Buyers considering the Cayenne E-Hybrid are unlikely to prioritize economy above all else, but the added electric capability makes frequent fuel stops less necessary.
interior:
Inside, the Cayenne E-Hybrid closely resembles Porsche's Taycan, featuring a highly digital environment highlighted by a 12.6-inch curved instrument cluster and a minimalist dashboard layout. Material quality is excellent, with even entry-level models providing a premium atmosphere. Base and S models feature heated faux-leather seats with eight-way power adjustment and a heated leather steering wheel. Turbo models upgrade to luxurious 18-way power-adjustable sport seats upholstered in genuine leather, while comfort-focused 14-way seats are available as an option.

Rear-seat space is generous for adults, although Coupe models sacrifice some headroom because of their sloping roofline. Heated rear seats and four-zone climate control are optional for additional passenger comfort. Cargo space remains practical despite the battery packaging. Standard SUV models provide 16 cubic feet behind the second row and up to 55 cubic feet with the seats folded. In testing, the cargo area accommodated eight carry-on suitcases, while folding the rear seats expanded capacity to 22 carry-ons.
technology: The Cayenne E-Hybrid features Porsche's latest digital ecosystem centered around a 12.3-inch touchscreen. The system includes integrated navigation, downloadable apps, Amazon Alexa voice assistance, and wireless smartphone charging. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard. Buyers can also specify an optional 10.9-inch passenger display capable of streaming video content independently. Audio options range from a standard 10-speaker system to premium Bose and Burmester setups with Dolby Atmos surround sound, creating a truly immersive listening experience. A crisp 12.6-inch digital gauge cluster further enhances the high-tech cabin environment.
safety: The Cayenne E-Hybrid offers an extensive suite of driver-assistance technologies. Standard equipment includes automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, and blind-spot monitoring. Parking sensors are fitted at both ends of the vehicle, improving maneuverability in tight spaces. Optional technologies include adaptive cruise control and an infrared night-vision camera system that enhances visibility in low-light conditions. These systems complement the Cayenne's excellent chassis and confidence-inspiring driving manners, making long-distance travel both relaxing and secure.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles
Hybrid Component Warranty: 8 years or 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 1 year or 10,000 miles
pros: Exceptional acceleration and sports-car-like handling in a family SUV.

car_name: 2027 Porsche Cayenne / Cayenne Coupe Review
overview:
The 2027 Porsche Cayenne continues to prove why it remains one of the benchmarks among luxury performance SUVs. Despite its practical mid-size dimensions and family-oriented mission, the Cayenne embodies Porsche's sports-car DNA more convincingly than almost any rival. Whether tackling winding roads, hauling luggage for a weekend getaway, or simply commuting through the city, the Cayenne blends everyday usability with driver engagement in a way few SUVs can replicate.

Available in traditional SUV and sleeker Coupe body styles, the Cayenne lineup offers everything from a refined turbocharged V-6 to ferocious twin-turbocharged V-8 engines producing up to 650 horsepower in the range-topping Turbo GT. The interior is spacious and luxurious, while Porsche's extensive customization options allow buyers to create a highly personalized vehicle. Although options can quickly push the price into six-figure territory, the Cayenne rewards enthusiasts with handling precision and performance that justify its premium positioning.
pricing:
Cayenne – Starting at $93,000 (est.)
Cayenne Coupe – Starting at $98,000 (est.)
Cayenne S – Starting at $111,000 (est.)
Cayenne S Coupe – Starting at $118,000 (est.)
Cayenne GTS – Starting at $135,000 (est.)
Cayenne GTS Coupe – Starting at $140,000 (est.)
Cayenne Turbo GT Coupe – Starting at $218,000 (est.)

The standard Cayenne represents the best value in the range. Equipped with a generous list of standard features, it can be further enhanced with the Premium Package and Sport Chrono Package for an ideal blend of luxury and performance.
drivetrain:
Porsche offers the nonhybrid Cayenne with several powertrain options, each engineered to deliver strong performance and a distinctive character. The base model employs a turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 producing 348 horsepower, providing brisk acceleration and impressive refinement. Moving up to the Cayenne S introduces a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 generating 468 horsepower, accompanied by an intoxicating exhaust note and considerably greater thrust. The GTS model raises output to 493 horsepower while adding a more aggressive chassis setup that transforms the Cayenne into a genuinely engaging driver's SUV. At the top of the hierarchy sits the Turbo GT Coupe, powered by a 650-horsepower twin-turbocharged V-8. Massive brakes, lightweight components, and bespoke suspension tuning elevate it into super-SUV territory. All variants are paired with an exceptionally smooth eight-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive. Adaptive dampers come standard throughout the lineup, while optional air suspension, rear-wheel steering, and active anti-roll bars further sharpen handling without compromising comfort. Even in standard form, the Cayenne delivers the poise and steering precision expected from a Porsche.

Efficiency varies depending on engine choice. The base V-6 model achieves EPA estimates of 17 mpg city and 23 mpg highway, making it the most economical nonhybrid version. Models equipped with the twin-turbo V-8 return approximately 15 mpg city and 21 mpg highway. While fuel economy isn't the Cayenne's primary focus, the trade-off is rewarded with exceptional performance and refinement.

Beyond its sporting credentials, the Cayenne is impressively capable when tasked with heavier duties. Properly equipped models can tow up to 7,716 pounds, making the SUV suitable for hauling boats, trailers, or recreational equipment. This level of capability adds to the Cayenne's appeal as an all-around luxury vehicle.
interior:
The cabin reflects Porsche's modern design philosophy, borrowing heavily from the Taycan electric sedan with a dashboard dominated by digital displays. A compact toggle gear selector mounted on the dash frees up additional storage space on the center console and contributes to the minimalist aesthetic. Customization possibilities are nearly endless. Buyers can select various upholstery materials, trim finishes, and even seatbelt colors to create a truly bespoke environment. Available features include heated and ventilated seats, massage functions, and four-zone automatic climate control.

Although competitors such as the Audi Q7 and Volvo XC90 offer third-row seating, the Cayenne focuses on providing generous room for five occupants. Rear passengers enjoy ample legroom, and the adjustable second-row seats enhance long-distance comfort. Cargo space remains practical. The standard SUV offers 27.3 cubic feet behind the rear seats and expands to 60.3 cubic feet with them folded flat. The Coupe sacrifices some utility in favor of its dramatic roofline, providing 20.9 cubic feet behind the seats and 53.0 cubic feet with the second row folded.
technology: Technology is one of the Cayenne's strongest areas. Standard equipment includes a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system paired with a 12.6-inch digital instrument cluster. An optional 10.9-inch passenger display allows the front passenger to access entertainment functions while remaining invisible to the driver. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, while Amazon Alexa integration expands voice-control capabilities. Porsche's App Center enables owners to download third-party applications directly to the vehicle. Audio enthusiasts can choose between the standard 10-speaker system or upgrade to premium Bose and Burmester sound systems, both featuring Dolby Atmos spatial audio for a more immersive listening experience.
safety: The Cayenne offers a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance safety and convenience. Standard equipment includes automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, lane-keeping assist, and parking sensors. Buyers can also equip adaptive cruise control with lane-centering capability and an advanced night-vision camera system that uses infrared technology to detect pedestrians and animals in low-light conditions. These technologies complement the Cayenne's inherently secure chassis and excellent visibility, helping it feel confidence-inspiring in a variety of driving situations.
