Complimentary Maintenance: 2 years / 24,000 miles

While warranty coverage is average for the class, Nissan's complimentary maintenance program adds some value during the first years of ownership.
pros: Comfortable ride, spacious cabin, excellent storage solutions, strong safety technology, upscale upper trims.
cons: Uninspiring handling, infotainment system can be slow, real-world fuel economy often trails EPA estimates.
mn_take: The 2026 Nissan Rogue is a comfort-focused family SUV that excels in practicality and refinement, but rivals offer more driving enjoyment and overall value.

car_name: 2027 Nissan Pathfinder Review
overview: The 2027 Nissan Pathfinder continues to serve as a practical and family-focused three-row SUV that prioritizes comfort, versatility, and towing capability over off-road adventure. Despite its rugged styling and adventurous nameplate, the Pathfinder is most at home handling school runs, road trips, and daily commuting duties. Its spacious cabin, refined V6 engine, and quiet highway manners make it a compelling choice for families seeking a comfortable midsize SUV. While it may not be the most engaging vehicle to drive in its segment, it offers a balanced combination of passenger space, technology, and capability.
pricing:
S: Starting at approximately $40,000
SV: Starting at approximately $42,000
SL: Starting at approximately $45,000
Rock Creek: Starting at approximately $47,000
Platinum: Starting at approximately $51,000

Recommended Trim: SL

The SL trim offers the best balance of value and equipment, adding premium features such as leather-appointed seating, advanced technology, available captain's chairs, and access to the Premium Package that includes a panoramic sunroof, Bose audio system, and enhanced towing capability.
drivetrain:
Every 2027 Pathfinder is powered by a naturally aspirated 3.5-liter V6 engine paired with a nine-speed automatic transmission. Most trims produce 284 horsepower, while the rugged Rock Creek variant receives a slight boost to 295 horsepower. Front-wheel drive comes standard on most trims, while all-wheel drive remains optional and adds multiple terrain management modes for improved traction.

The V6 delivers smooth and confident acceleration, making highway merging and overtaking effortless. A 0-60 mph time of approximately 6.8 seconds places the Pathfinder among the quicker options in its segment. Ride quality is generally comfortable, although larger wheel packages can introduce some firmness over rough surfaces. Steering feedback is limited and handling remains uninspiring, but excellent cabin insulation helps create a calm and refined driving experience.

Fuel economy remains competitive for a naturally aspirated V6-powered midsize SUV. All-wheel-drive S, SV, and SL models are rated at up to 21 mpg city and 27 mpg highway, while front-wheel-drive versions deliver similar efficiency. The more rugged Rock Creek trim sacrifices some efficiency due to its off-road-oriented equipment. In real-world highway testing, the all-wheel-drive Pathfinder Platinum returned 25 mpg, making it a respectable performer for long-distance travel.
interior: The Pathfinder’s interior focuses on family usability and comfort. The dashboard features a modern design with intuitive controls and high-quality materials throughout the cabin. Upper trims elevate the experience further with semi-aniline leather upholstery, ventilated front seats, and a panoramic sunroof. Passenger accommodation is one of the Pathfinder’s strongest qualities. The second row offers generous space and can be configured with either a bench seat or captain’s chairs. Nissan’s clever seat design allows easy access to the third row, although adults may find the rearmost seats cramped on longer journeys. Cargo flexibility is impressive, with numerous storage compartments throughout the cabin and up to 35 carry-on suitcases worth of space when both rear rows are folded.
technology: Technology is a strong point for the Pathfinder. Every model comes standard with a 12.3-inch touchscreen running Nissan’s latest infotainment software. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with integrated navigation and SiriusXM connectivity. Available upgrades include a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster, a head-up display, wireless smartphone charging, and a premium 13-speaker Bose sound system. The system is easy to operate and delivers a user-friendly experience that should satisfy most modern buyers.
safety: The 2027 Pathfinder comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of standard safety technologies. Automatic emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, lane-departure warning, rear parking sensors, and rear cross-traffic alert are included across the lineup. Higher trims offer additional driver-assistance technologies such as adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, and a 360-degree camera system. These features contribute to a reassuring ownership experience and strengthen the Pathfinder’s appeal as a family vehicle.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 2 years / 24,000 miles
pros: Strong V6 performance, family-friendly cabin, impressive towing capability, quiet highway manners.
cons: Uninspiring handling, firm ride on larger wheels, cramped third-row space for adults.
mn_take: A comfortable and capable family SUV that excels in practicality, refinement, and towing ability while sacrificing driving excitement.

car_name: 2027 Nissan Murano Review
overview: The 2027 Nissan Murano continues to position itself as a comfortable and stylish two-row midsize SUV aimed at buyers who prioritize refinement over outright performance. Sharing its platform and powertrain with the larger Pathfinder, the Murano focuses on delivering a smooth driving experience, premium interior materials, and a modern design that stands out in a crowded segment. While it may not be the most exciting SUV to drive, its spacious cabin, upscale ambiance, and standard all-wheel-drive system make it a compelling option for families seeking comfort and practicality.
pricing:
SV: Starting at approximately $44,000
SL: Starting at approximately $49,000
Platinum: Starting at approximately $52,000

Recommended Trim: SL

The SL trim offers the best value by adding premium features such as a panoramic sunroof, Bose audio system, navigation, ambient lighting, memory seats, and a 360-degree camera system without reaching the higher price point of the Platinum model.
drivetrain:
Powering every 2027 Murano is a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 241 horsepower, paired with a nine-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive. The powertrain delivers smooth acceleration suitable for everyday driving, and the nine-speed gearbox is a notable improvement over the previous generation’s CVT. On the road, the Murano prioritizes comfort rather than athleticism. Steering is light and easy to manage around town, while suspension tuning effectively absorbs most road imperfections. Although sharp bumps can still be felt inside the cabin, overall ride quality remains comfortable and composed. The Murano reaches 60 mph in approximately 7.2 seconds, making it competitive within the midsize crossover segment.

The EPA estimates fuel economy at 21 mpg in the city, 27 mpg on the highway, and 23 mpg combined. While these figures are respectable, they trail several rivals that offer hybrid powertrains. Buyers seeking maximum efficiency may find alternatives such as the Toyota Crown Signia or Hyundai Santa Fe Hybrid more appealing, but the Murano still delivers acceptable economy considering its standard all-wheel-drive setup.
interior:
One of the Murano's strongest attributes is its interior. Nissan has created a cabin that feels significantly more premium than many mainstream competitors. The dashboard features a clean, minimalist layout with touch-sensitive climate controls integrated into elegant wood trim elements. Soft-touch materials are used throughout the cabin, creating a genuinely upscale atmosphere. 

Nissan’s renowned Zero Gravity seats provide excellent support and long-distance comfort for both front and rear passengers. Rear-seat accommodations are particularly generous, offering impressive legroom and a nearly flat floor that enhances passenger comfort. Cargo capacity is equally impressive, with 33 cubic feet available behind the second row and up to 64 cubic feet with the seats folded.
technology: Technology is another area where the Murano performs well. Every model comes equipped with dual 12.3-inch displays that serve as the digital instrument cluster and infotainment touchscreen. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard across the lineup, along with a wireless charging pad and multiple USB-C ports. Higher trims benefit from Google-based infotainment software, integrated Google Maps navigation, Amazon Alexa functionality, and a premium 10-speaker Bose sound system. The interface is modern, responsive, and easy to use, helping the Murano feel competitive with newer rivals.
safety: The 2027 Murano includes a comprehensive suite of standard driver-assistance technologies. Features such as automatic emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert come standard across the range. Higher trims receive Nissan’s advanced ProPilot Assist system, which incorporates hands-free driving capability on compatible highways and can automatically adjust vehicle speed when approaching curves. These features contribute to a reassuring driving experience for families and long-distance travelers.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 2 years / 24,000 miles
pros: Premium cabin quality, comfortable seating, generous passenger space, modern technology features.
cons: Modest towing capacity, average fuel economy, uninspiring driving dynamics.
mn_take: A refined and comfortable midsize SUV that prioritizes luxury-like comfort and practicality over outright excitement.

car_name: 2027 Nissan Leaf Review
overview:
The 2027 Nissan Leaf marks a significant evolution for Nissan’s pioneering electric vehicle. Once known primarily as a practical electric hatchback, the Leaf has transformed into a far more appealing subcompact electric SUV that combines improved styling, competitive driving range, modern technology, and everyday usability. The shift to a crossover-inspired design makes the new Leaf considerably more attractive than its predecessor while maintaining the affordability that helped make the original model one of the world's most recognizable EVs. With up to 303 miles of estimated driving range, access to Tesla-compatible fast charging, and a spacious, tech-focused interior, the Leaf is now a far stronger competitor in the growing electric SUV segment.

Although performance remains focused more on comfort than excitement, the Leaf delivers the quiet, refined driving experience that many EV buyers prioritize. For shoppers seeking an affordable electric vehicle with substantial range and practical daily usability, the 2027 Leaf represents Nissan's most compelling electric offering yet.
pricing:
S+ — Starting at approximately $32,000
SV+ — Starting at approximately $36,000
Platinum+ — Starting at approximately $41,000

The S+ trim offers the best overall value. It provides the longest driving range in the lineup while including dual 12.3-inch displays, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, USB-C charging ports, and a comprehensive suite of safety technologies.
drivetrain:
Every 2027 Leaf is powered by a single electric motor producing 214 horsepower, sending power exclusively to the front wheels. While acceleration is not class-leading, the electric motor delivers smooth and immediate torque that makes city driving effortless. The Leaf feels responsive during daily commuting and has more than enough performance for highway merging and overtaking. Nissan has tuned the Leaf primarily for comfort rather than sportiness. The suspension absorbs road imperfections effectively, while the cabin remains impressively quiet even at highway speeds. Steering is light and predictable, making the vehicle easy to maneuver in urban environments. Body roll becomes noticeable when pushed through corners, and driving enthusiasts may prefer rivals with sharper handling characteristics. However, for most buyers, the Leaf's relaxed and refined driving behavior will be a major advantage. Multiple regenerative braking settings allow drivers to adjust energy recovery, although a true one-pedal driving mode remains absent.

The Leaf is equipped with a 75-kWh battery pack and offers some of the strongest range figures in its price category. The S+ model leads the lineup with an EPA-estimated 303 miles of driving range. The SV+ is rated at 288 miles, while the Platinum+ delivers an estimated 256 miles per charge. In real-world highway testing, the Platinum+ achieved approximately 250 miles of range, demonstrating strong long-distance capability for a compact electric SUV. Charging flexibility has improved significantly. The Leaf supports DC fast charging at speeds up to 150 kW, allowing the battery to charge from 10 to 80 percent in approximately 35 minutes under ideal conditions. A major advantage is the inclusion of a NACS charging port, giving Leaf owners access to the extensive Tesla Supercharger network. Traditional J1772 compatibility remains available for Level 2 charging at home or public stations.
interior: The Leaf's cabin adopts a clean, modern design that feels considerably more premium than previous generations. Horizontal dashboard elements create a sense of openness, while the minimalist layout contributes to a contemporary atmosphere. Front-seat comfort is excellent, with supportive seating and generous headroom. The elevated seating position provides a commanding view of the road while maintaining the easy entry and exit buyers expect from a crossover. Rear-seat passengers benefit from adequate legroom and comfortable seating for two adults. Higher trims add rear USB-C charging ports, improving convenience for passengers during longer trips. Cargo practicality remains strong despite the vehicle's sleek exterior design. While the sloping roofline slightly reduces vertical storage space, the Leaf still offers up to 56 cubic feet of cargo capacity behind the rear seats, making it suitable for family duties, road trips, and everyday errands.
technology: Technology is one of the Leaf's standout strengths. The S+ trim comes standard with dual 12.3-inch displays, while SV+ and Platinum+ models upgrade to larger dual 14.5-inch screens. The upgraded system also introduces a more sophisticated Google-based software platform with enhanced connectivity and navigation features. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard across the range, allowing seamless smartphone integration without cables. USB-C charging ports are also standard, while upper trims add wireless charging functionality. Audio options range from a standard four-speaker setup to an available 10-speaker Bose premium sound system in the Platinum+ trim. The infotainment interface is intuitive, responsive, and easy to navigate, contributing to the Leaf's modern character.
safety: Nissan equips every Leaf with its Safety Shield 360 suite of advanced driver-assistance technologies. Standard features include automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, adaptive cruise control, and lane-centering assistance.  Nissan's ProPilot Assist system is also standard, combining adaptive cruise control and steering assistance to reduce driver workload during highway journeys. The extensive list of standard safety features enhances the Leaf's value proposition and makes it a competitive choice for safety-conscious buyers.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles
Battery Warranty: 8 years or 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None

The battery warranty provides reassuring long-term coverage, although some competitors offer more generous overall vehicle warranties and complimentary maintenance programs.
pros: Excellent driving range, modern technology, and Tesla Supercharger compatibility.
cons: Front-wheel-drive only and lacks the acceleration excitement offered by some rivals.
mn_take: The new Leaf finally pairs strong EV range with attractive styling, making it one of Nissan’s most convincing electric vehicles to date.

car_name: 2027 Nissan Kicks Review
overview:
The 2027 Nissan Kicks continues to be one of the most affordable and stylish entries in the subcompact SUV segment. With its youthful design, practical interior, impressive list of standard safety features, and attractive pricing, the Kicks remains an appealing choice for urban commuters, first-time SUV buyers, and small families seeking a comfortable daily driver. While its sporty appearance may suggest energetic performance, the Kicks prioritizes comfort, efficiency, and ease of use over outright driving excitement. The cabin is thoughtfully designed, passenger space is competitive for the class, and Nissan has equipped the Kicks with modern technology that makes everyday driving more enjoyable.

For 2027, Nissan is expected to carry the model over unchanged, which is not a bad thing considering the recent redesign brought significant improvements in styling, technology, and overall refinement.
pricing:
S — Starting at approximately $24,000
SV — Starting at approximately $26,000
SR — Starting at approximately $29,000

The SV trim offers the best balance of value and features. It upgrades to a larger 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system, adds wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a wireless charging pad, and proximity keyless entry, making it the most sensible choice for most buyers.
drivetrain:
The Kicks is powered by a naturally aspirated 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 141 horsepower, paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT). Front-wheel drive comes standard, while all-wheel drive is available for buyers who frequently encounter poor weather conditions. AWD models also receive a dedicated Snow drive mode alongside Normal, Eco, and Sport settings. Performance is adequate for daily commuting, city driving, and highway cruising, but acceleration is not one of the Kicks’ strengths. Buyers looking for a more engaging driving experience may find alternatives such as the Mazda CX-30 more satisfying. That said, the Kicks delivers predictable handling and confidence-inspiring road manners. Steering is light and easy, making the SUV particularly well-suited for urban environments and tight parking situations. Ride quality is generally comfortable, although models equipped with the optional 19-inch wheels can feel firmer over rough pavement.

Efficiency remains one of the Kicks' strongest attributes. Front-wheel-drive models achieve EPA estimates of 28 mpg city and 35 mpg highway, while all-wheel-drive variants lose only a small amount of efficiency. Real-world testing has shown AWD models returning approximately 33 mpg during highway driving. These figures make the Kicks a cost-effective choice for buyers who prioritize low running costs without stepping into the hybrid segment.
interior: The Kicks offers a surprisingly modern and inviting cabin considering its affordable price point. The dashboard design is clean and contemporary, featuring wide digital displays positioned for easy visibility. The front seats provide excellent comfort for everyday use, with supportive cushioning that helps reduce fatigue during longer drives. Nissan's attention to seat comfort continues to be one of the brand's strengths. Rear-seat accommodations are competitive within the subcompact SUV segment. While not as spacious as larger crossovers such as the Nissan Rogue, the Kicks provides enough room for adults to travel comfortably on shorter and medium-distance journeys. Cargo versatility is another strong point. Front-wheel-drive models offer up to 29 cubic feet of cargo space behind the second row and up to 59 cubic feet with the seats folded. Choosing all-wheel drive reduces cargo capacity slightly, but storage remains practical for groceries, luggage, and everyday family needs.
technology: Technology has become a major selling point for the Kicks. Base S models receive a 7.0-inch touchscreen, while the SV and SR trims upgrade to a much more impressive 12.3-inch infotainment display. The larger system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, allowing seamless smartphone connectivity without cables. Higher trims also gain additional USB-C charging ports and available wireless charging functionality. Audio options range from a basic four-speaker system to an available 10-speaker Bose premium audio setup that significantly enhances sound quality. The infotainment interface is straightforward and easy to operate, making it friendly for drivers who prefer simple, intuitive controls.
safety: Safety remains a major highlight of the Kicks lineup. Nissan includes a generous suite of driver-assistance technologies as standard equipment. Key standard features include automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, adaptive cruise control, and lane-departure warning. Higher trims can also be equipped with lane-keeping assist and a 360-degree camera system, providing additional confidence during parking and highway driving. The extensive list of standard safety equipment helps the Kicks stand out against several competitors that reserve many of these features for higher trim levels.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 2 years or 24,000 miles

While warranty coverage is average for the segment, Nissan adds value through complimentary maintenance, covering up to three oil changes during the first two years of ownership.
pros: Stylish design, strong safety equipment, and excellent value for money.
cons: Modest engine performance limits driving excitement.
mn_take: A practical, efficient, and well-equipped subcompact SUV that delivers outstanding everyday usability at an attractive price.

car_name: 2027 Nissan Armada Review
overview:
The 2027 Nissan Armada continues to serve as Nissan’s flagship full-size SUV, offering a compelling blend of performance, comfort, and family-focused practicality. Built for buyers who need genuine three-row seating, substantial towing capability, and long-distance comfort, the Armada stands out with its bold styling, powerful twin-turbocharged V6 engine, and surprisingly refined driving manners. Unlike many traditional body-on-frame SUVs that feel cumbersome on the road, the Armada manages to feel smaller from behind the wheel than its dimensions suggest. Its comfortable cabin, modern technology, and generous passenger space make it an attractive alternative to rivals such as the Ford Expedition, Chevrolet Tahoe, and GMC Yukon. Higher trims push even further into premium territory, delivering luxury-like materials and features without crossing into luxury-brand pricing.

For 2027, Nissan is expected to carry over the recently redesigned Armada largely unchanged, allowing buyers to enjoy an already modern package that remains competitive in the segment.
pricing:
SV — Starting at approximately $62,000
SL — Starting at approximately $66,000
Platinum — Starting at approximately $73,000
Pro-4X — Starting at approximately $77,000
Platinum Reserve — Starting at approximately $80,000
NISMO — Starting at approximately $82,000

The SL trim offers the strongest value in the lineup. It adds premium features such as heated front seats, a heated steering wheel, a premium audio system, power-folding third-row seats, and a power liftgate. Buyers seeking off-road capability should consider the Pro-4X, while those prioritizing luxury will appreciate the Platinum Reserve.
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the Armada comes equipped with a twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6 engine paired with a nine-speed automatic transmission. Most trims produce 425 horsepower, while the performance-oriented NISMO variant raises output to 460 horsepower. Rear-wheel drive comes standard, while four-wheel drive is available across most trims and standard on the Pro-4X. Despite its considerable size, the Armada delivers strong acceleration and effortless highway passing power. Nissan’s turbocharged V6 provides smooth and immediate torque delivery, helping the SUV feel responsive in everyday driving situations.

Ride quality is generally comfortable and well-controlled, particularly on trims equipped with smaller wheel options. Available adaptive air suspension enhances comfort further while also improving off-road capability. The steering feels lighter than expected for a vehicle of this size, making parking lot maneuvers and urban driving less intimidating than many competitors. The NISMO trim introduces a more aggressive character with additional horsepower and sportier styling, although most buyers will likely find the standard powertrain more than sufficient.

Fuel economy remains a challenge for large body-on-frame SUVs, and the Armada performs about as expected in this category. EPA estimates reach up to 16 mpg city and 20 mpg highway, depending on configuration. Real-world highway testing has shown results ranging from 18 mpg in off-road-focused Pro-4X models to 22 mpg in more road-oriented trims. While these figures are acceptable for the segment, buyers prioritizing efficiency may find better results from some competitors.
interior: The Armada's cabin is one of its strongest selling points. The interior design is clean, modern, and thoughtfully arranged, creating an upscale atmosphere that feels far more premium than the vehicle’s starting price might suggest. Front-seat passengers benefit from supportive seats with generous cushioning and extensive adjustment ranges. Long-distance comfort is excellent, making the Armada a capable road-trip companion. The second row provides impressive space and comfort, whether equipped with a standard bench seat or optional captain’s chairs. Access to the third row is straightforward, and unlike many midsize three-row SUVs, the Armada's third row is genuinely usable for adults on shorter journeys. Higher trims elevate the experience with premium materials including quilted leather upholstery, soft-touch surfaces, and upscale trim accents that rival some luxury-branded SUVs. Cargo flexibility is another highlight. Even with all three rows in place, the Armada offers useful luggage space, while folding the rear seats creates a large cargo area capable of handling family vacations, sports equipment, or home-improvement supplies.
technology:
Technology receives a significant upgrade compared to previous-generation models. Every Armada comes standard with dual 12.3-inch displays, one serving as the digital instrument cluster and the other as the infotainment touchscreen. Higher trims upgrade to a larger 14.3-inch infotainment display, creating a more premium digital experience. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, allowing seamless smartphone integration without cables. Available Google Built-In functionality adds enhanced navigation, voice controls, and connected services.

Audio quality is impressive, particularly with the available 12-speaker Klipsch premium sound system, which delivers clear and powerful sound reproduction throughout the cabin. The interface is intuitive and responsive, helping drivers access features without unnecessary distractions.
safety: Nissan equips the Armada with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies as standard. Key standard features include automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, lane-keeping assist, pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert. Buyers can also add Nissan’s advanced ProPilot Assist 2.1 system, which introduces adaptive cruise control with hands-free highway driving capability on approved roadways. These technologies help reduce driver fatigue during long journeys while enhancing overall safety.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None

While warranty coverage is competitive with most full-size SUV rivals, Nissan falls behind some competitors that include complimentary scheduled maintenance programs.
pros: Powerful twin-turbocharged V6 delivers strong acceleration and towing capability.
cons: No extended-wheelbase version limits maximum cargo capacity.
mn_take: A refined, spacious, and value-packed full-size SUV that successfully balances family practicality, comfort, and performance.

car_name: 2027 Nissan Z
overview: The 2027 Nissan Z continues a sports-car legacy that stretches back to the iconic Datsun 240Z of the late 1960s. Blending retro-inspired styling with modern performance technology, the latest Z delivers an engaging rear-wheel-drive experience at a price that remains relatively accessible compared with many sports-car rivals. Its long hood, short rear deck, and nostalgic design cues pay tribute to previous generations while hiding a thoroughly modern twin-turbocharged powertrain underneath. For 2027, Nissan introduces a mild refresh that includes a redesigned front fascia, new wheel designs, and a fresh Shinkai Green Pearl Metallic paint option. More importantly, the high-performance NISMO model finally gains the option of a six-speed manual transmission, giving enthusiasts greater control and making the flagship Z even more appealing.
pricing:
Sport: Starting at $45,000 (est.)
Performance: Starting at $55,000 (est.)
Heritage Edition: Starting at $58,000 (est.)
NISMO: Starting at $67,000 (est.)

Recommended Trim: Performance, thanks to its upgraded suspension, limited-slip differential, larger brakes, summer-performance tires, enhanced seating, and excellent balance between daily usability and performance.
drivetrain:
The Nissan Z is powered by a twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter V6 engine that produces 400 horsepower and 350 lb-ft of torque in Sport and Performance trims. The NISMO variant raises output to 420 horsepower and 384 lb-ft of torque while adding numerous chassis and aerodynamic upgrades. Buyers can choose between a six-speed manual transmission and a nine-speed automatic transmission across the lineup. Power is delivered exclusively to the rear wheels, preserving the traditional sports-car formula that has defined the Z for decades. Acceleration is impressive. The Performance model reaches 60 mph in approximately 4.5 seconds, while the more aggressive NISMO cuts that figure to around 3.9 seconds. The twin-turbo V6 delivers strong mid-range torque and rapid throttle response, making the Z feel eager and energetic in virtually every driving situation. Handling is enjoyable and confidence-inspiring, although the standard suspension setup prioritizes road comfort slightly more than ultimate cornering precision. Drivers seeking maximum grip and track capability will appreciate the NISMO's upgraded suspension, wider tires, larger brakes, and sharper responses.

Despite its strong performance, the Nissan Z delivers reasonable fuel economy for a sports coupe. EPA estimates reach up to 19 mpg in the city, 28 mpg on the highway, and 22 mpg combined depending on configuration. Highway testing has shown the Performance model capable of achieving up to 29 mpg, while the more powerful NISMO returns approximately 27 mpg. These figures allow the Z to remain relatively practical for enthusiasts who intend to use it as a regular driver rather than a weekend-only toy.
interior: Inside, the Z combines modern technology with classic sports-car themes. The two-seat cabin features a driver-focused layout, premium materials, and several design elements that reference previous generations of Nissan Z cars. Supportive seats provide excellent comfort during spirited driving while remaining suitable for longer trips. Available Alcantara upholstery, power-adjustable seating, and dual-zone automatic climate control add a premium touch to higher trims. The cockpit remains compact, however, and taller drivers may find entry and exit somewhat challenging. Rear seating is absent entirely, reinforcing the Z’s commitment to being a dedicated sports coupe. Cargo space is respectable for the segment, with enough room for three carry-on suitcases in the trunk, making weekend getaways entirely realistic.
technology: The base Sport trim features an 8.0-inch touchscreen infotainment system with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility. Performance and NISMO models upgrade to a larger 9.0-inch touchscreen that adds navigation, wireless smartphone integration, and a built-in Wi-Fi hotspot. Every Z includes a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster that provides customizable performance information and modern graphics. Nissan also retains physical controls for commonly used functions, ensuring usability remains straightforward while driving. Audio choices include a standard six-speaker system and an available Bose premium sound system for buyers seeking enhanced audio quality.
safety: The Nissan Z comes equipped with a solid collection of driver-assistance technologies despite its performance-oriented nature. Standard features include automated emergency braking, pedestrian detection, blind-spot monitoring, lane-departure warning, and adaptive cruise control. These systems help improve everyday usability while maintaining the Z's enthusiast-focused character. Although safety technology is not the primary selling point of a sports coupe, Nissan has ensured the Z remains competitive with modern expectations.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 2 years or 24,000 miles
pros: Powerful twin-turbo V6 performance wrapped in timeless retro-inspired styling.
cons: Tight cabin space and less precise handling than some rivals.
mn_take: A fast, characterful sports coupe that stays true to the Z heritage.

car_name: 2027 Nissan Sentra
overview:
The 2027 Nissan Sentra continues to build on its reputation as one of the most value-focused compact sedans on the market. Combining attractive styling, a comfortable ride, generous standard equipment, and strong fuel economy, the Sentra offers a compelling package for buyers seeking affordable and dependable transportation. Recent updates have helped modernize both its appearance and technology, keeping it competitive in a segment increasingly dominated by SUVs.

For 2027, the Sentra carries over largely unchanged after receiving a significant refresh the previous year. A standard 12.3-inch infotainment display, updated suspension tuning, and improved cabin design have helped elevate the sedan's appeal. While its powertrain remains one of the least exciting in the class, the Sentra’s combination of affordability, comfort, and features makes it an attractive option for budget-conscious buyers.
pricing:
S: Starting at $24,000 (est.)
SV: Starting at $25,000 (est.)
SR: Starting at $26,000 (est.)
SL: Starting at $30,000 (est.)

Recommended Trim: SV, thanks to its excellent balance of value and equipment, including wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, alloy wheels, upgraded convenience features, and selectable drive modes.
drivetrain:
The 2027 Sentra is powered by a naturally aspirated 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 149 horsepower. Power is sent to the front wheels through a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT), which prioritizes efficiency and smoothness over outright performance. Acceleration is modest by segment standards. The Sentra feels perfectly capable during daily commuting, but overtaking maneuvers and highway merging require patience compared with more powerful rivals. Depending on trim level, the Sentra reaches 60 mph in approximately 8.3 to 9.1 seconds.

While the engine lacks enthusiasm, the Sentra’s chassis has improved considerably. Revised suspension tuning and a stiffer body structure contribute to a composed ride and predictable handling characteristics. The sedan remains comfortable over rough pavement and feels more refined than its affordable price tag might suggest. Buyers seeking sporty performance may look elsewhere, but those prioritizing comfort will appreciate the Sentra’s relaxed nature.

Fuel efficiency remains one of the Sentra’s strongest selling points. EPA estimates reach up to 31 mpg in the city, 39 mpg on the highway, and 34 mpg combined on certain trims. Higher-spec SR and SL models sacrifice a small amount of efficiency, returning up to 30 mpg city and 37 mpg highway. These figures place the Sentra among the more economical gasoline-powered compact sedans currently available, helping keep ownership costs low over the long term.
interior: The Sentra’s cabin feels more modern and upscale than many buyers might expect from an entry-level compact sedan. The redesigned dashboard creates a clean and contemporary appearance, while high-quality materials and thoughtful ergonomics contribute to a pleasant driving environment. Front seats are particularly impressive, offering excellent comfort and support during long journeys. Passenger space is generous for a compact sedan, providing enough room for most adults to travel comfortably. car_name: 2027 Nissan Altima
overview:
The 2027 Nissan Altima continues to serve as one of the most affordable midsize sedans on the market, combining attractive styling, a spacious cabin, and strong fuel economy in a practical family-friendly package. While SUVs continue to dominate sales charts, the Altima remains a sensible choice for buyers who prioritize comfort, efficiency, and value over flashy performance or cutting-edge technology.

Expected to carry over with minimal changes for 2027, the Altima enters what could potentially be its final model year. Despite increasing competition from rivals such as the Honda Accord, Toyota Camry, Hyundai Sonata, and Kia K5, the Altima still offers a comfortable ride, available all-wheel drive, and a roomy interior that make it an appealing everyday commuter. However, its uninspiring driving character and aging powertrain prevent it from leading the segment.

The engine is paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT), with buyers able to choose between front-wheel drive and all-wheel drive configurations. Performance is adequate for daily driving but far from exciting. Acceleration is smooth enough for commuting duties, although the engine becomes noticeably coarse when pushed hard. An all-wheel-drive Altima reaches 60 mph in approximately 7.6 seconds, which is respectable but slower than several key competitors, particularly hybrid-powered alternatives. Handling is predictable and secure, although steering feedback remains limited, reinforcing the sedan’s focus on comfort rather than driver engagement.

interior: Inside, the Altima focuses on practicality and comfort rather than luxury. Material quality is solid, offering a pleasant environment that feels durable and well assembled. Rear-seat passengers are treated to excellent legroom, making the Altima a comfortable choice for families and long-distance travel. technology: The Altima comes standard with an 8.0-inch touchscreen infotainment system featuring Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility. These technologies help keep the Altima competitive in a segment where advanced safety equipment has become increasingly important.

car_name: 2026 Mitsubishi Outlander Sport

While its styling remains reasonably attractive and standard all-wheel drive is a welcome inclusion, the Outlander Sport struggles to keep pace with rivals in nearly every major category. For buyers seeking basic transportation with a long warranty and a relatively affordable entry price, the Outlander Sport may still hold some appeal. However, its aging platform, underpowered engines, dated technology, and low-rent cabin make it difficult to recommend against newer alternatives such as the Chevrolet Trax, Mazda CX-30, and Kia Seltos.

Legroom is limited compared with many rivals, and while three passengers can technically sit across the bench, two adults will find the space considerably more comfortable. Storage solutions throughout the cabin are also limited, reducing everyday practicality. Cargo space is respectable for the segment, with room for six carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats and up to twenty-one with the rear seats folded flat. technology: Technology is another area where the Outlander Sport shows its age. Connectivity features are limited, and many rivals offer larger displays and more advanced software as standard equipment. While the infotainment system fulfills basic needs, it no longer feels competitive in a segment where technology increasingly plays a major role in purchasing decisions.
safety: The 2026 Outlander Sport includes a modest collection of driver-assistance technologies. Automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, and automatic high-beam assist are standard across the lineup. More advanced features such as blind-spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert require moving up the trim ladder, while adaptive cruise control is unavailable altogether. car_name: 2027 Mitsubishi Outlander Hybrid
overview: The 2027 Mitsubishi Outlander Hybrid continues to occupy a unique position in the compact SUV segment by combining plug-in hybrid capability, standard all-wheel drive, and an available third-row seat. With an EPA-estimated 45 miles of electric-only driving range, the Outlander PHEV allows many owners to complete daily commutes without using gasoline while still providing the flexibility of a conventional hybrid powertrain for longer journeys. For 2027, the Outlander Hybrid carries over unchanged following recent updates that introduced a larger battery and a more refined interior. While its plug-in hybrid system delivers stronger performance than the standard Outlander, its higher price places it against some of the segment’s most capable hybrid and plug-in rivals. Nevertheless, buyers seeking electric driving capability, premium cabin appointments, and family-friendly versatility may find the Outlander Hybrid an appealing alternative.

drivetrain:
The 2027 Outlander Hybrid is powered by a plug-in hybrid system that combines a 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine with dual electric motors, producing a combined 297 horsepower. A continuously variable automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive complete the drivetrain. Compared with the standard Outlander, the plug-in hybrid feels noticeably quicker, particularly during city driving where the electric motors provide immediate torque. The Outlander Hybrid can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in approximately 6.6 seconds, making it significantly faster than its gasoline-only counterpart.

Ride quality remains comfortable and composed, with suspension refinements helping improve overall stability and confidence. The Outlander Hybrid prioritizes comfort over athleticism, however, and steering feedback remains limited. While it does not offer the engaging handling of rivals such as the Mazda CX-50 Hybrid, it delivers a smooth and relaxed driving experience that suits family-oriented buyers. The plug-in hybrid model can tow up to 1,500 pounds when properly equipped.

The Outlander Hybrid offers an EPA-estimated 45 miles of electric-only driving range, allowing many owners to complete daily commuting without consuming fuel. Once the battery is depleted, the vehicle operates as a conventional hybrid. EPA estimates stand at 27 mpg in the city, 27 mpg on the highway, and 27 mpg combined. While these figures are respectable, they do not significantly outperform some traditional hybrid competitors, many of which deliver superior overall fuel economy at a lower purchase price. Charging flexibility is a major advantage. The battery can be replenished in approximately 6.5 hours using a Level 2 charger, while DC fast charging can restore up to 80 percent capacity in roughly 29 minutes.
interior:
The Outlander Hybrid features one of the most upscale cabins in Mitsubishi’s lineup. Front-seat comfort is excellent, with supportive seats and generous headroom and legroom. The second row offers sufficient space for adults, although some competitors provide slightly greater passenger room. Rear passengers benefit from thoughtful amenities and a comfortable seating position for longer journeys.

Like the standard Outlander, the Hybrid includes a third-row seat. While the additional seating increases versatility, the rear-most seats are best reserved for children due to limited space and difficult access. technology: A 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system comes standard across the lineup and serves as the centerpiece of the cabin. An eight-speaker setup is standard, while higher trims can be fitted with an impressive 12-speaker premium system that delivers rich sound quality throughout the cabin. Additional available technology features include a 10.8-inch head-up display, wireless smartphone charging, multiple USB-C ports, and connected vehicle services through Mitsubishi Connect.
safety: The 2027 Outlander Hybrid includes a comprehensive suite of safety technologies designed to support drivers during everyday travel. Standard equipment includes forward-collision warning, automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, and rear cross-traffic alert. Higher trims expand the package with advanced driver-assistance features such as adaptive cruise control, lane-change assist, and enhanced highway-driving support systems. Combined with Mitsubishi’s strong emphasis on occupant protection, the Outlander Hybrid remains a reassuring family vehicle.

Built on a platform shared with the Nissan Rogue, the Outlander delivers a refined driving experience, a surprisingly upscale interior in higher trims, and an extensive list of standard safety features. safety: The 2027 Outlander includes a comprehensive suite of standard driver-assistance technologies. car_name: 2026 Mini Countryman Electric
overview:
The 2026 Mini Countryman Electric brings Mini's distinctive personality into the electric SUV segment. As the brand's only fully electric model in many markets, it combines quirky styling, a premium cabin, standard all-wheel drive, and impressive practicality. While it remains fun to drive and offers significantly more interior space than traditional Mini models, its relatively modest driving range prevents it from being a class leader.

Powered by a dual-motor setup producing 308 horsepower, the Countryman Electric delivers brisk acceleration and confident all-weather capability. It retains Mini's playful character while offering the everyday usability expected from a compact premium crossover. However, rivals such as the Tesla Model Y, Kia Niro EV, and Volvo EX30 provide greater range, making the Mini a better choice for buyers prioritizing style and driving enjoyment over maximum efficiency.

Unlike some international markets that receive single-motor versions, all U.S.-spec models come exclusively with the more powerful All4 configuration. Acceleration is quick, with the Countryman Electric reaching 60 mph in just 4.8 seconds during testing. While those figures are impressive, the delivery feels less dramatic than some rival EVs due to the vehicle's additional weight. Handling remains one of the Mini's strongest attributes. Steering is precise, body control is well managed, and the vehicle feels composed through corners. One-pedal driving functionality is available and works smoothly, making city driving more convenient and efficient.

The overall design is clean and modern, avoiding the excessive complexity found in some competitors. Front-seat comfort is excellent, with supportive seats and standard heating. Visibility is good, and the elevated seating position contributes to a confident driving experience. Rear-seat passengers benefit from significantly more space than they would find in smaller Mini models, making the Countryman a genuinely practical family vehicle. Cargo capacity is also impressive. The rear cargo area accommodates eight carry-on suitcases with the rear seats in place and up to twenty-two carry-ons when the seats are folded. safety: The 2026 Countryman Electric comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance safety and convenience. drivetrain:
The 2026 Countryman S ALL4 is powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 241 horsepower. Power is sent to all four wheels through a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, providing strong acceleration and confident traction in various driving conditions. On the road, the Countryman feels noticeably more refined and substantial than earlier Mini models. Steering remains precise and responsive, giving drivers confidence through corners, while the suspension strikes a commendable balance between sporty handling and everyday comfort. Unlike the more aggressive John Cooper Works variant, the Countryman S prioritizes overall composure, making it a better fit for daily commuting and long-distance travel. Mini estimates a 0-60 mph time of approximately 6.3 seconds, which should be competitive within the segment. The Countryman also offers a useful towing capacity of up to 3,500 pounds, adding an extra layer of versatility that many buyers will appreciate.

Fuel efficiency remains respectable considering the vehicle's performance and all-wheel-drive configuration. EPA estimates stand at 24 mpg in the city, 32 mpg on the highway, and 27 mpg combined. These figures place the Countryman among the more efficient luxury-oriented compact crossovers while still delivering strong acceleration and confident highway performance.
interior:
Inside, the Countryman embraces Mini's unique design philosophy while significantly improving refinement and practicality. A fabric-covered dashboard creates a warm and modern atmosphere, while hidden LED lighting elements add visual flair and can change colors depending on selected drive modes. Front-seat occupants benefit from generous space and supportive seating, making long journeys comfortable. The rear seat is substantially roomier than the smaller Mini Cooper hatchback, providing adequate legroom and headroom for most adults. Families and frequent travelers will appreciate the increased cabin dimensions, which make the Countryman feel much more like a conventional premium SUV.

Material quality throughout the cabin is impressive, with soft-touch surfaces, premium finishes, and thoughtful details contributing to a genuinely upscale experience. Cargo capacity is another major strength. The Countryman offers significantly more storage space than other Mini models, accommodating eight carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats and up to twenty-two with the seats folded flat. This practicality makes it a viable alternative to more mainstream luxury crossovers.
technology: The centerpiece of the dashboard is Mini's distinctive 9.4-inch circular OLED touchscreen. While visually impressive, the touchscreen-based climate controls can be somewhat distracting to use while driving, and occasional lag has been reported within the infotainment system. Nevertheless, the overall technology package remains among the most distinctive and feature-rich in the segment.
safety: The 2026 Countryman comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance everyday safety and convenience. Standard safety equipment includes automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, lane-departure warning, and lane-keeping assist. Buyers seeking more advanced assistance features can opt for adaptive cruise control with lane-centering capability through the available Driving Assistant Plus package. These systems help position the Countryman competitively against premium rivals while maintaining Mini's focus on modern technology.

car_name: 2026 Mini Cooper JCW Review
overview: The 2026 Mini Cooper JCW remains one of the most entertaining hot hatches on sale today. Built around Mini’s iconic compact footprint and playful personality, the John Cooper Works model adds serious performance credentials through a turbocharged engine, upgraded suspension, larger brakes, and sharper handling dynamics. Available as either a hatchback or convertible, the JCW delivers a driving experience that prioritizes excitement over practicality. While competitors such as the Honda Civic Type R and Volkswagen Golf GTI offer more space and everyday usability, the JCW counters with unmistakable styling, agile cornering, and a premium cabin that feels unique in a segment increasingly dominated by conventional designs.

drivetrain:
Power comes from a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 228 horsepower and 280 lb-ft of torque. The engine is paired exclusively with a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission driving the front wheels. The JCW receives significant upgrades over the standard Cooper, including Brembo performance brakes, a sport-tuned suspension, and an electronically controlled locking front differential. These enhancements help maximize grip and sharpen cornering behavior, giving the car an energetic and highly responsive character. Acceleration feels strong throughout the rev range, while the turbocharged engine delivers immediate thrust. The chassis remains one of the most engaging in the segment, with quick steering and impressive agility. However, the aggressive suspension tuning can make rough roads feel harsh, and torque steer remains noticeable during hard acceleration. Mini estimates a 0–60 mph time of 5.9 seconds for the hatchback and 6.2 seconds for the convertible.

Despite its performance-oriented nature, the JCW maintains respectable efficiency figures. The EPA rates the hatchback at up to 27 mpg in the city and 37 mpg on the highway. Convertible models lose approximately 1–2 mpg due to their added weight and aerodynamic compromises. These numbers make the JCW one of the more fuel-efficient performance cars in its class.
interior: The JCW's cabin combines premium materials with sporty styling cues. A textured dashboard surface, contrast stitching, sport seats, and unique JCW trim elements create an environment that feels both upscale and playful. The front seats provide excellent support during spirited driving while remaining comfortable enough for longer journeys. Higher trims add power seat adjustments and additional comfort features. Rear-seat space remains one of the car's biggest compromises. Adults will find legroom tight, and accessing the rear seats requires folding the front seats forward. For occasional passengers the space is acceptable, but it is not ideal for regular family use. Ride quality is firmer than the standard Mini Cooper due to the sport suspension setup, resulting in greater road feel but reduced comfort on rough pavement.
technology: At the center of the dashboard sits a distinctive 9.4-inch circular touchscreen, one of the defining features of the new-generation Mini interior. The infotainment system includes wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility, Bluetooth connectivity, integrated navigation functions, voice controls, and wireless phone charging. safety: The 2026 Mini Cooper JCW comes equipped with several modern driver-assistance technologies. Standard features include automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, and lane-keeping assist. Higher trims and option packages add adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert. These systems help improve everyday usability while preserving the car's performance-focused nature.

car_name: 2027 Mini Cooper Electric Review
overview:
The 2027 Mini Cooper Electric marks a significant step forward for Mini's iconic hatchback formula. Built on an entirely new generation, the electric Cooper retains the brand's unmistakable design language while introducing improved range, stronger performance, and a more sophisticated cabin experience. Despite embracing electrification, the Cooper Electric remains true to Mini's core philosophy of delivering fun behind the wheel. Its compact dimensions, agile handling characteristics, and playful personality continue to define the driving experience. At the same time, a larger battery pack and more powerful electric motor help address some of the limitations of the previous-generation model.

The new Cooper Electric blends retro-inspired styling with modern technology, creating a vehicle that feels both familiar and futuristic. For buyers seeking a premium urban EV with character, the Mini Cooper Electric stands apart from more conventional electric hatchbacks.
pricing:
Official U.S. pricing has not been announced.
Cooper E (181 hp) expected as the entry-level model.
Cooper SE (215 hp) expected as the higher-performance variant.
Future All4 dual-motor AWD model may join the lineup with 313 hp.
John Cooper Works-inspired versions are available in some markets.
U.S. launch timing remains subject to market and import considerations.
drivetrain:
The Cooper Electric utilizes a front-mounted electric motor driving the front wheels, maintaining the traditional Mini layout. Two primary powertrain configurations are expected globally. The entry-level Cooper E produces 181 horsepower, while the more powerful Cooper SE delivers 215 horsepower. During prototype testing, the SE demonstrated lively acceleration and the sharp handling characteristics that have long been associated with the Mini brand. Mini estimates the Cooper SE can accelerate from 0 to 62 mph in approximately 6.7 seconds, making it quick enough to feel energetic in both city and highway driving. Instant electric torque enhances responsiveness, allowing the car to feel more powerful than the numbers alone suggest. Perhaps most importantly, the new electric model preserves Mini's entertaining driving dynamics. Quick steering responses, nimble cornering behavior, and compact dimensions continue to make the Cooper Electric one of the most engaging small EVs on the market. A future dual-motor All4 variant with 313 horsepower could significantly increase performance for enthusiasts seeking even greater acceleration and all-weather capability.

Range has been substantially improved compared to the previous-generation Mini Electric. The Cooper E is equipped with a 28.9-kWh battery pack, while the Cooper SE receives a larger 58.4-kWh battery. The larger battery is expected to deliver approximately 200 miles of driving range on a full charge. Although this figure trails some larger electric vehicles, it represents a meaningful improvement and should comfortably meet the needs of most urban and suburban drivers. Official U.S. EPA range estimates and charging performance specifications have not yet been finalized.
interior: Mini has taken a more premium approach to the cabin this time around. Inspired by the original 1959 Mini, the interior adopts a cleaner and more minimalist layout while incorporating significantly higher-quality materials. The dashboard features a textile-covered design with hidden LED lighting elements that illuminate during startup and change colors depending on drive mode and infotainment settings. This creates a unique atmosphere that feels both modern and distinctly Mini. A signature row of toggle switches remains, preserving one of the brand's most recognizable interior features. The switches have been redesigned with a more contemporary appearance while maintaining their tactile appeal. Although the exterior dimensions remain similar to the previous model, the interior feels noticeably more spacious and open. Improved packaging and a cleaner dashboard design contribute to a greater sense of roominess for front-seat occupants. Cargo capacity remains modest, as expected from a compact hatchback, but should be sufficient for everyday commuting and weekend use.
technology: The centerpiece of the Cooper Electric's interior is a large circular infotainment display mounted prominently in the center of the dashboard. This distinctive screen serves as the primary interface for vehicle functions, navigation, entertainment, and connectivity features. A head-up display is also available, allowing key driving information to be projected into the driver's field of vision. Mini has focused heavily on digital integration, pairing modern software capabilities with a design that remains faithful to the brand's heritage. The result is one of the most visually distinctive infotainment systems in the automotive industry. Additional feature details will become available closer to the vehicle's market launch.
safety: The 2027 Mini Cooper Electric comes equipped with a range of modern driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance safety and convenience. Standard safety features include automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, forward-collision warning, lane-departure warning, and lane-keeping assistance. These systems help reduce driver workload and improve accident avoidance capabilities. Adaptive cruise control is available for drivers seeking additional comfort during highway travel. The Cooper Electric's safety package ensures it remains competitive with other premium compact EVs.

pros: Distinctive styling, engaging driving dynamics, improved range, and a premium modern cabin make the Cooper Electric one of the most characterful compact EVs available.
cons: Driving range still trails several newer EV rivals, rear-seat space remains limited, and U.S. availability details are not fully finalized.
mn_take: The 2027 Mini Cooper Electric successfully modernizes Mini's legendary formula by combining improved electric performance and technology with the playful personality and driving enjoyment that have always defined the brand.

car_name: 2026 Mini Cooper Review
overview:
The 2026 Mini Cooper continues to embrace its iconic character while adding modern technology, improved refinement, and greater customization possibilities. Redesigned recently, the latest Cooper maintains its unmistakable compact proportions and playful personality while offering a more sophisticated driving experience than previous generations. Available as a two-door hatchback, four-door hatchback, and convertible, the Cooper remains one of the few vehicles that prioritizes driving enjoyment above all else. While practicality takes a back seat to style and fun, buyers looking for a distinctive premium small car will find plenty to appreciate.

The lineup includes the standard Cooper with 161 horsepower and the more spirited Cooper S with 201 horsepower. Both models feature a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine paired with a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Sharp handling, quick responses, and endless personalization options help the Mini stand out in a segment increasingly dominated by more conventional competitors.

drivetrain:
The 2026 Mini Cooper is powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine across the range. The standard Cooper produces 161 horsepower, while the Cooper S increases output to 201 horsepower, providing noticeably stronger acceleration and a more engaging driving character. A seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission comes standard. Although enthusiasts may miss the manual gearbox offered in earlier generations, the automatic shifts quickly and helps maximize performance and efficiency.

The Cooper S remains the enthusiast's choice, delivering strong mid-range torque, a distinctive exhaust note, and the lively cornering behavior that has long defined the Mini brand. Steering is quick, body control is excellent, and the car feels eager to change direction on winding roads. At the same time, the latest generation is quieter and more refined than its predecessor, making it easier to live with during everyday commuting. The convertible version retains much of the hatchback's entertaining dynamics while adding open-air driving enjoyment.

Fuel efficiency remains a strong point despite the Cooper's sporty character. Both the standard Cooper and Cooper S are EPA-rated at up to 28 mpg in city driving, 39 mpg on the highway, and 32 mpg combined. Convertible models are slightly less efficient but still respectable, returning up to 27 mpg city and 37 mpg highway. These figures make the Cooper one of the more economical premium small cars available.
interior: The new Cooper adopts a minimalist interior philosophy inspired by the original 1959 Mini. The dashboard design is clean and uncluttered, featuring premium materials, unique textile surfaces, and creative lighting elements that reinforce the vehicle's youthful personality. Despite its compact dimensions, the cabin feels surprisingly airy. Improved packaging and a simplified dashboard design help create a more open atmosphere for front-seat occupants. The front seats provide good comfort and support, especially in higher trims equipped with sport seats. Rear-seat space remains one of the Cooper's compromises. Adult passengers will find accommodations tight, particularly in the two-door model. Cargo space is similarly limited compared to larger hatchbacks and crossovers, though it remains adequate for daily errands and weekend travel. Ride quality is improved compared to previous generations but can still feel firm over rough pavement, especially when equipped with larger wheels.
technology: The centerpiece of the Cooper's interior is a unique circular infotainment display that appears to float above the dashboard. The updated infotainment software includes navigation, smartphone integration, SiriusXM capability, and various connected services. Although visually impressive, the system can require some familiarization due to its unconventional layout. Some users may find certain functions less intuitive than traditional infotainment systems.
safety: The 2026 Mini Cooper comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of modern safety technologies designed to improve driver awareness and accident avoidance. Standard features include automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, lane-departure warning, and lane-keeping assistance. These systems help provide an additional layer of protection during daily driving. Adaptive cruise control is available on higher trims, adding greater convenience during highway journeys. The Cooper's safety technology package brings it in line with many larger and more expensive premium vehicles.

car_name: 2026 Mercedes-Maybach GLS-Class Review
overview:
The 2026 Mercedes-Maybach GLS-Class represents the pinnacle of luxury SUV motoring within the Mercedes-Benz portfolio. Based on the already impressive GLS platform, the Maybach treatment transforms it into a rolling executive lounge designed to rival ultra-premium offerings from Bentley and Rolls-Royce. Every aspect of the GLS600 focuses on passenger comfort, craftsmanship, and effortless performance.

With a handcrafted interior, reclining rear executive seats, extensive use of premium materials, and a powerful twin-turbo V8 engine, the GLS600 caters to buyers who value comfort and exclusivity above all else. Despite its substantial size and weight, the SUV delivers impressive acceleration while maintaining an exceptionally smooth and serene driving experience.
pricing: GLS600 — Starting at $181,350
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the GLS600 features a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 engine producing 550 horsepower. The powertrain is enhanced by Mercedes-Benz's 48-volt mild-hybrid system, which provides additional torque assistance during acceleration while also improving overall smoothness and responsiveness. Power is delivered through a refined nine-speed automatic transmission and Mercedes-Benz's 4Matic all-wheel-drive system. Despite weighing significantly more than most luxury SUVs, the GLS600 feels remarkably effortless on the move. Acceleration is immediate and smooth, with abundant power available at virtually any speed.

The standard adaptive air suspension is one of the vehicle's defining characteristics. A dedicated Maybach drive mode softens throttle response, transmission behavior, and suspension settings to maximize passenger comfort. Road imperfections are absorbed with remarkable composure, creating a near-floating sensation that few competitors can match. Even at highway speeds, the GLS600 maintains outstanding stability while keeping wind and road noise almost entirely isolated from the cabin. Although comfort remains the primary objective, performance is far from lacking. The SUV can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in just 3.9 seconds, an astonishing figure for a vehicle of this size and luxury focus.
interior: The interior of the Maybach GLS600 is where the vehicle truly distinguishes itself from both the standard GLS and many of its luxury rivals. Virtually every surface is wrapped in premium Nappa leather, while genuine wood veneers, polished metal accents, and intricate detailing elevate the cabin to a truly bespoke level. The front seats offer heating, ventilation, massage functions, and extensive power adjustments, but it is the rear cabin that serves as the centerpiece of the Maybach experience. Buyers can select a four-seat executive configuration that transforms the second row into an ultra-luxurious retreat. These reclining rear seats offer massage functionality, heating, ventilation, and generous legroom that rivals some of the world's finest luxury sedans. Additional features such as folding tables, champagne flutes, refrigerated compartments, and premium rear-seat controls create an environment designed for passengers who prefer being chauffeured. The available fragrance system further enhances the cabin atmosphere, adding another layer of sensory refinement. Even long journeys become relaxing experiences thanks to exceptional sound insulation and the plush ride quality delivered by the sophisticated suspension setup.
technology: Mercedes-Maybach equips the GLS600 with an extensive suite of advanced technology features. The dashboard incorporates dual 12.3-inch displays that serve as both the digital instrument cluster and infotainment interface, powered by the latest generation of Mercedes-Benz's MBUX software. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto integration, natural voice commands, connected services, navigation, and wireless device charging. Rear passengers benefit from dedicated entertainment screens mounted behind the front seats, allowing access to media, navigation information, and vehicle settings. One of the standout features is the extraordinary 29-speaker Burmester High-End 3D surround sound system. Delivering concert-hall-quality audio throughout the cabin, it provides one of the finest in-car listening experiences available in any production SUV.
safety: Despite its focus on luxury, the GLS600 includes an impressive range of advanced safety and driver-assistance technologies. Mercedes-Maybach has made many of these features standard, helping reduce driver workload while enhancing occupant protection. The SUV includes automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, adaptive cruise control with lane-centering assistance, lane-departure warning, lane-keeping assist, blind-spot monitoring, traffic-sign recognition, and advanced parking assistance systems. These technologies work seamlessly in the background, allowing drivers and passengers to focus on enjoying the luxurious environment rather than managing the vehicle's operation.

car_name: 2026 Mercedes-Maybach EQS SUV Review
overview:
The 2026 Mercedes-Maybach EQS SUV represents the pinnacle of Mercedes-Benz's electric luxury ambitions. Combining the silent refinement of an advanced electric powertrain with the opulent craftsmanship expected from the Maybach badge, this ultra-luxury SUV is designed primarily for passengers who value comfort above all else. While its futuristic exterior and massive Hyperscreen dashboard showcase cutting-edge technology, the true highlight lies in the rear cabin, where airline-style seating, premium materials, and exceptional isolation create a first-class travel experience.

With 649 horsepower, all-wheel drive, and a whisper-quiet ride, the EQS SUV delivers effortless performance while maintaining the serene character expected from a chauffeur-driven flagship.
pricing:
EQS680: Starting at $181,350
EQS680 Night Series: Starting at $206,150
drivetrain:
Power comes from a dual-motor electric drivetrain producing a combined 649 horsepower and standard all-wheel drive. Despite its substantial size and luxury-focused mission, the EQS680 can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in an estimated 4.1 seconds. The standard air suspension with adaptive dampers prioritizes ride comfort above all else, effortlessly absorbing road imperfections. Four-wheel steering improves maneuverability in urban environments, making the large SUV surprisingly easy to place and park. While enthusiastic drivers may find the handling uninvolving, the EQS SUV excels at delivering a smooth, composed, and exceptionally refined driving experience.

A 108.4-kWh battery pack provides an EPA-estimated driving range of approximately 300 miles. The EQS SUV supports DC fast charging up to 200 kW, allowing the battery to charge from 10 to 80 percent in around 31 minutes under ideal conditions. Efficiency is rated at 84 MPGe in both city and highway driving, which is respectable considering the vehicle's size, luxury equipment, and performance capabilities.
interior:
The cabin is among the most luxurious interiors currently available in an electric SUV. Rich leather upholstery, beautifully crafted aluminum trim, and meticulous attention to detail create an environment worthy of the Maybach name. Front occupants enjoy exceptionally comfortable seats, but the rear compartment is where the EQS SUV truly shines. Buyers can choose between a traditional rear bench or individual executive seats with reclining functions and powered footrests. Optional features include a refrigerated compartment, folding tables, and a rear center console with a removable tablet controller. Excellent sound insulation, combined with the electric powertrain's near-silent operation, creates an extraordinarily peaceful atmosphere for long-distance travel.

Luxury takes precedence over practicality in the Maybach EQS SUV. The fixed rear-seat arrangement and sound-insulating bulkhead reduce cargo space to approximately 15 cubic feet, significantly less than the standard EQS SUV. While sufficient for everyday luggage, buyers frequently traveling with substantial cargo may find the space restrictive.
technology: Technology plays a major role in the EQS SUV experience. The dashboard is dominated by Mercedes-Benz's Hyperscreen setup, incorporating multiple displays beneath a single glass surface. Standard features include a 17.7-inch central touchscreen, a 12.3-inch passenger display, wireless Apple CarPlay, wireless Android Auto, Bluetooth connectivity, wireless charging, and a premium 15-speaker Burmester audio system. Rear passengers also benefit from dedicated 11.6-inch entertainment displays mounted behind the front seats, providing a comprehensive luxury experience throughout the cabin.
safety: Mercedes-Maybach equips the EQS SUV with an extensive suite of advanced driver-assistance systems as standard. Features include forward-collision warning, automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, automatic high-beam headlamps, and a self-parking system. These technologies complement the vehicle's luxury mission by reducing driver workload and enhancing passenger comfort during long journeys.

cons: Limited cargo capacity, technology-heavy interface, and less engaging driving dynamics.
mn_take: The 2026 Mercedes-Maybach EQS SUV successfully blends ultra-luxury craftsmanship with modern electric mobility, delivering one of the most comfortable and prestigious SUV experiences available today.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class EV Review
overview:
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class EV represents a new chapter in Mercedes-Benz's electric vehicle strategy. While it shares its name and overall shape with the gasoline-powered GLC, this model is built around a dedicated electric powertrain that delivers stronger performance, greater efficiency, and a distinctly modern driving experience. Positioned below the larger EQE SUV, the GLC EV combines the luxury and refinement expected from Mercedes-Benz with the benefits of electrification. It offers impressive projected driving range, rapid charging capability, a spacious cabin, and advanced technology that places it among the most competitive electric luxury SUVs in its segment. Buyers can choose between a rear-wheel-drive single-motor model or a more powerful dual-motor all-wheel-drive variant, allowing the GLC EV to cater to a wide range of driving preferences.

The result is an electric SUV that feels familiar to existing Mercedes-Benz owners while offering the advantages of next-generation EV technology.

Buyers seeking stronger acceleration and enhanced traction can opt for the GLC400 4Matic, which adds a second motor at the front axle and increases total output to 483 horsepower. Mercedes-Benz has equipped the GLC EV with a unique two-speed transmission designed to optimize both low-speed acceleration and highway efficiency. Unlike traditional gearboxes, shifts occur seamlessly and remain virtually imperceptible to occupants.

Performance is expected to be strong across the lineup.
