Ride quality is a major highlight, particularly when equipped with the optional air-suspension system, which delivers impressive comfort while also allowing the vehicle to raise its ride height for additional ground clearance when needed. Rather than focusing solely on outright sportiness, the GLC EV prioritizes smoothness, refinement, and effortless acceleration.

A large 94-kWh battery pack powers both GLC EV variants. Mercedes-Benz expects the dual-motor GLC400 4Matic to achieve approximately 380 miles of driving range, placing it among the segment leaders for long-distance capability. The company has not yet released final EPA estimates for the rear-wheel-drive GLC300+, but it may ultimately deliver even greater range due to its lighter and more efficient configuration. Charging performance is equally impressive. Mercedes claims the battery can gain approximately 188 miles of range in just ten minutes when connected to a compatible fast charger. This rapid charging capability significantly improves long-distance usability and reduces downtime during road trips. The combination of substantial range and fast charging makes the GLC EV one of the most promising luxury electric SUVs entering the market.
interior: The GLC EV's cabin embraces a futuristic luxury theme with premium materials, ambient lighting, and extensive digital integration. High-quality finishes cover most interior surfaces, helping maintain the upscale atmosphere expected from a Mercedes-Benz product. The front seats provide excellent comfort and support for long journeys, while the elevated seating position offers commanding outward visibility. Storage spaces throughout the cabin have been thoughtfully integrated, improving everyday practicality. Rear-seat passengers benefit from more space than they receive in the gasoline-powered GLC. Legroom is generous, and the flat floor created by the EV platform contributes to a more open and comfortable environment. Cargo practicality is also impressive. The rear luggage compartment offers 20.1 cubic feet of storage space, while an additional 4.5-cubic-foot front trunk provides extra room for charging cables and smaller items.
technology: Technology plays a central role in the GLC EV experience. Standard models feature a large 14.0-inch infotainment touchscreen paired with a digital instrument cluster. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay, wireless Android Auto, Bluetooth connectivity, navigation, and SiriusXM satellite radio. For buyers seeking the most advanced setup, Mercedes offers the optional 39.1-inch Hyperscreen, which stretches across nearly the entire dashboard and integrates multiple displays into a single glass surface. This feature transforms the cabin into one of the most technologically advanced interiors in the segment. Audio quality can also be upgraded through an optional 16-speaker Burmester sound system featuring Dolby Atmos spatial audio technology, creating a highly immersive listening experience. Although the technology is impressive, some drivers may find the sheer number of digital displays and touch-based controls overwhelming compared with more traditional luxury interiors.
safety: Mercedes-Benz equips the GLC EV with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies as standard. Features such as automatic emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, and blind-spot monitoring provide strong baseline protection for daily driving. Additional safety technologies are available through optional MB.Drive Assist packages. The vehicle's combination of active safety systems, advanced sensors, and driver-assistance technologies positions it among the most sophisticated offerings in the compact luxury EV segment.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC350e Hybrid Review
overview:
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC350e Hybrid occupies an increasingly important position in the GLC lineup. Sitting between the conventional gasoline-powered GLC300 and the fully electric GLC-Class EV, the plug-in hybrid offers an attractive compromise for buyers who want meaningful electric driving capability without fully committing to an EV lifestyle. At first glance, the GLC350e looks nearly identical to the standard GLC, with only subtle badging and a charging-port door distinguishing it from its gasoline-powered sibling. Underneath the elegant sheet metal, however, lies a sophisticated plug-in hybrid system that combines a turbocharged four-cylinder engine with an electric motor and a sizable battery pack. The result is a luxury SUV capable of delivering one of the longest electric-only driving ranges in its class while maintaining the practicality and refinement that have made the GLC one of Mercedes-Benz's best-selling models.

While the hybrid system introduces some compromises in responsiveness compared with the gas-only model, the GLC350e compensates with outstanding efficiency, generous EV capability, premium interior quality, and everyday usability. For buyers who can regularly charge at home or work, it represents one of the most compelling luxury plug-in hybrid SUVs currently available.
pricing:
GLC350e – Starting at $62,000 (estimated)
GLC350e Exclusive – Starting at $64,000 (estimated)
GLC350e Pinnacle – Starting at $66,000 (estimated)

The standard GLC350e offers excellent value and already includes most of the features buyers expect from a premium luxury SUV. Adding options individually, such as ventilated front seats, a heated steering wheel, and adaptive cruise control, may provide better value than stepping up to higher trims.
drivetrain:
The GLC350e utilizes a sophisticated plug-in hybrid powertrain that pairs a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine with an electric motor and a large 23.3-kWh battery pack. Combined output stands at 313 horsepower, significantly more than the 255 horsepower available in the standard GLC300. Despite the higher power rating, the GLC350e is not actually quicker than its gasoline-powered counterpart. The additional weight introduced by the battery pack and hybrid hardware affects acceleration and overall responsiveness. During everyday driving, the transition between electric and gasoline power is generally smooth, although there are moments when the system takes a brief pause to determine how best to distribute power.

The nine-speed automatic transmission works well with the hybrid system, and standard all-wheel drive enhances traction and confidence in varying weather conditions. Ride quality remains one of the vehicle's strongest attributes, offering a refined balance between comfort and composure. Most road imperfections are absorbed effectively, although sharper impacts can occasionally be felt inside the cabin. Braking performance is competent, but the blend between regenerative braking and traditional friction brakes can create inconsistent pedal feel, which may require an adjustment period for some drivers.

Efficiency is one of the GLC350e's primary strengths. The EPA estimates fuel economy at 23 mpg in the city, 28 mpg on the highway, and 25 mpg combined when operating as a conventional hybrid after battery depletion. When the battery is fully charged, the SUV achieves a combined rating of 64 MPGe. In real-world testing, the vehicle delivered 32 mpg during gasoline-only highway driving and an impressive 75 MPGe when operating primarily on electric power. For owners who regularly recharge the battery and complete shorter daily commutes, fuel consumption can be dramatically reduced compared with a traditional gasoline-powered luxury SUV.

The standout feature of the GLC350e is its exceptional electric-only driving range. Equipped with a substantial 23.3-kWh battery pack, the SUV carries an EPA-estimated electric range of 54 miles, which is among the best figures currently available in the luxury plug-in hybrid segment.

Real-world testing has proven even more impressive. During highway evaluation, the GLC350e managed to travel 58 miles before the gasoline engine was required to assist. This means many owners could complete their daily commute entirely on electric power without consuming any gasoline. Charging performance is equally practical. Mercedes-Benz claims the battery can recharge from low levels in approximately 30 minutes when connected to a 60-kW DC fast charger. This capability is unusual among plug-in hybrids and significantly improves convenience for drivers who frequently rely on electric operation.

The generous EV range transforms the GLC350e from a traditional hybrid into a vehicle capable of functioning like a small electric SUV during daily use while retaining unlimited long-distance capability thanks to its gasoline engine.
interior:
Inside, the GLC350e delivers the same upscale environment found throughout the GLC lineup. Premium materials cover nearly every surface, and the overall design strikes an effective balance between luxury and modern technology. The front seats are exceptionally comfortable, featuring heating, memory functions, and adjustable lumbar support as standard equipment. The seating position is excellent for long journeys, and cabin insulation effectively keeps outside noise to a minimum. The second row offers generous headroom and respectable legroom, making it comfortable for adult passengers. While not class-leading in outright passenger space, it provides ample room for everyday family use and long-distance travel. Cargo capacity remains practical despite the battery packaging. The GLC350e offers 24 cubic feet of storage space behind the rear seats and up to 56 cubic feet with the rear seats folded. These figures remain highly competitive within the compact luxury SUV segment.

Overall, the interior successfully delivers the premium experience buyers expect from a Mercedes-Benz while maintaining strong everyday usability.
technology: Technology plays a central role in the GLC350e's appeal. The dashboard features a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster paired with an 11.9-inch central touchscreen running Mercedes-Benz's latest MBUX infotainment system. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, voice commands, Bluetooth connectivity, and a variety of customizable displays. Navigation is available with augmented reality functionality that overlays directional graphics onto live camera feeds, making route guidance easier to follow. Optional upgrades include a head-up display and a premium 15-speaker Burmester audio system that significantly enhances the in-cabin entertainment experience. While the digital interface is visually impressive, the absence of traditional climate-control buttons and physical volume controls may frustrate some users. Many functions require interaction through touch-sensitive controls, which can be distracting while driving.
safety:
The GLC350e provides a solid foundation of safety equipment, although many of the most advanced systems remain optional. Standard equipment includes automated emergency braking and blind-spot monitoring, providing essential protection for everyday driving situations. Buyers can further enhance safety by adding optional technologies such as adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assistance, and a 360-degree camera system. These systems improve convenience and confidence during highway driving, urban traffic, and parking maneuvers.

Mercedes-Benz's suite of driver-assistance technologies continues to rank among the most sophisticated in the luxury SUV segment.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Battery Warranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None

The GLC350e offers warranty coverage comparable to most luxury competitors. The extended battery warranty provides valuable protection for hybrid system components, although the absence of complimentary maintenance remains a disadvantage compared with certain rivals from BMW and Jaguar.
pros: Outstanding electric-only driving range, luxurious interior quality, strong efficiency, practical cargo space, smooth ride quality, and fast charging capability for a plug-in hybrid.
cons: Power delivery can feel less responsive than the standard GLC300, brake pedal feel is inconsistent, and the touch-heavy interface lacks the convenience of physical controls.
mn_take: The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC350e Hybrid is one of the most convincing plug-in hybrid luxury SUVs on the market, offering class-leading electric range, premium comfort, and excellent efficiency for buyers who want EV-like daily driving without sacrificing long-distance flexibility.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class EV Review
overview:
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class EV represents a significant step forward in the brand's electric vehicle strategy, replacing the EQ naming convention with a model that more closely aligns with Mercedes-Benz's traditional lineup. While it shares its name and overall proportions with the gasoline-powered GLC, the electric version is an entirely different vehicle underneath, built specifically to deliver the performance, range, and refinement expected from a modern luxury EV.

Mercedes-Benz has focused heavily on combining long-distance capability with premium comfort, resulting in an electric SUV that feels every bit as luxurious as its combustion-powered sibling while offering substantially more technology and stronger performance. The new GLC EV introduces a dedicated electric architecture, advanced battery technology, rapid charging capabilities, and an interior dominated by next-generation digital displays.

Available in both rear-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive configurations, the GLC EV targets some of the most competitive luxury electric SUVs on the market, including the BMW iX3, Volvo EX60, Cadillac Optiq, and Porsche Macan Electric. With an expected driving range approaching 380 miles, impressive acceleration, and a spacious cabin, the GLC EV positions itself as one of the most compelling premium electric crossovers Mercedes-Benz has produced to date.
pricing:
GLC300+ – Starting at $60,000 (estimated)
GLC300+ Exclusive – Starting at $62,000 (estimated)
GLC400 4Matic – Starting at $65,000 (estimated)
GLC400 4Matic Exclusive – Starting at $67,000 (estimated)
GLC300+ Pinnacle – Starting at $67,000 (estimated)
GLC300+ Pinnacle Plus – Starting at $69,000 (estimated)
GLC400 4Matic Pinnacle – Starting at $69,000 (estimated)
GLC400 4Matic Pinnacle Plus – Starting at $72,000 (estimated)

The GLC300+ Exclusive appears to be the best value in the lineup. It adds premium features such as an illuminated grille, panoramic glass roof with adjustable transparency, enhanced ambient lighting, and a passenger-side display while likely maintaining the strongest range figures in the lineup.
drivetrain:
The GLC-Class EV launches with two distinct powertrain options designed to appeal to different types of buyers. The entry-level GLC300+ uses a single electric motor driving the rear wheels and generates an impressive 369 horsepower. Buyers seeking additional performance can move up to the GLC400 4Matic, which adds a second motor to create a dual-motor all-wheel-drive system producing a combined 483 horsepower. Unlike many electric vehicles that use a single-speed transmission, the GLC EV incorporates a sophisticated two-speed automatic gearbox designed to improve efficiency and high-speed performance. The transitions are virtually imperceptible, helping maintain the smooth driving experience expected from a Mercedes-Benz.

Performance is one of the vehicle's standout strengths. Mercedes estimates the rear-wheel-drive GLC300+ will accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in approximately 5.9 seconds, while the more powerful GLC400 4Matic is expected to complete the same sprint in around 4.0 seconds. That places it firmly among the quickest vehicles in the compact luxury EV segment. Ride comfort remains a key priority. The standard suspension delivers a composed and refined driving experience, while the optional air suspension further elevates comfort by absorbing road imperfections with remarkable effectiveness. The system can also raise ride height when additional ground clearance is needed, adding versatility for light off-road use or challenging weather conditions.

Rather than focusing on aggressive sportiness, the GLC EV prioritizes effortless acceleration, stability, and long-distance comfort, which aligns perfectly with its luxury-oriented mission.One of the most impressive aspects of the 2027 GLC-Class EV is its projected driving range. Mercedes-Benz expects the dual-motor GLC400 4Matic to achieve approximately 380 miles of range on a full charge, making it one of the longest-range luxury electric SUVs in its class. Power comes from a 94-kWh battery pack that supports rapid charging capabilities. According to Mercedes-Benz, the vehicle can add approximately 188 miles of range in just 10 minutes when connected to a compatible fast charger. This capability significantly reduces charging downtime and enhances the SUV's practicality for long-distance travel.

While official EPA figures for the rear-wheel-drive GLC300+ have not yet been released, it is expected to exceed the range of the all-wheel-drive variant due to its lower energy consumption and lighter drivetrain configuration. The combination of strong efficiency, long range, and rapid charging places the GLC EV among the most capable electric luxury SUVs currently under development.
interior:
Inside, the GLC-Class EV embraces Mercedes-Benz's latest design philosophy, combining premium craftsmanship with a highly digital environment. High-quality materials cover the cabin, and attention to detail remains consistent with the standards expected from the brand. The front seats are exceptionally comfortable and supportive, making the GLC EV an excellent companion for long-distance driving. Numerous storage compartments throughout the cabin enhance practicality, while the seating position offers excellent visibility. Rear-seat accommodations improve upon the gasoline-powered GLC. Thanks to the EV platform's packaging advantages, passengers benefit from increased legroom and a more spacious overall environment. Even taller adults should find the second row comfortable for extended journeys.

Cargo practicality is also impressive. The rear cargo area provides 20.1 cubic feet of storage space behind the second row, making it suitable for family travel, shopping trips, or weekend getaways. Additionally, the GLC EV includes a 4.5-cubic-foot front trunk, providing extra storage that is unavailable in the conventional GLC. Although some buyers may find the abundance of screens and lighting effects excessive, the overall cabin experience remains unmistakably luxurious and technologically advanced.
technology:
Technology is at the heart of the GLC EV experience. Standard models feature a large 14.0-inch central touchscreen paired with a digital instrument cluster, creating a modern and intuitive interface. For buyers seeking the ultimate technology showcase, Mercedes offers its striking 39.1-inch Hyperscreen. Stretching nearly the entire width of the dashboard, this display integrates multiple screens beneath a single glass surface and transforms the cabin into one of the most visually impressive interiors in the segment.

Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with built-in navigation, Bluetooth connectivity, and SiriusXM satellite radio. Mercedes-Benz's latest software platform delivers improved responsiveness and enhanced personalization options. Audio enthusiasts can upgrade from the standard five-speaker system to a premium 16-speaker Burmester sound system featuring Dolby Atmos spatial audio technology. The result is an immersive listening experience that rivals some dedicated home audio systems. The technology offering is undoubtedly impressive, although some users may find the sheer number of digital controls and displays overwhelming at first.
safety:
Mercedes-Benz equips the GLC EV with a broad range of standard safety technologies designed to enhance driver confidence and occupant protection. Standard equipment includes automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, and blind-spot monitoring. These systems work together to help prevent accidents and reduce driver workload during everyday driving situations. For buyers seeking more advanced capabilities, optional assistance packages add adaptive cruise control with hands-free driving functionality, further expanding the vehicle's semi-autonomous capabilities on highways and in heavy traffic.

The GLC EV's advanced electronics, sensor systems, and safety technologies position it among the most technologically sophisticated vehicles in its class.
warranty:

Complimentary Maintenance: None

Warranty coverage is competitive with other luxury electric vehicles from German manufacturers. The extended EV component warranty provides valuable long-term protection for the battery and electric drivetrain, although the absence of complimentary maintenance remains a disadvantage compared with some competitors.
pros: Excellent projected driving range, strong acceleration, luxurious cabin quality, spacious interior, advanced charging capabilities, and cutting-edge technology features make the GLC EV one of Mercedes-Benz's most promising electric vehicles.
cons: The oversized front grille design may divide opinions, the Hyperscreen can feel overwhelming, and higher trim levels can become expensive once options are added.
mn_take: The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class EV successfully blends long-range capability, premium luxury, advanced technology, and impressive performance into a highly desirable electric SUV that feels ready to challenge the best vehicles in the luxury EV segment.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz G580e
overview:
The 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class continues to set the benchmark for what many luxury SUV buyers expect from a premium compact crossover. Combining the refinement and sophistication of the C-Class sedan with the added practicality of an SUV body style, the GLC remains one of the most well-rounded vehicles in its segment. Mercedes-Benz has crafted the GLC around comfort, luxury, and everyday usability rather than outright sportiness. While competitors such as the BMW X3 and Porsche Macan place a greater emphasis on performance, the GLC appeals to buyers seeking a serene driving experience, a beautifully appointed cabin, and impressive passenger and cargo space.

For 2026, the GLC receives only minor updates following its recent redesign. New appearance packages add additional customization opportunities, while the core strengths that have made the model one of Mercedes-Benz's best-selling SUVs remain intact. Available in both traditional SUV and sleek Coupe body styles, the GLC offers something for buyers who prioritize either practicality or design flair. The result is a luxury SUV that excels at daily commuting, long-distance touring, and family transportation while maintaining the premium character expected from the three-pointed star.
pricing:
GLC300 – Starting at $50,900
GLC300 Exclusive – Starting at $52,900
GLC300 Pinnacle – Starting at $55,150
GLC300 Coupe – Starting at $61,000
GLC300 Coupe Pinnacle – Starting at $63,500

The GLC300 Exclusive represents the sweet spot in the lineup, adding desirable luxury and technology features without pushing the price into premium territory. Buyers who prioritize cargo capacity should choose the standard SUV body style, while the Coupe is best suited to those who value styling over practicality.
drivetrain:
Every 2026 GLC-Class is powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 255 horsepower. The engine is paired with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system that assists during acceleration, improves efficiency, and helps smooth power delivery. A nine-speed automatic transmission comes standard, with rear-wheel drive as the default configuration and Mercedes-Benz's 4Matic all-wheel-drive system available across the range. The powertrain's greatest strength is its refinement. The turbocharged engine operates with impressive smoothness and minimal noise, delivering power in a seamless and predictable manner. Acceleration is more than adequate for everyday driving, allowing the GLC to feel responsive in urban traffic and comfortable at highway speeds.

During testing, the GLC300 4Matic accelerated from 0 to 60 mph in 5.7 seconds, placing it competitively within the compact luxury SUV segment. While that figure is respectable, performance is not the GLC's primary mission. Instead, Mercedes-Benz has tuned the chassis to prioritize comfort and composure. The suspension absorbs road imperfections effectively, while cabin isolation minimizes wind and road noise. Steering feedback is limited, and the GLC lacks the engaging dynamics offered by rivals such as the Porsche Macan or Alfa Romeo Stelvio. However, buyers seeking a relaxed and luxurious driving experience will likely appreciate its calm and confident demeanor.

The GLC-Class delivers competitive efficiency for a luxury SUV in this category. Rear-wheel-drive models are rated at up to 24 mpg city and 32 mpg highway, while all-wheel-drive variants return approximately 23 mpg city and 31 mpg highway. The mild-hybrid system contributes to these respectable figures by assisting the gasoline engine during acceleration and improving efficiency during stop-and-go driving. As a result, the GLC strikes a good balance between performance and economy without requiring the compromises associated with a plug-in hybrid or fully electric powertrain. For drivers covering significant highway mileage, the GLC's efficiency and large fuel tank provide excellent long-distance touring capability.
interior:
The cabin remains one of the GLC-Class's greatest strengths. Mercedes-Benz has created an environment that feels modern, elegant, and unmistakably premium. High-quality materials cover nearly every surface, while the overall design reflects the brand's latest luxury philosophy. The front seats provide excellent comfort and support, making the GLC particularly enjoyable on long journeys. Heated front seats, memory settings, and adjustable lumbar support are standard equipment, enhancing everyday comfort. Passenger accommodation is equally impressive in the second row. Thanks to the SUV's upright proportions, rear-seat passengers enjoy generous headroom and above-average legroom. Adults can travel comfortably in the back seat, making the GLC a practical family vehicle as well as a luxury SUV.

Cargo capacity is among the best in the segment. The standard SUV offers 22 cubic feet of cargo space behind the rear seats and up to 56 cubic feet with the rear seats folded. This surpasses several competitors, including the Genesis GV70 and Volvo XC60. The Coupe variant sacrifices some practicality in favor of its sportier roofline, reducing cargo volume to 19 cubic feet. Overall, the standard GLC SUV remains the more versatile choice for most buyers.
technology:
The GLC features Mercedes-Benz's latest generation MBUX infotainment system, which blends advanced technology with an elegant dashboard design. A 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster sits ahead of the driver, while an 11.9-inch central touchscreen dominates the center console. The touchscreen is angled slightly toward the driver and provides access to vehicle settings, navigation, entertainment functions, and climate controls. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, ensuring seamless smartphone integration. The system also supports voice commands through Mercedes-Benz's intelligent voice assistant, allowing drivers to adjust settings using natural speech. Optional navigation includes an augmented-reality feature that overlays directional guidance onto live camera images, helping simplify complex intersections and unfamiliar routes.

Audiophiles can upgrade to the available 15-speaker Burmester 3D Surround Sound system, which delivers impressive clarity and richness throughout the cabin. While the technology is highly sophisticated, the touch-sensitive steering-wheel controls can occasionally prove frustrating during everyday use.
safety: Mercedes-Benz equips the GLC with a solid collection of safety and driver-assistance technologies. Standard features include automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection and blind-spot monitoring, helping enhance confidence during everyday driving. Buyers seeking more advanced assistance systems can opt for the Driver Assistance package, which adds adaptive cruise control with lane-centering capability. These features improve long-distance driving comfort and reduce driver fatigue during highway travel. The GLC's robust safety structure, advanced electronics, and available driver aids make it one of the safer offerings in the compact luxury SUV segment.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None

Mercedes-Benz provides warranty coverage that is competitive within the luxury segment. However, unlike certain rivals from BMW and Jaguar, the GLC does not include complimentary scheduled maintenance, which may increase ownership costs over time.
pros: Elegant interior design, exceptionally refined turbocharged powertrain, comfortable ride quality, spacious rear seating, and generous cargo capacity make the GLC one of the most complete luxury SUVs in its class.
cons: Steering lacks engagement, touch-sensitive steering-wheel controls can be frustrating to use, and optional features can significantly increase the final purchase price.
mn_take: The 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class excels by focusing on what luxury SUV buyers value most—comfort, refinement, technology, and practicality—making it one of the strongest all-around choices in the compact premium SUV segment.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLB-Class EV Review
overview:
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLB-Class EV marks a significant evolution in Mercedes-Benz's compact electric SUV strategy. Replacing the outgoing EQB, the new GLB-Class EV adopts a simpler naming structure while retaining the practical, boxy design that made its predecessor popular among buyers seeking maximum interior space in a compact footprint. Built on Mercedes-Benz's latest electric vehicle architecture, the GLB-Class EV combines premium luxury, advanced technology, and family-friendly practicality. Unlike many modern electric crossovers that prioritize styling over functionality, the GLB EV maintains its upright proportions, allowing for a spacious cabin and the availability of an optional third-row seat.

Mercedes-Benz has also placed a strong emphasis on technology, equipping the new model with a highly digitalized interior and the latest generation of infotainment features. With projected driving ranges exceeding 300 miles and improved charging capabilities, the GLB-Class EV aims to become one of the most practical luxury electric SUVs in its segment. For buyers seeking a premium electric SUV that prioritizes usability, passenger space, and everyday comfort, the GLB-Class EV presents a compelling alternative to rivals such as the Audi Q4 e-tron, Cadillac Optiq, and Volvo EX40.

GLB250+ – Starting at $55,000 (estimated)
GLB250+ Exclusive – Starting at $58,000 (estimated)

drivetrain:
Mercedes-Benz offers the GLB-Class EV with two distinct electric powertrains. The entry-level GLB250+ features a single rear-mounted electric motor producing 268 horsepower, while the GLB350 4Matic adds a second motor at the front axle, increasing total output to 349 horsepower and providing all-wheel-drive capability. The dual-motor setup intelligently disconnects the front motor during steady-state driving to maximize efficiency, automatically re-engaging it when additional power or traction is required. This approach helps balance performance and energy consumption, a strategy increasingly common among premium electric vehicles.

Mercedes-Benz claims the GLB250+ can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in 7.3 seconds, while the more powerful GLB350 4Matic completes the same sprint in approximately 5.4 seconds. Buyers can further enhance ride quality with an available adaptive suspension that continuously adjusts damping characteristics based on road conditions and driving style. The GLB EV also offers multiple regenerative braking settings, including full one-pedal driving capability. An intelligent automatic regeneration mode uses onboard sensors and navigation data to optimize energy recovery and improve overall efficiency.

A large 85-kWh battery pack powers every GLB-Class EV. Mercedes-Benz pairs this battery with an advanced 800-volt electrical architecture, enabling significantly faster charging speeds compared to many competitors in the segment.

While official EPA ratings have not yet been announced, Mercedes-Benz claims the GLB250+ can travel approximately 392 miles under the European WLTP testing cycle. Based on historical differences between WLTP and EPA testing standards, a real-world EPA estimate of around 330 miles appears realistic. The combination of strong range and fast-charging capability should make the GLB EV a practical choice for both daily commuting and long-distance travel. The 800-volt system is expected to deliver shorter charging stops and greater convenience during road trips. Official charging performance figures for the U.S. market will likely be announced closer to launch.
interior:
The GLB-Class EV continues Mercedes-Benz's tradition of creating cabins that feel significantly more expensive than their price points might suggest. Premium materials, elegant design elements, and sophisticated technology create an upscale environment throughout the interior. The front seats appear supportive and comfortable, offering excellent long-distance comfort while maintaining a commanding driving position. Storage solutions are thoughtfully integrated throughout the cabin, improving everyday usability for families and commuters alike. One of the GLB EV's biggest advantages is its spacious interior. Thanks to its tall roofline and upright body design, headroom and passenger space exceed expectations for a compact SUV. Mercedes-Benz has further improved second-row accommodations, making the rear seats even more comfortable for adult passengers.

An optional third-row seating configuration remains available, preserving one of the GLB's most distinctive features.
