Models without the third row provide approximately 19 cubic feet of cargo space behind the second row, while third-row-equipped versions offer around 17 cubic feet. The boxy shape maximizes usable storage volume and improves practicality compared with more style-focused competitors.
technology: Technology plays a central role in the GLB-Class EV experience. Every model comes standard with a 14.0-inch central touchscreen and a 10.3-inch digital instrument cluster running Mercedes-Benz's latest infotainment software. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, integrated navigation, Bluetooth connectivity, and SiriusXM satellite radio. The interface is designed to provide quick access to vehicle functions while maintaining the premium presentation expected from the brand. For buyers seeking a more futuristic environment, the optional Superscreen configuration adds a dedicated 14.0-inch passenger display. This creates a dramatic dashboard-wide digital experience that rivals some of Mercedes-Benz's flagship luxury models. An eight-speaker audio system comes standard, while a premium 16-speaker Burmester sound system is available for those who prioritize audio quality.
safety: Mercedes-Benz equips the GLB-Class EV with a comprehensive suite of standard driver-assistance technologies. Automated emergency braking, adaptive cruise control, and lane-keeping assist are included across the range, helping enhance driver confidence and occupant protection. Buyers who desire more advanced semi-autonomous driving capabilities can opt for the available Drive Assist package. This system adds lane-centering functionality, lane-change assistance, and enhanced adaptive cruise control features designed to reduce driver workload during highway travel. An available self-parking system further enhances convenience in urban environments and tight parking spaces. With both standard and optional safety technologies, the GLB EV is expected to offer one of the most comprehensive driver-assistance packages in the compact luxury EV segment.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None

Mercedes-Benz provides warranty coverage that aligns with most luxury competitors. While the protection is adequate, the absence of complimentary scheduled maintenance remains a disadvantage compared with certain rivals that include free maintenance programs during the ownership period.
pros: Spacious and practical cabin, available third-row seating, impressive projected driving range, fast-charging 800-volt architecture, and advanced technology make the GLB-Class EV one of the most versatile luxury electric SUVs.
cons: Optional features can quickly increase pricing, third-row seating is best suited for children, and some advanced driver-assistance technologies require additional packages.
mn_take: The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLB-Class EV successfully combines luxury, practicality, and modern electric technology, offering one of the most family-friendly and versatile packages in the premium compact EV segment while retaining the everyday usability that has always defined the GLB name.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLB-Class Review
overview:
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLB-Class enters its second generation with a comprehensive redesign, introducing a more modern platform, advanced technology, and a new hybrid powertrain. While it remains one of the smallest SUVs in the Mercedes-Benz lineup, the GLB continues to offer something many rivals cannot: available third-row seating in a compact luxury SUV package.

Its upright proportions, practical cabin, and premium design have always distinguished it from competitors, and the latest model builds upon those strengths. The exterior retains the boxy styling that has made the GLB popular among buyers seeking a more traditional SUV appearance, while the cabin adopts Mercedes-Benz's newest digital-first design philosophy with expansive screen displays and enhanced connectivity features. The addition of a hybrid powertrain reflects Mercedes-Benz's commitment to improving efficiency without sacrificing the luxury experience expected from the brand. For families seeking a premium compact SUV with genuine practicality, the new GLB appears well-positioned to remain one of the segment's most versatile choices.
pricing:
GLB Base – Starting at $45,000 (estimated)
GLB Exclusive – Starting at $47,000 (estimated)
GLB Pinnacle – Starting at $54,000 (estimated)

The Exclusive trim is expected to deliver the best value by balancing luxury features, advanced technology, and pricing. Buyers looking for the full premium experience will likely gravitate toward the Pinnacle model with its expanded technology and comfort equipment.
drivetrain:
Powering the 2027 GLB-Class is a newly developed hybrid system shared with the latest CLA-Class. The setup combines a turbocharged 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine with an electric motor, producing a combined 208 horsepower through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. All-wheel drive is expected to be standard across the lineup. Although the power figures may appear modest compared to some competitors, the electric motor's instant torque should provide responsive acceleration during city driving and low-speed maneuvers. The hybrid system is designed to prioritize efficiency while maintaining the smooth and refined driving characteristics expected from a Mercedes-Benz.

An optional adaptive suspension system adds multiple drive modes that can alter steering, throttle response, and suspension behavior. While official performance testing has not yet been completed, the GLB is expected to continue offering a comfortable and composed driving experience rather than a sport-focused personality. The emphasis remains on daily usability, comfort, and confidence in a variety of driving conditions, making the GLB an appealing choice for families and commuters alike.

Mercedes-Benz has not yet released official fuel economy figures for the redesigned GLB-Class. However, the introduction of the hybrid powertrain should deliver a noticeable improvement in efficiency compared to the outgoing gasoline-powered model. The combination of electric assistance and a downsized turbocharged engine is expected to provide competitive fuel economy within the luxury compact SUV segment while maintaining strong everyday performance. Official EPA estimates are expected closer to launch.
interior:
The cabin of the 2027 GLB-Class represents a significant step forward in technology and design. Mercedes-Benz has created a modern interior environment that blends premium materials with advanced digital interfaces while retaining the practicality that has long been one of the GLB's strongest attributes. The front seats feature supportive cushioning and adjustable thigh supports, making them comfortable for both short commutes and long-distance travel. Mercedes-Benz continues its signature door-mounted seat controls, providing a familiar and intuitive operating experience. The dashboard adopts a minimalist design theme, with clean surfaces and large digital displays dominating the visual landscape. Despite its focus on technology, the interior still delivers the upscale atmosphere buyers expect from a luxury vehicle.

Second-row accommodations remain generous for the segment, offering enough legroom and headroom for adults. Models equipped with the optional third row feature sliding second-row seats that improve flexibility and passenger access.

The available third-row seating remains a unique selling point in this class. While best suited for children or occasional adult use, it provides flexibility that many competitors simply cannot match. Cargo space remains practical, with approximately 19.1 cubic feet available behind the second row. Models equipped with the optional third row sacrifice a small amount of cargo capacity but gain significantly improved passenger versatility.
technology: Technology is one of the biggest highlights of the redesigned GLB-Class. Standard models feature a 14.0-inch central touchscreen paired with a 10.3-inch digital instrument cluster, both running the latest generation of Mercedes-Benz's infotainment software. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with navigation, Bluetooth connectivity, and SiriusXM capability. Buyers seeking a more futuristic experience can opt for the available Superscreen configuration, which adds a third 14.0-inch display for the front passenger. This setup creates a dramatic pillar-to-pillar digital dashboard similar to larger and more expensive Mercedes-Benz models. An eight-speaker audio system comes standard, while audiophiles can upgrade to a premium 16-speaker Burmester surround-sound system that delivers a significantly enhanced listening experience.
safety:
Mercedes-Benz equips the GLB-Class with an extensive suite of standard driver-assistance technologies. Automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control are included across the lineup, providing a strong foundation of active safety systems. For buyers seeking more advanced semi-autonomous functionality, the optional Drive Assist package adds adaptive cruise control with lane-centering capability, lane-change assistance, and additional highway-driving technologies. A self-parking system is also available, helping simplify parking in tight urban environments.

The combination of standard and optional safety technologies positions the GLB among the more advanced offerings in the compact luxury SUV segment.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Hybrid Component Warranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None

Mercedes-Benz provides warranty coverage that is competitive with rivals such as BMW and Audi. The addition of extended hybrid component coverage offers extra peace of mind for buyers transitioning to electrified vehicles. However, unlike some competitors, Mercedes-Benz does not include complimentary scheduled maintenance.
pros: Practical boxy design, available third-row seating, premium cabin quality, advanced technology, and efficient new hybrid powertrain make the GLB-Class one of the most versatile luxury compact SUVs.
cons: Modest horsepower output, advanced driver-assistance features require additional cost, and the third row remains best suited for occasional use.
mn_take: The 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLB-Class successfully blends luxury, technology, efficiency, and practicality into a compact package, and its available third-row seating continues to make it one of the most family-friendly choices in the premium compact SUV segment.

car_name: 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class Review
overview:
The 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class continues to serve as the entry point into the Mercedes-Benz SUV lineup, offering premium styling, a refined cabin, and everyday practicality in a compact package. While many rivals in the subcompact luxury SUV segment focus heavily on sporty handling and aggressive performance, the GLA takes a different approach by prioritizing comfort, sophistication, and ease of use.

Its elegant exterior design, upscale interior materials, and quiet driving manners make it feel more expensive than its size suggests. The turbocharged engine delivers smooth and adequate performance for daily commuting, while the suspension strikes a pleasing balance between comfort and control. Although competitors such as the BMW X1 and Volvo XC40 provide a more engaging driving experience, the GLA remains appealing for buyers who value refinement over outright excitement. For 2026, Mercedes-Benz introduces new appearance-focused packages, including the AMG Lite Plus Package and the Midnight Edition, while also adding a new Sun and Sound package that combines a panoramic sunroof with an upgraded audio system.
pricing:
GLA250 – Starting at $42,850
GLA250 Exclusive – Starting at $44,250 (Recommended)
GLA250 Pinnacle – Starting at $51,450

The GLA250 Exclusive offers the best balance of luxury and value. It adds proximity keyless entry, hands-free liftgate functionality, wireless smartphone charging, parking assistance technology, fingerprint recognition, and customizable ambient lighting. Buyers should also consider adding adaptive cruise control and heated front seats for a more premium ownership experience.
drivetrain:
Powering the GLA250 is a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 221 horsepower, paired with an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Buyers can choose between front-wheel drive and Mercedes-Benz's 4Matic all-wheel-drive system. The powertrain is supported by a 48-volt mild-hybrid system that helps improve responsiveness during initial acceleration while also enhancing efficiency. The turbocharged engine operates quietly and delivers smooth power delivery, making it well suited for urban commuting and highway cruising. Performance is competent rather than thrilling. The GLA250 AWD reaches 60 mph in approximately 6.3 seconds, which is respectable for the segment but falls short of the quicker BMW X1. Nevertheless, the GLA feels refined and composed, with precise steering and predictable handling characteristics. Its suspension effectively absorbs road imperfections, creating a comfortable and relaxed driving experience that aligns with the vehicle's luxury-focused mission.

Efficiency remains one of the GLA-Class's strengths. Front-wheel-drive models are rated at up to 26 mpg city and 34 mpg highway, while all-wheel-drive variants achieve approximately 25 mpg city and 33 mpg highway. These figures place the GLA among the more fuel-efficient luxury SUVs in its class, helping to reduce ownership costs without sacrificing performance or comfort.
interior:
Despite its compact dimensions, the GLA's cabin feels surprisingly spacious and welcoming. Mercedes-Benz has crafted an interior that blends modern design with premium materials, creating an atmosphere that feels appropriately upscale for the brand. Standard leatherette upholstery, carbon-fiber-style trim, and high-quality switchgear give the interior a premium appearance. Buyers seeking additional luxury can upgrade to genuine leather seating surfaces along with aluminum or wood trim accents. The front seats provide excellent comfort for long-distance driving, while visibility and ergonomics are generally well executed. Road and wind noise are well controlled, contributing to the GLA's quiet and refined personality.

Rear-seat passengers benefit from more legroom than many direct competitors, including the Audi Q3, BMW X1, and Volvo XC40. Two adults can comfortably occupy the second row without feeling cramped, making the GLA more practical than its exterior dimensions might suggest. Cargo capacity is competitive for the segment. While it does not lead the class, the low and flat cargo floor simplifies loading and unloading larger items. In testing, the cargo area accommodated six carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats, matching several key competitors.
technology: Technology is a major highlight of the GLA-Class. The dashboard features dual 10.3-inch displays housed beneath a single glass panel, creating a modern and sophisticated appearance. One screen serves as the digital instrument cluster, while the other manages infotainment functions through Mercedes-Benz's MBUX operating system. The interface supports voice commands, touchscreen operation, and steering-wheel controls. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, allowing seamless smartphone integration without cables. Navigation, premium audio systems, and a head-up display are available through optional packages for buyers seeking additional technology features. The optional Burmester sound system significantly enhances the audio experience, while the upgraded ambient lighting system adds a more luxurious atmosphere during nighttime driving.
safety: The GLA-Class offers a solid collection of safety technologies, although some advanced driver-assistance systems remain optional rather than standard. Standard safety equipment includes automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and automatic high-beam assistance. Optional technologies include adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, evasive steering assistance, and additional driver-support features designed to improve highway comfort and accident avoidance. While competitors increasingly include more advanced systems as standard equipment, the available technology on the GLA remains comprehensive when properly equipped.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None

Warranty coverage is consistent with most luxury competitors. However, Mercedes-Benz does not include complimentary scheduled maintenance, an area where brands such as BMW and Volvo offer additional value.
pros: Excellent cabin quality, comfortable ride, premium technology, spacious rear seat, and attractive styling make the GLA-Class a refined luxury SUV for everyday driving.
cons: Several desirable features cost extra, acceleration is merely average, and competitors offer more engaging driving dynamics.
mn_take: The 2026 Mercedes-Benz GLA-Class prioritizes comfort, refinement, and premium ambiance over sporty excitement, making it an excellent choice for buyers seeking a compact luxury SUV that feels sophisticated and effortless to live with every day.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz G580e
overview:
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz G580e represents one of the most ambitious transformations in the luxury SUV segment. Taking one of the most iconic off-road vehicles ever built and converting it into a fully electric machine could have easily diluted the G-Class's legendary character. Instead, Mercedes-Benz has managed to preserve nearly everything enthusiasts love about the G-Wagen while introducing cutting-edge electric technology that enhances its performance both on and off the road.

Visually, the G580e remains unmistakably a G-Class. The upright windshield, flat body panels, exposed hinges, and boxy silhouette continue to give it one of the most recognizable designs in the automotive world. Beneath that familiar shape, however, lies a sophisticated four-motor electric powertrain that transforms the driving experience. The result is a luxury SUV that combines extraordinary off-road capability, impressive straight-line performance, and a level of technological sophistication that few rivals can match. Although its driving range falls short of some newer luxury EV competitors, the G580e delivers something many electric SUVs cannot: authentic off-road capability backed by decades of G-Class heritage. It remains a status symbol, a luxury vehicle, and a serious trail machine all at once.
pricing: G580e — Starting at approximately $165,000
drivetrain:
The heart of the G580e is one of the most advanced electric powertrains currently available in a production SUV. Instead of using one or two electric motors, Mercedes-Benz equips the G580e with four individual electric motors, one dedicated to each wheel. Combined output stands at an impressive 579 horsepower and a massive 859 lb-ft of torque. This unique setup allows Mercedes-Benz to control each wheel independently, unlocking capabilities that are impossible in conventional SUVs. One of the most talked-about features is G-Turn, which allows the vehicle to perform a complete 360-degree rotation within its own footprint by spinning the wheels on opposite sides in different directions. While it may initially seem like a novelty, the technology demonstrates the remarkable precision of the vehicle's power distribution system.

Another innovation is G-Steering, which adjusts power delivery between individual motors to reduce the turning radius during challenging off-road situations. Combined with virtual differential locks, advanced torque vectoring, and dedicated off-road driving modes, the G580e delivers a level of trail capability that few electric vehicles can approach.

On the road, the instant torque of the electric motors makes the G580e feel considerably quicker than the gasoline-powered G550. Acceleration is immediate and effortless, with the SUV reaching 60 mph in just 4.1 seconds. Despite its substantial weight, the G580e feels responsive and remarkably maneuverable. The familiar commanding driving position remains, but the silent operation and smooth power delivery create a distinctly modern driving experience. Mercedes-Benz has also retained the ladder-frame chassis architecture that has long defined the G-Class. Combined with an independent front suspension and solid rear axle, the setup preserves the rugged durability expected from a true G-Wagen while benefiting from the precision offered by electric propulsion.

The G580e utilizes a substantial 116.0-kWh battery pack integrated into the vehicle's frame. According to EPA estimates, the electric SUV can travel approximately 239 miles on a full charge. While this figure is respectable for a heavy off-road-focused luxury SUV, it falls short of many premium electric competitors that now comfortably exceed 300 miles of range. Real-world highway testing has highlighted this limitation even further. During independent testing, the G580e achieved approximately 160 miles of range at sustained highway speeds, which may concern buyers planning frequent long-distance travel. Charging performance is more competitive. The G580e supports DC fast charging at rates up to 200 kW, allowing the battery to recharge from 10 percent to 80 percent in roughly 32 minutes under ideal conditions. Mercedes-Benz has also incorporated extensive underbody protection for the battery pack, ensuring the vehicle can tackle demanding off-road terrain without risking damage to critical electrical components.
interior:
Inside, the G580e retains the premium atmosphere that has made the G-Class one of the most desirable luxury SUVs on the market. High-quality Nappa leather upholstery, meticulously crafted materials, and customizable ambient lighting create an environment that feels both luxurious and contemporary. The upright dashboard design and elevated seating position provide an excellent view of the road ahead while reinforcing the commanding character that G-Class owners have come to expect. The front seats offer exceptional comfort for long journeys and can be equipped with Mercedes-Benz's Active Multicontour Seat Plus package, which adds massage functions and adjustable bolsters designed to improve support during off-road driving. Rear-seat accommodations are comfortable, although they do not provide the expansive space found in larger luxury SUVs such as the Mercedes-Benz GLS. Nevertheless, passenger comfort remains impressive, and material quality throughout the cabin is consistently excellent.

One compromise of the electric powertrain is cargo capacity. The packaging requirements of the battery system and rear electric motors reduce available cargo space compared with the gasoline-powered G550. The G580e offers 19.6 cubic feet of cargo volume behind the rear seats, significantly less than the conventional model, although still adequate for everyday luxury SUV duties.
technology:
Technology plays a major role in the G580e experience. The dashboard is dominated by dual 12.3-inch displays that serve as both the digital instrument cluster and infotainment touchscreen. Mercedes-Benz's latest MBUX software powers the system, offering crisp graphics, quick responses, and a wide range of customization options. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, while the integrated navigation system includes augmented-reality functionality designed to improve route guidance. Voice recognition technology has also been enhanced, allowing drivers to control numerous vehicle functions using natural language commands.

A unique Offroad Cockpit interface provides detailed off-road information, including steering angles, vehicle pitch and roll, altitude measurements, tire pressures, and other useful data. The system reinforces the G580e's serious off-road intentions while showcasing the advantages of its sophisticated electric architecture. The standard Burmester premium audio system with Dolby Atmos technology delivers outstanding sound quality and further elevates the luxury experience.
safety: Mercedes-Benz equips the G580e with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance systems. Standard safety technologies include automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control with lane-centering capability, lane-keeping assist, traffic-sign recognition, and self-parking functionality. These systems work seamlessly to improve convenience and safety during both urban commuting and long-distance highway travel. The inclusion of advanced semi-autonomous driving features helps ensure the G580e remains competitive with other flagship luxury electric SUVs.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Battery Warranty: 10 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None
pros: Innovative four-motor electric powertrain, exceptional off-road capability, rapid acceleration, luxurious interior, and unique G-Turn technology.
cons: Driving range trails many premium EV rivals, cargo capacity is reduced compared with the gasoline G-Class, and the purchase price is extremely high.
mn_take: The 2027 Mercedes-Benz G580e successfully electrifies one of the automotive world's most iconic SUVs without sacrificing its legendary character, delivering extraordinary off-road capability, cutting-edge technology, and unmistakable presence in a package that feels both futuristic and authentically G-Class.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz G-Class Review
overview: The 2027 Mercedes-Benz G-Class remains one of the most recognizable luxury SUVs ever built. Despite countless competitors attempting to replicate its formula, the G-Wagen continues to stand alone with its iconic boxy styling, military-inspired heritage, and genuine off-road capability. Unlike many luxury SUVs that merely look rugged, the G-Class combines handcrafted luxury with serious trail-conquering hardware, making it equally comfortable outside a five-star hotel or on a remote mountain trail. For 2027, Mercedes-Benz keeps changes minimal, which is hardly surprising given the G-Class's enduring popularity. Beneath its unmistakable silhouette lies a modern turbocharged and supercharged inline-six engine supported by a 48-volt mild-hybrid system, delivering strong performance while maintaining the refinement expected from a vehicle carrying a six-figure price tag. The result is a luxury SUV that remains as desirable as ever, even if practicality and efficiency are not among its strongest attributes.
pricing:
G550 — Starting at approximately $156,000
G550 Exclusive — Starting at approximately $161,000
G550 Manufaktur — Starting at approximately $165,000
G550 Exclusive Plus — Starting at approximately $168,000
G550 Manufaktur Plus — Starting at approximately $169,000
G550 G Professional — Starting at approximately $170,000

The standard G550 offers more luxury and technology than many flagship SUVs, making it the sweet spot in the lineup. Buyers can then personalize their vehicle extensively through Mercedes' Exclusive and Manufaktur programs, creating a virtually unique G-Class tailored to individual tastes.
drivetrain:
Under the hood of every 2027 G550 is a turbocharged and supercharged 3.0-liter inline-six engine producing 443 horsepower. Mercedes pairs the engine with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system that helps improve low-end response while smoothing power delivery. A nine-speed automatic transmission and permanent all-wheel drive come standard. While some enthusiasts may miss the characterful V-8 previously available in standard G-Class models, the new electrified six-cylinder delivers impressive performance. Power arrives smoothly and effortlessly, helping the nearly three-ton SUV accelerate with surprising urgency. Mercedes estimates a 0-60 mph time of approximately 5.0 seconds, which is remarkably quick for a vehicle with the aerodynamic profile of a luxury apartment building.

Off-road capability remains among the best in the luxury SUV segment. The G-Class retains its legendary trio of locking differentials, low-range transfer case, and rugged body-on-frame construction. Few luxury SUVs can match its ability to crawl over rocks, tackle deep mud, or navigate steep terrain while maintaining a premium driving experience. On paved roads, the G-Class feels far more refined than its rugged origins would suggest. The steering is more precise than previous generations, highway stability is excellent, and ride quality has improved significantly. Nevertheless, buyers should remember that the G-Class prioritizes character and capability over sports-car-like agility.

Fuel economy remains one of the G-Class's biggest compromises.

The EPA estimates:
- 17 mpg city
- 19 mpg highway
- 18 mpg combined
While the mild-hybrid system improves efficiency compared to older V-8-powered versions, the vehicle's substantial weight, upright design, and permanent four-wheel-drive system inevitably impact fuel consumption.
interior:
The interior of the 2027 G-Class perfectly balances rugged heritage with modern luxury. Every surface feels solid, expensive, and carefully assembled, creating an environment that immediately communicates quality. Premium leather upholstery, metal accents, and customizable trim options allow buyers to tailor the cabin to their preferences, while Mercedes-Benz's attention to detail ensures that every journey feels special. The front seats are exceptionally comfortable and offer excellent support for both daily commuting and long-distance touring. Heated seats come standard, while optional ventilation and massage functions further enhance comfort. The commanding seating position provides excellent outward visibility and reinforces the vehicle's sense of authority on the road.

Rear passengers benefit from generous headroom thanks to the G-Class's upright design, but legroom is somewhat tighter than expected for a vehicle of this size and price. Competitors such as the Cadillac Escalade and Mercedes-Benz GLS offer more spacious rear accommodations. Nevertheless, the rear cabin remains luxurious and well-appointed, with premium materials and available entertainment features. Cargo space is another strength. The large rear cargo area can accommodate substantial luggage, sports equipment, or shopping loads, making the G-Class more practical than its fashion-icon reputation might suggest.
technology:
Mercedes-Benz equips the 2027 G-Class with a sophisticated infotainment system centered around a 12.3-inch touchscreen running the latest generation of MBUX software. The interface is responsive and visually impressive, offering seamless access to navigation, entertainment, vehicle settings, and connected services. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, allowing effortless smartphone integration without cables. Navigation functionality is comprehensive, while voice-command technology enables drivers to control various systems using natural language commands. An 18-speaker Burmester premium audio system with Dolby Atmos processing delivers exceptional sound quality, transforming the cabin into a mobile concert hall.

The technology package strikes an effective balance between modern functionality and ease of use, ensuring that the G-Class remains competitive with newer luxury SUVs while preserving its distinctive personality.
safety: The 2027 G-Class comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance both safety and convenience. Mercedes-Benz includes adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, lane-keeping assist, parking assistance, and a 360-degree camera system as standard equipment. These systems work together to make the large SUV easier to maneuver in urban environments while also improving confidence during highway travel. An optional trailer-maneuvering assist system is available for buyers who plan to take advantage of the G-Class's impressive towing capability. While official crash-test ratings may vary by market, the G-Class benefits from extensive active and passive safety technologies expected in a flagship luxury SUV.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None
pros: Timeless design, genuine off-road capability, exceptional build quality, luxurious interior, and virtually endless customization possibilities.
cons: Extremely expensive, rear-seat legroom trails some rivals, fuel economy remains poor, and the vehicle attracts constant attention.
mn_take: The 2027 Mercedes-Benz G-Class remains one of the most desirable SUVs ever created, combining authentic off-road capability, unmatched road presence, and handcrafted luxury into a package that continues to define the modern ultra-premium SUV segment.

car_name: 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV
overview:
The 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV represents the pinnacle of the brand’s electric SUV lineup, blending ultra-luxury comfort with cutting-edge EV technology in a spacious family-focused package. Positioned above the smaller EQE SUV, the EQS SUV focuses less on sporty dynamics and more on delivering a serene, first-class travel experience for up to seven passengers. Its smooth ride quality, whisper-quiet cabin, and lavish interior materials create an atmosphere that feels unmistakably flagship Mercedes-Benz.

For 2026, Mercedes-Benz simplifies the lineup by replacing the previous EQS450 and EQS580 naming structure with the EQS400 and EQS550 badges, while also enhancing standard equipment. Every model now includes a NACS adapter for access to Tesla Supercharger stations, along with upgraded second-row amenities such as heated seats, wireless charging, luxurious headrests, and rear side airbags.

Despite its impressive refinement and strong technology suite, the EQS SUV still faces stiff competition from newer rivals like the Lucid Gravity, BMW iX, and Rivian R1S, many of which offer sharper driving dynamics or more distinctive styling. Still, for buyers prioritizing comfort, luxury, and effortless long-distance cruising, the EQS SUV remains one of the most sophisticated electric SUVs on the market.
pricing:
EQS400 4Matic — $91,300
EQS400 Exclusive — $95,200
EQS400 Pinnacle — $99,450
EQS550 4Matic — $113,800
EQS550 Exclusive — $116,350
EQS550 Pinnacle — $120,600

The EQS400 Exclusive trim offers the best value in the lineup, adding desirable luxury features such as massaging front seats, enhanced ambient lighting, head-up display, and Mercedes-Benz’s Air Balance fragrance system without pushing pricing into six-figure territory too aggressively.
drivetrain:
The 2026 EQS SUV is powered exclusively by dual-motor all-wheel-drive configurations. The EQS400 4Matic produces 355 horsepower and 590 lb-ft of torque, while the more powerful EQS550 4Matic generates an impressive 536 horsepower and 633 lb-ft of torque. Acceleration is strong for a luxury SUV of this size. The EQS400 reaches 60 mph in approximately 5.2 seconds, while the EQS550 cuts that figure down to just 4.0 seconds. Although those numbers are undeniably quick, the EQS SUV prioritizes smoothness and refinement over aggressive driving engagement.

Mercedes-Benz equips every EQS SUV with adaptive air suspension and rear-axle steering as standard, helping the large SUV feel surprisingly maneuverable in urban environments. The rear-wheel steering system significantly reduces the turning radius, making parking and low-speed navigation easier than expected for a vehicle of this size.

Ride comfort is among the EQS SUV’s greatest strengths. The suspension absorbs road imperfections with exceptional composure, maintaining a soft and isolated driving character that suits long highway journeys perfectly. Steering feedback, however, is limited, and despite its capable handling, the EQS SUV never feels particularly sporty or emotionally engaging from behind the wheel. An Off-Road driving mode is also available, raising the suspension and adjusting power delivery for light trail use, though most owners are unlikely to venture far beyond paved roads.

The EQS SUV uses a large 118-kWh battery pack that delivers competitive driving range figures for the luxury EV segment.

The EQS400 4Matic is EPA-rated for up to 312 miles of range, while the more powerful EQS550 4Matic slightly improves that figure to 317 miles. Real-world highway testing has shown both versions achieving approximately 290 miles during sustained high-speed driving conditions. DC fast-charging capability reaches up to 200 kW, allowing the battery to charge from 10 to 80 percent in roughly 30 minutes under ideal conditions. Mercedes-Benz also includes a standard NACS charging adapter for 2026, giving drivers access to Tesla’s extensive Supercharger network and greatly improving charging convenience across North America.

While the range figures are respectable, competitors like the Lucid Gravity and certain trims of the Cadillac Lyriq still offer more impressive efficiency and overall range performance.

The EPA estimates the EQS400 4Matic at 80 MPGe city and 78 MPGe highway, while the EQS550 achieves 82 MPGe city and 78 MPGe highway. In real-world highway testing, previous EQS SUV variants returned between 78 and 83 MPGe, which is solid for a large three-row luxury EV but no longer class-leading within this rapidly evolving segment.
interior:
The EQS SUV’s cabin is unquestionably one of the most luxurious interiors currently offered in an electric SUV. High-end materials, excellent fit and finish, expansive ambient lighting, and sophisticated design elements give the interior a truly premium atmosphere. The front seats are exceptionally comfortable and come standard with heating, ventilation, leather upholstery, and extensive power adjustment. Higher trims add massage functionality and even more upscale interior detailing.

The second row is equally impressive, offering generous legroom, heated seating, wireless phone charging, and plush headrests designed for maximum passenger comfort. An optional third row expands seating capacity to seven passengers, though the sloping roofline slightly compromises headroom for adults in the rear-most seats. Cargo space is competitive for the segment. Two-row models provide 31 cubic feet of storage behind the second row, while folding the rear seats dramatically expands hauling capability. The floating center console also creates additional storage compartments throughout the cabin.

Overall cabin refinement is outstanding. Road noise, wind noise, and vibration are exceptionally well controlled, creating an almost lounge-like driving environment during long journeys.
technology:
Technology is one of the EQS SUV’s headline features. Dominating the dashboard is Mercedes-Benz’s massive 56-inch Hyperscreen setup, which integrates a digital instrument cluster, a 17.7-inch central touchscreen, and a dedicated 12.3-inch passenger display beneath a single glass surface. The visual presentation is undeniably futuristic and dramatic, immediately giving the cabin a flagship-level wow factor. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with wireless charging and a premium 15-speaker Burmester audio system.

Mercedes-Benz’s MBUX infotainment software remains feature-rich and visually impressive, though the heavy reliance on touchscreen controls can occasionally feel distracting while driving. The near-complete absence of physical buttons may frustrate users who prefer tactile controls for common functions. Still, the EQS SUV remains among the most technologically advanced luxury SUVs currently available.
safety:
Mercedes-Benz equips the EQS SUV with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance technologies as standard.

Key safety features include:

Adaptive cruise control
Automated emergency braking
Blind-spot monitoring
Lane-keeping assist
Automatic high-beam headlights
Self-parking functionality

Additional advanced systems, including enhanced parking assistance and evasive steering support, are also available depending on trim and package selection.
warranty:
Limited warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles
Powertrain warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles
Battery warranty: 10 years or 155,000 miles
Complimentary maintenance: None

While warranty coverage is competitive within the luxury EV segment, rivals like BMW still offer complimentary scheduled maintenance, something Mercedes-Benz continues to omit.
pros: Exceptionally luxurious cabin, superb ride comfort, advanced technology suite, strong real-world range, spacious three-row practicality.
cons: Styling remains polarizing, touchscreen-heavy controls reduce usability, lacks engaging driving dynamics, expensive in higher trims.
mn_take: The 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV excels as a serene, ultra-luxurious electric family cruiser, prioritizing comfort, refinement, and technology over driving excitement, making it ideal for buyers seeking effortless premium EV travel rather than sporty engagement.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQE SUV
overview:
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQE SUV represents the brand’s attempt to blend traditional Mercedes luxury with the rapidly evolving premium electric SUV segment. Positioned beneath the larger EQS SUV, the EQE SUV focuses on delivering a serene, luxurious, and technologically advanced driving experience rather than aggressive performance or sporty character.

Inside, the EQE SUV feels unmistakably premium, with rich materials, elegant ambient lighting, supportive seating, and an exceptionally quiet cabin environment that makes long-distance travel relaxing and refined. Mercedes has clearly prioritized comfort and isolation, giving the EQE SUV a smooth and plush personality that aligns closely with the brand’s luxury heritage.

The EQE SUV is offered in two primary variants: the rear-wheel-drive EQE320+ and the dual-motor all-wheel-drive EQE320 4Matic. Both models receive increased power for 2027, though the EQE SUV still leans more toward comfort-oriented cruising than enthusiastic driving dynamics.

While its maximum driving range exceeds 300 miles in rear-wheel-drive form, several newer EV rivals such as the Lucid Gravity and Rivian R1S now surpass it in outright range capability and driving engagement. The EQE SUV succeeds best as a luxurious electric cruiser rather than a performance-focused electric SUV.
pricing:
EQE320+: $67,000 (est.)
EQE320 4Matic: $69,000 (est.)
Recommended: EQE320+ Exclusive: $70,000 (est.)
EQE320 4Matic Exclusive: $73,000 (est.)
drivetrain:
The 2027 EQE SUV lineup consists of two configurations, both producing 315 horsepower but offering different drivetrain layouts and torque characteristics.

The EQE320+ uses a single rear-mounted electric motor driving the rear wheels, while the EQE320 4Matic adds a second motor to enable all-wheel drive. Although horsepower remains identical between the two variants, the dual-motor model generates substantially more torque at 564 pound-feet compared to 416 pound-feet in the rear-drive model. Acceleration feels smooth and immediate, particularly in city driving where electric torque delivery provides effortless responsiveness. Even the base rear-wheel-drive version feels adequately quick for daily driving and highway merging duties.

Mercedes offers an optional adjustable air suspension capable of raising ride height for added versatility. However, while the air suspension improves body control, it also introduces a firmer ride over rough pavement compared to the standard steel-spring setup. The available rear-axle steering system improves maneuverability in urban settings while helping the SUV feel more stable at higher speeds. Still, despite these technologies, the EQE SUV prioritizes comfort over sporty handling. Steering feedback remains muted, and the overall driving experience lacks the engagement found in rivals like the BMW iX or Porsche Macan Electric. The EQE SUV also supports one-pedal driving functionality, allowing drivers to maximize regenerative braking and minimize use of the brake pedal in daily traffic situations.

The rear-wheel-drive EQE320+ reaches 60 mph in approximately 5.7 seconds according to testing. The dual-motor EQE320 4Matic is expected to deliver quicker acceleration thanks to its substantial torque advantage and added traction from all-wheel drive. While those figures are respectable for a luxury SUV, several competing electric SUVs now offer considerably quicker acceleration and more engaging performance characteristics.

The EQE SUV offers a maximum towing capacity of 3,500 pounds, which is sufficient for small utility trailers, light recreational equipment, or compact campers. However, buyers requiring serious towing capability may find alternatives like the Porsche Cayenne Electric or Rivian R1S more suitable.

Range remains one of the stronger aspects of the EQE SUV lineup, especially in rear-wheel-drive form.

The EQE320+ utilizes a 96.0-kWh battery pack and delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 302 miles on a full charge. The all-wheel-drive EQE320 4Matic uses a slightly smaller 90.5-kWh battery pack and offers up to 253 miles of range. Interestingly, real-world highway testing showed the EQE320 4Matic outperforming its EPA estimate by achieving approximately 260 miles during highway driving. Charging performance is competitive for the segment. Mercedes claims the EQE SUV can replenish battery charge from 10 to 80 percent in approximately 32 minutes using a DC fast charger. Real-world testing achieved a 10-to-90 percent charge in roughly 43 minutes. While respectable, these numbers no longer lead the luxury EV segment, where several rivals now offer both longer range and faster charging capabilities.

The rear-wheel-drive EQE320+ is the most efficient model in the lineup, earning EPA estimates of 98 MPGe city, 87 MPGe highway, and 93 MPGe combined. The dual-motor EQE320 4Matic sacrifices some efficiency due to its added performance and traction advantages, returning EPA estimates of 84 MPGe city and 78 MPGe highway. In real-world highway testing, the 4Matic model performed impressively by achieving 90 MPGe at sustained highway speeds.
interior:
The EQE SUV’s interior is among its strongest selling points. The cabin feels richly assembled, exceptionally quiet, and unmistakably luxurious. Even the standard synthetic leather upholstery delivers a convincingly premium appearance and feel, while optional genuine leather further elevates the experience. Heated front seats come standard, and buyers can add ventilation and massage functions for greater comfort. The cabin design embraces Mercedes’ futuristic aesthetic, highlighted by expansive digital displays, flowing ambient lighting, and elegant trim finishes.

Rear-seat space is generous for most adults, and the flat-floor EV platform helps maximize passenger comfort. Cargo space is competitive for the segment, though still noticeably smaller than the gasoline-powered Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class. In testing, the EQE SUV accommodated seven carry-on bags behind the rear seats and up to 21 with the second row folded flat. Despite its sleek roofline and rounded styling, the EQE SUV remains practical enough for family and road-trip duties.
technology:
Technology is a centerpiece of the EQE SUV experience. A large 12.8-inch touchscreen dominates the dashboard and operates Mercedes’ latest MBUX infotainment software. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with wireless charging, integrated navigation, voice-command functionality, and a Burmester audio system. Buyers seeking an even more futuristic cabin can opt for Mercedes’ Hyperscreen setup, which places multiple displays beneath one continuous glass panel spanning the width of the dashboard. This system combines a 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster, a 17.7-inch infotainment screen, and an additional passenger-side display.

While visually impressive, some of the touch-sensitive steering-wheel controls and menu structures can feel overly complicated during everyday use.
safety: Mercedes equips the EQE SUV with a broad suite of standard safety and driver-assistance technologies. Standard features include automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keeping assist. More advanced systems such as adaptive cruise control, evasive-steering assist, and enhanced semi-autonomous driving functions are bundled into higher trims like the Exclusive package. The EQE SUV continues Mercedes-Benz’s strong reputation for occupant safety and advanced driver-assistance technology.

pros: Exceptionally quiet cabin, luxurious interior materials, plush ride quality, and impressive highway comfort make the EQE SUV a superb long-distance cruiser.
cons: Bland exterior styling, uninspiring driving dynamics, shorter range than some newer EV rivals, and adaptive cruise control not being standard hurt overall value.
mn_take: The 2027 Mercedes-Benz EQE SUV delivers the serene luxury and comfort expected from a modern Mercedes EV, but while it excels as a refined electric cruiser, rivals now outperform it in driving excitement, range, and overall innovation.

car_name: 2027 Mercedes-Benz S-Class
overview:
The 2027 Mercedes-Benz S-Class continues its long-standing legacy as the benchmark for full-size luxury sedans. For decades, the S-Class has represented the pinnacle of Mercedes-Benz engineering, combining timeless styling, cutting-edge technology, exceptional ride comfort, and effortless performance into one cohesive package. The 2027 model refines that formula even further with updated powertrains, enhanced rear-wheel steering technology, and a dramatic new dash-spanning infotainment interface.

Unlike many modern luxury cars that chase aggressive styling or overt flashiness, the S-Class remains understated and dignified. Its proportions are elegant, its presence commanding, and its attention to detail extraordinary. Whether chauffeuring executives or serving as a high-speed grand tourer, the S-Class continues to excel in virtually every environment. Mercedes offers three distinct powertrains for 2027, including a turbocharged inline-six, a twin-turbocharged V-8, and a plug-in hybrid variant. All models come standard with all-wheel drive, a nine-speed automatic transmission, and adaptive air suspension technology designed to isolate passengers from rough road surfaces with remarkable sophistication.

The S-Class remains one of the finest expressions of traditional automotive luxury, blending advanced technology with comfort and refinement in a way few rivals can truly match.
pricing:
S500: $122,000 (est.)
Recommended: S580: $133,000 (est.)
S580e Plug-In Hybrid: $133,500 (est.)
drivetrain:
The 2027 S-Class lineup offers three highly refined powertrains, each designed to deliver effortless acceleration and silky-smooth operation.

The S500 uses a turbocharged and supercharged 3.0-liter inline-six producing 443 horsepower. Mercedes has further refined this engine for 2027, improving both responsiveness and smoothness. An overboost function temporarily increases torque output during hard acceleration, helping the large luxury sedan feel surprisingly energetic.

The S580 elevates the experience with a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 producing 530 horsepower. This engine receives substantial updates for 2027, including a revised flat-plane crankshaft, optimized intake and exhaust systems, and improved turbocharger components. The result is stronger performance combined with exceptional refinement and effortless highway cruising power.

At the top sits the S580e plug-in hybrid, which combines the inline-six engine with an electric motor for a combined 577 horsepower. This model delivers impressive acceleration while also offering meaningful electric-only driving capability for daily commuting.

Every S-Class model utilizes a 48-volt mild-hybrid system that assists with energy recuperation, smoother engine operation, and additional low-end torque support. A nine-speed automatic transmission comes standard across the lineup and works seamlessly with the engines to provide virtually imperceptible gear changes.

Ride quality remains one of the S-Class’s defining strengths. The adaptive air suspension and new intelligent iDamping system constantly adjust based on road conditions using cloud-based data from other Mercedes vehicles. The result is an exceptionally composed and isolated driving experience that feels almost detached from rough pavement. Despite its size, the S-Class remains remarkably manageable thanks to standard rear-wheel steering. Buyers can also opt for a more advanced system capable of turning the rear wheels up to 10 degrees, dramatically improving low-speed maneuverability and parking ease.

Mercedes estimates the S500 will accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in approximately 4.3 seconds, while the more powerful S580 lowers that figure to around 3.9 seconds. Those figures are extremely impressive considering the S-Class prioritizes comfort and refinement over outright sportiness. Acceleration is delivered with remarkable smoothness and composure rather than aggression. The plug-in hybrid S580e is also expected to provide strong straight-line performance while offering additional electric driving flexibility.

The S580e plug-in hybrid continues to offer meaningful electric-only capability for a luxury sedan of this size. While official 2027 EPA estimates have not yet been released, the outgoing version offered up to 48 miles of electric range. In real-world testing, previous S580e models achieved approximately 58 miles of electric driving range under favorable conditions. This setup allows many owners to complete short daily commutes entirely on electric power while retaining the long-distance convenience and effortless cruising ability of a gasoline-powered luxury sedan.

Official EPA fuel economy ratings for the 2027 model have not yet been finalized, though previous versions of the S500 achieved approximately 20 mpg city and 29 mpg highway. The more powerful V-8-powered S580 naturally sacrifices some efficiency in exchange for additional performance and refinement. The S580e plug-in hybrid will likely remain the most efficient model in the lineup for buyers who regularly recharge the battery and maximize electric driving.
interior:
The S-Class cabin remains one of the most luxurious automotive interiors currently available. Every surface, material, and control feels meticulously engineered and carefully assembled. Front passengers are treated to heated, ventilated, and massaging seats with available heated seatbelts and advanced comfort functions designed to reduce fatigue during long journeys. The updated center console incorporates new wood trim designs, dual wireless charging pads, illuminated cupholders, and additional premium detailing.

Rear-seat passengers enjoy limousine-like comfort, particularly in higher-end configurations. Mercedes offers executive rear seating with reclining functions, an ottoman, folding work tables, wireless charging, USB-C connectivity, and integrated rear entertainment displays featuring built-in cameras for video conferencing. The S-Class creates an environment that feels more like a luxury lounge than a conventional automobile. Cargo space remains respectable for the segment and should continue offering approximately 13 cubic feet of trunk capacity.
technology:
Technology receives a major upgrade for 2027 with the introduction of Mercedes’ new full-width dashboard screen setup. The system combines a 14.4-inch central touchscreen, a 12.3-inch passenger display, and a digital instrument cluster into one dramatic high-tech layout. The latest fourth-generation MBUX software powers the system, bringing improved responsiveness, enhanced voice controls, and expanded customization options. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with dual wireless phone charging pads and high-speed USB-C charging ports.

Audiophiles can opt for an available 39-speaker Burmester sound system designed to create a truly immersive listening experience. While visually impressive, the abundance of digital displays somewhat reduces the traditional elegance that older S-Class interiors were famous for. Certain steering-wheel touch controls also require a learning period due to their complexity.
safety:
Mercedes equips every S-Class with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance and occupant-protection technologies. Standard systems include automated emergency braking, adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go capability, lane-keeping assist, and lane-departure warning. The S-Class also offers advanced innovations such as rear-seat airbags and an active suspension system capable of raising the vehicle during certain side-impact scenarios to reduce occupant injury risk.

Few vehicles in the world combine luxury and safety technology as comprehensively as the S-Class.
warranty:

pros: Timeless luxury design, exceptionally refined powertrains, world-class ride comfort, and one of the finest interiors in the automotive industry.
cons: Massive digital screens reduce traditional cabin elegance, steering-wheel controls can feel overly complicated, and warranty coverage trails some rivals.
mn_take: The 2027 Mercedes-Benz S-Class remains the gold standard for luxury sedans, delivering unmatched comfort, refinement, technology, and prestige in a package that continues to define what a flagship luxury automobile should feel like.

car_name: 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQE
overview:
The 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQE represents the brand’s attempt to bring traditional Mercedes luxury into the rapidly evolving electric sedan segment. Positioned below the flagship EQS, the EQE focuses heavily on comfort, cabin refinement, and quietness rather than outright sportiness or dramatic styling. It delivers a smooth and isolated driving experience, wrapped inside a highly aerodynamic body designed to maximize efficiency and range.

While the EQE succeeds in many traditional luxury-car areas, it faces extremely tough competition from rivals such as the Lucid Air, BMW i5, Porsche Taycan, and Audi e-tron GT. Many competitors offer sharper driving dynamics, stronger performance, or more emotionally appealing designs. The EQE instead leans into relaxed cruising comfort and futuristic technology.

Its rounded “one-bow” design may divide opinions, but the slippery shape helps improve efficiency and contributes to the car’s impressive highway refinement. Inside, however, the EQE feels every bit like a modern Mercedes-Benz, featuring high-end materials, advanced digital displays, plush seating, and one of the quietest cabins in the class. For buyers prioritizing comfort, luxury, and electric refinement over aggressive performance, the EQE remains a compelling premium EV sedan.
pricing:
EQE320+: $66,300
EQE320 4Matic: $68,800
Recommended: EQE320+ Exclusive: $69,600
EQE320 4Matic Exclusive: $72,100
EQE320+ Pinnacle: $72,100
EQE320 4Matic Pinnacle: $74,600
drivetrain:
The 2026 EQE lineup consists of two primary variants. The EQE320+ uses a single electric motor driving the rear wheels, while the EQE320 4Matic adds a second motor for all-wheel drive. Both versions produce 315 horsepower, though the dual-motor model benefits from a significant increase in torque. The EQE is tuned primarily for comfort and serenity rather than aggressive performance. Acceleration feels smooth and immediate, as expected from an electric vehicle, but the overall driving character remains calm and composed rather than thrilling. Mercedes prioritizes ride quality above all else, and the EQE excels in this regard.

Optional adaptive air suspension further enhances the experience, helping the sedan glide over rough pavement with impressive isolation. Cabin quietness is exceptional, reinforcing the luxurious atmosphere during highway cruising and urban commuting alike. Despite optional rear-wheel steering and sophisticated chassis technologies, the EQE lacks the dynamic engagement offered by rivals like the BMW i5 or Porsche Taycan. Steering feedback is minimal, and the overall handling experience feels detached from the road. It is competent and stable, but not particularly entertaining for enthusiastic drivers. Still, for buyers who value smoothness and effortless luxury over sportiness, the EQE delivers exactly the kind of relaxed electric driving experience Mercedes intended.

The previous EQE350 4Matic accelerated from 0 to 60 mph in 5.3 seconds, making the EQE respectably quick by traditional luxury sedan standards. However, in the modern luxury EV segment, those numbers are relatively modest. Competitors such as the Lucid Air and several Tesla models deliver substantially quicker acceleration. The EQE focuses more on refinement and comfort than neck-snapping performance.

Range remains one of the EQE’s strongest qualities. The rear-wheel-drive EQE320+ delivers an EPA-estimated range of up to 308 miles on a full charge, making it highly competitive for long-distance travel. The all-wheel-drive EQE320 4Matic offers a lower but still respectable estimated range of 267 miles. Mercedes equips the EQE with fast-charging capability up to 170 kW. Under ideal conditions, the battery can recharge from 10 to 80 percent in slightly over 30 minutes using a DC fast charger. For home charging, the EQE requires roughly 11 hours on a Level 2 charger depending on the configuration. The addition of a standard NACS adapter for 2026 improves charging convenience and broadens compatibility with charging infrastructure.

The EQE performs well in official efficiency testing, particularly in rear-wheel-drive form. EPA estimates rate the EQE320+ at up to 94 MPGe city and 94 MPGe highway, while the all-wheel-drive 4Matic model achieves slightly lower ratings. Real-world highway efficiency, however, can vary noticeably. During testing, previous all-wheel-drive EQE models returned lower real-world figures than their official EPA estimates, particularly during sustained high-speed driving. Nonetheless, the EQE remains a relatively efficient luxury EV considering its size, comfort orientation, and weight.
interior:
The EQE’s interior is unquestionably one of its strongest attributes. The cabin feels rich, modern, and beautifully assembled, with high-quality materials covering nearly every surface. The front seats are exceptionally comfortable and supportive, making the EQE an excellent long-distance touring sedan. Heating comes standard, while ventilation and massage functions are available for buyers seeking maximum luxury. Mercedes also gives the EQE a panoramic glass roof as standard equipment, helping the cabin feel open and airy.

Rear-seat accommodations are surprisingly spacious thanks to the dedicated EV platform, which allows for efficient packaging and improved legroom. Cargo capacity is adequate rather than class-leading, but the sedan offers practical cabin storage solutions and a useful center-console pass-through Compartment. Overall, the EQE delivers the kind of premium cabin ambiance expected from a modern Mercedes-Benz luxury vehicle.
technology:
Technology is a major focal point inside the EQE. Standard models feature a large 12.8-inch central touchscreen running Mercedes’ MBUX infotainment system alongside a digital instrument cluster. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, voice controls, navigation, and biometric profile recognition via fingerprint scanning. For buyers seeking a more futuristic appearance, Mercedes offers the optional Hyperscreen setup, which combines multiple displays beneath a single continuous glass panel stretching across the dashboard. This setup includes a dedicated passenger display and creates one of the most visually dramatic interiors in the segment.

While visually impressive, the infotainment interface can occasionally feel overly complex, with certain functions buried within menus that require extra attention from the driver.
safety: The EQE includes a solid range of standard safety and driver-assistance systems designed to support comfortable daily driving and highway cruising. Standard features include automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keeping assist. Optional systems include adaptive cruise control, evasive steering assistance, and more advanced semi-autonomous driving technologies. Mercedes continues to place strong emphasis on occupant protection and advanced electronic safety systems throughout the EQE lineup.

pros: Exceptionally quiet cabin, superb ride comfort, premium interior quality, and impressive electric driving refinement.
cons: Uninspiring styling, lacks engaging driving dynamics, and trails some rivals in outright performance and innovation.
mn_take: The 2026 Mercedes-Benz EQE is a luxurious and comfortable electric sedan that excels at quiet long-distance cruising, but stronger competitors in the luxury EV segment make it harder for the EQE to stand out beyond its traditional Mercedes comfort and cabin refinement.

car_name: 2026 Mercedes-Benz E-Class All-Terrain Wagon
overview: The 2026 Mercedes-Benz E-Class All-Terrain Wagon continues to stand as one of the finest luxury wagons available today, blending classic long-roof practicality with premium comfort, advanced technology, and confident all-weather capability. While the “All-Terrain” badge suggests rugged off-road ambitions, this wagon is fundamentally a refined luxury cruiser designed for long-distance travel, family road trips, and comfortable daily driving rather than serious trail work. Unlike many SUVs that prioritize height and bulk over driving sophistication, the E-Class All-Terrain delivers a lower, more elegant driving experience while still offering raised suspension, all-wheel drive, protective body cladding, and useful cargo versatility. It feels distinctly upscale from behind the wheel, combining smooth power delivery, rich interior craftsmanship, and exceptional highway composure. The E-Class wagon’s blend of utility and luxury remains increasingly rare in today’s market, which is precisely why it continues to earn praise from enthusiasts and luxury buyers alike. With its handsome wagon silhouette, sophisticated inline-six engine, and spacious cabin, the All-Terrain successfully captures old-school Mercedes grand-touring character in a modern package.
pricing:
Recommended: E450: $79,650
E450 Pinnacle: $83,190
drivetrain:
The E-Class All-Terrain is powered exclusively by a turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six engine producing 375 horsepower. Mercedes pairs this smooth and responsive engine with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system that helps improve throttle response and reduce turbo lag during low-speed acceleration. Power delivery feels effortless and refined, perfectly matching the wagon’s luxury-oriented personality. The mild-hybrid assistance gives the drivetrain immediate responsiveness, while the nine-speed automatic transmission shifts smoothly and unobtrusively during everyday driving. Standard 4Matic all-wheel drive ensures excellent traction in rain, snow, and slippery road conditions. One of the standout qualities of the E-Class All-Terrain is its standard air suspension. The setup delivers a remarkably cushioned ride, soaking up road imperfections with impressive composure. Long highway journeys feel exceptionally relaxed and isolated, reinforcing the wagon’s role as a premium touring machine. Despite its size and comfort-focused tuning, the wagon still handles with confidence. It remains stable and composed through corners, although it can feel somewhat large and heavy during aggressive driving. The brake pedal lacks some tactile precision, but overall braking performance remains strong and reassuring. The E-Class All-Terrain is not designed to be a sports wagon, but it strikes an excellent balance between comfort, power, and everyday usability.

The E450 All-Terrain accelerates from 0 to 60 mph in just 4.4 seconds, making it impressively quick for a luxury wagon of this size. The inline-six engine delivers strong mid-range performance, and acceleration feels smooth, refined, and effortless rather than aggressively sporty. Its performance is comparable to the E450 sedan, proving that the additional practicality of the wagon body style comes with very little compromise in straight-line speed. 

The E-Class All-Terrain offers more utility than many traditional luxury sedans, with a towing capacity of approximately 4,600 pounds when properly equipped. While it features skid plates, increased ride height, and off-road-inspired styling elements, the wagon is best suited for gravel roads, snowy conditions, and light outdoor adventures rather than demanding off-road trails. Its true strength lies in combining luxury-car refinement with everyday practicality and all-weather confidence.

The E450 All-Terrain delivers respectable fuel efficiency considering its size, power output, and standard all-wheel-drive system. EPA estimates rate the wagon at 22 mpg city, 31 mpg highway, and 25 mpg combined. These figures make it surprisingly efficient for a large luxury wagon powered by a turbocharged inline-six engine. The mild-hybrid system contributes to smoother stop-start operation and improved efficiency during daily driving, particularly in urban conditions.
interior: The E-Class All-Terrain’s cabin is exceptionally elegant and comfortable, embodying the premium craftsmanship expected from a modern Mercedes-Benz flagship wagon. Even the base configuration feels richly appointed, featuring upscale trim materials, soft-touch surfaces, ambient lighting, and a beautifully integrated digital dashboard layout. The seats are especially impressive, offering generous cushioning and excellent long-distance comfort. Mercedes includes heated front seats and its “energizing seat kinetics” system as standard equipment. This feature subtly adjusts seating positions during long drives to reduce fatigue. Buyers can further upgrade the experience with optional massage functionality, ventilation, quilted leather upholstery, and heated rear seats. Rear-seat comfort is equally strong, with generous legroom and supportive seating making the wagon genuinely accommodating for adults on longer trips. Practicality is another major strength. Behind the rear seats, the E-Class wagon offers 33.1 cubic feet of cargo space, expanding to 64.6 cubic feet with the second row folded flat. The wide cargo opening and low load floor make hauling luggage, shopping runs, or road-trip gear significantly easier than in many luxury SUVs. The wagon body style also provides excellent outward visibility and a uniquely elegant silhouette rarely seen in today’s market.
technology: The E-Class All-Terrain features one of the most advanced infotainment setups in the segment. A 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster sits ahead of the driver, while a large 14.4-inch central touchscreen dominates the dashboard. Mercedes’ latest MBUX software supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, voice controls, connected services, and customizable display layouts. The system feels visually impressive and highly modern, though some menu structures can occasionally feel overly complex. Every model comes standard with a premium 17-speaker Burmester audio system that delivers rich, immersive sound quality. For buyers seeking an even more futuristic cabin experience, Mercedes offers the optional MBUX Superscreen setup, which adds a dedicated front-passenger display and transforms nearly the entire dashboard into a digital interface.
safety: The E-Class All-Terrain comes equipped with a strong suite of standard driver-assistance technologies, reinforcing its role as a luxurious long-distance cruiser. Standard safety features include automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and a 360-degree camera system. Mercedes also offers advanced optional systems such as adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assist, and evasive steering assistance. These technologies enhance highway comfort and improve driver confidence during long journeys or heavy traffic conditions.

Limited Warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles

pros: Beautiful wagon styling paired with a luxurious cabin, silky inline-six performance, and outstanding long-distance comfort.
cons: The “All-Terrain” branding overstates its off-road capability, and the brake pedal lacks satisfying feedback.
mn_take: The 2026 Mercedes-Benz E-Class All-Terrain Wagon is one of the most complete luxury wagons on sale today, offering an exceptional combination of comfort, practicality, elegance, and refined performance that many SUVs still struggle to match.

car_name: 2026 Mercedes-Benz CLE-Class
overview: The 2026 CLE-Class represents Mercedes-Benz’s effort to combine the elegance of the former C-Class Coupe and the sophistication of the E-Class Coupe into a single, modern grand touring model. Available in both Coupe and Cabriolet body styles, the CLE delivers the classic proportions and premium atmosphere buyers expect from a Mercedes two-door, while integrating the latest generation of infotainment and mild-hybrid technology. Positioned above the C-Class sedan in terms of style and exclusivity, the CLE leans more toward refined luxury cruising than outright sports-car aggression. The sleek fastback-inspired silhouette, frameless doors, sculpted bodywork, and upscale detailing give the CLE a distinctly expensive appearance on the road. Whether in four-cylinder CLE300 form or six-cylinder CLE450 guise, the CLE balances performance, comfort, and daily usability impressively well. Inside, the cabin feels richly crafted and technologically advanced, with high-quality materials, ambient lighting, and a dashboard design closely inspired by Mercedes’ latest luxury models. While it lacks the sheer practicality of a sedan or SUV, the CLE succeeds as an elegant personal luxury coupe for buyers who prioritize style and driving refinement.

CLE300 Pinnacle Coupe: $63,300

drivetrain:
The CLE-Class is offered with two mild-hybrid turbocharged powertrains, both paired with a smooth-shifting nine-speed automatic transmission and standard 4Matic all-wheel drive. The CLE300 uses a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 255 horsepower. It delivers strong low-end response, respectable passing power, and refined cruising manners. For most buyers, the CLE300 offers enough performance for comfortable grand touring duties while maintaining strong efficiency. The more desirable CLE450 upgrades to a turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six generating 375 horsepower. This engine transforms the CLE into a genuinely quick luxury coupe, delivering effortless acceleration and a smoother, richer character that perfectly suits the car’s premium personality. Mercedes’ 48-volt mild-hybrid system helps reduce turbo lag while adding extra responsiveness during acceleration. On the road, the CLE feels composed and stable at highway speeds while remaining agile enough through corners. Steering precision is decent, although the experience prioritizes refinement over razor-sharp athleticism. Ride quality is comfortable overall, though it still falls short of the plushness offered by the larger E-Class sedan because the CLE does not offer air suspension. The optional Engineering Package further enhances the driving experience by adding rear-wheel steering and adaptive suspension hardware, improving both maneuverability and high-speed stability.

The CLE450 Coupe reaches 60 mph in just 4.1 seconds, making it genuinely quick for a luxury grand tourer. The CLE300 is estimated to complete the sprint in approximately 5.2 seconds, while the heavier Cabriolet models are slightly slower due to the added structural reinforcement required for convertible construction. Acceleration in the CLE450 feels smooth and effortless rather than explosive, perfectly matching the coupe’s refined personality.

The CLE-Class delivers respectable efficiency considering its luxury positioning and available six-cylinder performance. The CLE300 Coupe is rated at up to 24 mpg city and 33 mpg highway, while the Cabriolet sees slightly lower ratings due to its additional weight and aerodynamic compromises. The CLE450 maintains surprisingly competitive efficiency figures, with highway ratings reaching up to 33 mpg depending on configuration. The mild-hybrid system helps improve responsiveness and fuel economy during everyday driving conditions. Overall, the CLE manages to combine strong highway refinement with reasonable operating costs for the segment.
interior: The CLE-Class cabin is one of its strongest attributes. The interior design closely mirrors newer Mercedes models, featuring flowing surfaces, premium materials, ambient lighting, and a strong focus on digital integration. The front seats are supportive and comfortable for long-distance touring, and buyers can equip features such as ventilation, massage functionality, and premium leather upholstery. Standard heated seats enhance comfort during colder weather, while the optional upgrades elevate the CLE into near-luxury grand touring territory. Unlike many compact coupes, the CLE’s rear seats are genuinely usable for adults on shorter to medium-length journeys. The Coupe provides slightly better practicality than the Cabriolet, especially when it comes to trunk capacity. Cargo space is acceptable rather than generous, but still practical enough for weekend travel or daily errands. The Coupe offers more usable luggage space, while the Cabriolet sacrifices some practicality to accommodate its folding soft-top mechanism. Overall cabin isolation is impressive, particularly at highway speeds, reinforcing the CLE’s relaxed and sophisticated driving character.
technology: The CLE-Class comes standard with Mercedes-Benz’s latest MBUX infotainment system, centered around an 11.9-inch vertically oriented touchscreen and a 12.3-inch fully digital instrument cluster. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, voice controls, connected services, and over-the-air software functionality. The interface looks modern and visually impressive, although some functions are buried within menus, requiring a learning curve for new users. Every CLE model includes a premium 17-speaker Burmester sound system, delivering excellent audio quality and adding to the luxury experience. Optional technology features include augmented-reality navigation, surround-view cameras, and adaptive cruise control. While the technology suite is comprehensive, Mercedes’ touch-sensitive steering-wheel controls remain somewhat fiddly during real-world use.
safety: The CLE-Class includes a strong suite of standard driver-assistance technologies. Automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keeping assist are all included as standard equipment. Mercedes also offers additional safety and semi-autonomous driving technologies through optional packages. Features such as adaptive cruise control enhance long-distance comfort and improve highway usability significantly. The CLE’s solid structure, advanced safety systems, and refined road manners make it a reassuring luxury touring car for everyday driving.
