car_name: 2027 Mazda 3
overview:
The 2027 Mazda 3 continues to stand out as one of the most refined and engaging compact cars on the market, blending near-premium craftsmanship with a genuinely fun-to-drive personality. Available in both sedan and hatchback body styles, the Mazda 3 offers a level of versatility that few rivals can match, while maintaining a consistent focus on driving enjoyment and upscale appeal. Its sleek exterior design carries a mature, almost European sophistication, while subtle updates ensure it remains fresh without straying from its already successful formula.

What truly defines the Mazda 3 is its dual nature—it can be both a practical daily commuter and a rewarding driver’s car. Whether navigating urban streets or carving through winding roads, the chassis delivers impressive composure, with precise steering and well-controlled body movements. Unlike many competitors that prioritize comfort over engagement, the Mazda 3 strikes a delicate balance, offering a ride that feels planted and refined without sacrificing responsiveness. Compared to rivals like the Honda Civic, the Mazda leans more toward luxury and driver involvement rather than outright practicality.
pricing:
Base: $26,000 (est)
Select Sport: $27,000 (est)
Preferred (Recommended): $29,000 (est)
Carbon Edition: $32,000 (est)
Premium: $33,000 (est)
Turbo Premium Edition: $38,000 (est)
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the Mazda 3 offers two distinct personalities depending on engine choice. The standard 2.5-liter naturally aspirated four-cylinder produces 186 horsepower, delivering smooth and predictable performance suited for everyday driving. It’s refined, linear, and responsive enough for most drivers, especially when paired with the well-calibrated six-speed automatic transmission. For enthusiasts, the availability of a six-speed manual transmission—exclusively on the front-wheel-drive hatchback—adds a rare layer of engagement in this segment. The manual gearbox feels precise and mechanical, reinforcing Mazda’s commitment to driving purists.

At the top of the range, the turbocharged 2.5-liter engine transforms the Mazda 3 into one of the quickest cars in its class, producing up to 250 horsepower on premium fuel. With standard all-wheel drive, the turbo model delivers strong acceleration and confident traction in varying conditions. Its 0–60 mph time of around 5.6 seconds puts it ahead of nearly every mainstream compact competitor, giving it a performance edge that few can rival.

Despite its engaging performance, the Mazda 3 maintains respectable fuel efficiency across its lineup. Front-wheel-drive models deliver the best numbers, reaching up to 27 mpg in the city and 36 mpg on the highway. All-wheel-drive variants see a slight drop but remain competitive, while turbocharged models trade some efficiency for performance, returning around 23 mpg city and 32 mpg highway. Real-world testing has shown that the Mazda 3 often meets or even exceeds its EPA estimates, particularly on highway drives, reinforcing its reputation as an efficient yet enjoyable daily driver.
interior:
Step inside the Mazda 3, and the cabin immediately impresses with its premium ambiance. Soft-touch materials, elegant design, and thoughtful ergonomics elevate the experience well beyond what’s typical in the compact segment. The layout is clean and driver-focused, with controls that feel intuitive and satisfying to use. Front seats are supportive and comfortable for long journeys, offering excellent driving position and visibility in the sedan. The hatchback, while visually striking, compromises rear visibility due to its sloping design. Rear-seat space is adequate for the class, though not class-leading, and taller passengers may find legroom slightly restricted.

Cargo practicality varies between body styles. The sedan surprisingly offers slightly better trunk usability, while the hatchback provides flexibility with fold-down rear seats. However, competitors like the Honda Civic still hold an advantage in outright space and practicality.
technology:
Mazda takes a unique approach to infotainment, prioritizing usability over flashy interfaces. The standard 8.8-inch display is controlled via a rotary dial rather than touch inputs, which reduces distractions while driving but may feel unconventional to new users. Higher trims feature a larger 10.3-inch display with added functionality. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, with wireless capability available on higher trims. The system is responsive and logically structured, though its placement deep within the dashboard can make it slightly harder to view at a glance.

Audiophiles will appreciate the available 12-speaker Bose sound system, which delivers crisp, well-balanced audio that enhances the premium feel of the cabin.
safety: The Mazda 3 comes well-equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies. Standard features include automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and adaptive cruise control, even on manual-transmission models—an uncommon but welcome inclusion. Optional upgrades add features such as a 360-degree camera system and parking sensors, enhancing convenience and safety in tight urban environments. Overall, the Mazda 3 provides a strong safety package that aligns well with modern expectations in the segment.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None
pros: Premium interior quality, engaging driving dynamics, strong turbo performance option
cons: Limited rear visibility in hatchback, less rear-seat space than rivals, infotainment placement may feel awkward
mn_take: The 2027 Mazda 3 delivers a rare blend of near-luxury refinement and genuine driving enjoyment, making it the enthusiast’s choice in the compact segment.

car_name: 2026 Maserati Grecale Folgore
overview: The 2026 Maserati Grecale Folgore represents the brand’s electrified vision for the compact luxury SUV segment, blending Italian design elegance with modern EV performance. As the all-electric counterpart to the standard Maserati Grecale, the Folgore pushes the model into a new era, offering more power, near-silent operation, and a distinctly futuristic character. With its sculpted bodywork and unmistakable Maserati identity, the Folgore doesn’t just aim to compete—it aims to stand out. However, while it delivers strong acceleration and a premium cabin experience, it enters a fiercely competitive segment where rivals like the Porsche Macan Electric and Audi SQ6 e-tron offer sharper performance and better value. The result is an SUV that appeals strongly to emotion and design sensibilities, even if it doesn’t dominate on paper.
pricing: Grecale Folgore: $121,290
drivetrain:
Powering the Grecale Folgore is a dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup producing a combined 550 horsepower, making it the most powerful Grecale variant outside of limited models. This setup delivers immediate torque and smooth, relentless acceleration typical of high-performance EVs. Acceleration is estimated at around 3.9 seconds for the 0–60 mph sprint, placing it firmly in performance SUV territory. While not class-leading, it’s more than quick enough to feel genuinely exciting in everyday driving.

The driving experience is defined by refinement rather than aggression. The standard air-spring suspension and adaptive dampers provide a supple, composed ride in everyday conditions, while Sport mode sharpens responses and unlocks the full performance potential. Handling is confident and balanced, though it leans more toward comfort and stability than razor-sharp athleticism. One unique feature is the use of paddle shifters to adjust regenerative braking levels, allowing drivers to fine-tune energy recovery and driving feel. However, the absence of true one-pedal driving may disappoint some EV enthusiasts.

The Grecale Folgore is equipped with a 105.0-kWh battery pack, delivering:
- EPA Range: 206–245 miles (depending on wheel size)

While respectable, this range falls short of some key competitors in the segment. Efficiency figures are similarly mid-pack:
- 80 MPGe city / 70 MPGe highway (with 20-inch wheels)
- 65 MPGe city / 59 MPGe highway (with 21-inch wheels)
Charging performance is competitive, though not class-leading, and real-world range can drop significantly under aggressive driving conditions.
interior:
Inside, the Grecale Folgore showcases Maserati’s flair for design and material quality. The cabin feels modern, upscale, and thoughtfully crafted, with a strong emphasis on sustainability. Standard upholstery uses recycled materials with intricate patterns inspired by Italian architecture, giving the interior a unique visual identity. The front seats are supportive and comfortable, while the second row benefits from the EV platform’s flat floor, improving legroom and overall usability. Acoustic glass and extensive sound insulation create an exceptionally quiet cabin, reinforcing the luxury experience.

Cargo capacity stands at around 19 cubic feet, offering practical space for daily use, though the absence of a front trunk is a notable omission in an EV of this class.
technology: The Grecale Folgore features a multi-screen setup, including a 12.3-inch infotainment display, an 8.8-inch secondary control screen, and a digital instrument cluster. Maserati’s Google-based interface provides smooth operation and integrates seamlessly with modern connectivity features. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with voice assistant compatibility. Audiophiles can opt for a 21-speaker Sonus Faber audio system, delivering a rich, immersive sound experience that complements the cabin’s premium ambiance.
safety: The Grecale Folgore comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance both safety and convenience. Standard features include automated emergency braking, adaptive cruise control, and lane-keeping assist. Optional enhancements add a 360-degree camera system, traffic-sign recognition, and more advanced driver-assistance capabilities for urban and highway driving.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Battery Warranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None
pros: Striking design, refined and quiet cabin, strong EV performance.
cons: Expensive for its segment, average driving range, artificial sound effects detract from authenticity.
mn_take: The Grecale Folgore delivers style and electrified performance with unmistakable Maserati character, but its high price and middling range make it a choice driven more by passion than pure practicality.

car_name: 2026 Maserati Grecale
overview:
The 2026 Maserati Grecale continues to carve its identity as one of the most stylish and brand-driven offerings in the compact luxury SUV segment. Positioned as the gateway into the Maserati lineup, the Grecale blends Italian design flair with everyday usability, offering a compelling mix of performance, comfort, and unmistakable road presence. For 2026, Maserati simplifies the lineup significantly by eliminating the base four-cylinder engine, leaving a more potent twin-turbo V-6 as standard across the range. This move elevates the Grecale’s performance credentials, aligning it more closely with premium rivals while reinforcing its positioning as a more exclusive alternative to mainstream luxury SUVs like the Porsche Macan and BMW X3.

Despite its strong brand appeal and refined demeanor, the Grecale walks a fine line between luxury cruiser and performance SUV—delivering comfort and sophistication, though not quite matching the dynamic sharpness of the segment’s most athletic contenders.
pricing: Modena: $86,495
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the Grecale now features a 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged V-6 producing 386 horsepower, derived from Maserati’s Nettuno engine architecture. This engine is paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission and a standard all-wheel-drive system, ensuring confident traction and smooth power delivery across a variety of driving conditions. The inclusion of an air-spring suspension and an electronically controlled limited-slip rear differential as standard equipment significantly enhances the Grecale’s versatility. In Comfort mode, the SUV delivers a plush, composed ride that isolates occupants from road imperfections, making it ideal for long-distance cruising. Switch to more aggressive driving modes, and the Grecale tightens its responses, offering improved body control and a more engaging driving experience.

That said, while the chassis feels balanced and capable, steering feedback remains somewhat muted—particularly when compared to benchmark drivers’ SUVs like the Porsche Macan. Performance is expected to be brisk, with acceleration figures likely in the sub-4-second range for 0–60 mph, placing it firmly within the competitive set.

Efficiency remains reasonable given the Grecale’s performance-oriented V-6 engine:
- 18 mpg city
- 25 mpg highway
- 20 mpg combined
These figures position it competitively among six-cylinder luxury SUVs, though not class-leading.
interior:
Step inside the Grecale, and it becomes immediately clear that Maserati has prioritized craftsmanship and ambiance. The cabin is richly appointed with premium materials, including fine leather upholstery, soft-touch surfaces, and elegant trim finishes that elevate the overall sense of luxury. The front seats are supportive and comfortable for long journeys, while the second row provides adequate space for adult passengers, though it’s best suited for two rather than three across. The overall cabin layout emphasizes a modern, minimalist aesthetic, blending traditional luxury cues with contemporary digital elements.

Cargo capacity stands at around 20 cubic feet, making the Grecale practical enough for daily use and weekend trips, though not class-leading in outright space.
technology: The Grecale embraces a tech-forward approach with a dual-touchscreen setup, consisting of a 12.3-inch central display and a secondary 8.8-inch screen dedicated to climate and auxiliary controls. A fully digital instrument cluster complements the setup, providing crisp and customizable driver information. Maserati’s Google-based infotainment system offers smooth operation and integrates features like wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with voice assistant compatibility via Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant. Audiophiles will appreciate the available Sonus Faber sound system, which can be upgraded to a 21-speaker, 1285-watt configuration, delivering a rich and immersive listening experience.
safety: The Grecale comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of standard driver-assistance features, ensuring a solid baseline of safety and convenience. Advanced systems are available through optional packages for those seeking additional functionality. Standard features include automated emergency braking, adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, and parking sensors. Optional enhancements add more sophisticated capabilities such as lane-centering assist, intersection collision avoidance, and traffic-sign recognition.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None
pros: Striking Italian design, refined ride quality, strong V-6 performance as standard.
cons: Expensive for the segment, steering lacks feedback, rivals offer sharper handling dynamics.
mn_take: The Grecale delivers style, comfort, and exclusivity in a segment crowded with competence, but it appeals more to the heart than to driving purists seeking ultimate performance precision.

car_name: 2026 Maserati MCPura
overview: The 2026 Maserati MCPura represents the Italian marque’s most focused expression of a modern supercar, blending dramatic styling with a purist, driver-centric philosophy. Evolving from the MC20 lineage, the MCPura refines the formula with subtle design enhancements, improved interior execution, and the same charismatic twin-turbo V-6 that defines its personality. Unlike some rivals that chase outright performance supremacy, the MCPura leans into emotional appeal—its sculptural bodywork, butterfly doors, and unmistakable road presence make it as much a design statement as it is a performance machine. While competitors like the McLaren 750S or Ferrari 296 GTB may edge ahead in raw numbers, the MCPura counters with a more engaging, analog-like driving experience and a sense of exclusivity that feels distinctly Maserati.
pricing:
Coupe: $250,000 (est)
Cielo (Convertible): $280,000 (est)
drivetrain:
At the heart of the MCPura lies a 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged V-6 producing 621 horsepower and 538 lb-ft of torque, mounted mid-ship for optimal balance. This engine features Maserati’s Formula 1-inspired twin-combustion chamber technology, delivering both efficiency and a uniquely sharp throttle response. Power is sent exclusively to the rear wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, ensuring rapid gear changes and precise control under acceleration. The MCPura sprints from 0–60 mph in around 3.2 seconds—quick by any standard, though not class-leading. What truly defines the MCPura is its chassis tuning. The lightweight carbon-fiber monocoque provides exceptional rigidity, while the adaptive suspension offers a rare duality—capable of soaking up imperfections in its softer settings while transforming into a razor-sharp track tool in more aggressive modes. Steering feel is direct and communicative, reinforcing Maserati’s focus on driver engagement over sheer speed metrics.

Efficiency is understandably secondary in this segment, but expectations hover around:
15 mpg city
25 mpg highway
18 mpg combined
These figures align with most mid-engine supercars, where performance takes clear priority over economy.
interior: Step inside, and the MCPura reveals a cockpit designed with intent and restraint. Unlike many modern supercars overloaded with digital clutter, Maserati has opted for a clean, driver-focused layout. Premium materials dominate the cabin—leather upholstery, exposed carbon fiber, and aluminum accents create an environment that feels both luxurious and purposeful. The seats are supportive enough for spirited driving yet comfortable for longer journeys, reinforcing the car’s surprising usability. There is no rear seating, and practicality is minimal, with just about 5 cubic feet of combined cargo space. Still, for a supercar of this nature, the MCPura offers a commendable level of day-to-day livability.
technology: The MCPura features a dual 10.3-inch display setup—one for infotainment and another for the digital instrument cluster. The interface is based on Maserati’s latest Google-integrated system, delivering smooth responsiveness and intuitive navigation. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with connected services via the Maserati Connect app. While not overly complex, the system strikes a balance between modern functionality and driver focus, avoiding unnecessary distractions.
safety:
- Limited driver-assistance availability reflects the MCPura’s performance-first intent
- Optional blind-spot monitoring
- Structural safety enhanced by carbon-fiber monocoque construction
This is a car designed primarily for driving purity rather than autonomous convenience.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: None
pros: Exotic styling, engaging driving dynamics, surprisingly usable ride quality for a supercar.
cons: Limited practicality, high price tag, fewer driver-assistance features than rivals.
mn_take: The MCPura isn’t about dominating spec sheets—it’s about delivering an emotional, design-led supercar experience that prioritizes connection over outright speed.

car_name: 2026 Maserati GranTurismo
overview: The 2026 Maserati GranTurismo is a masterclass in modern grand touring, blending seductive Italian styling with a deeply luxurious cabin and performance that feels both effortless and exhilarating. Positioned as the coupe sibling to the Maserati GranCabrio, the GranTurismo delivers a more focused, coupe-like experience while retaining the brand’s unmistakable sense of occasion. Its flowing proportions, long hood, and sculpted rear haunches give it undeniable road presence, while its dual personality allows it to transition seamlessly between relaxed highway cruising and spirited backroad driving. Unlike sharper rivals such as the Porsche 911, the GranTurismo leans into its grand touring roots—prioritizing comfort, elegance, and long-distance usability without sacrificing speed.
pricing:
Modena (Base): $147,495
Trofeo: $168,495
drivetrain:
At its core, the GranTurismo features a 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged V-6 engine derived from the Maserati MC20, incorporating advanced twin-combustion chamber technology inspired by Formula 1. In Modena form, it produces 483 horsepower, while the Trofeo variant raises output to a potent 542 horsepower. Paired with a smooth eight-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive, the GranTurismo delivers strong, consistent performance in all conditions. The Trofeo model is particularly impressive, accelerating from 0–60 mph in just 3.2 seconds—placing it firmly among elite grand touring machines. Driving dynamics are where the GranTurismo truly shines. In Comfort mode, the adaptive air suspension absorbs imperfections with remarkable composure, making long-distance journeys relaxing and refined. Switch to Sport or Corsa modes, and the car sharpens significantly—offering firmer suspension, heavier steering, and a more aggressive exhaust note. The intermediate GT mode strikes an ideal balance, making it the most versatile setting for everyday driving.

For a high-performance luxury coupe, the GranTurismo delivers respectable efficiency. EPA estimates stand at 18 mpg city and 27 mpg highway. These figures reflect the balance between performance capability and real-world usability, especially for long-distance touring.
interior: Inside, the GranTurismo offers a rich and immersive environment, characterized by premium materials, elegant design, and a driver-focused layout. Leather upholstery, refined stitching, and carefully curated trim elements create a cabin that feels both luxurious and modern. The front seats are exceptionally comfortable, providing excellent support for extended journeys. The rear seats, while more accommodating than some rivals, remain best suited for short trips or additional storage. The 2+2 layout ensures practicality without compromising the car’s sleek proportions. Cargo capacity stands at 11 cubic feet, offering enough space for weekend getaways—perfectly aligning with the GranTurismo’s grand touring mission.
technology: The GranTurismo features a contemporary infotainment setup centered around a 12.3-inch touchscreen, complemented by a secondary 8.8-inch display dedicated to climate controls. The system runs on a Google-based interface, delivering smooth operation and modern connectivity. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, while a head-up display enhances driver awareness by projecting key information onto the windshield. Audio quality is exceptional, with a standard Sonus Faber system and an optional 19-speaker setup that transforms the cabin into a concert-like environment. That said, the reliance on touchscreen controls may require some acclimation, particularly for drivers who prefer physical buttons.
safety: The GranTurismo comes equipped with essential safety systems, including automated emergency braking and parking sensors. More advanced features—such as adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keeping assist—are available through optional packages, rather than being standard.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: Not included
pros: Stunning design, powerful and refined V-6 engine, exceptional balance between comfort and performance.
cons: Touchscreen-heavy interface, limited standard driver-assistance tech, high price tag.
mn_take: The 2026 GranTurismo captures the essence of a true grand tourer—effortlessly blending beauty, performance, and comfort into a machine that feels as special as it looks.

car_name: 2026 Maserati GranCabrio Folgore
overview: The 2026 Maserati GranCabrio Folgore reimagines the classic Italian grand tourer for the electric era, combining open-top elegance with cutting-edge EV performance. Sharing its sculptural silhouette with the gasoline-powered Maserati GranCabrio, the Folgore replaces combustion theatrics with silent, electrified intensity—delivering a distinctly modern yet still emotional driving experience. Its flowing bodywork, fabric soft-top, and unmistakable Maserati design language make it an object of desire, while its tri-motor setup introduces a level of performance that rivals some of the fastest grand tourers on the planet. While it lacks the visceral soundtrack of a traditional engine, the Folgore compensates with relentless acceleration and a refined, serene driving character.
pricing: GranCabrio Folgore: $208,590
drivetrain:
The GranCabrio Folgore is powered by a sophisticated tri-motor electric setup producing up to 818 horsepower in Corsa mode, with standard output capped at 751 horsepower for everyday driving. This immense power is distributed through an advanced all-wheel-drive system with torque vectoring, allowing for precise handling and exceptional traction. Performance is nothing short of breathtaking. Maserati claims a 0–60 mph sprint of just 2.7 seconds, placing it firmly in high-performance territory alongside elite machines like the Porsche 911 and other premium grand tourers. Despite its performance credentials, the Folgore retains a refined ride quality, offering a balance between sharp handling and long-distance comfort. Unlike many EVs, the braking system maintains a natural pedal feel, avoiding the artificial sensation often associated with regenerative systems. Multiple regeneration levels are available, though the absence of one-pedal driving keeps the experience closer to traditional driving dynamics.

The Folgore is equipped with an 83.0-kWh battery pack, delivering an EPA-estimated range of up to 233 miles. While this figure is modest compared to some luxury EV sedans like the Lucid Air, it aligns with the performance-focused nature of the vehicle. Fast-charging capability is a highlight, with support for up to 270 kW charging speeds. Maserati claims that approximately 62 miles of range can be added in just five minutes under optimal conditions, making it well-suited for quick top-ups during long journeys. Efficiency ratings stand at 83 MPGe city and 81 MPGe highway.
interior: Inside, the GranCabrio Folgore blends sustainability with luxury. Standard EcoNyl upholstery—crafted from recycled materials—offers a modern twist on traditional luxury, while optional leather finishes elevate the cabin further. The design is driver-focused, wrapping occupants in high-quality materials and ambient sophistication. Front-seat comfort is excellent, making the Folgore a capable long-distance cruiser. The rear seats, however, remain compact and are better suited for short trips or additional storage. With the roof down, the cabin transforms into an open-air sanctuary, enhancing the sensory experience of every drive. Cargo space is limited at just around 4 cubic feet, a compromise largely due to the folding soft-top mechanism and battery packaging—something to consider for longer touring ambitions.
technology: The GranCabrio Folgore features a dual-screen setup, anchored by a 12.3-inch infotainment display and complemented by an 8.8-inch touchscreen for climate controls. The system runs on a Google-based interface, offering smooth functionality along with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. A head-up display keeps essential driving data within the driver’s line of sight, while the Sonus Faber audio system delivers a rich, immersive sound experience—available in both 13-speaker and optional 16-speaker configurations. While the technology suite is advanced, the heavy reliance on touch controls may not appeal to purists who prefer tactile interfaces.
safety: The Folgore comes equipped with essential driver-assistance technologies, ensuring a baseline level of safety without detracting from its driver-focused nature. Standard features include automated emergency braking and lane-keeping assistance, while adaptive cruise control is available as an option.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: Not included
pros: Stunning design, explosive EV acceleration, refined and comfortable ride quality.
cons: Limited cargo space, heavy reliance on screens, significantly more expensive than the V-6 model.
mn_take: The GranCabrio Folgore is a bold, electrified take on Italian grand touring—effortlessly fast and undeniably beautiful, though its heart still feels more emotional in V-6 form.

car_name: 2026 Maserati GranCabrio
overview: The 2026 Maserati GranCabrio is a statement of effortless Italian grand touring—blending open-air luxury with genuine performance pedigree. Built on the same platform as the Maserati GranTurismo, this convertible transforms the coupe’s elegance into a more emotional, sensory experience. With its sculpted bodywork, fabric soft-top, and unmistakable Maserati presence, the GranCabrio feels equally at home cruising coastal boulevards or stretching its legs on long-distance highway drives. Underneath its refined demeanor lies serious engineering, including a Formula 1-derived twin-turbo V-6. While it may not chase outright lap times like a Porsche 911, the GranCabrio prioritizes a balance of comfort, speed, and theater—making it a true grand tourer in the purest sense.
drivetrain:
At the heart of the GranCabrio sits a sophisticated 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged V-6 engine derived from the Maserati MC20. In standard form, it produces 483 horsepower, while the Trofeo variant elevates output to a commanding 542 horsepower. Power is delivered through a quick-shifting eight-speed automatic transmission paired with an all-wheel-drive system, ensuring confident traction in varied conditions. Performance is both strong and accessible. Maserati claims 0–60 mph times of around 3.7 seconds for the base model and an impressive 3.4 seconds for the Trofeo. The driving experience is defined by versatility—Comfort mode delivers a composed, plush ride, while Sport and Corsa modes sharpen throttle response, steering weight, and exhaust intensity. The adaptive air suspension seamlessly transitions between these personalities, allowing the GranCabrio to feel relaxed one moment and assertive the next.

Efficiency isn’t the GranCabrio’s primary mission, but it remains reasonable for a high-performance luxury convertible. EPA estimates stand at 17 mpg city and 26 mpg highway. These figures place it close to its coupe sibling, reflecting the balance between performance and usability.
interior: Step inside, and the GranCabrio delivers a rich, tactile environment that embodies Italian craftsmanship. Premium leather, intricate stitching, and carefully curated materials create a cabin that feels both luxurious and intimate. The front seats are designed for long-distance comfort, offering excellent support for extended journeys. The rear seats, while present, are best suited for short trips or additional luggage space. Maserati cleverly enhances open-top comfort with features like a neck warmer system that circulates warm air around occupants—making top-down driving enjoyable even in cooler conditions. The optional wind deflector further refines the experience by minimizing cabin turbulence at higher speeds.
technology: The GranCabrio features a modern, dual-screen setup centered around a 12.3-inch infotainment display, complemented by a secondary 8.8-inch touchscreen for climate controls. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, ensuring seamless smartphone integration. Audio quality is a highlight, thanks to collaboration with Sonus Faber. The standard 13-speaker system already delivers rich acoustics, while the optional 16-speaker setup elevates the experience with immersive surround sound. A head-up display adds convenience, projecting key driving information directly into the driver’s line of sight.
safety: While performance remains the focus, the GranCabrio includes essential safety technologies. Standard features include automated emergency braking and parking sensors, while optional packages add more advanced systems such as adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keeping assistance. These features enhance usability without diluting the car’s driver-focused character.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: Not included
pros: Elegant design, exhilarating twin-turbo V-6 performance, luxurious open-top experience.
cons: Elegant design, exhilarating twin-turbo V-6 performance, luxurious open-top experience.
mn_take: The 2026 GranCabrio is less about outright speed and more about the experience—it’s a beautifully crafted grand tourer that turns every drive into an occasion.

car_name: 2026 Lucid Air Review
overview: The 2026 Lucid Air doesn’t simply participate in the luxury EV segment—it quietly reshapes it. Built as a dedicated electric platform rather than an adaptation of a combustion-era design, the Air delivers a level of efficiency, range, and refinement that feels genuinely forward-thinking. What sets it apart is its dual personality. On one hand, it is an extraordinarily capable long-distance cruiser with industry-leading range; on the other, it offers explosive performance that rivals exotic machinery. This balance of serenity and strength gives the Air a unique identity—one that leans more toward effortless sophistication than outright theatrics.
pricing:
Pure – $72,400
Touring – $81,400
Grand Touring – $116,400
Sapphire – $250,500
drivetrain:
The Lucid Air’s powertrain lineup spans from refined to outright outrageous. The entry-level Pure model, with its single rear-mounted motor, delivers 430 horsepower and a smooth, linear driving character that feels more than adequate for everyday use. Moving up the range introduces dual-motor all-wheel-drive configurations with significantly higher outputs, culminating in the tri-motor Sapphire, which produces a staggering 1234 horsepower. Acceleration is immediate and relentless, yet never chaotic. Even in its most aggressive form, the Air maintains composure, translating immense power into controlled forward motion rather than drama. The Sapphire’s near-hypercar acceleration is remarkable, but equally impressive is how usable that performance feels in real-world conditions. Despite this performance potential, the Air remains tuned for comfort. Its suspension leans toward a plush, composed ride, soaking up imperfections with ease. However, models equipped with larger wheels can transmit noticeable road noise, slightly detracting from the otherwise serene experience.

Efficiency is the Lucid Air’s defining strength. With EPA-estimated ranges stretching from 420 miles to an astonishing 512 miles in the Grand Touring, it stands as one of the longest-range electric vehicles currently available. What makes these numbers even more impressive is their real-world credibility. In highway testing, the Air has demonstrated the ability to travel over 400 miles on a single charge—an achievement that fundamentally changes how EV ownership is perceived. Fast-charging capability further enhances usability, allowing substantial range recovery in minimal time, making long-distance journeys feel almost effortless.
interior: Inside, the Lucid Air embraces a modern interpretation of luxury that prioritizes openness, calmness, and precision. The cabin design is minimalist yet warm, with carefully selected materials that emphasize both visual elegance and tactile richness. Space is a standout feature. The Air’s electric architecture allows for exceptional legroom, particularly in the rear, where passengers benefit from a near executive-class seating experience. The optional glass canopy roof enhances this sense of space, flooding the interior with natural light and creating an almost lounge-like atmosphere. Comfort is further reinforced by well-cushioned seating and a ride quality that isolates occupants from the outside world. Whether navigating city streets or cruising at highway speeds, the Air maintains a consistent sense of quiet composure.
technology: Technology plays a central role in the Lucid Air’s identity. The dashboard is dominated by a sweeping curved display that integrates the instrument cluster and infotainment system into a single, cohesive interface. Below it, a secondary retractable touchscreen handles additional controls, adding a layer of futuristic functionality. The system is visually impressive and highly responsive, offering features such as wireless smartphone integration, over-the-air updates, and an available immersive 21-speaker audio system. While the heavy reliance on touch inputs may not appeal to traditionalists, the overall execution feels polished and thoughtfully integrated once familiarity sets in.
safety: The Lucid Air is equipped with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance systems designed to enhance both safety and convenience. Features such as adaptive cruise control, automated emergency braking, and blind-spot monitoring come standard, while more advanced capabilities are available through the DreamDrive Pro system. These technologies work seamlessly in the background, supporting the driver without feeling intrusive, and are particularly beneficial during extended highway journeys where fatigue can set in.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 2 years / 24,000 miles
pros: Exceptional real-world range, effortless yet extreme performance, spacious and modern luxury interior.
cons: Touchscreen-heavy interface may not suit all users, noticeable tire noise with larger wheels, high-end trims are very expensive.
mn_take: The 2026 Lucid Air sets the gold standard for luxury EVs, blending unmatched range with refined performance and a truly modern, serene driving experience.

car_name: 2026 Lotus Evija Review
overview: The 2026 Lotus Evija is not just a hypercar—it’s a radical redefinition of what Lotus stands for in the electric era. Known historically for lightweight, driver-focused machines, Lotus has taken a bold leap into the future with the Evija, delivering staggering performance without abandoning its core philosophy of engagement and precision. With over 2000 horsepower, cutting-edge aerodynamics, and a surprisingly analog driving feel for an EV, the Evija blends futuristic engineering with traditional driver feedback. It’s an ultra-exclusive, track-focused masterpiece that challenges established hypercar norms—though its limited practicality and restricted road legality make it more of a collector’s weapon than a daily indulgence.
drivetrain:
At the heart of the Evija lies a quad-motor electric powertrain producing a staggering 2012 horsepower and 1257 lb-ft of torque. Power is distributed through an advanced torque-vectoring all-wheel-drive system, delivering instantaneous acceleration that borders on the surreal. Performance is nothing short of extraordinary, with a claimed 0–60 mph time of under two seconds. The Evija feels brutally fast in a straight line, yet its brilliance lies in how it handles that power. Thanks to its relatively low curb weight for an EV hypercar and sophisticated chassis tuning, it remains composed and agile through corners. What truly sets the Evija apart is its use of hydraulic steering and braking systems—an uncommon approach in modern EVs. This delivers exceptional feedback and control, giving the driver a level of connection rarely found in electric performance vehicles. Driving modes ranging from Range to Track allow the experience to be tailored, though aggressive use dramatically drains the battery.

Efficiency is largely irrelevant in this segment, and the Evija is no exception. While official EPA ratings are unavailable due to its limited road legality, real-world performance driving can deplete the battery in minutes when pushed to its limits.
interior: The Evija’s cabin is minimalistic yet dramatic, reflecting its hypercar status. Dihedral doors open into a cockpit designed around the driver, with carbon-fiber seats, microfiber upholstery, and a focus on weight reduction. Despite its extreme nature, the interior incorporates essential comforts such as climate control and premium materials. Storage is minimal, and practicality is secondary, but the design delivers an immersive, race-inspired atmosphere that complements the car’s performance credentials.
technology: Unlike many modern hypercars, the Evija adopts a restrained approach to infotainment. A digital display provides key driving data, while connectivity features such as Bluetooth, wireless Apple CarPlay, and Android Auto are included. A dedicated smartphone app allows remote monitoring of battery status and vehicle data, aligning the Evija with modern EV expectations while maintaining its driver-focused ethos.
safety: Safety technology is not the Evija’s primary focus, but it is expected to include essential driver-assistance systems. Given its track-oriented nature and exclusivity, the emphasis remains on driver skill and control rather than advanced automation.
warranty: Warranty coverage is relatively modest for a vehicle at this price point, with both limited and powertrain warranties capped at three years or 36,000 miles. Complimentary maintenance is not included, reflecting the Evija’s niche positioning as a collectible hypercar.
pros: Mind-bending acceleration and power, exceptional steering and braking feedback for an EV, groundbreaking performance engineering.
cons: Rapid battery drain under hard driving, lacks emotional engine sound, not road-legal in certain markets including the U.S.
mn_take: The 2026 Lotus Evija is a technological tour de force that proves electric hypercars can still deliver raw driver engagement, making it a landmark machine for collectors and performance purists embracing the electric future.

car_name: 2026 Lotus Emira Review
overview: The 2026 Lotus Emira stands as a defining moment for the British marque—a final celebration of internal combustion before Lotus transitions fully into an electric future. With its mid-engine layout, exotic styling, and deeply engaging driving dynamics, the Emira channels the raw essence of classic sports cars while incorporating just enough modern refinement to make it livable. It’s not the fastest or most polished option in its class, but it delivers something increasingly rare: an unfiltered, analog driving experience wrapped in a surprisingly premium package.
pricing:
Turbo SE – $109,400
Turbo SE Racing Line – $112,400
V-6 SE – $115,400 (Recommended)
V-6 SE Racing Line – $118,400
Jim Clark Special Edition – $142,400
drivetrain:
The Emira offers two distinct powertrains, both delivering 400 horsepower but offering very different personalities. The highlight is the Toyota-sourced supercharged 3.5-liter V-6, available with a six-speed manual or automatic transmission, delivering a more traditional and engaging sports car experience. Alternatively, a turbocharged four-cylinder from Mercedes-AMG provides higher torque and is paired exclusively with an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic. Performance is brisk rather than class-leading, with 0–60 mph achieved in approximately 4.3 seconds. However, outright speed is not the Emira’s primary focus. Instead, it excels in steering precision and chassis balance. The hydraulic steering system—an increasingly rare feature—delivers exceptional feedback, making the car feel alive in the driver’s hands. Handling is razor-sharp, and the mid-engine layout ensures remarkable composure through corners. That said, the experience isn’t without quirks. The manual gearbox can feel notchy, and the brakes are overly aggressive at low speeds, requiring careful modulation.

Efficiency is not a priority for the Emira, with EPA estimates hovering around 18 mpg city, 26 mpg highway, and 21 mpg combined. This aligns with expectations for a high-performance sports coupe in this segment.
interior: The Emira’s cabin marks a significant step forward for Lotus, offering a more premium and user-friendly environment than its predecessors. The layout is clean and driver-focused, with a digital instrument cluster and improved ergonomics. Material quality is noticeably upgraded, featuring leather, Alcantara, and metallic accents. While still compact, the cabin feels more accommodating, with improved ingress and egress compared to earlier Lotus models. Practicality remains limited, but usable storage spaces and dual cargo compartments provide some everyday usability.
technology: A 10.2-inch touchscreen infotainment system sits at the center of the dashboard, supporting wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. The interface is modern and functional, though physical controls are minimal aside from a volume knob. Compared to rivals, the tech offering is adequate rather than cutting-edge, but it complements the Emira’s driver-focused ethos without becoming a distraction.
safety: Breaking away from Lotus tradition, the Emira now includes a suite of driver-assistance technologies such as automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and available adaptive cruise control. While not class-leading, these additions improve everyday usability and safety.
warranty: Warranty coverage is modest for the segment, with limited and powertrain warranties capped at three years or 36,000 miles. Unlike many rivals, the Emira does not include complimentary scheduled maintenance, which may be a consideration for long-term ownership.
pros: Exceptional steering feel and chassis balance, engaging analog driving experience, significantly improved interior quality.
cons: Notchy manual transmission, overly sensitive brakes, fit and finish still trail top rivals.
mn_take: The 2026 Lotus Emira delivers one of the purest driving experiences left in the modern automotive world, making it a compelling choice for enthusiasts who value feel and engagement over outright speed or luxury polish.

car_name: 2026 Lincoln Nautilus Hybrid Review
overview: The 2026 Lincoln Nautilus Hybrid embodies modern American luxury with a calm, technology-forward personality. It isn’t engineered to thrill on twisty roads—instead, it delivers a serene, near-silent driving experience wrapped in one of the most visually striking cabins in the segment. With a smooth hybrid powertrain, an expansive digital interface, and a focus on passenger comfort, the Nautilus Hybrid positions itself as a refined sanctuary on wheels rather than a performance-oriented SUV.
pricing:
Premiere – $58,990
Reserve – $68,590 (Recommended)
Black Label – $82,125
drivetrain:
The Nautilus Hybrid is powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four engine paired with dual electric motors, producing a combined 310 horsepower. Power is delivered through a continuously variable transmission (CVT) with standard all-wheel drive. On the road, the hybrid system feels exceptionally smooth and well-integrated, prioritizing quietness and refinement over outright speed. Acceleration is adequate rather than exciting, with a 0–60 mph time of around 6.6 seconds. The driving dynamics lean toward comfort, with soft suspension tuning that isolates occupants from road imperfections. Switching to the “Excite” mode sharpens responses slightly but introduces some unwanted harshness, subtly undermining the SUV’s otherwise tranquil nature.

The Nautilus Hybrid delivers solid efficiency figures for a luxury midsize SUV, with EPA estimates of 29 mpg city, 31 mpg highway, and 30 mpg combined. However, real-world highway performance doesn’t significantly surpass the non-hybrid model, making its efficiency advantage more noticeable in urban driving conditions.
interior: Inside, the Nautilus Hybrid offers one of the most luxurious and visually unique cabins in Lincoln’s lineup. Premium materials, ambient lighting, and a minimalist design philosophy create a calming environment that feels more like a high-end lounge than a traditional SUV interior. The seats are exceptionally comfortable, with available 24-way adjustability, heating, ventilation, and massage functions. Lincoln’s “Rejuvenate” feature elevates the experience further, combining lighting, seat adjustments, fragrances, and soundscapes to create a spa-like atmosphere. Rear-seat passengers enjoy generous space, while cargo capacity remains practical, accommodating everyday usability without compromise.
technology: The highlight of the Nautilus Hybrid’s interior is its massive 48-inch panoramic display stretching across the dashboard, complemented by an 11.1-inch central touchscreen. This setup delivers a futuristic yet intuitive user experience once familiarized. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with integrated Alexa voice assistance. Higher trims offer a premium 28-speaker Revel Ultima 3D audio system, delivering an immersive sound experience. Lincoln’s BlueCruise hands-free driving system is also standard, now enhanced with automatic lane-change capability.
safety: The Nautilus Hybrid comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies, including automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, and a hands-free driving system. These features contribute to a confident and stress-free driving experience, particularly on highways.
warranty: Lincoln provides competitive coverage in this segment, with extended powertrain and hybrid component warranties. Black Label trims further enhance ownership with premium maintenance perks and concierge-style services.
pros: Exceptionally quiet and refined ride, class-leading interior tech and ambiance, smooth and well-integrated hybrid powertrain.
cons: Performance remains average, real-world highway efficiency not significantly improved, premium features locked behind higher trims.
mn_take: The 2026 Lincoln Nautilus Hybrid is a luxury-first SUV that prioritizes serenity, technology, and comfort over excitement, making it an ideal choice for buyers seeking a relaxing, premium daily driving experience.

car_name: 2026 Lincoln Nautilus
overview: The 2026 Lincoln Nautilus embodies a modern interpretation of American luxury, placing a strong emphasis on comfort, technology, and a calming in-cabin experience. Positioned as a two-row midsize luxury SUV, it appeals to buyers who prioritize refinement and innovation over outright performance or driving engagement.Its exterior design carries a clean, upscale presence, while the interior takes a bold leap into the future with one of the most visually striking dashboard layouts in the segment. Lincoln’s focus here is clear—the Nautilus is designed to be a sanctuary on wheels, offering a quiet ride, plush materials, and an immersive technology experience that sets it apart from more conventional rivals. While competitors such as the BMW X5 or Mercedes-Benz GLE-Class may offer sharper dynamics, the Nautilus leans into its strengths, delivering a smooth, relaxed driving character paired with an abundance of luxury features.
pricing:
Premiere – $55,990
Reserve – $65,590
Black Label – $79,655
drivetrain: Under the hood, the Nautilus is powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 250 horsepower, paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive. This setup delivers adequate performance for everyday driving, offering smooth and predictable acceleration rather than outright excitement.On the road, the Nautilus excels in refinement. The suspension is tuned to absorb imperfections effortlessly, creating a composed and serene ride that aligns perfectly with Lincoln’s luxury philosophy. In its standard driving mode, the vehicle isolates occupants from road noise and vibrations, making long journeys feel effortless. Switching to the more aggressive drive mode sharpens responses slightly and reduces body roll, but it also introduces some firmness into the ride, especially on larger wheels. Even then, the Nautilus never transforms into a sporty SUV—it remains firmly focused on comfort. Fuel efficiency is respectable for the segment, with the Nautilus delivering balanced performance between city and highway driving. Real-world testing shows it can even exceed its official highway ratings under steady cruising conditions. However, for buyers seeking improved efficiency and stronger performance, the available hybrid variant presents a more compelling alternative, offering both better acceleration and enhanced fuel economy.
interior: The Nautilus truly shines inside, where it delivers one of the most distinctive and luxurious cabins in its class. High-quality materials, soft-touch surfaces, and carefully curated ambient lighting create an upscale atmosphere that feels both modern and inviting. The front seats are designed with comfort as a priority, offering heating, ventilation, and extensive adjustability. Optional features such as massaging seats elevate the experience further, making long drives exceptionally relaxing. One of the standout features is Lincoln’s “Rejuvenate” system, which transforms the cabin into a spa-like environment by combining ambient lighting, seat adjustments, screen visuals, and even fragrance diffusion. It’s a unique touch that reinforces the Nautilus’s focus on wellness and comfort. Rear-seat passengers are well accommodated, with generous space and supportive seating. Cargo capacity is practical for a two-row SUV, offering sufficient room for daily use and longer trips.
technology: Technology is a defining element of the Nautilus experience. Dominating the dashboard is an expansive 48-inch panoramic display that stretches across its width, creating a futuristic and immersive interface. Complementing it is an 11.1-inch central touchscreen that handles primary controls. Despite its initial visual complexity, the system is surprisingly intuitive after a short learning curve. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with integrated voice assistance powered by Amazon Alexa. Higher trims offer a premium 28-speaker Revel Ultima 3D audio system, delivering exceptional sound quality and enhancing the overall cabin ambiance.
safety: The Nautilus comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance features as standard. Lincoln’s Co-Pilot360 system includes automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control. A highlight is the inclusion of the latest BlueCruise hands-free driving system, which now supports automatic lane changes, allowing for a more seamless and relaxed highway driving experience.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 6 years / 70,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: up to 4 years / 50,000 miles (Black Label only)
pros: Ultra-luxurious and tech-forward interior, exceptionally quiet and comfortable ride, innovative features like Rejuvenate, strong value in mid-level trims.
cons: Base engine feels merely adequate, some tech features feel gimmicky, limited towing capability, lacks driving excitement compared to rivals.
mn_take: The 2026 Lincoln Nautilus stands out with its futuristic cabin and serene driving experience, making it a compelling choice for luxury-focused buyers who value comfort and innovation over performance.

car_name: 2026 Lincoln Aviator
overview: The 2026 Lincoln Aviator represents a distinctly American take on modern luxury, blending elegant styling, effortless power, and a serene driving character into a three-row SUV that prioritizes comfort above all else. Sitting just below the flagship Navigator in the brand’s lineup, the Aviator carries forward Lincoln’s core philosophy—quiet sophistication, plush ride quality, and a focus on passenger well-being. Its design is sleek and understated rather than aggressively bold, and that same philosophy extends inside. The cabin is richly appointed, thoughtfully laid out, and designed to create a calming environment for both driver and passengers. While it may not project the same badge prestige as some European competitors, the Aviator compensates with a unique charm and a deeply refined driving experience. For 2026, subtle updates such as improved hands-free functionality and enhanced driver-assistance capabilities ensure it remains competitive in an increasingly tech-focused segment.
pricing:
Premiere – $58,605
Reserve – $68,425
Black Label – $87,075
drivetrain:
At the heart of the Aviator lies a powerful 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged V6 engine producing 400 horsepower, paired with a smooth-shifting 10-speed automatic transmission. This powertrain delivers strong, effortless acceleration, making the Aviator feel confident whether navigating city traffic or cruising on the highway. Despite its performance capabilities, the Aviator’s primary focus is refinement. The suspension is tuned to prioritize comfort, absorbing road imperfections with a soft, composed demeanor. It glides over most surfaces with ease, maintaining a quiet and isolated cabin that reinforces its luxury credentials. Handling is stable and predictable, though not particularly engaging. Even with the optional adaptive suspension and air springs, the driving experience remains relaxed rather than sporty. This is a vehicle designed for calm, composed travel—not spirited driving.

Fuel efficiency is not the Aviator’s strongest attribute, especially when compared to newer hybridized rivals. The twin-turbo V6 delivers respectable highway efficiency but lags slightly behind key competitors in overall economy. Real-world performance reflects this positioning, with the Aviator favoring power and smoothness over outright efficiency, making it better suited for buyers who prioritize performance and refinement over fuel savings.
interior: Step inside, and the Aviator immediately impresses with its upscale materials and tranquil atmosphere. The design leans toward understated elegance, with high-quality finishes and a clean layout that avoids unnecessary complexity. The front seats are a highlight, especially when equipped with Lincoln’s optional Perfect Position seats, which offer extensive adjustability and even massage functionality. These seats elevate long-distance comfort to a level that few competitors can match. The second row is spacious and comfortable, particularly with captain’s chairs that enhance the premium feel. However, the third row is noticeably tighter, making it more suitable for children or short journeys rather than extended adult use. Cargo space is competitive for the segment, with practical usability across different seating configurations, although the focus on passenger comfort slightly limits maximum capacity compared to some rivals.
technology: The Aviator features a straightforward and user-friendly technology setup, anchored by a 10.1-inch central touchscreen and a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster. The system emphasizes ease of use over visual complexity, making it intuitive even for less tech-savvy users. Wireless connectivity features such as Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with a built-in Wi-Fi hotspot. Higher trims introduce a premium Revel Ultima 3D audio system, delivering an immersive listening experience with exceptional clarity. Lincoln’s approach to technology feels cohesive and practical, avoiding the overcomplication seen in some competitors while still offering modern functionality.
safety: Safety is a strong point for the Aviator, with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance features included as standard. Systems such as forward-collision warning, automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keeping assist provide a solid foundation. More advanced features, including adaptive cruise control with lane centering, automatic lane changes, and self-parking capability, are available through upgraded packages, enhancing convenience during daily driving and long highway journeys.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 6 years / 70,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 4 years / 50,000 miles (Black Label only)
pros: Strong twin-turbo V6 performance, exceptionally comfortable ride quality, refined and elegant cabin, intuitive technology interface.
cons: Third row is cramped, fuel efficiency trails competitors, brand prestige not as strong as European rivals, unconventional controls like piano-key shifter require adjustment.
mn_take: The 2026 Lincoln Aviator delivers a uniquely serene and powerful luxury experience, but its limited third-row space and modest brand prestige hold it back from true segment leadership.

car_name: 2026 Lexus TX Hybrid
overview: The 2026 Lexus TX Hybrid positions itself as a refined, family-focused luxury SUV that blends efficiency with genuine three-row usability. Unlike many rivals that treat the third row as an afterthought, the TX Hybrid emphasizes space, comfort, and long-distance usability, all wrapped in Lexus’s signature calm and insulated driving experience. Built on the same foundation as the Toyota Grand Highlander Hybrid, the TX Hybrid carries a more premium intent, though it doesn’t completely distance itself from its mainstream roots. What it does exceptionally well is deliver a serene, well-appointed cabin, generous passenger room, and a powertrain lineup that balances performance with efficiency. It is not designed to excite in corners or deliver razor-sharp handling; instead, it focuses on making every journey feel effortless, quiet, and composed. The availability of a plug-in hybrid variant further enhances its appeal, offering meaningful electric-only driving capability for short commutes, while still retaining the flexibility of a gasoline engine for longer trips.
pricing:
TX500h F Sport Performance Premium – $71,710
TX500h F Sport Performance Luxury – $74,860
TX550h+ Luxury – $82,060
drivetrain:
The TX Hybrid offers two distinct electrified personalities, each catering to a slightly different buyer. The TX500h models feature a turbocharged 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine paired with dual electric motors, producing a combined 366 horsepower. This setup delivers confident acceleration and feels more than adequate for a vehicle of this size, especially when merging onto highways or carrying a full load of passengers. For those seeking more power and electrification, the TX550h+ plug-in hybrid steps in with a more robust 3.5-liter V6-based system, paired with electric motors to generate an impressive 404 horsepower. This version feels noticeably stronger and more responsive, delivering brisk acceleration for a three-row SUV, with a 0–60 mph time of around 5.2 seconds. Despite the added performance, the TX Hybrid remains firmly tuned for comfort. The suspension absorbs most road imperfections with ease, though rough surfaces can occasionally unsettle the ride—especially in hybrid variants. Handling is competent but never engaging, reinforcing the TX’s role as a relaxed cruiser rather than a sporty contender.

Efficiency is a strong suit, particularly in urban environments where the hybrid system operates most effectively. The TX500h delivers respectable fuel economy for its size, while the TX550h+ plug-in hybrid adds an extra layer of efficiency with its ability to drive on electricity alone. The TX550h+ offers an EPA-estimated 33 miles of all-electric range, making it ideal for daily commutes without using fuel. Once the battery is depleted, it continues to operate as a conventional hybrid, maintaining competitive efficiency within its class.
interior: Inside, the TX Hybrid prioritizes comfort and usability over dramatic design. The cabin may not immediately dazzle with visual flair, but its materials feel premium to the touch, and the overall layout is practical and thoughtfully executed. The front seats are supportive and come standard with heating and ventilation, ensuring comfort across climates. The second row features captain’s chairs as standard, offering excellent space, individual climate controls, and a genuinely premium experience for passengers. The third row, while usable, is best suited for children or shorter trips with adults. Unlike some competitors, however, it is not entirely unusable, making the TX a practical option for families who occasionally need all three rows. Cargo space is another highlight, with generous capacity across configurations. Even with all seats in place, it offers usable storage, and with rows folded, it transforms into a highly versatile hauler.
technology: The TX Hybrid comes equipped with a large 14-inch touchscreen that serves as the centerpiece of the cabin. The system is responsive and relatively intuitive, though some deeper settings require navigating through menus. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with multiple USB-C ports across all three rows, ensuring connectivity for every passenger. Higher trims offer a premium Mark Levinson audio system, which significantly enhances the in-cabin experience with rich and immersive sound quality. Additional available features such as a head-up display, 360-degree camera system, and remote parking assist add to the TX’s modern luxury appeal.
safety: Lexus equips the TX Hybrid with its latest suite of driver-assistance technologies, ensuring a strong emphasis on safety and convenience. Standard systems include adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, and automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection. More advanced features, such as hands-free driving assistance in traffic conditions and automated parking, are available on higher trims, further enhancing the vehicle’s usability in everyday scenarios.

car_name: 2026 Lexus TX
overview: The 2026 Lexus TX is a family-focused luxury SUV that leans heavily into comfort, space, and day-to-day usability rather than performance or visual drama. Positioned as a more road-oriented alternative to the rugged Lexus GX, the TX is built on the same foundation as the Toyota Grand Highlander, but it layers on Lexus’s signature refinement and quietness to create a more premium experience. From the moment you step inside, the TX makes its priorities clear—it is designed to move people in comfort. Unlike many three-row SUVs that compromise the last row, the TX genuinely accommodates adults across all three rows, making it one of the more practical luxury offerings in its class. The ride quality is smooth and composed, effectively isolating passengers from road imperfections and outside noise, which enhances its long-distance touring ability. However, while the TX excels in comfort and practicality, it lacks a sense of excitement. The styling is clean but not particularly striking, and the interior, though pleasant to touch, doesn’t deliver the visual wow factor seen in some European rivals. Still, for buyers seeking a serene, spacious, and dependable luxury SUV, the TX delivers exactly what it promises.

F Sport – $67,460
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the TX350 is powered by a 275-horsepower turbocharged 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission. Front-wheel drive comes standard, while all-wheel drive is available for those who need added traction in varying conditions. In practice, the engine feels adequate rather than exciting. Acceleration is smooth but not particularly quick, and the TX’s size means the powertrain occasionally feels like it’s working hard under load. That said, the tuning is consistent with the vehicle’s overall character—calm, composed, and predictable. On the road, the TX prioritizes ride comfort above all else. The suspension is softly tuned to absorb bumps and imperfections, delivering a plush experience that suits highway cruising and urban commutes alike. Handling is secure but not engaging, and the steering lacks feedback, reinforcing the TX’s focus on relaxed driving rather than spirited performance. For those seeking stronger acceleration and more dynamic capability, the hybrid variants—reviewed separately—offer a more compelling alternative.

Despite its size, the TX350 manages respectable efficiency figures for a three-row luxury SUV. Its turbocharged four-cylinder engine strikes a reasonable balance between performance and fuel consumption, particularly on the highway where it feels most at ease. In real-world driving, the TX tends to perform better during steady cruising than in stop-and-go traffic, making it a strong candidate for long-distance family trips. While it won’t lead the segment in efficiency, it remains competitive and practical for its class.
interior: The cabin of the TX emphasizes comfort and usability over visual flair. While the design may appear conservative at first glance, the materials themselves feel premium to the touch, with soft surfaces and thoughtful ergonomics throughout. The front seats are wide, supportive, and well-suited for long journeys, offering heating and available ventilation. Visibility is excellent, contributing to a confident driving experience. Moving to the second row, buyers can choose between a traditional bench seat or captain’s chairs, both of which provide generous space and comfort for adult passengers. The third row is where the TX truly distinguishes itself. Unlike many competitors, it offers enough legroom and headroom for adults, along with reclining seatbacks that enhance comfort on longer trips. This makes the TX one of the few luxury SUVs where all three rows feel genuinely usable. Cargo space is equally impressive, with ample room behind the third row and a flexible layout that expands significantly when the rear seats are folded. Whether it’s luggage, groceries, or family gear, the TX handles it with ease.
technology: At the center of the dashboard sits a large 14.0-inch touchscreen infotainment system, which serves as the command hub for most vehicle functions. The interface is modern and responsive, though some menus can require a bit of navigation. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, ensuring seamless smartphone integration. Built-in navigation, wireless charging, and multiple USB ports add to the convenience, while the available 21-speaker Mark Levinson sound system elevates the in-cabin experience with rich, high-quality audio. The TX also includes a digital instrument cluster and optional head-up display, helping drivers stay informed without distraction.
safety: Safety remains a strong point for Lexus, and the TX is no exception. It comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance systems designed to enhance both safety and convenience. Features such as adaptive cruise control, lane-centering assist, and automated emergency braking work together seamlessly, making highway driving less stressful and urban navigation more manageable. Additional options like a 360-degree camera system and automated parking further enhance usability in tight spaces.

car_name: 2026 Lexus RZ
overview: The 2026 Lexus RZ represents a significant evolution of Lexus’s first dedicated electric luxury SUV, refining its earlier shortcomings while staying true to the brand’s core philosophy of comfort, serenity, and understated sophistication. Where the previous iteration felt slightly underwhelming in both performance and driving range, the updated RZ arrives with meaningful upgrades to its electric motors and battery technology, transforming it into a far more competitive offering in the compact luxury EV segment. At its heart, the RZ continues to prioritize a calming, near-silent driving experience over outright excitement. The cabin isolates occupants from the outside world with impressive effectiveness, delivering a smooth, almost gliding ride quality that aligns perfectly with Lexus’s reputation. Yet for 2026, there is now a broader spectrum of capability—from the efficient and value-focused RZ350e to the considerably more energetic RZ550e F Sport—giving buyers more choice depending on their preferences. Despite these improvements, the RZ still leans heavily toward comfort rather than practicality or driving engagement. Its coupe-like silhouette, while visually appealing and aerodynamically efficient, slightly compromises cargo versatility, reminding you that this is a design-led luxury EV rather than a purely functional one.

drivetrain:
The 2026 RZ lineup introduces a more diverse and capable range of electric powertrains. The entry-level RZ350e features a single-motor front-wheel-drive setup producing 221 horsepower, delivering smooth and predictable acceleration that suits daily commuting and urban driving. It is not particularly quick, but it feels refined and consistent—qualities that matter more in this segment. Moving up, the RZ450e adopts a dual-motor all-wheel-drive configuration generating 308 horsepower, offering noticeably stronger acceleration and improved traction. This setup enhances confidence in varied driving conditions, particularly in wet or slippery environments.

At the top of the range, the newly introduced RZ550e F Sport brings genuine performance credentials with 402 horsepower. It delivers brisk acceleration and a more engaging driving character, aided by features like simulated gear shifts and paddle shifters. While it still doesn’t rival the sharpness of sport-focused EVs, it adds a layer of excitement that was previously missing from the RZ lineup. Overall, the driving experience remains composed and comfort-oriented, with well-balanced ride and handling characteristics that make long journeys effortless rather than thrilling.

One of the most notable improvements for 2026 lies in the RZ’s enhanced driving range. The RZ350e now offers an estimated range of up to 300 miles, making it far more competitive and alleviating concerns about long-distance usability. The RZ450e follows with approximately 260 miles, while the more performance-focused RZ550e delivers around 225 miles due to its higher power output. Charging capabilities have also been upgraded. The inclusion of an 11-kW onboard AC charger improves home charging speeds, while the adoption of the NACS port enables compatibility with Tesla Supercharger networks—an important advantage in terms of charging infrastructure and convenience. Fast-charging performance is respectable, with the ability to recharge from 10 to 80 percent in roughly 30 minutes under optimal conditions.
interior: Inside, the RZ showcases a minimalist yet luxurious cabin that emphasizes clean design and high-quality materials. Lexus has reduced physical buttons to a minimum, instead relying on a large central touchscreen to control most functions. While this modern approach enhances visual appeal, it may require some acclimatization for traditional users. Material quality remains a highlight, with soft-touch surfaces, synthetic leather, and suede-like finishes creating a premium atmosphere. The seats are exceptionally comfortable, offering excellent support for long-distance travel, and the cabin maintains a quiet, insulated environment even at highway speeds. Rear-seat passengers benefit from generous legroom and adequate headroom, making the RZ a practical choice for small families or executive transport. However, the sloping roofline slightly impacts cargo capacity, making it less versatile than some rivals in terms of storage.
technology: The RZ features a large infotainment display—up to 14.0 inches—serving as the focal point of the dashboard. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with voice command functionality for a more intuitive user experience. A fully digital instrument cluster and available head-up display provide clear driving information, while the optional Mark Levinson premium sound system enhances the in-cabin audio experience with crisp, immersive sound quality. Overall, the technology suite feels modern and well-integrated, though the reliance on touchscreen controls may not appeal to all users.
safety: The RZ comes equipped with Lexus’s comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies, reinforcing its focus on safety and ease of use. Features such as adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assist, and automated emergency braking work seamlessly to reduce driver fatigue and enhance confidence on long journeys. Advanced systems like automated parking are available, further simplifying urban driving and tight parking situations.

car_name: 2026 Lexus RX Hybrid
overview: The 2026 Lexus RX Hybrid refines the RX formula by blending its signature comfort-focused luxury with improved efficiency and a wider range of electrified powertrains. Visually, it retains the same striking presence as its gasoline counterpart, with sharp creases, a bold front fascia, and a sleek, coupe-like silhouette that gives it a modern and upscale road presence. However, beneath its sporty appearance lies a vehicle engineered primarily for tranquility rather than excitement. The RX Hybrid caters to buyers who prioritize a serene driving experience, whisper-quiet cabin isolation, and long-distance comfort. Whether in conventional hybrid or plug-in hybrid form, the RX Hybrid delivers a relaxed, refined character that aligns perfectly with Lexus’s core identity.

The RX Hybrid lineup offers a diverse set of electrified powertrains, each tailored to different priorities. It excels in efficiency and refinement rather than outright performance. Stepping up, the RX500h F Sport Performance introduces a more powerful turbocharged setup producing 366 horsepower. While this variant offers noticeably stronger acceleration, it still stops short of delivering the dynamic engagement its sporty branding suggests. The chassis tuning remains comfort-oriented, prioritizing ride softness over cornering sharpness. The RX450h+ plug-in hybrid combines a 2.5-liter engine with three electric motors to produce 304 horsepower. It offers the added advantage of short-distance electric-only driving, making it ideal for urban commutes. Despite its added power, it maintains the same composed and relaxed driving demeanor. Across all variants, the RX Hybrid emphasizes smoothness, quietness, and ease of use, making it an excellent companion for daily driving and long highway journeys rather than spirited back-road driving.

Efficiency is a key strength of the RX Hybrid. The RX350h leads the range with impressive fuel economy figures, reaching up to 37 mpg in the city and 34 mpg on the highway. The more powerful RX500h trades some efficiency for performance, while the plug-in RX450h+ offers a balance of fuel savings and electric driving capability, making it particularly appealing for short, daily commutes.
interior: Inside, the RX Hybrid delivers a premium environment that feels both modern and calming.
