Both engines are paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission, with rear-wheel drive standard and all-wheel drive optional. The new turbo engine is expected to deliver stronger low-end torque, making it more suitable for both urban driving and off-road scenarios. The V-6, while proven, feels dated in comparison. On the road, the Grand Cherokee L offers a composed and smooth ride, with confident braking and well-weighted steering. Off-road capability remains a strong suit, especially with the available two-speed transfer case and Jeep’s Selec-Terrain system, although the absence of a Trailhawk variant limits its extreme off-road appeal.

Fuel efficiency remains competitive for the segment. The V-6 engine is rated at approximately 19 mpg city and 26 mpg highway (21 mpg combined), while real-world testing has returned around 24 mpg on highways. The new turbocharged engine is expected to improve both efficiency and performance, though official EPA ratings are yet to be released.
interior: Inside, the Grand Cherokee L delivers a spacious and versatile cabin designed for families. The front seats are comfortable and supportive, with a well-laid-out dashboard and high-quality materials in upper trims. The second row benefits from increased legroom compared to the standard model, while the third row is genuinely usable for adults—something many competitors struggle to achieve. Higher trims introduce luxury touches such as quilted leather, open-pore wood, and massaging seats.
technology: The Grand Cherokee L is equipped with a modern infotainment suite, including a 12.4-inch touchscreen as standard. An optional 10.3-inch passenger display adds a premium, tech-forward feel. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with available features like built-in navigation, rear-seat entertainment screens, and a premium 19-speaker McIntosh sound system. car_name: 2026 Jeep Compass Review – Specs, Price, Mileage, Features & Off-Road Capability
overview: The 2026 Jeep Compass continues to serve as the entry point into the Jeep lineup, blending compact SUV practicality with genuine off-road DNA. While rivals like the Honda CR-V and Toyota RAV4 focus more on comfort and efficiency, the Compass leans heavily into its rugged identity—especially in Trailhawk trim. Despite its aging platform, the Compass still delivers a distinctive character with standard all-wheel drive, respectable real-world efficiency, and trail-ready capability that most competitors simply can’t match. However, its dated interior and slightly firm ride quality remind you that a newer generation is overdue.
pricing:

Latitude Altitude – $33,345
Limited – $35,245

The Limited trim strikes the best balance, offering premium features like adaptive cruise control, dual-zone climate control, leatherette upholstery, and a power-adjustable driver’s seat without a significant jump in price.
drivetrain:
The Compass is powered by a 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine producing 200 horsepower, paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive across all trims. Acceleration is adequate, with a 0–60 mph time of around 7.5 seconds, making it competitive within the segment. On-road dynamics are stable and predictable, though steering feedback is limited and the ride can feel firm over uneven surfaces. Where the Compass truly stands out is off-road. The Trailhawk trim adds a more advanced AWD system with a crawler gear and Rock mode, enabling it to tackle challenging terrain with surprising ease—something few compact SUVs can replicate.

The Compass delivers solid efficiency for an AWD-only SUV. EPA estimates sit at around 24 mpg city and 32 mpg highway, while real-world highway testing returned an impressive 35 mpg. This strong real-world efficiency makes it a practical choice for long-distance driving despite its off-road bias.
interior:
Inside, the Compass offers a functional but slightly outdated cabin. The design is clean and straightforward, but material quality and overall refinement fall short of newer competitors. Front seats provide decent comfort and space, while the rear seats offer acceptable legroom, though accommodating three adults can feel tight. Cargo capacity is also below average for the segment, with space for about 17 carry-on bags with the rear seats folded.

Overall, the cabin prioritizes usability over luxury, aligning with the Compass’s rugged personality.
technology: The Compass comes with an 8.4-inch touchscreen as standard, while higher trims get a larger 10.1-inch display with improved functionality. Features include wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, voice recognition, navigation, and multiple USB ports. The system is user-friendly, but graphics and responsiveness are not as advanced as newer rivals. Optional upgrades like a premium Alpine sound system enhance the experience, especially on higher trims.

mn_take: The 2026 Jeep Compass remains a niche but compelling choice—offering genuine off-road ability in a compact SUV, though it lags behind rivals in refinement and modern appeal.

car_name: 2026 Jeep Cherokee Review – Price, Specs, Hybrid Performance, and Features Explained
overview:
The all-new 2026 Jeep Cherokee marks a bold reinvention of one of Jeep’s most recognizable nameplates. Returning after its discontinuation in 2023, the Cherokee re-enters the market as a hybrid-only compact SUV, signaling a decisive shift toward efficiency, refinement, and everyday usability. While previous generations balanced off-road capability with urban practicality, the 2026 model clearly prioritizes comfort, fuel economy, and modern technology. Its design remains unmistakably Jeep, with the signature seven-slot grille and squared-off proportions, but the overall execution is more contemporary and aerodynamic.

This new Cherokee is not aimed at hardcore adventurers—instead, it targets families and urban buyers who want the Jeep identity combined with hybrid efficiency and long-distance comfort.
pricing:
Base (Cherokee 4x4) – $37,590
The entry-level trim is notably well-equipped, reflecting Jeep’s strategy of offering strong value from the start. It includes standard all-wheel drive, a full hybrid powertrain, a 12.3-inch infotainment system, wireless smartphone connectivity, adaptive cruise control, and a comprehensive safety suite. Unlike many rivals, there’s no need to pay extra for AWD or hybrid technology, which enhances its value proposition.

Laredo – $40,590 (Recommended)
The Laredo trim represents the sweet spot in the lineup, adding meaningful comfort and convenience upgrades without a significant price jump. It introduces 18-inch alloy wheels, fog lamps for improved visibility, a 10-way power-adjustable driver’s seat, upgraded cloth upholstery, and additional exterior enhancements. This trim strikes an ideal balance between affordability and everyday usability.

Limited – $42,590
Moving into the premium territory, the Limited trim enhances both comfort and in-cabin experience. It offers available faux leather upholstery, a larger suite of driver-assistance features, upgraded interior finishes, and access to a premium 10-speaker audio system. Buyers seeking a more refined and upscale environment will find this trim appealing.

85th Anniversary – $42,900
This special edition trim celebrates Jeep’s heritage with unique styling elements, exclusive badging, and bundled premium features. It essentially builds on the Limited trim while adding aesthetic distinction and improved value through packaged equipment.

Overland – $45,590 (Top Trim)
The Overland sits at the top of the range, delivering a near-luxury experience within the compact SUV segment. It includes premium interior materials, advanced driver-assistance systems, larger wheels, and optional features such as a panoramic sunroof and enhanced audio system. This trim is designed for buyers who want maximum comfort and technology without stepping into a larger SUV class.
drivetrain:
The 2026 Cherokee introduces an entirely new hybrid powertrain that combines a turbocharged 1.6-liter four-cylinder engine with two electric motors, producing a combined output of 210 horsepower and 230 lb-ft of torque. This setup is paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) and standard all-wheel drive. The driving experience is centered around smoothness and efficiency. The transition between electric and gasoline power is largely seamless, particularly during low-speed city driving, where the electric motors handle a significant portion of the workload. Under heavier acceleration, the gasoline engine becomes more prominent and slightly noisier, but overall refinement remains acceptable for the segment.

Performance is modest, with an estimated 0–60 mph time of just over 8 seconds. However, the Cherokee compensates with a comfortable ride quality and predictable handling. The suspension is tuned for softness, absorbing road imperfections effectively and making it well-suited for long-distance travel. Unlike traditional Jeep models, this Cherokee lacks off-road-focused hardware such as low-range gearing or locking differentials. Instead, it prioritizes on-road composure and everyday usability, though Jeep has hinted that more rugged variants could arrive in the future.

Fuel efficiency is one of the Cherokee’s strongest attributes. The hybrid system delivers EPA-estimated figures of 39 mpg in the city, 35 mpg on the highway, and 37 mpg combined. These numbers are particularly impressive given the standard all-wheel-drive configuration. The efficient powertrain also enables a driving range of over 500 miles on a full tank, making it a practical option for both daily commuting and extended road trips. Compared to its predecessor, the improvement in fuel economy is substantial, reflecting Jeep’s shift toward electrification.
interior:
The interior of the Cherokee has been redesigned with a focus on space, comfort, and usability. The cabin feels more open than before, with improved front-seat dimensions and slightly increased rear-seat legroom. While the increase in rear space may seem modest on paper, it translates into noticeably better comfort for passengers. Material quality varies depending on the trim level. Base models feature more utilitarian finishes, while higher trims introduce faux leather upholstery, improved textures, and additional soft-touch surfaces. Despite these improvements, some lower-quality plastics are still present, particularly in less visible areas.

Comfort features play a significant role in the Cherokee’s appeal. Available ventilated front seats, heated rear seats, and dual-zone climate control enhance the overall experience, especially on longer journeys. Cargo capacity has also seen a meaningful upgrade, with 31 cubic feet of space behind the second row and up to 68 cubic feet with the seats folded. This makes the Cherokee more versatile for family use, road trips, and carrying larger items.
technology: Technology is a key strength of the 2026 Cherokee. Every model comes equipped with a 12.3-inch touchscreen running Jeep’s Uconnect 5 system. The interface is intuitive, responsive, and easy to navigate, making it one of the better infotainment systems in the segment. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, allowing seamless smartphone integration without the need for cables. The system also supports over-the-air updates, ensuring that software and features remain current over time. Additional connectivity features include a smartphone app for remote vehicle access, navigation services, and emergency assistance functions. Higher trims offer a premium 10-speaker audio system, delivering a richer and more immersive sound experience. Overall, the Cherokee’s tech suite strikes an excellent balance between modern functionality and user-friendly operation.
safety: The Cherokee is equipped with a comprehensive suite of standard safety and driver-assistance features. These include adaptive cruise control, automatic emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist detection, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert. These systems work cohesively to enhance driver confidence, particularly in urban environments and highway driving. While it may not offer the most advanced semi-autonomous driving capabilities in the segment, it provides all the essential features expected in a modern compact SUV.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 50,000 miles
Battery Warranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 2 years / unlimited miles
pros: Strong hybrid efficiency, smooth and refined ride quality, and improved practicality make it a compelling everyday SUV.
cons: Lacks true Jeep off-road hardware, interior quality is inconsistent in lower trims, and performance feels modest.
mn_take: A refined, efficiency-first evolution of the Cherokee that prioritizes hybrid comfort and usability over rugged heritage, making it ideal for modern urban SUV buyers.

car_name: 2026 Infiniti QX60 Review: Price, Specs, Features, Mileage, Interior & Luxury SUV Comparison
overview: The 2026 Infiniti QX60 enters the new model year with a refreshed design and a continued focus on delivering accessible luxury in the competitive three-row SUV segment. With its elegant styling, upscale cabin, and family-friendly practicality, the QX60 makes a strong first impression. However, beneath its premium surface lies a driving experience that doesn’t quite match the refinement of its European rivals. Built on a platform shared with the Nissan Pathfinder, the QX60 prioritizes comfort, usability, and value over outright performance. It’s designed for buyers who want a stylish and well-equipped luxury SUV without stepping into significantly higher price brackets. While it may not lead the class in driving dynamics, it remains a compelling option for those prioritizing comfort, features, and overall ease of ownership.
pricing:
The pricing for the 2026 Infiniti QX60 starts at $53,085 and goes up to $69,185 depending on the trim and options.

The base Pure trim begins at $53,085, offering a well-equipped entry point into the luxury SUV space. The Luxe trim, priced at $58,485, stands out as the best value in the lineup, adding a host of premium features that significantly enhance comfort and technology. The newly introduced Sport trim at $63,685 brings a more aggressive visual appeal with unique styling elements and gloss-black accents. At the top, the Autograph trim at $69,185 delivers the most luxurious experience, with high-end materials and exclusive features such as semi-aniline leather and a 20-speaker Klipsch audio system.

For most buyers, the Luxe trim strikes the ideal balance between price and features, offering a near-complete luxury experience without venturing into top-tier pricing.
drivetrain:
Powering the QX60 is a 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine producing 268 horsepower, paired with a nine-speed automatic transmission. Front-wheel drive comes standard, while all-wheel drive is available for those seeking additional traction. 

While the engine is efficient and smooth for everyday driving, it lacks the urgency expected in this segment. Acceleration feels modest, with a 0–60 mph time of around 7.5 seconds, which trails key rivals like the Volvo XC90. The transmission prioritizes fuel efficiency, often shifting early and hesitating to downshift when quick acceleration is needed. The ride quality leans toward the firmer side, which is somewhat surprising for a vehicle positioned as a comfort-oriented luxury SUV. While it remains composed and stable at highway speeds, it doesn’t deliver the plush, refined ride that some competitors offer. That said, for relaxed, family-oriented driving, the QX60 remains perfectly adequate.

Fuel efficiency is one of the QX60’s stronger points in the segment. The front-wheel-drive model is rated at 22 mpg in the city, 28 mpg on the highway, and 24 mpg combined. Opting for all-wheel drive slightly reduces highway efficiency to 27 mpg. These figures make the QX60 relatively competitive among gasoline-powered luxury SUVs, especially considering its size and three-row configuration.
interior: Step inside the QX60, and the cabin immediately impresses with its upscale design and thoughtful layout. Infiniti has focused on creating a serene and premium environment, with high-quality materials, soft-touch surfaces, and elegant design elements throughout. The three-row configuration allows seating for up to seven passengers, while higher trims like the Sport and Autograph feature second-row captain’s chairs, reducing capacity to six but enhancing comfort. The front seats are supportive and well-equipped, with available heating, ventilation, and even massage functions in top trims. Passenger space is generous across all three rows, making it a practical choice for families. Cargo capacity is also commendable, with space for three carry-on suitcases behind the third row, expanding to 13 with the third row folded, and up to 28 with both rear rows down. Overall, the QX60 strikes a strong balance between luxury and practicality.
technology:
Step inside the QX60, and the cabin immediately impresses with its upscale design and thoughtful layout. Infiniti has focused on creating a serene and premium environment, with high-quality materials, soft-touch surfaces, and elegant design elements throughout. The three-row configuration allows seating for up to seven passengers, while higher trims like the Sport and Autograph feature second-row captain’s chairs, reducing capacity to six but enhancing comfort. Passenger space is generous across all three rows, making it a practical choice for families. Overall, the QX60 strikes a strong balance between luxury and practicality.
safety:
Safety is a key strength of the QX60, with a wide array of standard and available driver-assistance features. The SUV has earned a strong five-star overall safety rating from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), reinforcing its family-friendly appeal. Standard features include forward-collision warning with automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, and a suite of essential driver aids designed to enhance everyday safety.

More advanced features are available, including adaptive cruise control with lane-centering capability and a navigation-linked system that can automatically adjust speed based on upcoming curves in the road. A 360-degree camera system further improves visibility, making parking and maneuvering easier in tight spaces. These systems work together to create a comprehensive safety net, ensuring confidence whether driving in the city or on long highway journeys.
warranty: Infiniti offers a competitive warranty package that stands out in certain areas. The limited warranty covers four years or 60,000 miles, which is slightly better than many rivals. More impressively, the powertrain warranty extends to six years or 70,000 miles, providing added peace of mind for long-term ownership. In addition, Infiniti includes complimentary scheduled maintenance for three years or 30,000 miles, a benefit that helps reduce ownership costs and enhances the overall value proposition. This combination of coverage and maintenance support makes the QX60 an attractive option for buyers seeking worry-free ownership.
pros: Elegant styling, upscale and practical interior, strong value with generous standard features.
cons: Elegant styling, upscale and practical interior, strong value with generous standard features.
mn_take: A stylish and well-equipped luxury SUV that prioritizes comfort and value, but falls slightly short of segment leaders in performance and driving refinement.

car_name: 2026 Ineos Grenadier Station Wagon Review – Price, Specs, Off-Road Capability, and Features Explained
overview: The 2026 Ineos Grenadier Station Wagon stands apart in a world increasingly dominated by tech-heavy, comfort-focused SUVs. Instead of chasing luxury trends, it doubles down on old-school mechanical toughness, offering a body-on-frame construction, solid axles, and a utilitarian design inspired by classic off-roaders. This is not an SUV built to impress on city streets—it’s engineered for durability, rugged terrain, and serious adventure. For 2026, improvements to the steering system have made it more manageable on-road, but the Grenadier still prioritizes off-road capability over refinement. It appeals to a niche audience that values mechanical simplicity, durability, and authentic off-road performance over modern luxury.
pricing:
Base – $72,995
Core utilitarian setup with steel wheels, durable interior, full-time 4WD, and minimal luxury features

Trialmaster – $80,995
Off-road focused with BFGoodrich all-terrain tires, snorkel intake, auxiliary battery, and heavy-duty equipment

Fieldmaster – $80,995 (Recommended)
Adds comfort features like leather upholstery, heated seats, upgraded audio, and Safari roof windows

Trialmaster X – $87,990
Fully loaded off-road variant with added accessories, rugged styling, and enhanced expedition readiness
drivetrain:
The Grenadier is powered by a BMW-sourced 3.0-liter turbocharged inline-six engine producing 282 horsepower and 331 lb-ft of torque, paired with an 8-speed automatic transmission. Power is sent to all four wheels through a two-speed transfer case, reinforcing its serious off-road intent. Unlike modern SUVs with terrain management systems, the Grenadier relies on mechanical hardware and driver skill. It comes standard with a locking center differential, while optional front and rear locking differentials enhance capability further. This setup makes it extremely capable off-road but also contributes to its old-school driving feel on pavement, where steering precision and ride comfort lag behind modern rivals.

Acceleration is respectable, with a 0–60 mph time of around 7.3 seconds, but performance is clearly not its primary focus.

The Grenadier excels where most SUVs hesitate. Its rugged ladder-frame chassis, solid axles, and available locking differentials allow it to tackle challenging terrain with confidence. Features like the Rough Pack and Trialmaster trims add serious expedition readiness, including off-road tires and electrical support for accessories. Towing capacity stands at 7716 pounds, which is competitive for the segment and sufficient for hauling trailers, boats, or off-road gear. However, unlike some rivals, it lacks advanced electronic aids, meaning capability depends more on driver expertise.

Efficiency is not a strong point for the Grenadier. EPA estimates sit at around 14–15 mpg city and highway, with real-world highway testing returning approximately 16 mpg. This makes it one of the least fuel-efficient options in its class, but that trade-off is expected given its heavy-duty construction and off-road focus.
interior: Inside, the Grenadier embraces a functional, industrial design rather than luxury. Materials are rugged and built to withstand harsh conditions, with large physical switches and controls that are easy to operate even with gloves—an intentional nod to aviation-inspired ergonomics. While the front seats are comfortable enough, rear-seat space is somewhat limited compared to similarly sized SUVs. The lack of a third row may be a drawback for families, but it allows for a larger cargo area. With 44 cubic feet of space behind the rear seats, practicality remains strong, especially for outdoor adventures.

safety: The Grenadier includes essential safety systems such as automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, parking sensors, and driver drowsiness monitoring. However, it lacks many advanced driver-assistance systems found in rivals, reinforcing its focus on simplicity over sophistication.

Limited Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Maintenance: No complimentary plan; service intervals every 12,000 miles (or 6,000 miles under heavy use)
pros: Exceptional off-road capability, rugged and durable construction, unique retro-inspired design.
cons: Poor fuel efficiency, limited luxury and tech features, on-road driving feels outdated.
mn_take: A hardcore, no-nonsense off-roader that prioritizes durability and capability over comfort, making it a niche but highly capable alternative to modern SUVs.

car_name: 2026 GMC Sierra EV Review – Price, Range, Specs, Performance, and Features Explained
overview: The 2026 GMC Sierra EV emerges as one of the most compelling premium electric pickups on the market, blending traditional truck capability with cutting-edge EV technology. Built on GM’s Ultium platform, it offers a refined, quiet driving experience while still delivering the brute strength expected from a full-size pickup. Compared to its mechanical sibling, the Chevrolet Silverado EV, the Sierra EV leans more toward luxury with enhanced materials, better cabin insulation, and a more upscale design language. With a significantly reduced starting price for 2026 and new trims like the rugged AT4, the Sierra EV now caters to a wider audience—from lifestyle buyers to serious truck users.
pricing:
- Elevation Standard Range – $64,995
Comes with ~283 miles range, 645 hp, AWD, 16.8-inch touchscreen, 11-inch digital cluster, and strong towing capability

- Denali Standard Range – $72,295
Adds premium interior finishes, advanced driver aids, and enhanced comfort features

- Elevation Extended Range – $73,195 (Recommended)
~385 miles range, best value balance with maximum towing capacity (12,500 lbs) and strong feature set

- Denali Extended Range – $80,495
Focuses on luxury with extended range, upgraded materials, and Super Cruise availability 

- AT4 Extended Range – $81,895
Off-road trim with lifted suspension, 35-inch all-terrain tires, additional ground clearance, and rugged styling

- AT4 Max Range – $92,195
Combines off-road hardware with larger battery, up to 725 hp, and improved range

- Denali Max Range – $101,195
Top-spec luxury trim with up to 410 miles of range, 760 hp, and maximum tech and comfort features
drivetrain:
Every Sierra EV comes equipped with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup, delivering instant torque and strong acceleration across all trims. Output ranges from 645 horsepower in Standard Range models to 760 horsepower in the Denali Max Range, making it one of the most powerful trucks in its class. Despite its massive footprint and weight, the Sierra EV feels surprisingly quick, with tested 0–60 mph times around 4.1 seconds, which is sports car territory for a full-size pickup.

On the road, the Sierra EV delivers a smooth and composed ride, aided by its low center of gravity from the battery pack. It handles better than expected for its size, though aggressive throttle inputs can make it feel slightly unsettled due to its sheer mass. The regenerative braking system offers a one-pedal driving mode, enhancing efficiency and ease in urban driving conditions.

The Sierra EV offers three battery configurations, making it adaptable for different buyers. The Standard Range delivers approximately 283 miles, while the Extended Range pushes that to around 385 miles. The Max Range battery tops out at an impressive 410 miles, placing it among the leaders in the electric truck segment. Fast-charging capability is a strong point, with GM claiming the truck can add up to 100 miles of range in just 10 minutes using a high-speed DC fast charger (up to 350 kW). This makes long-distance travel more feasible, especially when combined with its large battery reserves.

The Sierra EV retains the core capability expected from a GMC truck. It offers a maximum towing capacity of up to 12,500 pounds, which is competitive within the segment. The AT4 trims are slightly lower at 12,300 pounds due to their off-road setup. One standout feature is the MultiPro Midgate, which allows the bed to extend into the cabin, enabling the transport of longer items. Additionally, the front trunk (frunk) provides about 11 cubic feet of secure storage, adding practicality not found in traditional pickups.
interior: Inside, the Sierra EV offers a spacious and modern cabin, available exclusively in a crew-cab configuration. The interior is designed to feel airy and quiet, thanks to acoustic glass and additional sound insulation. Higher trims like Denali introduce premium touches such as open-pore wood, leather upholstery, and refined finishes that elevate the experience closer to luxury SUVs. Passenger space is generous, especially in the rear seats, making it a comfortable long-distance cruiser. The innovative midgate further enhances versatility, allowing users to prioritize either passenger space or cargo flexibility depending on their needs.
technology: The Sierra EV features a large 16.8-inch vertical touchscreen paired with an 11-inch digital instrument cluster. The system includes Google built-in services such as navigation, voice assistant, and app integration. While the interface looks modern and offers deep functionality, it notably skips Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, which may be a drawback for users who prefer smartphone mirroring. Other tech highlights include wireless charging, multiple USB ports, over-the-air updates, and advanced vehicle monitoring systems tailored for EV usage.
safety: Safety is a strong suit for the Sierra EV, with a wide range of standard and advanced driver-assistance systems. Features like automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control come standard. Higher trims, particularly Denali, include Super Cruise, GM’s advanced hands-free driving system that allows for extended hands-free operation on compatible highways, enhancing both convenience and long-distance comfort.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Battery & EV Components: 8 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: First scheduled visit covered
pros: Extremely quick acceleration for its size, class-leading range up to 410 miles, premium and quiet cabin experience.
cons: Very heavy and bulky, infotainment lacks Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, top trims are expensive.
mn_take: A bold, premium electric truck that blends luxury with serious capability, making it one of the most well-rounded EV pickups today despite its size and pricing.

car_name: 2026 GMC Sierra HD Review: 2500HD & 3500HD Specs, Pricing, Towing, Features & MotorNation Verdict
overview: The 2026 GMC Sierra HD lineup—comprising the 2500HD and 3500HD—steps in where the standard Sierra 1500 leaves off, delivering serious heavy-duty capability for buyers who need extreme towing, payload, and durability. Built to tackle demanding workloads, these trucks combine brute strength with a surprisingly composed ride quality, making them suitable for both job sites and long highway hauls. While rivals like the Ford Super Duty and Ram HD may edge ahead in outright towing figures and interior polish, the Sierra HD holds its ground with a highly configurable lineup, a powerful Duramax diesel engine, and a growing list of premium features in higher trims. From work-ready Pro models to ultra-luxurious Denali Ultimate variants, the Sierra HD spans a wide spectrum of buyers.
pricing:
The 2026 GMC Sierra HD starts at $49,795 and goes up to $96,995, depending on configuration, trim level, and equipment.
- Pro – $49,795
- SLE – $56,795
- SLT (Recommended) – $67,995
- AT4 – $74,995
- Denali – $77,995
- AT4X – $87,995
- Denali Ultimate – $96,995

The SLT trim offers the best value, blending comfort features like heated seats, remote start, and the versatile MultiPro tailgate with strong capability. Moving higher, the Denali Ultimate introduces a luxury-focused experience, but at a price that begins to rival premium SUVs.
drivetrain:
The Sierra HD is powered by two robust V8 engines, each engineered for heavy-duty applications.

The standard 6.6-liter gasoline V8 produces 401 horsepower and 464 lb-ft of torque, delivering consistent and reliable performance for moderate hauling needs. However, the standout option is the 6.6-liter Duramax turbo-diesel V8, generating an impressive 470 horsepower and a massive 975 lb-ft of torque. Both engines are paired with a smooth-shifting 10-speed automatic transmission, and buyers can choose between rear-wheel drive and four-wheel drive setups. The diesel engine transforms the Sierra HD into a powerhouse, offering effortless acceleration even under load, with a 0–60 mph time of around 6.6 seconds—remarkable for a truck of this size.

Despite its bulk, the Sierra HD delivers a relatively smooth ride for its class, though steering feedback remains vague and maneuverability in tight spaces can be challenging.

Capability is where the Sierra HD truly shines, especially in properly configured variants.

The Sierra 3500HD can tow up to an impressive 36,000 pounds when equipped with the diesel engine, dual rear wheels, and a gooseneck hitch. With a fifth-wheel setup, it can still handle up to 32,000 pounds. Meanwhile, the Sierra 2500HD offers a maximum towing capacity of 22,500 pounds, which is more than sufficient for most heavy-duty needs. Advanced trailering technologies, including a 15-view camera system, make towing large trailers significantly easier and safer.

As expected in the heavy-duty segment, official EPA fuel economy ratings are not available. However, real-world testing of the diesel variant shows highway efficiency of around 17 mpg, which is respectable given the truck’s size and capability. Gas-powered models are expected to return lower efficiency figures, making the diesel the preferred choice for long-distance hauling and towing.
interior:
Inside, the Sierra HD balances durability with comfort, though material quality varies depending on the trim level.

Lower trims focus on functionality with hard-wearing materials, while higher trims like Denali and Denali Ultimate introduce leather upholstery, premium finishes, and advanced comfort features. Crew Cab models provide generous space for passengers, and rear-seat accommodations are spacious enough for adults on long journeys. Storage is practical, with multiple compartments and a highly functional bed featuring steps, lighting, and tie-downs. The MultiPro tailgate adds versatility, making loading and unloading easier.
technology: Technology ranges from basic to advanced depending on the trim. Base models come with a 7.0-inch touchscreen, while higher trims upgrade to an 8.0-inch or a large 13.4-inch display with Google built-in. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are supported across most variants, and a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster is available. Premium trims offer Bose audio systems and additional connectivity features, ensuring a modern driving experience even in a work-focused truck.
safety: The Sierra HD offers essential safety features as standard, but many advanced systems are optional. Standard equipment includes automatic emergency braking, lane-departure warning, and automatic high beams. Optional upgrades add blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, adaptive cruise control, and an advanced multi-camera system designed for towing.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: First scheduled visit covered

The warranty coverage is competitive for the segment, though not class-leading.
pros: Exceptional towing capability, powerful diesel engine, wide range of configurations, relatively smooth ride for a heavy-duty truck.
cons: High top-end pricing, rivals offer better towing and interiors, difficult to maneuver in tight spaces.
mn_take: A capable and versatile heavy-duty truck that excels in real-world towing and usability, but falls short of segment leaders in refinement and overall value.

car_name: 2026 GMC Sierra 1500 Review: Specs, Pricing, Features, Mileage & MotorNation Verdict
overview: The 2026 GMC Sierra 1500 continues to blend traditional American pickup toughness with a layer of premium sophistication that separates it from its work-focused siblings. Positioned above the mechanically similar Chevrolet Silverado, the Sierra leans into refinement, offering a wide spectrum of trims—from barebones work trucks to ultra-luxurious Denali Ultimate variants that rival high-end SUVs in comfort and technology. What makes the Sierra compelling is its sheer versatility. Whether you’re towing heavy loads, venturing off-road, or cruising long highways in near-silence, the Sierra adapts effortlessly. While it may not deliver the most polished ride in the segment, its strong engine lineup, massive cabin space, and advanced tech make it one of the most well-rounded full-size pickups available today.
pricing:
The 2026 GMC Sierra 1500 starts at $39,745 and goes up to $87,690, offering a broad range of configurations tailored for both commercial and premium buyers.
- Pro – $39,745
- SLE – $50,145
- Elevation (Recommended) – $51,945
- SLT – $57,895
- Denali – $69,390
- AT4 – $69,795
- AT4X – $82,395
- Denali Ultimate – $87,690

The Elevation trim strikes the best balance with its bold styling upgrades and strong feature set, while the Denali Ultimate transforms the Sierra into a near-luxury flagship with massaging seats, Super Cruise, and premium materials throughout.
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the Sierra offers one of the most diverse engine lineups in the segment, catering to different needs—from efficiency to outright performance.

The base 2.7-liter turbocharged four-cylinder produces 310 horsepower and an impressive 420 lb-ft of torque, delivering strong low-end pull for daily usability. Moving up, the legendary 5.3-liter V8 offers 355 horsepower, while the range-topping 6.2-liter V8 delivers a robust 420 horsepower, making it the most exciting option for performance enthusiasts. For those prioritizing efficiency and torque, the 3.0-liter Duramax diesel inline-six stands out with 305 horsepower and a massive 495 lb-ft of torque, making it ideal for long-distance towing and highway cruising.

Performance is solid across the board, with the 6.2L V8 powering the Sierra to 0–60 mph in just 5.4 seconds—impressive for a truck of this size. Ride quality, however, leans slightly toward firmness compared to rivals like the Ram 1500, though handling remains composed with controlled body roll.

Fuel efficiency varies significantly depending on the engine choice, cab configuration, and drivetrain. The diesel engine is the most efficient, delivering up to 23 mpg city and 28 mpg highway, making it a standout for long-haul users. The 6.2L V8, while powerful, is less efficient, offering around 15 mpg city and 19 mpg highway. Real-world testing shows the Sierra Denali with the V8 returning around 18 mpg on highways, which is respectable given its size and capability.
interior: Step inside the Sierra, and the experience varies dramatically depending on the trim—but even mid-level models feel thoughtfully designed. Higher trims elevate the cabin with premium materials, open-pore wood, and leather-wrapped surfaces. The Denali Ultimate stands at the pinnacle, offering 16-way power-adjustable massaging front seats, a refined dashboard layout, and exceptional attention to detail. Crew Cab models provide an enormous amount of space, making long journeys exceptionally comfortable for both front and rear passengers. Practicality is equally strong, with clever storage solutions and a multi-function tailgate that enhances usability. The available carbon-fiber-reinforced bed adds both durability and a premium touch.
technology: Technology is a strong suit for the Sierra 1500, especially in higher trims. Most models feature a 13.4-inch touchscreen infotainment system paired with a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster, creating a modern and intuitive cockpit. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with Google built-in services that allow access to navigation, apps, and voice commands. Available upgrades include a Bose premium sound system, wireless charging, and multiple connectivity ports. One of the standout features is Super Cruise, GMC’s hands-free driving system, available on Denali trims and standard on Denali Ultimate—making long highway drives significantly more relaxed.
safety: The Sierra 1500 offers a comprehensive suite of safety and driver-assistance features designed to enhance confidence on and off the road. Standard features include forward-collision warning, automatic emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert. Higher trims introduce advanced features like a multi-camera towing system and hands-free driving with Super Cruise, even while towing.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: First scheduled visit covered

While competitive, the warranty package falls slightly short of some rivals offering longer coverage, but it remains adequate for the segment.
pros: Strong engine lineup, excellent towing capability, spacious and upscale cabin in higher trims, advanced tech features.
cons: Ride not as refined as key rivals, base trims feel less premium, Super Cruise limited to higher variants.
mn_take: A highly versatile and premium-leaning full-size pickup that delivers strong performance, advanced tech, and serious capability, though it falls just short of class-leading ride comfort.

car_name: 2026 GMC Hummer EV Pickup Review: Price, Range, Specs, Performance & Towing
overview: The 2026 GMC Hummer EV Pickup is one of the most outrageous electric trucks ever built, combining brute-force power with futuristic EV technology and serious off-road capability. Massive in size and presence, it redefines what an electric pickup can be, delivering supercar-like acceleration in a vehicle that weighs nearly five tons. Built to challenge traditional perceptions of electric trucks, the Hummer EV Pickup backs up its aggressive styling with staggering performance figures, advanced four-wheel steering, and impressive towing capability. It isn’t designed to be efficient or subtle—instead, it thrives on excess, making it a bold alternative to more conventional electric pickups.
pricing:
The 2026 GMC Hummer EV Pickup lineup offers multiple configurations with significant differences in performance and features:

- EV2X – $99,895 (dual-motor, 570 hp, standard battery ~311 miles range)
- EV3X – $107,995 (tri-motor, 1000 hp, ~314 miles range, higher performance)
- EV3X Carbon Fiber Edition – $121,800 (limited edition with carbon fiber wheels, exclusive styling, and quicker 0–60 performance ~2.8 sec est.)

Optional packages and upgrades:
- Extreme Off-Road Package – Adds 35-inch all-terrain tires, skid plates, locking differentials, underbody cameras, and enhanced suspension hardware
- Larger 24-module battery (EV3X) – Up to ~381 miles range (reduced to ~359 miles with off-road package)
- Off-Road Readiness Package – Includes full-size spare tire and bed-mounted carrier
- Removable roof panels – Adds open-air driving experience
Fully loaded models can easily exceed $120,000+, depending on options and configurations.
drivetrain:
The Hummer EV Pickup delivers extreme performance regardless of configuration. The dual-motor EV2X produces 570 horsepower, while the tri-motor EV3X generates a staggering 1000 horsepower. Acceleration is nothing short of mind-bending. With the Watts to Freedom (WTF) launch mode, the tri-motor variant rockets from 0–60 mph in just 3.3 seconds, making it one of the quickest pickup trucks ever built. The Carbon Fiber Edition pushes this even further with an estimated 2.8-second sprint—territory usually reserved for exotic sports cars.

Despite its size, low-speed maneuverability is surprisingly manageable thanks to rear-wheel steering and CrabWalk mode. However, at higher speeds, its sheer weight becomes evident, and braking performance is a weak point, requiring longer stopping distances than expected.

The Hummer EV Pickup offers strong towing capability, though it varies by configuration. Dual-motor models can tow up to 12,100 pounds, while tri-motor variants are rated between 7,500 and 8,500 pounds. Real-world towing significantly impacts range, with highway tests showing range dropping to around 140 miles when towing a heavy trailer.

Range varies depending on battery size and configuration. Standard models offer around 311–314 miles of range, while the larger battery pack available on the EV3X increases this to approximately 381 miles under ideal conditions. Charging performance is supported by 800-volt architecture, allowing fast charging that can add around 100 miles in about 10–20 minutes depending on conditions. However, due to the massive battery size, full charging sessions can still take considerable time. Efficiency is not a strong suit, with the Hummer EV Pickup returning around 58 MPGe combined—lower than many rivals due to its extreme weight.
interior: Inside, the Hummer EV Pickup blends rugged design with futuristic themes. The cabin features a large crew-cab layout with seating for five and a five-foot bed. Unique design elements inspired by space exploration—such as lunar-themed graphics and textures—add character, while removable roof panels provide an open-air experience similar to a convertible truck. However, interior quality does not fully match its premium price tag, with some materials feeling less upscale than expected. Space is adequate but not class-leading compared to traditional full-size pickups.
technology: The Hummer EV Pickup features a 13.4-inch infotainment system paired with a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster. The interface, developed with Epic Games, offers high-resolution graphics and unique animations, although occasional lag can affect responsiveness. Connectivity features include wireless Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Wi-Fi hotspot, and OnStar services. The truck also supports bidirectional charging, allowing it to power external devices or even a home.
safety: The Hummer EV Pickup comes equipped with a strong suite of safety technologies, including automated emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, blind-spot monitoring, and adaptive cruise control. GM’s Super Cruise hands-free driving system is standard, offering one of the most advanced semi-autonomous driving experiences available in this segment.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Battery Warranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: First service visit covered
pros: Insane acceleration, strong towing capability, advanced off-road tech and standout design.
cons: Very expensive, heavy and inefficient, braking performance could be better, interior quality underwhelming.
mn_take: A wildly powerful and futuristic electric pickup that delivers unmatched performance and presence, but demands compromises in efficiency, price, and refinement.

car_name: 2026 GMC Hummer EV SUV Review: Price, Range, Specs, Interior & Off-Road Capability
overview: The 2026 GMC Hummer EV SUV is one of the most extreme electric SUVs ever built, combining supercar-level acceleration with serious off-road capability and unmistakable road presence. It doesn’t attempt to follow the traditional luxury EV formula—instead, it embraces boldness, excess, and cutting-edge engineering. Built on GM’s advanced electric platform, the Hummer EV SUV delivers massive power, innovative features like CrabWalk and King Crab steering, and a level of off-road hardware that rivals purpose-built 4x4s. It’s not subtle, efficient, or lightweight—but that’s exactly the point. This is an EV designed to dominate attention as much as terrain.
pricing:
The 2026 GMC Hummer EV SUV lineup is relatively simple but packed with features, and pricing varies depending on configuration, packages, and performance upgrades. 

The base 2X trim starts at around $97,200–$99,895, depending on configuration and market adjustments, making it the entry point into the Hummer EV SUV lineup. The 3X trim starts at approximately $105,300–$107,995, adding a third motor, significantly higher performance, and additional off-road capability.

In real-world scenarios, pricing can go well beyond these figures depending on options:
- The Extreme Off-Road Package adds specialized hardware like 35-inch tires, skid plates, locking differentials, and underbody cameras.
- The Carbon Fiber Edition (3X only) introduces exclusive styling, carbon-fiber wheels, and enhanced performance tuning, pushing acceleration figures even further.
- Fully loaded models or dealer-adjusted pricing can push the SUV well into the $110,000+ range, especially with premium packages and accessories.

Even the base 2X comes heavily equipped with large wheels, four-wheel steering, advanced infotainment, and off-road capability, making it far from “entry-level” in real-world terms.
drivetrain:
Performance is where the Hummer EV SUV dominates. The 2X trim uses a dual-motor setup producing 570 horsepower, while the 3X features a tri-motor system delivering up to 830 horsepower. Acceleration is astonishing for a vehicle of this size, with 0–60 mph times around 3.4 seconds. The sheer force of acceleration makes it feel more like a supercar than a traditional SUV. Advanced features like four-wheel steering, CrabWalk, and King Crab mode allow this massive SUV to maneuver in ways that defy its size, especially in off-road situations. Combined with adjustable air suspension and Extract mode, it becomes one of the most capable electric off-roaders available.

The Hummer EV SUV offers an EPA-estimated range of up to around 315 miles, supported by a massive battery pack. Charging performance is strong thanks to its 800-volt architecture, enabling rapid charging that can add roughly 100 miles of range in about 14 minutes under ideal conditions. It also supports bidirectional charging, allowing it to power homes, tools, or even other EVs—an increasingly valuable feature in modern EV ownership.
interior:
Inside, the Hummer EV SUV blends rugged design with futuristic elements. The cabin features large digital displays, bold shapes, and a mix of physical controls and touchscreen interfaces. While visually impressive, some interior materials fall short of expectations at this price point. However, unique features like the removable Infinity Roof panels elevate the experience, offering an open-air driving feel rarely found in SUVs.

Passenger space is generous, and cargo capacity is substantial, although the high loading floor can make practicality slightly challenging when handling heavy items.
technology: The SUV comes equipped with a large 13.4-inch infotainment system, advanced navigation including off-road mapping, wireless connectivity, and a premium Bose sound system. One standout feature is its ability to function as a mobile power source, thanks to its onboard generator and bidirectional charging capabilities—turning the Hummer into more than just a vehicle.
safety: The Hummer EV SUV includes a comprehensive suite of safety technologies such as automatic emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control. It also offers GM’s Super Cruise hands-free driving system, one of the most advanced driver-assistance systems currently available, enhancing long-distance comfort and usability.
warranty: Warranty coverage includes a three-year/36,000-mile limited warranty, a five-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty, and an eight-year/100,000-mile battery warranty. Complimentary maintenance is limited to the first visit.
pros: Explosive performance, unmatched road presence, advanced off-road tech with unique features like CrabWalk and removable roof.
cons: Extremely expensive, heavy and inefficient, interior quality not fully premium for the price.
mn_take: A bold, over-the-top electric SUV that delivers insane performance and off-road capability, but trades efficiency and practicality for pure spectacle.

car_name: 2027 GMC Acadia Review: Big Space, Bold Looks, but Lacking True Premium Feel
overview:
The 2027 GMC Acadia positions itself as a more premium alternative within General Motors’ midsize three-row SUV lineup, sitting above its sibling, the Chevrolet Traverse. With bold GMC styling, a spacious cabin, and a strong list of standard features, the Acadia makes a solid first impression. However, beneath the surface, it struggles to fully justify its premium positioning in a segment filled with highly polished rivals like the Kia Telluride and Mazda CX-90.

Redesigned recently and carried forward unchanged for 2027, the Acadia leans heavily into comfort, practicality, and rugged design—especially in AT4 guise—rather than delivering an engaging or refined driving experience. It’s a capable family SUV, but not necessarily the most compelling one in its class.
pricing:
The 2027 Acadia spans a wide pricing spectrum, offering a mix of value-oriented and near-luxury trims. While it starts competitively, higher trims begin to overlap with more refined and better-performing competitors, making value perception more dependent on buyer priorities.

- Elevation – $46,000 (est)
- AT4 – $55,000 (est)
- Denali – $58,000 (est)
- Denali Ultimate – $66,000 (est)

The Elevation trim stands out as the best value, offering a generous list of standard equipment including a surround-view camera, heated front seats, heated steering wheel, power-adjustable driver’s seat, and a hands-free tailgate. Moving up the range introduces more luxury elements such as leather upholstery, advanced driver aids, and premium audio systems, but the price climbs quickly into territory where stronger rivals exist.
drivetrain:
Under the hood, every Acadia is powered by a 2.5-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine producing 328 horsepower, paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission. Front-wheel drive is standard, while all-wheel drive is optional on most trims and standard on the off-road-focused AT4. On paper, the output looks strong, but in practice, the engine lacks the smoothness and refinement expected from a premium-oriented SUV. Acceleration is adequate, with a 0–60 mph time estimated between 6.5 and 6.7 seconds, but the power delivery feels less polished compared to rivals offering V-6 engines or more refined turbo setups.

The ride quality is comfortable and well-suited for long-distance cruising, and the Acadia feels stable and composed on highways. However, driving dynamics remain uninspiring, with limited engagement and feedback. The AT4 trim adds some off-road credibility with features like Active Torque Control AWD, increased ground clearance, skid plates, and terrain modes, making it a better choice for adventurous buyers.

The Acadia delivers solid capability for its class, with a maximum towing capacity of 5,000 pounds. The standard trailering package includes a Class III hitch, heavy-duty cooling system, hitch guidance with camera integration, and a seven-pin wiring harness. This puts it on par with key competitors, making it suitable for towing small trailers, boats, or recreational equipment without breaking a sweat.

Fuel efficiency is average for the segment, with front-wheel-drive models rated at 20 mpg city and 26 mpg highway, while all-wheel-drive variants return 20 mpg city and 23 mpg highway. These figures place the Acadia squarely in the middle of the pack, neither excelling nor disappointing, but reinforcing its role as a practical rather than performance-focused SUV.
interior:
Inside, the Acadia delivers one of its strongest performances, offering a spacious and flexible cabin designed with families in mind. The first row comes well-equipped even in base trims, with heated seats, a heated steering wheel, and triple-zone climate control. Higher trims introduce ventilated seats, leather upholstery, and additional premium touches. The second row offers generous space and comfort, especially when equipped with available captain’s chairs, which enhance the sense of luxury and improve accessibility to the third row via GMC’s Smart Slide feature.

The third row is usable but not particularly plush, with limited cushioning and support compared to the front rows—best suited for shorter trips or younger passengers. Cargo space is practical, with 23 cubic feet available behind the third row, and flexible seating configurations allow for easy expansion when carrying larger loads.
technology: The Acadia features a modern and user-friendly tech setup centered around a vertically oriented 15-inch touchscreen paired with an 11-inch digital instrument cluster. The system runs Google built-in software, offering intuitive navigation, voice control, and app integration. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with wireless charging and multiple connectivity options, including USB ports in all three rows and household-style power outlets. Audio quality is strong, with a standard Bose system and an upgraded 16-speaker version available on higher trims. Features like a head-up display and customizable interface layouts further enhance the tech experience, making the Acadia competitive in this area.
safety:
Safety is a key strength for the Acadia, with a comprehensive suite of standard driver-assistance features. These include automated emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist detection, lane-keeping assist, blind-spot monitoring, and adaptive cruise control. One standout feature is the availability of GM’s Super Cruise system, one of the most advanced hands-free driving technologies currently available. It allows for hands-free highway driving on compatible roads, significantly enhancing long-distance comfort and convenience.

Overall, the Acadia provides strong safety credentials, though many rivals now offer similarly advanced systems as standard.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: First visit covered

While adequate, the warranty package falls short compared to competitors like Hyundai and Kia, which offer significantly longer coverage periods.
pros: Spacious and comfortable cabin, bold styling, solid towing capability, strong tech features.
cons: Powertrain lacks refinement, driving dynamics are uninspiring, expensive compared to similarly equipped rivals.
mn_take: A practical and stylish three-row SUV that delivers comfort and tech but falls short of true premium refinement in a highly competitive segment.

car_name: 2026 Genesis GV80 Review: Flagship Luxury Without the Flagship Price Tag
overview: The 2026 Genesis GV80 continues to assert itself as one of the most compelling alternatives to established European luxury SUVs like the BMW X5 and Porsche Cayenne. With a perfect 10/10 rating, it blends high-end craftsmanship, modern technology, and serene road manners into a package that undercuts its rivals significantly on price. For 2026, Genesis expands the GV80 lineup with a newly introduced rear-wheel-drive base model, making entry into the brand more accessible. At the same time, enhancements such as broader third-row availability, improved feature packaging, and terrain drive modes for AWD variants further elevate its appeal. The GV80 doesn’t try to be the sportiest SUV in the segment—instead, it leans into comfort, refinement, and luxury, and executes that philosophy exceptionally well.
pricing:
The 2026 GV80 delivers exceptional value across its lineup, offering a wide range of trims that cater to both entry-level luxury buyers and those seeking near-ultra-luxury experiences. Even at its highest price point, it remains significantly more affordable than similarly equipped German rivals, while offering comparable—if not superior—features and materials.

- 2.5T – $59,195
- 2.5T Select – $65,245
- 2.5T Advanced – $70,095
- 2.5T Prestige – $74,995
- 3.5T Advanced – $77,445
- 3.5T Prestige – $83,825
- 3.5T Prestige Black – $85,395

The sweet spot in the range is the 3.5T Advanced trim, which combines the powerful V-6 engine with high-end features such as adaptive suspension, leather upholstery, four-zone climate control, and a full suite of driver-assistance systems—delivering a near flagship-level experience without breaching six figures.
drivetrain:
The GV80 offers two refined engine choices, each tailored to a different type of luxury buyer. The base 2.5-liter turbocharged four-cylinder produces 300 horsepower and is now available with rear-wheel drive, improving affordability while still delivering adequate performance for everyday driving. For those seeking more effortless power, the twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V-6 generates 375 horsepower and transforms the GV80 into a more authoritative cruiser. Acceleration figures of 0–60 mph in 5.7 seconds for the V-6 (and 6.1 seconds for the four-cylinder) are respectable, though not class-leading.

Where the GV80 truly excels is in ride quality. The available road-scanning adaptive suspension reads the road surface ahead and adjusts damping in real time, resulting in an exceptionally smooth and composed ride. The SUV feels planted and predictable, prioritizing comfort over aggressive cornering—making it ideal for long-distance cruising rather than spirited driving.

Fuel efficiency is competitive for the segment, though not groundbreaking. The 2.5T rear-wheel-drive variant achieves up to 20 mpg city and 26 mpg highway, while all-wheel-drive versions see a slight drop. Opting for the V-6 engine reduces efficiency to around 16 mpg city and 22 mpg highway. Real-world testing shows the GV80 slightly exceeding expectations, with the AWD 2.5T returning 25 mpg on highway runs, reinforcing its capability as a comfortable long-distance tourer.
interior:
Step inside the GV80, and it immediately becomes clear why this SUV stands out. The cabin is meticulously crafted with premium materials, including genuine wood trims, brushed metal accents, and soft-touch surfaces throughout. Genesis’s “Mood Curator” system adds a unique sensory experience by adjusting ambient lighting, music, and even fragrance to match the driver’s chosen setting. The front seats are exceptionally comfortable and available with heating, ventilation, and massage functions, making long journeys effortless. The second row offers generous legroom and excellent cushioning, ensuring passengers enjoy the same level of luxury as those in the front.

An optional third row is available, though it’s best suited for children due to limited space. Cargo capacity is impressive, with the GV80 accommodating up to 28 carry-on suitcases with the rear seats folded. Even with all seats in place, practicality remains strong for everyday use.
technology: Technology is one of the GV80’s strongest areas, highlighted by a stunning 27.0-inch OLED display that seamlessly integrates the digital instrument cluster and infotainment system. The interface is crisp, responsive, and visually impressive, offering a truly modern luxury experience. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with a Wi-Fi hotspot and wireless charging. The infotainment system can be controlled via touchscreen or a rotary controller, providing flexibility depending on driver preference. Audio quality is equally impressive, with a standard 12-speaker setup and an available 18-speaker Bang & Olufsen system delivering rich, immersive sound. Features like a head-up display, digital key functionality, and over-the-air updates further enhance the tech-forward appeal.
safety:
Genesis equips the GV80 with one of the most comprehensive safety suites in its class. Standard features include adaptive cruise control with semi-autonomous driving capability, lane-keeping assist, blind-spot monitoring, and front and rear parking sensors. The system is tuned for smooth, natural operation, making highway driving less stressful. Optional upgrades such as a 360-degree camera system and advanced parking assist further enhance convenience and safety.

With top-tier crash-test ratings and advanced driver-assistance systems, the GV80 delivers strong confidence behind the wheel, whether navigating city traffic or long highway journeys.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 10 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 36,000 miles

Genesis continues to lead the luxury segment with one of the best warranty packages available, significantly outperforming most European competitors and adding long-term peace of mind.
pros: Ultra-luxurious interior, exceptional ride comfort, advanced technology, strong value proposition.
cons: Not as sporty as rivals, third row is cramped, fuel economy drops with V-6.
mn_take: A near-perfect luxury SUV that prioritizes comfort, technology, and value—making it one of the smartest alternatives to traditional European flagships.

car_name: 2027 Genesis GV70 Review: A Perfect Blend of Style, Refinement, and Everyday Luxury
overview:
The 2027 Genesis GV70 continues to define what a modern compact luxury SUV should feel like—effortlessly stylish, quietly refined, and thoughtfully engineered. It stands confidently alongside established rivals such as the Porsche Macan and Audi Q5, but instead of chasing outright sportiness or badge prestige, the GV70 leans into delivering a more complete and well-rounded ownership experience.

What makes the GV70 particularly appealing is how it balances its personality. It looks bold and contemporary on the outside, yet inside it feels warm, inviting, and unmistakably premium. For 2027, the introduction of the Prestige Graphite trim adds a darker, more aggressive aesthetic with exclusive wheels, subtle chrome accents, and a more bespoke interior finish, further elevating its desirability.
pricing:
- 2.5T – $51,000 (est)
- 2.5T Select – $54,000 (est)
- 2.5T Advanced – $58,000 (est)
- 2.5T Sport Prestige – $62,000 (est)
- 3.5T Sport Advanced (Recommended) – $66,000 (est)
- 3.5T Sport Prestige – $73,000 (est)
- 3.5T Graphite Prestige – $73,000 (est)

Even before stepping into higher trims, the GV70 feels generously equipped, which is where Genesis continues to outshine many competitors. As you move up the lineup, the experience becomes noticeably richer—adding finer materials, advanced comfort features, and premium audio systems that elevate the SUV into near-flagship territory. The pricing strategy feels carefully calibrated, ensuring that buyers get a luxury experience without stretching into the higher cost brackets typically associated with European rivals.
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the GV70 offers two powertrains that emphasize smoothness and refinement over outright aggression. The base 2.5-liter turbocharged engine produces 300 horsepower and feels lively enough for everyday driving, delivering strong mid-range performance and a composed demeanor. For those seeking more effortless acceleration, the twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6, with 375 horsepower, adds a layer of muscular performance that transforms the SUV into a genuinely quick machine. Both engines are paired with an 8-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive, ensuring consistent traction and confidence across varying road conditions. The V6-powered models can reach 60 mph in around 5.0 seconds, making them impressively quick for the segment.

On the road, the GV70 strikes a fine balance. It isn’t as razor-sharp as the Porsche Macan, but it compensates with a smoother ride, quieter cabin, and more relaxed driving character. It feels equally at home carving through a winding road or gliding along the highway during long commutes.

Efficiency remains competitive, with the four-cylinder model offering up to 28 mpg on the highway, while the V6 delivers respectable figures for its performance level. In real-world conditions, the GV70 manages to stay practical enough for daily use without compromising its premium character.
interior:
Step inside the GV70, and it becomes immediately clear that Genesis has prioritized craftsmanship and design. The cabin feels carefully curated rather than simply assembled, with sweeping lines that mirror the exterior styling and create a cohesive visual flow. The centerpiece is the expansive 27-inch integrated display, which stretches elegantly across the dashboard, combining the instrument cluster and infotainment system into a single, seamless unit. Surrounding it are high-quality materials—soft-touch surfaces, finely stitched leather, and metallic accents—that give the interior a genuinely upscale feel.

Front seats are plush and supportive, designed for long-distance comfort, while available features such as heating, ventilation, and premium upholstery enhance the experience further. The second row is comfortable and flexible, though not the most spacious in the segment due to the GV70’s sleek proportions. Cargo space is practical for daily needs, offering 27 cubic feet behind the rear seats and expanding to 59 cubic feet when folded. It’s not class-leading, but it strikes a good balance between usability and design.
technology: The GV70’s technology suite feels modern without being overwhelming. The large 27-inch display is sharp, responsive, and easy to navigate, supported by both touch inputs and a rotary controller that adds convenience while driving. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with multiple connectivity options and an available Bang & Olufsen sound system that delivers a rich and immersive audio experience. Features like the digital key, which allows smartphone-based access, reflect Genesis’s focus on integrating everyday convenience into the luxury experience.
safety: Safety is another area where the GV70 delivers confidently. A comprehensive suite of driver-assistance systems comes standard, including forward collision warning with emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, and blind-spot monitoring. More advanced features, such as adaptive cruise control with lane-centering, enhance long-distance driving comfort and reduce fatigue. The overall safety package feels robust and well-integrated, contributing to the SUV’s sense of security and ease of use.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 10 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 36,000 miles

Genesis continues to lead the segment with its ownership benefits, offering peace of mind that few competitors can match.
pros: Elegant design, refined performance, premium interior quality, excellent value, advanced tech features.
cons: Not as sporty as key rivals, no hybrid option, slightly tight rear space.
mn_take: A beautifully balanced luxury SUV that prioritizes comfort, design, and value, making it one of the most compelling all-rounders in the compact premium segment.

car_name: 2026 Genesis GV60 Review: Futuristic Luxury Meets Everyday Electric Performance
overview: The 2026 Genesis GV60 stands out as one of the most distinctive offerings in the compact luxury EV space. With its quirky, almost concept-car-like styling and a cabin packed with futuristic tech, it takes a different approach compared to more traditional rivals. Underneath its unique design, however, lies proven electric architecture shared with the Hyundai Ioniq 5, giving it strong fundamentals in performance, efficiency, and charging capability. What makes the GV60 particularly appealing is how it blends luxury with innovation. It doesn’t just rely on performance numbers or range figures—it creates an experience. From biometric access to its signature crystal sphere shifter, this is a car designed to feel modern and different. At the same time, it delivers refined road manners and quick acceleration, making it both exciting and easy to live with. For 2026, Genesis has refined the formula with updated styling, a larger 84.0-kWh battery, improved driving range, and a new 27-inch widescreen display that enhances the already tech-forward cabin.
pricing:
The GV60 is positioned as an entry point into Genesis’s electric luxury lineup, but it still carries a premium feel across all variants. The pricing structure reflects a balance between accessibility and high-end equipment, making it competitive against both mainstream and luxury EV rivals.

- Standard – $54,020
- Advanced (Recommended) – $60,900
- Performance – $73,370

What stands out here is the value proposition. Even the base model comes well-equipped, while the Advanced trim adds meaningful luxury features such as ventilated seats, a premium audio system, and advanced driver aids. The Performance trim, on the other hand, is aimed at enthusiasts, offering significantly higher output and sportier hardware—but at the cost of reduced driving range. Overall, the GV60’s pricing strategy makes it one of the more accessible premium EVs without feeling stripped down.
drivetrain:
The GV60 offers multiple powertrain configurations, catering to both efficiency-focused buyers and performance enthusiasts. The base rear-wheel-drive model produces 225 horsepower, while all-wheel-drive variants step up to 314 horsepower. At the top of the range, the Performance trim delivers 429 horsepower, which can be temporarily boosted to 483 horsepower using Boost mode. This results in a 0–60 mph time of just 3.7 seconds, placing it firmly among the quicker EVs in its segment. On the road, the GV60 feels refined and composed. The ride quality is smooth, and the cabin remains impressively quiet, even at higher speeds. The Performance variant adds adaptive suspension and an electronic rear differential, giving it more engaging handling characteristics. While it can be fun on twisty roads, it still doesn’t quite match the sharpness of rivals like the Porsche Macan Electric. What the GV60 does exceptionally well is balance comfort with capability—it’s enjoyable to drive without ever feeling demanding.

For 2026, the GV60 receives a larger 84.0-kWh battery pack, which improves both range and usability.
- Maximum range: 306 miles (RWD)
- AWD range: up to ~280 miles (varies by trim)
- Performance trim: 252 miles
These figures make the GV60 competitive, especially in rear-wheel-drive form. However, opting for higher performance trims does reduce range, which is something buyers will need to consider.

Charging is where the GV60 truly shines. Thanks to its 800-volt architecture, it supports ultra-fast DC charging:
- 10–80% charge: ~18 minutes
- Level 2 (AC) full charge: ~7 hours
Real-world testing confirms these claims, making the GV60 one of the fastest-charging EVs in its class. This significantly enhances convenience, especially for long-distance travel.
interior:
Step inside the GV60, and it becomes clear that Genesis wanted to create something different. The cabin feels modern, almost futuristic, with unique design elements that set it apart from the more traditional interiors of the Genesis GV70 and Genesis GV80. The highlight is the crystal sphere gear selector, which rotates to reveal the drive controls—a feature that’s as much a design statement as it is a functional element. The GV60 also introduces biometric technology, allowing drivers to unlock and start the car using facial recognition and fingerprint authentication. Material quality is excellent, with soft-touch surfaces, premium leather, and metallic accents throughout the cabin. The seats are comfortable and supportive, making it well-suited for long drives. However, practicality is where the GV60 falls slightly short. Rear-seat space is tighter than some rivals, and cargo capacity is modest:
- 25 cubic feet behind rear seats
- Small front trunk (0.71 cubic feet)
- 7 carry-on bags capacity in testing

While it’s perfectly usable for daily life, it’s not the most spacious option in the segment.
technology:
The 2026 GV60 takes a significant step forward in technology with the introduction of a 27-inch widescreen display that seamlessly integrates the instrument cluster and infotainment system. The layout is clean, modern, and highly intuitive. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with a wireless charging pad and multiple connectivity options. The system is responsive and easy to use, supported by both touchscreen inputs and a rotary controller on the center console. Higher trims include a Bang & Olufsen premium audio system, delivering rich and immersive sound quality. The GV60 also offers over-the-air updates, ensuring the system remains up-to-date over time.

Overall, the technology experience feels cutting-edge without being overwhelming, striking a good balance between innovation and usability.
safety: The GV60 comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance features as standard. These systems are designed to enhance safety without intruding on the driving experience. Key features include automated emergency braking, blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control with lane-centering. The vehicle has also received strong crash-test ratings, reinforcing its position as a safe and dependable luxury EV. Advanced parking assistance and surround-view cameras further improve ease of use in urban environments.
warranty:
Limited Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
Powertrain Warranty: 10 years / 100,000 miles
Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 36,000 miles

Genesis continues to lead in warranty coverage, offering long-term peace of mind that surpasses most luxury competitors.
pros: Premium and futuristic cabin, quick acceleration with Boost mode, ultra-fast charging capability, strong value for a luxury EV.
cons: Limited rear space and cargo capacity, performance trims sacrifice range, small front trunk reduces practicality.
mn_take: The 2026 Genesis GV60 is a bold, tech-forward luxury EV that delivers strong performance and standout design, making it perfect for buyers who value innovation and style over outright practicality.

car_name: 2026 Genesis Electrified GV70 Review: A Refined Electric Luxury SUV with Serious Pace
overview:
The 2026 Genesis Electrified GV70 takes everything that made the standard GV70 such a compelling luxury SUV and elevates it with a fully electric powertrain. It’s a vehicle that doesn’t try to reinvent the EV formula but instead refines it—offering strong performance, exceptional interior quality, and a quiet, composed driving experience that feels genuinely premium. With 483 horsepower on tap and a 0–60 mph time of just 3.8 seconds, the Electrified GV70 is undeniably quick. Yet, unlike performance-oriented rivals such as the Porsche Macan Electric, it focuses more on comfort and everyday usability rather than razor-sharp handling. This makes it an ideal choice for buyers who want an EV that feels luxurious first and sporty second.

For 2026, Genesis has refined the formula further with subtle exterior updates, a redesigned interior featuring a massive 27-inch OLED display, and a slightly larger battery pack that improves range. While it may not lead the segment in outright efficiency, it compensates with fast charging and a richly appointed cabin.
pricing:
The Electrified GV70 sits firmly in the premium segment, but it still manages to offer strong value compared to its European competitors. Genesis has positioned it as a well-equipped luxury SUV right from the base trim, ensuring buyers don’t feel shortchanged even at the entry level.
- Base – $65,875
- Advanced (Recommended) – $70,745
- Prestige – $76,845
