safety: Despite its focus on extreme capability, the Bronco Raptor doesn’t compromise on safety. It comes equipped with a comprehensive set of driver-assistance features, including adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, lane-keeping assist, and a 360-degree camera system. These systems not only enhance on-road safety but also prove useful in off-road situations, where visibility and situational awareness are crucial.
warranty: Despite its focus on extreme capability, the Bronco Raptor doesn’t compromise on safety. It comes equipped with a comprehensive set of driver-assistance features, including adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, lane-keeping assist, and a 360-degree camera system. These systems not only enhance on-road safety but also prove useful in off-road situations, where visibility and situational awareness are crucial.
pros: Exceptional off-road capability, powerful twin-turbo performance, and surprisingly comfortable for daily driving.
cons: Poor fuel economy, high price tag, and noticeable wind noise at highway speeds.
mn_take: An extreme, no-compromise off-road SUV that delivers race-level capability while remaining usable enough for everyday life, making it one of the most exciting adventure vehicles on sale today.

car_name: 2026 Ford Bronco Review: Pricing, Specs, Off-Road Capability, Interior, Features, Safety and Warranty
overview:
The Ford Bronco remains one of the most capable and characterful off-road SUVs on the market, blending rugged capability with everyday usability. Built by Ford Motor Company, the Bronco is designed as a true go-anywhere machine—equally comfortable tackling dunes, rocky trails, or daily commutes. Revived in its modern form with strong retro-inspired styling, the Bronco stands out with its boxy design, removable doors and roof, and a wide range of trims tailored for different types of adventure seekers. Whether you’re into hardcore off-roading or simply want an SUV with strong road presence, the Bronco offers a highly customizable experience.

For 2026, Ford celebrates the model’s legacy with a special 60th Anniversary Edition, adding exclusive styling elements and heritage-inspired touches. Despite its rugged focus, the Bronco also delivers decent comfort and technology, making it more livable than traditional off-roaders.
pricing:
The 2026 Ford Bronco starts at $42,490 and goes up to $71,990, depending on the trim and equipment.

The lineup begins with the Base trim at $42,490, offering essential off-road capability and core features. Just above it, the Big Bend starts at $42,990, adding convenience features and improved interior touches.

A strong mid-range option is the Black Diamond, starting at $47,485, which enhances durability with steel bumpers, skid plates, and off-road-ready hardware. The Outer Banks, priced from $50,085, leans more toward comfort and style, while the Badlands, starting at $50,885, focuses on serious off-road performance.

For those seeking a nostalgic design, the Heritage Edition begins at $53,620, while the exclusive 60th Anniversary Edition comes in at $61,545, featuring unique badging and styling upgrades.

At the top of the range, the Stroppe Edition starts at $71,990, delivering a bold design and enhanced off-road credentials.
drivetrain:
The Bronco offers two engine choices, both designed to deliver strong off-road capability and respectable on-road performance.

The base engine is a turbocharged 2.3-liter four-cylinder, producing 300 horsepower. It can be paired with either a 7-speed manual transmission—a rare offering in today’s SUV market—or a 10-speed automatic transmission. For more power, the Bronco offers a twin-turbocharged 2.7-liter V6, delivering 330 horsepower. This engine comes exclusively with the 10-speed automatic transmission and provides stronger acceleration and better performance for highway driving and heavy off-road use.

All Bronco models come standard with four-wheel drive, reinforcing its off-road-focused design. The system must be manually engaged for off-road driving and disengaged for regular road use. Performance varies by configuration, but testing shows the V6-powered Bronco can reach 0–60 mph in about 6.2 seconds, while the four-cylinder models range between 7.1 to 7.4 seconds. What truly sets the Bronco apart is its off-road hardware. Features such as 35-inch mud-terrain tires, locking front and rear differentials, beadlock-capable wheels, and an electronic sway-bar disconnect system allow it to tackle extreme terrain with confidence.

Fuel economy is not the Bronco’s primary focus, but it remains reasonable for a vehicle of its capability. The turbocharged four-cylinder engine delivers up to 18 mpg in the city and 22 mpg on the highway with the automatic transmission. Opting for the manual gearbox slightly reduces efficiency. The V6 engine returns approximately 19 mpg city and 21 mpg highway, depending on configuration. Models equipped with heavy off-road packages, such as the Sasquatch package, tend to see fuel economy drop into the mid-to-high teens.
interior:
Inside, the Bronco prioritizes durability over luxury, which aligns with its rugged purpose.

The cabin features a utilitarian design with extensive use of hard plastics. While this may not feel premium, it ensures the interior can withstand dirt, water, and rough usage. Ford also offers rubberized flooring and marine-grade vinyl upholstery, ideal for buyers who plan to take their Bronco into harsh environments. Front seats are spacious and comfortable, even for taller occupants, making long drives manageable. The second row offers enough space for adults, especially in the four-door model, which provides significantly more legroom. One of the Bronco’s standout features is its removable doors and roof, allowing for an open-air driving experience similar to classic off-road vehicles. However, this design leads to increased wind noise at highway speeds, which can affect long-distance comfort. Cargo space is practical, especially in the four-door version, which can accommodate large items—including the removable doors themselves. The two-door model offers less space but remains usable for everyday needs.
technology:
Despite its rugged focus, the Bronco includes a solid suite of modern technology.

At the center of the dashboard is a 12.0-inch touchscreen infotainment system running Ford’s Sync 4 software. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, allowing seamless smartphone integration. Many models also include built-in navigation and offer an optional 12-speaker Bang & Olufsen sound system, delivering a more premium audio experience. The infotainment system supports over-the-air updates, ensuring the vehicle can receive software improvements and new features over time.
safety:
The 2026 Bronco includes a range of safety features, though it is not as heavily equipped as some urban-focused SUVs.

Standard features include automatic emergency braking and automatic high-beam headlights, helping improve safety during everyday driving. Optional features include blind-spot monitoring, adaptive cruise control, and parking sensors, which enhance convenience and driver confidence. Crash-test ratings can be referenced through organizations such as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, though ratings may vary depending on configuration.
warranty:
The Bronco offers warranty coverage that is competitive within its segment.

Ford provides a three-year or 36,000-mile limited warranty, covering defects in materials and workmanship. The powertrain warranty extends to five years or 60,000 miles, covering major mechanical components. Unlike some competitors, Ford does not include complimentary scheduled maintenance, meaning owners will need to cover routine servicing costs.
pros: Exceptional off-road capability, wide range of trims and configurations, and rugged design with open-air driving experience.
cons: Exceptional off-road capability, wide range of trims and configurations, and rugged design with open-air driving experience.
mn_take: The Bronco is one of the most capable and customizable off-road SUVs available today, delivering true adventure-ready performance without sacrificing everyday usability.

car_name: 2026 Ford Mustang GTD Review: Price, Specs, 815-HP V8 Performance, Interior, Technology, Safety and Warranty
overview:
The Ford Mustang GTD is unlike any Mustang that has come before it. Created as the ultimate road-legal interpretation of Ford’s GT3 race program, the GTD pushes the iconic pony car into true supercar territory with a price tag, engineering complexity, and performance envelope few expected from a Mustang. Developed by Ford Motor Company in collaboration with Multimatic, the GTD borrows heavily from the Mustang GT3 race car that competes in global endurance racing. The result is a limited-production performance machine with extreme aerodynamics, a track-focused suspension system, and a supercharged V8 producing more than 800 horsepower.

Despite its outrageous capability, the Mustang GTD remains road legal and surprisingly usable on public roads. It blends race-car engineering with the everyday drivability of a production vehicle—though practicality takes a clear back seat to performance. Rear seats are gone, the trunk space has been sacrificed for advanced mechanical hardware, and the car’s design screams motorsport from every angle. In short, the GTD is not simply the fastest Mustang ever built—it’s a Mustang engineered to challenge the world’s most elite exotic sports cars.
pricing:
The 2026 Ford Mustang GTD is expected to start at around $328,000, placing it firmly in the territory of exotic supercars rather than traditional American muscle cars. 

The lineup is expected to include a few specialized configurations depending on performance equipment and exterior materials.

The Mustang GTD serves as the core version and is expected to start at approximately $328,000. This model already includes extensive motorsport-inspired engineering, including advanced aerodynamics, active suspension, and the powerful supercharged V8.

The Mustang GTD Performance Pack is expected to cost around $368,000. This version adds additional track-focused upgrades such as improved aerodynamics, performance tires, and further suspension tuning designed for aggressive driving and track use.

At the top of the range is the Mustang GTD Liquid Carbon, estimated to reach about $375,000. This model features exposed carbon-fiber body panels that showcase the raw composite material beneath the paint, giving the car a distinctive high-tech appearance while reducing overall weight.

Production will be extremely limited—roughly 1,000 units globally—and prospective buyers must typically apply for the opportunity to purchase one, making the GTD as exclusive as many European supercars.
drivetrain:
The Mustang GTD’s performance credentials are extraordinary, beginning with its supercharged 5.2-liter V8 engine. This engine produces an astonishing 815 horsepower, making it the most powerful Mustang ever built. Power is sent to the rear wheels through an 8-speed dual-clutch transaxle mounted at the rear of the car, a configuration normally found in high-end supercars. This layout improves weight distribution and enhances handling precision.

Key performance specifications include:
- Engine: Supercharged 5.2-liter V8
- Horsepower: 815 hp
- Transmission: 8-speed dual-clutch automatic
- Drivetrain: Rear-wheel drive
- 0–60 mph: Approximately 2.8 seconds
- Top Speed: Over 200 mph

One of the GTD’s most impressive features is its pushrod rear suspension, which is typically reserved for race cars. Instead of traditional springs mounted directly near the wheels, the pushrod setup moves the suspension components inboard for improved aerodynamics and handling performance. Combined with advanced aerodynamics—including a massive swan-neck rear wing—the GTD delivers immense grip and stability at high speeds. Even more surprising is the car’s ability to maintain a relatively comfortable ride on public roads, making it far more usable than most track-focused machines.

Fuel economy is understandably not a priority for an 815-horsepower supercharged V8 performance car. According to EPA estimates, the Mustang GTD delivers approximately 10 mpg in the city and 17 mpg on the highway, resulting in a combined rating of about 12 mpg. These figures are typical for extreme performance vehicles in this class, where the focus remains squarely on speed, power, and track capability.
interior:
Although the exterior of the Mustang GTD resembles a full-blown race car, the interior maintains a layout that feels familiar to anyone who has driven a modern Mustang. The cabin features a mix of premium leather, suede upholstery, and exposed carbon fiber, creating a more upscale environment than standard Mustang models while still maintaining a motorsport-inspired aesthetic. Deeply bolstered Recaro bucket seats provide excellent support during aggressive driving and keep both the driver and passenger firmly planted during high-speed cornering. One major difference from regular Mustangs is the absence of rear seats. The GTD is strictly a two-seat sports car, and the space where rear passengers would normally sit has been replaced by a small window that allows occupants to view the sophisticated pushrod suspension system in action.

Cargo space is essentially nonexistent. The traditional trunk area has been replaced by the rear-mounted transaxle, cooling systems, and aerodynamic ducting necessary to support the car’s extreme performance capabilities. While the GTD may sacrifice practicality, its cockpit still delivers an engaging environment that blends everyday usability with race-inspired design elements.
technology: Despite its motorsport focus, the Mustang GTD still includes a modern digital technology suite similar to that found in other current Mustang models. The driver faces a 12.4-inch digital instrument cluster that can display performance data, navigation information, and customizable driving metrics. The interface allows drivers to prioritize track-focused information such as lap timing, engine performance statistics, and vehicle telemetry. At the center of the dashboard sits a 13.2-inch touchscreen infotainment system, which provides access to media, navigation, vehicle settings, and connectivity features. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, allowing drivers to seamlessly integrate their smartphones for music, navigation, and messaging. The GTD also includes a 12-speaker Bang & Olufsen premium sound system, ensuring that the cabin can deliver high-quality audio when the driver isn’t listening to the thunderous soundtrack of the supercharged V8. While the technology itself is similar to other Mustang models, the GTD includes several exclusive performance menus that allow drivers to monitor advanced performance data and configure track-focused driving settings.
safety: Given the Mustang GTD’s track-focused nature, driver-assistance features are relatively limited compared with typical luxury vehicles. However, Ford still includes several important safety technologies designed to assist drivers during everyday driving conditions. The car comes equipped with automatic emergency braking, which can detect potential frontal collisions and apply the brakes if the driver fails to respond in time. This system helps reduce the likelihood of accidents during sudden traffic slowdowns. Another standard feature is lane-keeping assist, which monitors road markings and gently steers the vehicle back into its lane if it begins drifting unintentionally. This can be particularly useful during long highway drives when driver fatigue may become a factor. Like most low-volume exotic vehicles, the Mustang GTD has not undergone formal crash testing by agencies such as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration or the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, but it incorporates modern safety technologies and structural engineering consistent with Ford’s high-performance vehicles.
warranty:
The Mustang GTD comes with warranty coverage similar to other vehicles produced by Ford, although it lacks the complimentary maintenance plans offered by some luxury brands.

Ford provides a three-year or 36,000-mile limited warranty, covering defects in materials and workmanship during the early ownership period. The powertrain warranty extends to five years or 60,000 miles, offering additional protection for the engine, transmission, and drivetrain components. Unlike some competitors in the exotic sports car segment, Ford does not include complimentary scheduled maintenance for the Mustang GTD. Owners are responsible for routine service costs such as oil changes, inspections, and maintenance procedures. However, Ford’s widespread dealer network can make servicing the vehicle more convenient than many European exotic cars, which often require specialized service centers.
pros: Extreme supercar performance and race-car engineering make the Mustang GTD the most radical and capable Mustang ever produced.
cons: Sky-high price, minimal practicality, and limited driver-assistance features make it less usable as a daily sports car.
mn_take: The Mustang GTD transforms America’s most iconic muscle car into a genuine exotic performance machine capable of challenging the world’s best supercars.

car_name: 2026 Ferrari Purosangue Review: Pricing, Specs, V12 Performance, Interior, Technology, Safety and Warranty
overview:
The Ferrari Purosangue represents one of the most significant moments in Ferrari’s modern history. Known globally for building some of the world’s most desirable sports cars, Ferrari entered the ultra-luxury SUV segment with a model that refuses to behave like a conventional sport-utility vehicle. The Purosangue—Italian for “pureblood”—is Ferrari’s interpretation of an SUV, blending the practicality of four doors with the emotional drama and performance DNA expected from a car bearing the iconic prancing horse badge.

Unlike many performance SUVs that rely on turbocharged or hybrid powertrains, the Purosangue proudly retains a naturally aspirated V12 engine. Its design is sculpted and athletic rather than bulky, and its proportions lean closer to a grand-touring shooting brake than a traditional SUV. Yet despite its performance focus, it offers genuine space for four adults and a usable rear cargo area, making it the most practical Ferrari ever produced. The result is a vehicle that feels less like Ferrari adapting to the SUV trend and more like Ferrari redefining what a high-performance luxury SUV can be.
pricing:
The 2026 Ferrari Purosangue starts at $428,636 in the United States. Ferrari offers the Purosangue as a single highly equipped model rather than multiple trim levels, but the brand’s extensive personalization program means no two vehicles are likely to be configured the same. Buyers can choose from a vast range of exterior colors, including historic Ferrari paints and bespoke finishes. Wheel designs, brake caliper colors, carbon-fiber exterior accents, and numerous aerodynamic styling elements can also be customized. Inside, Ferrari offers a wide selection of leather, Alcantara, and carbon-fiber trim combinations, along with unique stitching patterns and personalized interior color themes.

Optional equipment includes features such as massaging front seats, an electrochromic panoramic glass roof, upgraded audio systems, and additional carbon-fiber interior detailing. Because of these customization options, many Purosangue models easily exceed $500,000 depending on the chosen specification.
drivetrain:
At the heart of the Purosangue lies one of the most extraordinary engines in the automotive world—a naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12. Producing 715 horsepower and 528 lb-ft of torque, this engine delivers the kind of power and soundtrack that has defined Ferrari’s flagship models for decades. The engine is paired with an 8-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission that sends power to all four wheels through Ferrari’s advanced all-wheel-drive system. Despite its SUV proportions, the Purosangue offers performance figures that rival many exotic sports cars.

The Purosangue can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in around 3.2 seconds, delivering explosive acceleration accompanied by the unmistakable sound of a high-revving Ferrari V12. One of the most remarkable engineering features is Ferrari’s active suspension system, which uses electric motors at each wheel to control body movement during cornering. This technology virtually eliminates body roll while maintaining exceptional ride comfort. The suspension can even lower the vehicle slightly during aggressive driving to improve stability and handling. The result is an SUV that feels astonishingly agile, delivering the same precise steering response and dynamic balance that drivers expect from Ferrari’s traditional sports cars.

Fuel efficiency is naturally not the Purosangue’s strongest attribute. The powerful V12 engine prioritizes performance over efficiency, resulting in modest fuel economy figures. According to EPA estimates, the Purosangue delivers 11 mpg in city driving and 15 mpg on the highway. While these numbers are low compared with typical SUVs, buyers in this segment are unlikely to prioritize fuel savings over performance and exclusivity.
interior:
Inside the Purosangue, Ferrari blends luxury craftsmanship with a distinctly driver-focused cockpit design. Premium materials such as finely stitched leather, aluminum trim, and carbon-fiber accents dominate the cabin, creating an environment that feels both sophisticated and performance-oriented. The front seats are sculpted and supportive, designed to keep occupants comfortable even during spirited driving. Ferrari’s unique design philosophy places many of the vehicle’s primary controls directly on the steering wheel, ensuring that drivers can adjust key functions without taking their hands off the wheel.

Unlike most SUVs, the Purosangue features four individual bucket seats instead of a traditional rear bench, providing exceptional comfort for all occupants. Access to the rear seats is made easier by the distinctive rear-hinged coach doors, which open opposite the front doors and add a dramatic visual element to the vehicle’s design. Cargo space is more limited than in traditional luxury SUVs, but the rear liftgate still provides enough room for luggage during weekend trips or long grand-touring journeys.
technology:
Ferrari takes a different approach to technology in the Purosangue compared with most modern luxury SUVs. Instead of installing a large central touchscreen dominating the dashboard, the brand focuses on a driver-centric digital environment that integrates technology directly into the driving experience. The driver sits behind a fully digital instrument cluster that displays navigation data, performance metrics, and vehicle information through configurable graphics. Many of the car’s features are controlled through touch-sensitive inputs and haptic buttons located on the steering wheel, allowing drivers to adjust settings without diverting their attention from the road.

For passengers, Ferrari includes a 10.2-inch passenger-side display that mirrors key vehicle information and allows the front passenger to interact with navigation, media, and performance data. This screen adds a unique interactive element to the driving experience, letting passengers share in the excitement rather than simply ride along. Connectivity features include wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, Bluetooth integration, and smartphone-based navigation functionality. Interestingly, Ferrari does not include a built-in navigation system, assuming that most drivers will rely on smartphone apps for directions. The Purosangue’s technology suite focuses less on gadgetry and more on enhancing the driving experience, making it feel distinctly different from typical tech-heavy luxury SUVs.
safety:
Although Ferrari vehicles traditionally prioritize performance, the Purosangue includes a comprehensive array of modern driver-assistance technologies to improve safety during everyday driving. 
The SUV comes standard with automated emergency braking, which can detect potential frontal collisions and apply braking force automatically if the driver fails to respond in time. Blind-spot monitoring helps drivers identify vehicles approaching from behind when changing lanes, improving safety on highways and in busy traffic. Another important feature is lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, which alerts the driver if the vehicle begins drifting from its lane and can gently guide it back into position when necessary. This system is particularly helpful during long highway journeys.

The Purosangue also features adaptive cruise control, which automatically adjusts the vehicle’s speed to maintain a safe distance from traffic ahead. Automatic high-beam headlights improve nighttime visibility by switching between high and low beams depending on surrounding traffic conditions. Like many ultra-luxury vehicles, the Purosangue has not been crash-tested by organizations such as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration or the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, but its advanced driver-assistance systems and robust construction aim to provide a high level of occupant protection.
warranty:
Ferrari provides warranty coverage that is typical for ultra-luxury performance vehicles but pairs it with an unusually generous maintenance program.

The Purosangue comes with a three-year limited warranty with unlimited mileage, covering defects in materials and workmanship. The powertrain warranty also lasts three years with unlimited mileage, protecting major mechanical components such as the engine, transmission, and drivetrain. Where Ferrari stands apart is its seven-year complimentary maintenance program, which covers scheduled service including oil changes, fluid replacements, brake inspections, and routine maintenance procedures. This extended maintenance plan helps ensure that the vehicle remains maintained according to Ferrari’s factory standards while reducing ownership costs during the early years. Ferrari also offers optional extended warranty plans for owners who plan to keep their vehicles beyond the initial coverage period.
pros: A naturally aspirated V12 engine combined with Ferrari-level handling makes the Purosangue one of the most exhilarating SUVs ever built.
cons: The ultra-high price, limited cargo capacity, and control-heavy steering wheel layout may not appeal to buyers seeking traditional SUV practicality.
mn_take: The Purosangue proves that even an SUV can deliver the emotional intensity, performance, and exclusivity that define a true Ferrari.

car_name: 2026 Ferrari F80 Review: 1184-HP Hybrid Hypercar, Specs, Price, Performance and Features
overview:
The 2026 Ferrari F80 stands as the latest flagship hypercar from Ferrari and represents the most advanced road-going machine the Italian automaker has ever created. Designed to succeed legendary halo models such as the Ferrari 288 GTO and the Ferrari LaFerrari, the F80 blends cutting-edge hybrid technology with Formula 1–inspired engineering to push the boundaries of speed, aerodynamics, and performance. Instead of the traditional V-12 engine that powered many previous Ferrari flagships, the F80 adopts a more modern approach with a highly sophisticated hybrid powertrain. Beneath its dramatic bodywork sits a twin-turbocharged V-6 engine working alongside multiple electric motors, producing an astonishing 1184 horsepower. This powertrain architecture not only delivers breathtaking acceleration but also demonstrates Ferrari’s commitment to integrating electrification without sacrificing performance.

Visually, the F80 looks like a machine straight from the future. Its aggressive aerodynamic surfaces, sculpted carbon-fiber body panels, and race-inspired proportions give it a presence that is unmistakably Ferrari yet entirely new. The design is heavily influenced by the company’s motorsport expertise, with active aerodynamic elements that dynamically adjust to improve downforce and stability at high speeds. With production limited to just 799 units worldwide, the F80 is as exclusive as it is technologically advanced. Every example has already been allocated to Ferrari’s most loyal clients, cementing the car’s status as one of the most desirable and collectible hypercars ever built.
pricing:
The Ferrari F80 occupies the very top tier of Ferrari’s lineup and is priced accordingly.
- Ferrari F80 — Starting at $3,735,000
Unlike typical production cars, the F80 is not offered in multiple trims. Instead, Ferrari provides buyers with an extensive level of customization through its bespoke personalization programs. Owners can tailor nearly every element of the car, from exterior colors and carbon-fiber finishes to unique interior materials and stitching patterns. Ferrari will build only 799 units of the F80 globally, ensuring that each example remains incredibly rare. With such a limited production run, the car is expected to become one of the most collectible Ferraris of the modern era.
drivetrain:
The Ferrari F80’s performance credentials begin with its extraordinary hybrid powertrain, which integrates racing-derived technology from Ferrari’s Formula 1 program. At its core is a mid-mounted 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged V-6 engine. This engine is supported by three electric motors, creating a combined output of 1184 horsepower. Two of these electric motors drive the front wheels, effectively giving the F80 an advanced all-wheel-drive system, while the internal combustion engine and the third electric motor power the rear wheels.

Power is delivered through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, allowing lightning-fast gear changes and seamless integration between electric and gasoline power. The F80 also features a highly sophisticated active suspension system that uses four independent 48-volt electric motors to control damper stiffness at each corner. This technology continuously adjusts the suspension to maintain optimal grip and stability, whether the car is carving through corners on a racetrack or cruising on public roads. Aerodynamics also play a major role in the F80’s performance. Active aerodynamic components automatically adjust to generate massive downforce at high speeds while reducing drag when maximum acceleration is required. Despite its extreme performance, early driving impressions suggest the F80 is surprisingly manageable on normal roads, offering a level of drivability that few hypercars can match.

With over 1100 horsepower and advanced hybrid traction, the Ferrari F80 delivers truly staggering acceleration.
- 0–62 mph: 2.2 seconds (manufacturer claim)
- 0–124 mph: 5.8 seconds
Independent testing has not yet been conducted, but industry estimates suggest the F80 could reach 0–60 mph in under 2.0 seconds, placing it among the fastest road-legal cars ever produced. Such performance levels rival dedicated track machines and highlight Ferrari’s ability to translate racing technology directly into a road car.

Fuel economy figures are rarely the primary focus of hypercar buyers, and official ratings for the F80 have not yet been published. However, the hybrid powertrain is expected to provide an estimated combined fuel economy of around 14 mpg. While modest compared with conventional vehicles, this level of efficiency is notable for a hypercar producing well over 1,000 horsepower.
interior: Inside the Ferrari F80, the cabin design emphasizes the driver above all else. Ferrari describes the seating layout as “1+” rather than a conventional two-seat arrangement, highlighting the car’s extreme driver-focused philosophy. The driver’s seat is finished in striking red upholstery and positioned prominently within the cockpit, visually reinforcing the idea that the driver is the central element of the vehicle. The passenger seat, in contrast, is integrated into the carbon-fiber monocoque chassis and finished in black, appearing intentionally understated. The steering wheel is compact and flat-bottomed, resembling a racing wheel and incorporating a wide array of performance controls. Most driving settings can be adjusted directly from the wheel, allowing the driver to manage the vehicle without removing their hands from the steering wheel. Materials inside the F80 emphasize lightweight performance. Extensive use of carbon fiber, high-performance fabrics, and minimalist trim helps reduce weight while maintaining Ferrari’s signature sense of craftsmanship.
technology:
Unlike many modern luxury vehicles, the Ferrari F80 avoids complex infotainment systems in favor of a simplified, performance-oriented technology layout. The main interface inside the cabin is a fully digital instrument cluster, which provides critical information such as speed, hybrid system data, engine performance, and navigation functions. Drivers control most vehicle systems using steering-wheel-mounted buttons. A smaller secondary display on the center console manages basic functions such as climate control and vehicle settings. Ferrari intentionally avoids installing large infotainment screens or entertainment features, ensuring the driver remains focused on the road. Connectivity features are minimal, and buyers should not expect features like streaming services or in-car gaming systems.

For a hypercar like the F80, the true entertainment lies in the driving experience itself.
safety:
Although the Ferrari F80 is primarily engineered for performance, it still incorporates several advanced driver-assistance systems to enhance safety during everyday driving. Standard features include automated emergency braking, which can detect obstacles and apply the brakes automatically if a collision risk is detected. The vehicle also includes lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, which gently corrects the steering if the car begins drifting out of its lane.
 
Another useful feature is adaptive cruise control, which automatically adjusts the vehicle’s speed to maintain a safe distance from traffic ahead. The F80 also includes automatic high-beam headlights to improve nighttime visibility. Because of its extremely limited production, the F80 has not been crash-tested by agencies such as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration or the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.
warranty:
Ferrari provides a warranty package that is competitive within the exotic-car segment while also offering one of the most generous maintenance programs in the industry. The limited warranty covers the vehicle for three years with unlimited mileage, ensuring protection regardless of how frequently the car is driven. Similarly, the powertrain warranty also lasts three years with unlimited mileage, covering key mechanical components including the hybrid system, engine, and transmission.

One of Ferrari’s standout ownership benefits is its seven-year complimentary maintenance program. This service package includes scheduled maintenance such as oil changes, brake fluid replacement, and comprehensive inspections performed at authorized Ferrari dealerships. Importantly, the maintenance program is tied to the vehicle rather than the owner, meaning future buyers can continue to benefit from the remaining coverage—an important factor for maintaining long-term value.
pros: Unmatched hybrid power, Formula 1-derived technology, and breathtaking performance make the Ferrari F80 one of the most extraordinary hypercars ever produced.
cons: Its multi-million-dollar price and extremely limited production make the F80 virtually unattainable for most enthusiasts.
mn_take: The 2026 Ferrari F80 represents the absolute peak of Ferrari engineering—an ultra-exclusive hybrid hypercar that blends race-car technology, futuristic design, and mind-bending performance into one of the most remarkable road cars ever built.

car_name: 2026 Ferrari Roma Review: Price, Specs, Performance, Interior, Technology and Features
overview:
The 2026 Ferrari Roma represents one of the most elegant and approachable grand touring models in Ferrari’s modern lineup. Designed to blend classic Italian styling with contemporary performance, the Roma delivers a more relaxed interpretation of Ferrari’s performance philosophy without losing the thrilling character that defines the brand. Unlike Ferrari’s more aggressive mid-engine supercars, the Roma adopts a front-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout, positioning it as a refined grand tourer meant for long-distance driving as much as spirited performance. Its flowing body lines, minimalist surfaces, and low-slung proportions draw inspiration from classic Ferraris of the 1960s, while modern lighting signatures and aerodynamic detailing bring the design firmly into the present.

For the 2026 model year, the Roma is offered exclusively as the Roma Spider, meaning the coupe version has been discontinued. The convertible design enhances the car’s grand touring character, allowing drivers to enjoy open-air cruising while still benefiting from Ferrari’s remarkable performance engineering. This also marks the final model year for the Roma, as Ferrari prepares to replace it with the upcoming Ferrari Amalfi in 2027. As a result, the 2026 Roma Spider represents the final evolution of a model that successfully combined Ferrari’s racing heritage with the relaxed sophistication of a luxury grand tourer.
pricing:
For 2026, Ferrari simplifies the Roma lineup by offering only the convertible version.
- Roma Spider – Starting at $279,965
Although there is only one core model, Ferrari’s extensive personalization options allow buyers to tailor nearly every element of the car. Exterior paint finishes range from contemporary metallic tones to heritage colors inspired by Ferrari’s classic models. Wheel designs, carbon-fiber trim pieces, interior materials, and stitching patterns can all be customized. Buyers can also select from a wide range of leather colors and Alcantara upholstery options to create a cabin that reflects their personal taste. This level of customization ensures that no two Roma Spiders are likely to be identical.
drivetrain:
Under the long sculpted hood of the Ferrari Roma Spider sits a powerful 3.9-liter twin-turbocharged V-8 engine, one of the most celebrated engines in Ferrari’s modern portfolio. This engine produces 612 horsepower and 561 lb-ft of torque, delivering power exclusively to the rear wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. The gearbox is derived from the advanced transmission used in the Ferrari SF90 Stradale, allowing lightning-fast shifts and seamless power delivery.

The Roma’s performance character differs slightly from Ferrari’s more track-focused models. Instead of prioritizing razor-sharp lap times, the Roma focuses on delivering smooth, effortless acceleration combined with refined ride quality. Selectable drive modes allow the car to transform from a relaxed grand tourer into a much more aggressive sports car. Switching to Sport or Race mode sharpens throttle response, quickens gear changes, and tightens the chassis dynamics, revealing the Roma’s true Ferrari DNA. While the steering is lighter than that of Ferrari’s hardcore performance models, it remains extremely precise, providing drivers with confidence and control when navigating winding roads.

Despite its grand touring focus, the Roma Spider delivers impressive performance figures.
- 0–60 mph: 3.4 seconds (manufacturer estimate)
This level of acceleration allows the Roma to compete comfortably with other luxury performance grand tourers, including rivals like the Aston Martin DB12 Volante. The twin-turbo V-8’s responsiveness and distinctive exhaust note ensure that every burst of acceleration feels dramatic and unmistakably Ferrari.

Fuel efficiency is not a primary focus for vehicles in this segment, but the Roma Spider offers respectable numbers for a high-performance V-8 grand tourer.
- City: 17 mpg
- Highway: 22 mpg
- Combined: 19 mpg
These figures reflect the balance Ferrari aimed to achieve between performance and everyday usability.
interior:
Inside the cabin, the Ferrari Roma Spider combines luxury craftsmanship with a modern digital interface. The interior is wrapped in premium leather and suede-like materials, with flowing design elements that extend from the dashboard into the door panels to create an enveloping cockpit. The driver sits behind a 16-inch fully digital instrument cluster, which provides customizable driving information and performance data. The steering wheel features numerous touch-sensitive controls that allow drivers to manage key vehicle functions without removing their hands from the wheel.

One unique feature of the Roma is its 2+2 seating configuration, making it one of the few Ferraris to include small rear seats. While these rear seats are best suited for short trips or additional storage, they add a layer of practicality rarely found in exotic sports cars. The Roma Spider also provides a usable 10.3-cubic-foot trunk, offering enough space for luggage on a weekend getaway—an important feature for a car designed with grand touring in mind.
technology:
Unlike some Ferrari models that prioritize minimalism and performance-focused technology, the Roma Spider incorporates a more comprehensive infotainment experience suited to long-distance touring. At the center of the dashboard sits a vertically mounted 8.4-inch touchscreen, which serves as the primary hub for navigation, media controls, and vehicle settings. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, allowing seamless smartphone integration without the need for cables.

Ferrari also includes a dedicated passenger display, enabling the passenger to view performance data, navigation directions, and media information. This feature helps create a more engaging experience for both occupants during spirited drives. Audio performance is handled by a seven-speaker sound system as standard, while an optional 12-speaker JBL premium audio system delivers a richer listening experience for those who prioritize high-quality sound during long journeys. Overall, the Roma’s technology suite strikes a balance between luxury convenience and Ferrari’s driver-focused philosophy.
safety:
Although performance is the primary focus of most Ferrari models, the Roma Spider includes a selection of modern driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance everyday usability. Optional safety features include adaptive cruise control, which automatically maintains a safe distance from vehicles ahead during highway driving. The car can also be equipped with lane-departure warning, which alerts the driver if the vehicle begins drifting from its lane.

Additional available features include blind-spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert, both of which help improve awareness when changing lanes or reversing in tight spaces. As with many exotic sports cars, official crash-test ratings are not available from organizations such as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration or the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.
warranty:
Ferrari provides a warranty package that reflects the ownership experience of exotic vehicles, combined with one of the most generous maintenance programs in the supercar industry. The limited warranty covers the vehicle for three years with unlimited mileage, ensuring owners are protected regardless of how frequently the car is driven.

Similarly, the powertrain warranty also extends for three years with unlimited mileage, covering critical components such as the engine and transmission. Ferrari also includes a seven-year complimentary maintenance program, which covers scheduled service items such as oil changes, fluid replacements, inspections, and other routine maintenance tasks performed at authorized Ferrari service centers. An important advantage of this program is that it follows the vehicle rather than the owner, meaning subsequent owners can continue to benefit from the remaining maintenance coverage—helping preserve the car’s long-term value.
pros: Elegant styling, thrilling twin-turbo V-8 performance, and rare 2+2 practicality make the Roma Spider one of Ferrari’s most versatile grand tourers.
cons: Light steering feel and the absence of a coupe option in 2026 may disappoint drivers seeking a more focused Ferrari driving experience.
mn_take: The 2026 Ferrari Roma Spider is a beautifully balanced grand tourer that combines timeless Italian design, everyday usability, and exhilarating Ferrari performance into one of the most stylish open-top sports cars on the market.

car_name: 2026 Ferrari 12Cilindri Review: 819-HP V12 Supercar, Pricing, Specs & Spider Explained
overview:
Few automotive experiences can match the emotional intensity of a naturally aspirated Ferrari V-12, and the 2026 Ferrari 12Cilindri exists primarily to celebrate that tradition. At a time when much of the industry is rapidly embracing electrification, Ferrari has chosen a different path for this flagship grand touring supercar—retaining a screaming V-12 engine and pairing it with the brand’s latest chassis and electronic technology. The 12Cilindri replaces the iconic Ferrari 812 Superfast lineage, carrying forward the formula of front-mounted V-12 power and rear-wheel drive. Its styling blends futuristic surfaces with subtle nods to Ferrari grand tourers of the late 1960s and early 1970s, giving the car a distinctive identity that feels both modern and timeless.

Ferrari offers the model in two body styles: a sleek glass-roofed coupe and the open-air 12Cilindri Spider convertible. Both share the same mechanical hardware and driving philosophy, but the Spider adds the sensory thrill of hearing the V-12 engine echo through open air. With 819 horsepower, a 9,500-rpm redline, and advanced handling technologies such as rear-wheel steering and adaptive suspension, the 12Cilindri represents one of the purest expressions of Ferrari’s grand-touring philosophy: enormous performance combined with long-distance comfort and unmistakable drama.
pricing:
The 2026 Ferrari 12Cilindri is positioned among the brand’s most exclusive grand tourers, and pricing reflects its flagship status.

2026 Ferrari 12Cilindri Pricing (Trim-wise)
- 12Cilindri Coupe — $465,994
- 12Cilindri Spider — $512,394

Ferrari buyers typically spend significantly more than the base price thanks to the brand’s extensive personalization program. Customers can choose from a vast palette of paints, interior leathers, carbon-fiber trim pieces, bespoke stitching patterns, and unique wheel designs. This level of customization ensures that almost every Ferrari leaving the factory is unique. Choosing between the coupe and the Spider ultimately depends on personal preference. The coupe offers slightly better structural rigidity and a large glass roof, while the Spider’s retractable soft top transforms the driving experience by allowing the V-12 soundtrack to fill the cabin.
drivetrain:
At the heart of the 12Cilindri is one of the most remarkable engines currently available in any production car: a naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V-12 producing 819 horsepower and 500 lb-ft of torque. This engine revs to an astonishing 9,500 rpm, delivering an unmistakable Ferrari soundtrack that builds from a deep mechanical growl to a soaring high-pitched crescendo as the tachometer approaches its redline. Power is delivered to the rear wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, which shifts with lightning speed while maintaining smoothness during everyday driving.

Ferrari has also introduced a sophisticated software system called Aspirated Torque Shaping, designed to optimize torque delivery in lower gears. This technology enhances responsiveness at mid-range engine speeds while preserving the linear power delivery that naturally aspirated engines are famous for. Handling is equally impressive. The 12Cilindri features rear-wheel steering, which improves agility at low speeds and stability at high speeds. Combined with Ferrari’s adaptive suspension system, the car delivers sharp cornering performance while still maintaining a comfortable ride on longer journeys. Acceleration is predictably ferocious. Ferrari claims the 12Cilindri will reach 60 mph in about 2.9 seconds, though real-world testing suggests the number could drop closer to 2.7 seconds under ideal conditions.

Fuel efficiency is not a primary concern for a high-performance V-12 grand tourer, but the 2026 Ferrari 12Cilindri delivers reasonable numbers for its class.
EPA estimates indicate:
- Coupe: 12 mpg city / 19 mpg highway
- Spider: 12 mpg city / 17 mpg highway
While these figures may seem modest, they are typical for large naturally aspirated engines producing more than 800 horsepower.
interior:
The cabin of the 12Cilindri represents a significant evolution compared with the interior of its predecessor. Ferrari has adopted a “dual-cockpit” design philosophy, which visually separates the driver and passenger into two distinct zones. Both occupants sit within sculpted seats surrounded by sweeping dashboard surfaces and high-quality materials. Ferrari uses premium leather, aluminum trim, and Alcantara fabrics throughout the cabin, including environmentally conscious Alcantara materials made with 65 percent recycled polyester. The seating position is low and sporty, emphasizing the car’s performance character, yet the seats remain supportive enough for long-distance touring. Some drivers may wish for slightly thicker seat padding, but overall comfort remains excellent for a high-performance coupe. 

Headroom and legroom are adequate for most adults, although the cabin is naturally more compact than that of larger grand touring cars. Cargo capacity is surprisingly practical for a Ferrari. The coupe features a relatively spacious rear cargo area beneath its hatch, making it possible to carry luggage for weekend trips. The Spider sacrifices some cargo room due to the retractable soft-top mechanism, but it still offers enough space for smaller bags. The Spider’s fabric roof retracts in approximately 14 seconds, allowing drivers to transition quickly from enclosed grand tourer to open-air supercar.
technology:
The 2026 Ferrari 12Cilindri incorporates one of the most technologically advanced interiors ever seen in a front-engine Ferrari. Unlike older Ferrari models that relied heavily on analog controls, the 12Cilindri adopts a digital-focused cockpit centered around three high-resolution displays. Directly ahead of the driver sits a 15.6-inch digital instrument cluster, which provides a wide range of vehicle data including speed, navigation directions, engine performance metrics, and dynamic driving information. The display can be customized to prioritize different types of information depending on the selected driving mode.

At the center of the dashboard is a 10.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system, which acts as the main hub for navigation, media, and connectivity features. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, allowing drivers to integrate their smartphones seamlessly for music streaming, messaging, and navigation. A particularly unique feature is the 8.8-inch passenger display mounted in front of the co-driver. This screen allows passengers to view performance data such as engine speed, gear selection, and speed, helping them feel more involved in the driving experience. The system also includes a wireless smartphone charging pad and advanced voice-command functionality for hands-free operation.

Standard audio comes from a seven-speaker sound system, which delivers clear sound quality within the compact cabin. However, buyers seeking a more immersive audio experience can upgrade to a 15-speaker Burmester premium sound system, widely regarded as one of the finest automotive audio systems available. Despite its impressive technology suite, the interior interface relies heavily on touch-sensitive controls, which some drivers may find less intuitive than traditional physical buttons.
safety:
As with most exotic sports cars, the focus of the 12Cilindri is on driving engagement rather than extensive driver-assistance technology. However, Ferrari still includes a selection of modern safety systems designed to improve everyday usability. Standard safety features include forward collision warning with automated emergency braking, which can detect potential frontal collisions and apply the brakes if necessary. The car also includes blind-spot monitoring, which helps drivers detect vehicles approaching from adjacent lanes.

Another standard feature is lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, which provides gentle steering corrections if the vehicle begins to drift from its lane without signaling. Additionally, the 12Cilindri offers adaptive cruise control, which automatically adjusts vehicle speed to maintain a safe following distance on highways. While the list of driver-assistance technologies is shorter than that found in mainstream luxury vehicles, it reflects Ferrari’s philosophy of keeping the driver fully engaged with the driving experience. Crash-test data for the 12Cilindri has not been published, though general safety ratings are typically issued by organizations such as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.
warranty:
Ferrari offers a distinctive ownership program that includes a relatively short warranty period but an unusually generous maintenance package.

Warranty Coverage
- Limited Warranty: 3 years with unlimited miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 3 years with unlimited miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 7 years with unlimited miles
The seven-year maintenance program covers all scheduled servicing, including oil changes, fluid replacements, and regular inspections. Services are typically performed once every year or approximately every 12,500 miles, whichever comes first. This long-term maintenance coverage significantly reduces ownership costs during the early years of the vehicle’s life and is a key part of Ferrari’s premium ownership experience.
pros: A glorious naturally aspirated V-12 with a 9,500-rpm redline delivers one of the most thrilling soundtracks in the supercar world.
cons: Touch-sensitive interior controls can be frustrating to use, and rear visibility is limited due to the car’s dramatic styling.
mn_take: The Ferrari 12Cilindri is a rare celebration of pure internal-combustion performance, pairing an unforgettable V-12 engine with cutting-edge chassis technology to create one of the most exhilarating grand touring supercars available today.

car_name: 2026 Dodge Durango Review: V8 Power, 8,700-lb Towing, Pricing and Trims Explained
overview:
The 2026 Dodge Durango continues to stand apart in the crowded three-row SUV segment by leaning heavily into its performance roots. While many family SUVs prioritize efficiency and soft-road comfort, the Durango retains a distinct muscle-car personality, thanks largely to its powerful V-8 engines and rear-wheel-drive architecture. Despite being well into its second decade on the market, Dodge has managed to keep the Durango relevant through incremental updates to technology, styling, and cabin features. The SUV still offers bold design cues, strong towing capabilities, and the type of engine choices rarely seen in family vehicles today.

For 2026, Dodge has also reversed its earlier plan to restrict the V-6 engine to fleet buyers only. The 295-hp 3.6-liter V-6 returns as the standard engine, while buyers can still opt for the 360-hp 5.7-liter HEMI V-8 or the even more potent 6.4-liter “392” V-8, which now powers the Durango R/T models. The result is a three-row SUV that delivers an unusual blend of family practicality, serious towing capability, and classic American muscle-car attitude—a combination few competitors can match.
pricing:
The 2026 Dodge Durango starts at approximately $40,990 and climbs to around $51,000 depending on trim level and equipment.

2026 Dodge Durango Pricing (Trim-wise)
- GT — $40,990
- GT V8 — $44,690
- R/T — $45,000 (est.)
- GT Plus — $47,590
- R/T Plus — $48,000 (est.)
- GT Plus V8 — $50,990
- GT Premium V8 — $50,990
- R/T Premium — $51,000 (est.)
Among the available configurations, the GT Plus V8 offers one of the most balanced packages in the lineup. It combines the performance of the HEMI V-8 engine with premium features such as all-wheel drive, ventilated front seats, heated second-row seating, rear load-leveling suspension, and larger 20-inch wheels, making it an appealing choice for buyers seeking both capability and comfort.
drivetrain:
The Durango’s biggest strength remains its range of powerful engines, which give the SUV a personality closer to a muscle car than a typical family crossover. The lineup begins with a 3.6-liter Pentastar V-6 producing 295 horsepower, paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission. This engine provides adequate performance for everyday driving while delivering the best fuel economy in the range. Stepping up to the 5.7-liter HEMI V-8 dramatically transforms the Durango’s character. With 360 horsepower, the V-8 brings stronger acceleration and a distinctive exhaust note that reinforces the SUV’s performance credentials.

For drivers seeking maximum power, the Durango R/T comes equipped with the 6.4-liter “392” V-8, producing 475 horsepower. This engine turns the Durango into one of the most powerful SUVs in its class, delivering brisk acceleration and confident highway performance. The Durango is available with rear-wheel drive or all-wheel drive, and its rear-drive platform helps give it a more athletic driving feel than many front-drive-based competitors. Despite its performance focus, the suspension remains comfortable enough for daily family use. In previous testing, the V-8 Durango with all-wheel drive accelerated from 0–60 mph in around 6.2 seconds, while the V-6 version completed the sprint in roughly 7.4 seconds.

One of the Durango’s standout capabilities is its impressive towing strength. When properly equipped, V-8 models can tow up to 8,700 pounds, making the Durango one of the most capable SUVs in the midsize segment. This level of towing performance makes it suitable for hauling boats, campers, or large trailers. The V-6 version also remains capable, offering a maximum towing capacity of 6,200 pounds, which is more than enough for smaller trailers or recreational gear.

Fuel economy has never been the Durango’s strongest attribute, particularly with its larger engines.
EPA estimates suggest:
- V-6 models: up to 18 mpg city / 25 mpg highway
- V-8 models: around 14 mpg city / 22 mpg highway
In independent highway testing, a V-8-powered Durango R/T has returned 23 mpg, slightly exceeding its official EPA rating. Still, buyers prioritizing efficiency will likely find more economical options in the segment.
interior:
Although the Durango’s basic design dates back many years, the cabin still manages to feel relatively modern thanks to recent technology upgrades and thoughtful interior touches. The dashboard layout combines rugged styling with subtle luxury elements, creating the “muscle-meets-premium” atmosphere that Dodge is known for. Materials quality varies depending on trim level, but higher trims add leather upholstery, contrast stitching, and premium trim accents.

The front seats are spacious and supportive, making long journeys comfortable for both driver and passenger. Optional features such as ventilated seats, heated steering wheel, and upgraded upholstery help elevate the experience in upper trims. In the second row, passenger space is adequate, though some rivals offer slightly more legroom. Buyers can choose between a three-person bench seat or optional captain’s chairs, the latter improving comfort and access to the third row. The third row provides enough space for occasional adult use but is better suited to children or shorter trips. Cargo capacity is respectable for the class. With all rear seats folded, the Durango can accommodate up to 30 carry-on suitcases, though space behind the third row is limited to around four carry-on bags.
technology:
Technology inside the Durango is centered around a 10.1-inch touchscreen infotainment system, which runs the widely praised Uconnect interface. Despite the vehicle’s age, this system helps the Durango remain competitive with newer SUVs thanks to its intuitive design and responsive controls. The Uconnect interface features clear graphics, logical menu layouts, and quick processing speeds, making everyday tasks such as adjusting climate settings, selecting music, or accessing navigation simple and distraction-free. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, allowing drivers to seamlessly connect their smartphones without using cables.

Bluetooth connectivity is included as standard, and voice command functionality allows drivers to control key features without taking their hands off the steering wheel. Navigation is also available on higher trims, helping drivers find destinations while displaying directions on the large touchscreen. Audio performance varies depending on the trim level. Entry-level models come equipped with a six-speaker sound system, which delivers acceptable audio quality for daily use. However, buyers looking for a richer listening experience can upgrade to a 10-speaker Alpine audio system, while the range-topping configuration features a 20-speaker Harman Kardon premium sound system that significantly enhances clarity and depth.

Additional technology features available in higher trims include:
- Wireless smartphone integration
- Navigation system
- Rear-seat entertainment options
- Multiple USB charging ports
- Premium digital driver displays
Overall, while some competitors offer larger screens or more advanced digital dashboards, the Durango’s infotainment system remains one of the easiest and most user-friendly systems in the segment.
safety:
Safety technology on the Durango is somewhat dependent on trim level and optional packages, meaning buyers may need to add certain features to access the full suite of driver-assistance systems. Standard safety equipment includes blind-spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert, which help drivers detect vehicles approaching from adjacent lanes or behind the SUV when reversing. More advanced driver-assistance features are available as optional upgrades. These include forward collision warning with automated emergency braking, which can detect potential frontal impacts and automatically apply the brakes if the driver fails to react. Another available system is adaptive cruise control, which automatically adjusts the vehicle’s speed to maintain a safe distance from traffic ahead during highway driving. This feature helps reduce driver fatigue on long journeys.

Additional available safety technologies include:
- Lane departure warning
- Forward collision mitigation
- Parking sensors
- Rearview camera systems

The Durango has received strong crash-safety scores from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, reflecting solid structural protection and safety performance. Crash-test results from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety can also provide additional insight into real-world safety performance.
warranty:
Warranty coverage for the Durango is competitive but not class-leading compared with some rivals.

Warranty Coverage
- Limited Warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: None
While this level of protection is typical among American SUVs, some competitors—such as those from Korean manufacturers—offer longer powertrain warranties or complimentary maintenance programs. Because of this, Durango buyers should expect to cover routine service costs themselves, including oil changes, tire rotations, brake maintenance, and general inspections.
pros: Strong V-8 engines and exceptional towing capability give the Durango a performance character rarely found in three-row SUVs.
cons: Strong V-8 engines and exceptional towing capability give the Durango a performance character rarely found in three-row SUVs.
mn_take: The Durango remains a unique choice in the three-row SUV segment, delivering genuine muscle-car power and serious towing strength for buyers who want performance alongside family practicality.

car_name: 2026 Dodge Charger Daytona EV Review: 670-HP Electric Muscle Car With 308-Mile Range
overview:
The 2026 Dodge Charger Daytona EV represents one of the most radical transformations in modern muscle-car history. For decades, the Charger nameplate has been synonymous with thunderous V-8 engines and tire-smoking rear-wheel-drive theatrics. Now, Dodge is rewriting that formula with an electric powertrain while attempting to preserve the bold personality that made the Charger legendary. At first glance, the Charger Daytona remains unmistakably a Dodge muscle car. Its aggressive stance, wide body, and retro-inspired styling echo classic Chargers from the late 1960s. However, beneath the sculpted bodywork lies a thoroughly modern electric architecture built around a 94-kWh battery pack and dual-motor all-wheel-drive system.

Despite the shift to electricity, Dodge hasn’t abandoned performance. In fact, the Charger Daytona delivers acceleration that rivals—or even surpasses—some of the brand’s most powerful gasoline models. With features like Drift Mode, Donut Mode, launch control, and performance telemetry pages, Dodge is clearly aiming to maintain the rebellious spirit that enthusiasts expect from the brand. The Daytona lineup is available in both two-door coupe and four-door sedan body styles, giving buyers a choice between classic muscle-car aesthetics and modern practicality. With its hatchback design, spacious cabin, and everyday usability, the Charger Daytona EV blends high performance with surprising versatility.
pricing:
The 2026 Dodge Charger Daytona EV starts at $61,990 and reaches $68,985 depending on trim level, equipment, and body style.

2026 Dodge Charger Daytona EV Trim Pricing
- Scat Pack Coupe — $61,990
- R/T Sedan — $63,590
- Scat Pack Sedan — $63,990
- Scat Pack Plus Coupe — $66,985
- R/T Plus Sedan — $68,585
- Scat Pack Plus Sedan — $68,985

For most enthusiasts, the Scat Pack Coupe is likely the sweet spot in the lineup. It combines the Charger’s iconic two-door silhouette with high-performance electric hardware and includes desirable features such as 20-inch wheels, faux-leather upholstery, a head-up display, and power-adjustable front seats. The sedan variants offer added practicality, especially for buyers who want the Charger’s muscle-car personality but require easier rear-seat access and improved passenger space.
drivetrain:
Unlike traditional Chargers that relied on large displacement V-8 engines, the Daytona EV uses a dual-motor electric drivetrain paired with a 94-kWh battery pack. One motor sits at the front axle and another at the rear, delivering standard all-wheel drive and instantaneous electric torque. In its Scat Pack configuration, the Charger Daytona produces up to 670 horsepower when equipped with Dodge’s Direct Connection Stage power upgrade, which temporarily boosts output for maximum acceleration. The system also allows drivers to unleash additional power for short bursts, reinforcing the car’s high-performance personality. Acceleration is exceptionally strong for such a large vehicle. During testing, the Scat Pack coupe reached 60 mph in just 3.3 seconds, making it quicker than the previous gasoline-powered Charger Hellcat in similar tests.

Dodge has also equipped the Charger Daytona with several performance-focused driving features designed to keep the muscle-car experience alive in an EV era. These include:
- Launch Control for optimized acceleration
- Drift Mode and Donut Mode for controlled slides
- Line Lock for burnouts and track launches
- Performance Pages that display power output, g-forces, and performance timers
On the road, the Charger Daytona behaves more like a powerful grand tourer than a lightweight sports coupe. Its large dimensions and substantial weight mean it isn’t as agile as smaller performance cars, but the ride quality is impressively composed, especially when equipped with optional adaptive dampers.

Range remains one of the most important considerations for any electric vehicle, and the Charger Daytona EV delivers competitive—but not class-leading—figures. The Scat Pack model is rated for approximately 241 miles of driving range on a full charge, while some earlier configurations were capable of exceeding 300 miles before being discontinued for the 2026 model year.
Charging performance is respectable for a performance-focused EV:
- Peak DC fast-charging rate: 183 kW
- Level 3 fast charging (20–80%): about 27 minutes
- Onboard AC charging: up to 11 kW
Owners can also access Stellantis’s Free2Move Charge network, which integrates public charging stations and provides charging credits in certain markets.

EPA efficiency estimates for the Charger Daytona EV Scat Pack are:
- 82 MPGe city
- 72 MPGe highway
Vehicles equipped with higher-performance tires see slightly reduced efficiency ratings of 74 MPGe city and 66 MPGe highway.
interior:
Inside, the Charger Daytona blends retro design elements with contemporary technology. The dashboard layout takes inspiration from the 1968 Dodge Charger, featuring a long horizontal design and distinctive trim details. Stitching patterns across the dashboard and door panels reinforce the car’s nostalgic character. A modern reinterpretation of the classic pistol-grip shifter sits in the center console, accompanied by a start button and wireless smartphone charging pad.

The cabin comfortably accommodates five passengers, although the coupe version is better suited for four adults due to rear-seat access. The newly introduced four-door sedan greatly improves everyday usability by making entry and exit easier for rear passengers. Cargo practicality is surprisingly strong for a performance coupe. Instead of a traditional trunk, the Charger Daytona uses a large rear hatchback design, which improves cargo access and expands the usable storage area. Additionally, a small front trunk (frunk) provides extra space for charging cables or small bags.
technology:
The technology suite in the Charger Daytona EV represents a major leap forward for Dodge’s muscle-car lineup. At the center of the dashboard sits a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system running the Uconnect 5 interface, widely regarded as one of the most intuitive systems in the industry. Uconnect 5 offers crisp graphics, quick responses, and a straightforward menu layout that allows drivers to easily access navigation, entertainment, and vehicle settings. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with Amazon Alexa voice assistant integration, enabling drivers to control navigation, music, and smart-home devices using voice commands.

For EV owners, Dodge has integrated dedicated electric vehicle information pages that display real-time power flow, battery usage, regenerative braking activity, and charge status. The navigation system can also locate nearby charging stations and plan routes that include charging stops. Driver information is displayed through a 10.3-inch digital instrument cluster, which can be upgraded to a larger 16.0-inch curved display on higher trims. The interface provides customizable layouts that allow drivers to prioritize performance data, navigation instructions, or battery statistics. Audio performance is equally impressive. Standard models include a nine-speaker Alpine sound system with a 506-watt amplifier and subwoofer, while buyers seeking a more immersive listening experience can upgrade to a premium 18-speaker Alpine system producing 914 watts of power.

Additional technology highlights include:
- Head-up display projecting key information onto the windshield
- Digital key smartphone integration with NFC smart card backup
- Remote vehicle monitoring via the Dodge mobile app
- Wireless phone charging
Together, these features ensure the Charger Daytona EV feels every bit as modern as its electric rivals while maintaining its muscle-car identity.
safety:
The Charger Daytona EV comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance safety and reduce driver workload during daily driving. Standard safety features include forward collision warning with automated emergency braking, which can detect potential collisions and apply braking if the driver fails to react in time. The system also incorporates pedestrian and cyclist detection, which Dodge refers to as “vulnerable road user detection.”

Additional standard systems include adaptive cruise control, which automatically maintains a safe distance from vehicles ahead, and lane-keeping assist, which gently corrects steering if the vehicle begins drifting out of its lane. Parking and low-speed maneuvering are supported by optional technologies such as camera-based parking assistance systems and parking sensors, helping drivers manage the Charger’s large dimensions in tight spaces.

Other safety technologies available or standard across the lineup include:
- Blind-spot monitoring
- Rear cross-traffic alert
- Traffic sign recognition
- Surround-view parking cameras
- Automatic high-beam headlights
Crash-test ratings from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety are expected to be published once testing is completed.
warranty:
Warranty coverage for the Charger Daytona EV is typical for a performance-oriented electric vehicle, offering separate protections for standard components and the electric drivetrain.

Warranty Coverage:
- Limited vehicle warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles
- Electric battery and components: 8 years or 100,000 miles

While these coverage periods are competitive within the muscle-car segment, some EV competitors offer longer basic warranties or complimentary maintenance programs. Unfortunately, Dodge does not include free scheduled maintenance, meaning routine servicing—such as brake inspections, tire rotations, and cabin filter replacements—must be paid for by the owner. However, electric vehicles generally require less maintenance than gasoline-powered cars due to fewer moving parts and the absence of oil changes or complex engine systems.
pros: Explosive electric performance and distinctive retro styling make the Charger Daytona EV one of the most exciting electric muscle cars on the market.
cons: Driving range is modest compared with some EV rivals and certain interior materials feel less premium than expected at this price.
mn_take: The Charger Daytona EV proves that muscle cars can survive the electric transition, blending thrilling performance with modern technology while keeping Dodge’s rebellious spirit alive.

car_name: 2026 Dodge Charger Review – Price, Specs, Hurricane Engine, Interior Tech and Performance
overview:
The 2026 Dodge Charger marks a dramatic reinvention of one of America’s most iconic muscle cars. After the previous generation ended production, Dodge has brought the Charger back with a completely new platform, modern technology, and a fresh lineup of powertrains. Despite the extensive redesign, the new Charger still retains the bold attitude and muscular presence that made earlier models legendary. For the first time, the Charger lineup now includes two body styles—a classic four-door sedan and a sleek two-door fastback coupe. Both versions maintain the Charger’s large proportions and aggressive stance, while incorporating styling cues inspired by Dodge muscle cars of the late 1960s and early 1970s.

Under the hood, the 2026 Charger introduces Dodge’s new Hurricane twin-turbocharged inline-six engine, replacing the old HEMI V-8 at launch. While some traditionalists may miss the rumble of a V-8, the new turbocharged engine produces impressive power and modern efficiency while maintaining serious muscle-car performance. The redesigned Charger also brings a much more advanced interior with large digital displays, improved connectivity, and enhanced driver-assistance technology. As a result, the 2026 Charger combines classic muscle car design with modern performance and technology, competing directly with vehicles like the Ford Mustang.
pricing:
The 2026 Dodge Charger is available in multiple trims and two body styles, allowing buyers to choose between a more accessible performance model and a high-output version with significantly more power.

2026 Dodge Charger Pricing (MSRP)
R/T Models:
- R/T Sixpack Coupe – $51,990
- R/T Sixpack Sedan – $53,990
- R/T Plus – $56,985
Scat Pack Models:
- Scat Pack Sixpack Coupe – $56,990
- Scat Pack Sixpack Sedan – $58,990
- Scat Pack Sixpack Plus Coupe – $61,985
The Scat Pack Sixpack models are the most appealing option for enthusiasts because they feature the higher-output engine with significantly more horsepower.
drivetrain:
The 2026 Charger introduces Dodge’s new Hurricane twin-turbocharged inline-six engine, which replaces the traditional V-8 engines used in previous generations.

Two versions of this engine are offered:
Hurricane Sixpack S.O.
- Engine: Twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six
- Output: 420 horsepower
- Transmission: 8-speed automatic
- Drivetrain: Standard all-wheel drive

Hurricane Sixpack H.O.

Engine: Twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six
- Output: 550 horsepower
- Transmission: 8-speed automatic
- Drivetrain: Standard all-wheel drive

Although the Charger now comes standard with all-wheel drive, Dodge has engineered the system with a rear-wheel-drive mode that allows drivers to enjoy classic muscle-car driving dynamics. Dedicated drift and donut modes are also available, allowing drivers to unlock the car’s more playful side on closed tracks. Despite its large size and weight, the new Charger feels surprisingly agile on winding roads and delivers strong straight-line performance.

The high-performance Scat Pack model offers impressive acceleration figures for a large muscle car.
- 0–60 mph: approximately 3.9 seconds
This puts the Charger firmly in high-performance territory, making it one of the quickest gasoline-powered muscle cars in its class.

Official fuel-economy ratings have not yet been released, but early estimates suggest the Charger’s turbocharged engine will deliver slightly better efficiency than the previous V-8 models.
Estimated fuel economy:
- City: about 16 mpg
- Highway: about 26 mpg
- Combined: approximately 19 mpg
Official ratings will eventually be confirmed by the United States Environmental Protection Agency.
interior:
The 2026 Charger’s interior blends retro design inspiration with modern materials and technology. The dashboard layout takes cues from classic Dodge muscle cars, particularly the layered design and driver-focused cockpit arrangement. A distinctive pistol-grip style gear selector adds a nostalgic touch, recalling classic Dodge performance cars of the past. The front seats are wide, supportive, and designed to keep occupants comfortable during spirited driving.
