car_name: 2026 Bentley Continental GT Review: Hybrid Supercar Performance with Handcrafted Luxury
overview: The 2026 Bentley Continental GT continues to define the modern grand touring experience, combining breathtaking performance, exquisite craftsmanship, and long-distance comfort in a single package. Built by Bentley Motors, the Continental GT blends supercar-like acceleration with the refined luxury expected from one of the world’s most prestigious automotive brands. Available as both a two-door coupe and the convertible GTC, the Continental GT offers a striking blend of elegance and athleticism. For 2026, Bentley expands the lineup with new trims and updated plug-in hybrid powertrains that deliver staggering performance figures of up to 771 horsepower. Despite its immense power, the Continental GT remains a true grand tourer—quiet, comfortable, and perfectly suited for cross-country drives. Competing against exotic luxury sports cars such as the Ferrari Roma and Aston Martin DB12, the Continental GT stands apart by offering an unmatched balance of luxury, refinement, and effortless speed.
pricing:
The 2026 Continental GT lineup offers a wide range of coupe and convertible variants, each offering unique styling, performance levels, and customization possibilities. Pricing begins around $250,000 and can exceed $370,000 depending on the trim level and bespoke options selected through Bentley’s Mulliner customization program.

Estimated Trim Pricing:
GT – $250,000
GTC Convertible – $270,000
GT Azure – $280,000
GT S – $290,000
GTC Azure Convertible – $300,000
GTC S – $310,000
GT Speed – $320,000
GTC Speed Convertible – $340,000
GT Mulliner – $340,000
GTC Mulliner Convertible – $370,000
Among these options, the GT Speed offers the most compelling combination of performance and exclusivity, unlocking the full potential of the hybrid powertrain.
drivetrain:
The 2026 Continental GT introduces an advanced plug-in hybrid powertrain that combines a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 engine with a powerful electric motor and battery pack. This electrified setup allows Bentley to deliver extraordinary performance while also enabling limited electric-only driving capability. In standard GT models, the hybrid system produces 671 horsepower, delivering strong acceleration and smooth power delivery. For those seeking ultimate performance, the Speed and Mulliner variants increase output to an incredible 771 horsepower, making this the most powerful road-going Continental GT ever produced. Power is transmitted through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, while all-wheel drive ensures optimal traction during aggressive acceleration or challenging driving conditions. Although the Continental GT is a large and luxurious grand tourer, Bentley’s advanced chassis tuning—including adaptive air suspension and active damping systems—helps maintain impressive handling composure. While its substantial weight can be noticeable during aggressive cornering, the car remains remarkably stable and comfortable during high-speed cruising.

Performance is where the Continental GT truly shines. When equipped with the high-output hybrid system found in the Speed variant, the coupe can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in just 2.8 seconds, placing it firmly in supercar territory. Even the lower-powered 671-horsepower variants provide breathtaking acceleration, making highway overtakes and spirited driving effortless.

The Continental GT’s hybrid system includes a 21.8-kWh battery pack, allowing the car to travel up to 30 miles on electric power alone according to official estimates. This capability enables quiet, emissions-free driving for short city trips. Despite its hybrid assistance, the Continental GT remains a performance-focused grand tourer, with fuel-economy ratings reaching approximately 17 mpg in the city and 22 mpg on the highway.
interior: Step inside the Continental GT and the cabin immediately showcases Bentley’s legendary craftsmanship. The interior is filled with hand-stitched leather upholstery, real wood veneers, precision-machined metal controls, and intricate stitching patterns, creating a luxurious environment that feels both timeless and modern. The front seats are heavily cushioned and highly adjustable, offering up to 20-way power adjustment along with optional heating, ventilation, and massage functions. Bentley also includes an intelligent climate seat system that automatically activates heating or cooling depending on passenger comfort levels. Rear seating is more compact, but it can accommodate two adults for shorter journeys, making the Continental GT more practical than most sports coupes. For those choosing the Continental GTC convertible, a beautifully engineered power-operated fabric roof can open or close in approximately 19 seconds, allowing drivers to enjoy open-air motoring without sacrificing luxury or comfort. Buyers seeking even greater exclusivity can turn to Bentley’s Mulliner bespoke customization program, which offers nearly limitless options for colors, materials, and finishes.
technology: Technology in the Continental GT blends modern functionality with classic luxury design. The centerpiece of the dashboard is a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system, which supports navigation, wireless Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, and a Wi-Fi hotspot for seamless connectivity. Bentley’s signature rotating display remains one of the most distinctive features in the automotive world. With the press of a button, the infotainment screen rotates out of sight, revealing either a handcrafted wood panel or a trio of traditional analog gauges displaying temperature, compass direction, and time. Audio performance is equally impressive. A 10-speaker sound system is standard, while optional upgrades include a 16-speaker Bang & Olufsen premium audio system or the flagship 18-speaker Naim sound system, which incorporates bass transducers integrated into the front seats for a more immersive listening experience.
safety: Despite its performance focus, the Continental GT includes a comprehensive range of driver-assistance technologies designed to improve safety and convenience. Standard safety equipment includes automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control. These systems help reduce driver fatigue during long journeys while improving overall road safety. Bentley also offers advanced features such as remote parking, which allows the driver to park or summon the vehicle using a smartphone app—particularly useful in tight parking spaces. For official crash-test ratings and safety data, buyers can refer to evaluations conducted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.
warranty: Bentley provides warranty coverage that reflects the exclusivity of the Continental GT, though the coverage duration is relatively modest compared to some luxury brands. The vehicle includes a three-year limited warranty with unlimited mileage, ensuring owners are covered regardless of how far they drive during that period. The powertrain warranty also lasts three years with unlimited mileage, covering major components such as the engine, transmission, and hybrid system. Bentley also provides complimentary scheduled maintenance for the first year or 10,000 miles, ensuring the vehicle receives proper service during the early stages of ownership.
pros: Stunning handcrafted interior, immensely powerful hybrid V-8 delivering up to 771 hp, breathtaking 2.8-second 0–60 mph acceleration, and grand-touring comfort make the Continental GT one of the finest luxury performance cars in the world.
cons: High pricing, noticeable weight during aggressive cornering, and modest fuel efficiency slightly temper an otherwise exceptional grand-touring experience.
mn_take: The 2026 Bentley Continental GT perfectly captures the essence of grand touring, blending supercar performance, hybrid innovation, and handcrafted luxury into one of the most desirable two-door luxury cars on the planet.

Bentley also equips the Flying Spur with rear-wheel steering, allowing this large sedan to feel remarkably agile during low-speed maneuvering while maintaining stability at higher speeds. An adaptive air suspension with dual-valve dampers allows the Flying Spur to seamlessly switch between luxury cruiser and performance sedan. In Comfort mode, the ride quality is exceptionally smooth and isolated, but switching to Sport mode significantly sharpens steering response and body control.

Despite its luxury focus, the Flying Spur delivers performance that rivals many dedicated sports sedans. The Flying Spur Speed, with its 771-horsepower hybrid powertrain, is estimated to accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in approximately 3.1 seconds. This remarkable performance places it among the quickest ultra-luxury sedans currently available. Even the less powerful 671-horsepower variants provide effortless acceleration, delivering smooth and rapid power delivery that feels strong even under light throttle inputs.

Thanks to its plug-in hybrid configuration, the Flying Spur can operate in electric-only mode for short distances. The onboard battery pack provides an estimated 30 miles of electric driving range, allowing owners to complete short urban trips without using gasoline. When operating as a hybrid, the Flying Spur achieves fuel-economy ratings of approximately 17 mpg in the city and 22 mpg on the highway. While efficiency is not the primary focus for buyers in this segment, the hybrid system helps reduce emissions while also enhancing low-speed refinement.
interior: Inside the Flying Spur, Bentley’s commitment to craftsmanship is immediately evident. The cabin is finished with hand-stitched leather upholstery, open-pore wood veneers, polished metal accents, and meticulously detailed switchgear, creating an environment that feels more like a handcrafted luxury lounge than a traditional car interior. Both front and rear passengers enjoy generous space, with the rear seats offering the option of either a traditional bench or individually adjustable luxury bucket seats. Rear passengers benefit from extensive comfort features including heated, ventilated, and massaging seats, as well as adjustable climate controls. Bentley has also integrated modern convenience into the traditional design. A removable touchscreen controller mounted in the rear center console allows passengers to adjust climate settings, control window shades, and activate seat massage functions. The Flying Spur’s spacious trunk offers ample room for luggage, making it well suited for long-distance travel despite its luxury focus.
technology: Technology inside the Flying Spur is both advanced and beautifully integrated into the cabin’s classic design. The dashboard features a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system seamlessly integrated within the wood-trimmed center stack. One of Bentley’s signature features is the optional rotating display, which allows the touchscreen to rotate out of view, revealing a panel with three elegant analog gauges—a compass, a temperature gauge, and a traditional clock—preserving the cabin’s classic luxury aesthetic when digital screens are not desired. The infotainment system supports wireless Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, navigation, and a Wi-Fi hotspot, ensuring modern connectivity for all occupants. Audio quality is equally impressive. A 10-speaker sound system is standard, while optional upgrades include a 16-speaker Bang & Olufsen audio system or the flagship 19-speaker Naim premium sound system, widely considered one of the best in the automotive industry.
safety: The Flying Spur incorporates a range of modern safety technologies designed to assist the driver and enhance overall vehicle safety. However, like many ultra-luxury vehicles, several advanced systems are available as optional upgrades rather than standard equipment. Standard features include forward-collision warning with pedestrian detection, which alerts the driver when a potential collision is detected ahead. The system can be paired with automatic emergency braking, which can apply braking force to help mitigate or prevent an impact. Optional driver-assistance technologies include adaptive cruise control, lane-keeping assistance, and a night-vision system that uses infrared sensors to detect pedestrians or animals beyond the reach of the headlights. For official crash-test ratings and safety evaluations, buyers can consult the testing results provided by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.
warranty: The Flying Spur is backed by a warranty program typical for ultra-luxury vehicles. Bentley provides a three-year limited warranty with unlimited mileage, ensuring coverage regardless of how far the vehicle is driven during the coverage period. The powertrain warranty also lasts three years with unlimited mileage, covering major mechanical components such as the engine and transmission. Complimentary scheduled maintenance is included for one year or 10,000 miles, ensuring the vehicle receives proper servicing during the initial ownership period.
pros: Stunning handcrafted interior, powerful hybrid V-8 delivering up to 771 hp, remarkable sports-sedan performance, and nearly limitless customization make the Flying Spur one of the most desirable ultra-luxury sedans available.
cons: Extremely high pricing, optional advanced driver-assistance features, and occasional hesitation during hybrid power transitions slightly affect the otherwise flawless luxury experience.
mn_take: The 2026 Bentley Flying Spur perfectly blends limousine luxury, handcrafted elegance, and supercar-like hybrid performance, making it one of the most complete ultra-luxury sedans on the road today.

car_name: 2026 Bentley Bentayga Review: Ultra-Luxury Performance Meets Bespoke Craftsmanship
overview: The 2026 Bentley Bentayga continues to stand as one of the most opulent and powerful SUVs ever produced by Bentley Motors. Blending traditional Bentley craftsmanship with modern performance engineering, the Bentayga offers the rare ability to deliver limousine-like luxury while still providing sports-car-level acceleration. From its imposing grille and jewel-like LED lighting to its lavish interior filled with handcrafted leather, real wood veneers, and polished metal accents, the Bentayga embodies the brand’s signature approach to luxury. Despite its large size and weight, this SUV remains surprisingly agile, thanks to sophisticated suspension systems, all-wheel steering, and powerful engine options. With rivals such as the Rolls‑Royce Cullinan and Lamborghini Urus competing in the ultra-luxury SUV segment, the Bentayga strikes a unique balance between grand-touring comfort and high-performance capability.
pricing:
The 2026 Bentayga lineup offers a wide range of trims and customization options, allowing buyers to tailor the vehicle to their exact preferences. Pricing begins around $210,000 and can climb beyond $340,000 depending on trim level and bespoke features from Bentley’s Mulliner division.

Estimated Trim Pricing

- Hybrid – $210,000
- V-8 – $210,000
- S Hybrid – $238,000
- V-8 Extended Wheelbase – $239,000
- Azure Hybrid – $244,000
- S V-8 – $246,000
- Azure V-8 – $252,000
- S Black Edition V-8 – $267,000
- Azure V-8 Extended Wheelbase – $276,000
- Speed – $280,000
- Mulliner Extended Wheelbase – $342,000

Among these variants, the S V-8 offers a compelling balance of performance, luxury features, and relative value, while the Speed model represents the most performance-focused Bentayga available.
drivetrain:
The Bentayga lineup offers multiple powertrain choices that cater to different buyer priorities—from efficiency to outright performance. At the entry level sits a plug-in hybrid powertrain pairing a turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 engine with an electric motor, producing a combined 456 horsepower. This setup allows the Bentayga to deliver quiet electric driving for short distances while still maintaining the effortless power expected from a Bentley. For buyers seeking traditional Bentley muscle, the twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 generates 542 horsepower in the Bentayga S, delivering rapid acceleration and a muscular soundtrack. The flagship Bentayga Speed raises the performance bar further with a 641-horsepower twin-turbo V-8, making it the most powerful Bentayga to date. All models utilize an eight-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive, ensuring strong traction and smooth power delivery. Bentley’s advanced chassis technologies—including adaptive air suspension, active anti-roll systems, and all-wheel steering—allow this large SUV to corner with surprising composure while still maintaining exceptional ride comfort.

Despite its substantial size and luxury-focused mission, the Bentayga delivers sports-car-like acceleration depending on the chosen powertrain. The Bentayga Azure Hybrid can reach 0–60 mph in approximately 4.5 seconds, an impressive figure for a plug-in luxury SUV. Models equipped with the twin-turbo V-8 are significantly quicker, with the Bentayga S achieving 0–60 mph in just 3.5 seconds. According to Bentley, the high-performance Bentayga Speed is capable of accelerating from 0–60 mph in around 3.4 seconds, placing it among the quickest luxury SUVs on the market.

Efficiency varies depending on the selected powertrain. The plug-in hybrid version uses an 18-kWh battery pack and offers approximately 25 miles of electric-only driving range according to official estimates, though real-world testing has shown that the vehicle can exceed this figure under favorable conditions. For traditional gasoline models, the V-8 variants deliver EPA estimates of roughly 14 mpg in the city and 21 mpg on the highway, while the hybrid models improve efficiency with ratings around 19 mpg city and 23 mpg highway.
interior: Inside, the Bentayga showcases the meticulous craftsmanship that defines the Bentley brand. The cabin is filled with hand-stitched leather upholstery, genuine wood veneers, knurled metal controls, and customizable ambient lighting, creating an environment that feels more like a luxury lounge than a traditional SUV interior. The Bentayga is typically configured as a two-row SUV, although buyers can choose between a three-seat rear bench or individual rear bucket seats that offer extensive adjustment, heating, ventilation, and massage functions. The optional Extended Wheelbase (EWB) version significantly increases rear legroom, transforming the second row into a true executive-class seating area. Bentley offers extraordinary customization options through its Mulliner bespoke division, allowing owners to specify unique materials, colors, stitching patterns, and trim finishes. Additional luxury touches include 22-way adjustable rear seats, reclining up to 40 degrees, a rear bottle cooler, and even a biometric safe with fingerprint recognition. Cargo capacity remains practical for a luxury SUV, with enough space for approximately nine carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats.
technology: Technology in the Bentayga blends modern digital interfaces with classic Bentley design. The centerpiece of the dashboard is a 10.9-inch touchscreen infotainment system that supports navigation, wireless Apple CarPlay, and Android Auto connectivity, allowing seamless smartphone integration. Rear passengers can enjoy optional 10.2-inch entertainment displays mounted behind the front seats, which provide access to streaming media, web browsing, and vehicle controls. The system effectively transforms the rear cabin into a private entertainment lounge during long journeys. Audio quality is equally impressive. A 12-speaker sound system comes standard, but audiophiles will likely prefer the optional 20-speaker Naim premium audio system, widely regarded as one of the finest in any production vehicle.
safety: Despite its luxury focus, the Bentayga also incorporates modern driver-assistance technology to enhance safety and driver confidence. However, many advanced features are optional rather than standard, reflecting the vehicle’s bespoke luxury positioning. Standard safety equipment includes automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, which can help prevent or mitigate collisions by automatically applying the brakes if the system detects an imminent impact. Optional driver-assistance features include lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, and an advanced night-vision system that uses infrared technology to detect pedestrians or animals beyond the reach of the headlights. For official crash-test ratings and safety evaluations, buyers can refer to assessments conducted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.
warranty: Warranty coverage for the Bentayga is typical for an ultra-luxury brand, though it is not as comprehensive as some rivals in the segment. The vehicle comes with a three-year limited warranty with unlimited mileage, meaning owners are protected regardless of how many miles they accumulate during that period. The powertrain warranty also lasts three years with unlimited mileage, covering major components such as the engine and transmission. Bentley also includes complimentary scheduled maintenance for the first year or 10,000 miles, ensuring the vehicle receives proper servicing during the early ownership period.
pros: Exceptional craftsmanship, powerful V-8 performance with up to 641 hp, extensive customization options, and limousine-level luxury make the Bentayga one of the most desirable ultra-luxury SUVs on the market.
cons: Extremely high pricing, optional driver-assistance features that should be standard at this level, and a ride that can feel firm in sportier variants slightly diminish the otherwise lavish experience.
mn_take: The 2026 Bentley Bentayga blends handcrafted luxury, immense power, and near-limitless customization into a flagship SUV that feels as exclusive and indulgent as any Bentley grand tourer.

car_name: 2026 Audi RS Q8 Review: 631-HP Super SUV with Lamborghini-Level Performance
overview: The 2026 RS Q8 stands as the most powerful and performance-focused SUV in the lineup of Audi. Built on the same platform as the Lamborghini Urus, the RS Q8 quietly hides extraordinary performance beneath the styling of a sophisticated luxury SUV. While the Urus screams for attention, the RS Q8 takes a more understated approach—yet it delivers nearly identical mechanical capability and thrilling acceleration. Under its sculpted hood lies a brutal twin-turbocharged V-8 capable of launching the large SUV with astonishing force. Despite weighing over two tons, the RS Q8 feels agile and composed thanks to advanced suspension technology, precise steering, and Audi’s legendary all-wheel-drive system. The vehicle also balances its performance credentials with impressive practicality, offering generous passenger space and cargo capacity, making it equally capable as a daily luxury family vehicle. For buyers who want supercar-level performance in a vehicle that still blends into everyday traffic, the RS Q8 delivers a unique proposition: a stealthy, brutally quick luxury SUV that combines performance, technology, and practicality in a single package.
pricing:
The 2026 RS Q8 lineup is straightforward, with a single high-performance model available.

RS Q8 Performance: Starting at $140,190

Even in base form, the RS Q8 Performance comes extremely well equipped. Standard features include adaptive air suspension, 22-inch alloy wheels, heated and ventilated sport seats, and a 17-speaker Bang & Olufsen premium audio system. Buyers can further enhance the vehicle with optional cosmetic upgrades, carbon-ceramic brakes, and additional driver-assistance features. Although the price exceeds $140,000, the RS Q8 still represents strong value compared with the mechanically related Lamborghini Urus, which costs significantly more while offering similar performance hardware.
drivetrain:
The RS Q8 Performance is powered by a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 engine that produces 631 horsepower, making it one of the most powerful SUVs currently offered by Audi. This engine is paired with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system, which improves efficiency and helps smooth the start-stop function during everyday driving. Power is delivered to all four wheels through an eight-speed automatic transmission and Audi’s quattro all-wheel-drive system, providing exceptional traction in all weather conditions. The RS Q8 also features a mechanical center differential and electromechanical active roll stabilization, a system that uses electric motors to stiffen the suspension during aggressive cornering to reduce body roll. Despite its size, the RS Q8 handles corners with surprising agility. The adaptive air suspension continuously adjusts ride stiffness, allowing the SUV to transition smoothly from comfortable highway cruising to sharp performance handling when the driver selects a sportier drive mode. During testing, the RS Q8 demonstrated remarkable balance between ride comfort and performance capability, making it one of the most versatile performance SUVs available.

For a large luxury SUV, the RS Q8 delivers breathtaking acceleration. With launch control engaged, it rockets from 0 to 60 mph in just 3.1 seconds, a figure that places it among the quickest SUVs in the world. Remarkably, that time matches the acceleration recorded by the far more expensive Lamborghini Urus, highlighting just how closely related the two vehicles are beneath their different bodywork. The RS Q8’s explosive power delivery and immense grip make high-speed acceleration feel effortless.

Performance of this level inevitably comes at the cost of efficiency.
EPA Fuel Economy Estimates
- City: 14 mpg
- Highway: 20 mpg
- Combined: 16 mpg
While these numbers are relatively low, they are typical for high-performance V-8 SUVs in this class. In real-world highway testing, the RS Q8 performed slightly better, returning approximately 22 mpg at steady cruising speeds during a 75-mph highway evaluation.
interior: Inside, the RS Q8 offers a luxurious and high-tech cabin that blends sporty character with everyday comfort. The design is largely shared with the standard Q8, but the RS model adds sportier trim elements, contrast stitching, and RS-specific badging throughout the interior. The front seats are heavily bolstered to hold occupants in place during spirited driving, yet they remain comfortable enough for long highway journeys. High-quality materials such as fine leather upholstery, aluminum accents, and optional carbon-fiber trim give the cabin a premium atmosphere. Rear-seat passengers benefit from the Q8’s spacious design, which provides generous legroom and headroom for adults. This makes the RS Q8 one of the more practical performance SUVs for families or long-distance travel. Cargo capacity also remains impressive. In testing, the RS Q8 accommodated eight carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats and a total of 23 suitcases with the rear seats folded flat, giving it the versatility expected from a luxury SUV.
technology: Inside, the RS Q8 offers a luxurious and high-tech cabin that blends sporty character with everyday comfort. The design is largely shared with the standard Q8, but the RS model adds sportier trim elements, contrast stitching, and RS-specific badging throughout the interior. The front seats are heavily bolstered to hold occupants in place during spirited driving, yet they remain comfortable enough for long highway journeys. High-quality materials such as fine leather upholstery, aluminum accents, and optional carbon-fiber trim give the cabin a premium atmosphere. Rear-seat passengers benefit from the Q8’s spacious design, which provides generous legroom and headroom for adults. This makes the RS Q8 one of the more practical performance SUVs for families or long-distance travel. Cargo capacity also remains impressive. In testing, the RS Q8 accommodated eight carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats and a total of 23 suitcases with the rear seats folded flat, giving it the versatility expected from a luxury SUV.
safety: The RS Q8 comes equipped with a comprehensive range of driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance safety and driver confidence without compromising performance. Standard safety equipment includes automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection, which can detect potential collisions and apply braking if the driver fails to react in time. The SUV also includes lane-departure warning and lane-keeping assist, helping keep the vehicle centered within its lane during highway driving. Another key standard feature is adaptive cruise control, which automatically adjusts the vehicle’s speed to maintain a safe following distance from traffic ahead. This system is particularly helpful during long-distance highway travel or in stop-and-go traffic conditions. Crash-test safety evaluations for the RS Q8 can be reviewed through the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, both of which independently evaluate vehicle safety performance and structural crash protection.
warranty:
Warranty coverage for the RS Q8 follows the standard plan offered by Audi, which provides protection comparable to most European luxury brands.
- Limited Warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years or 30,000 miles
The complimentary maintenance program helps reduce ownership costs during the first few years by covering scheduled service visits such as oil changes, inspections, and basic maintenance tasks. While the coverage is competitive within the luxury segment, some mainstream manufacturers offer longer powertrain warranties.
pros: Massive 631-hp twin-turbo V-8 performance, impressive handling for a large SUV, luxurious and tech-rich cabin, and exceptional practicality for a high-performance vehicle.
cons: Fuel economy is predictably poor, exhaust note lacks the drama expected from such a powerful engine, and the RS6 Avant offers a more engaging driving experience at a similar price.
mn_take: The 2026 Audi RS Q8 delivers Lamborghini-level performance in a more subtle and practical package, making it one of the most versatile and powerful luxury SUVs on the road today.

car_name: 2026 Audi RS7 Review: A 621-HP Luxury Super Sedan with Supercar Acceleration
overview:
The 2026 RS7 continues to stand as one of the most dramatic performance sedans in the luxury segment. Built on Audi’s elegant fastback four-door design, the RS7 blends a sleek coupe-like roofline with the practicality of a hatchback and the brutal acceleration of a high-performance sports car. Wide fenders, aggressive air intakes, and signature oval exhaust tips instantly distinguish it from the regular A7 lineup, while the sloping rear profile gives it a striking silhouette that remains one of the most attractive designs in the premium sport-sedan class.

Although its platform is nearing the end of its lifecycle, the RS7 still delivers an incredibly compelling combination of luxury, speed, and everyday usability. Under the hood lies a ferocious twin-turbocharged V-8 capable of launching the large four-door sedan with near-supercar intensity, yet the cabin maintains the calm refinement and craftsmanship expected from a flagship Audi performance model. With its spacious interior, generous cargo capacity, and blistering acceleration, the RS7 remains a multi-talented machine that balances performance excitement with real-world practicality.
pricing:
The 2026 RS7 lineup is simple, with a single well-equipped Performance model available.

RS7 Performance: Starting at $135,295

Because Audi offers only one trim, buyers primarily choose from optional packages and performance upgrades. Popular additions include the Driver Assistance Package, which brings advanced safety systems such as adaptive cruise control and lane-keeping assist. Enthusiasts may also opt for the RS Sport Exhaust system, which amplifies the V-8’s aggressive sound, or the RS Sport Suspension Plus package featuring Dynamic Ride Control for sharper handling dynamics. For maximum braking capability, Audi offers optional carbon-ceramic brakes, which improve heat resistance and stopping power while also raising the electronically limited top speed to approximately 190 mph. However, this upgrade alone can cost more than $8,000, making it one of the most expensive options available.
drivetrain:
The RS7 Performance is powered by a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 engine paired with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system that improves efficiency and throttle response. In its latest Performance specification, the engine produces 621 horsepower and 627 lb-ft of torque, representing a noticeable increase over earlier RS7 models that delivered 591 horsepower. Power is sent to all four wheels through a smooth eight-speed automatic transmission and Audi’s renowned quattro all-wheel-drive system, ensuring exceptional traction in both dry and slippery conditions. The RS7 also features rear-wheel steering, which improves maneuverability at low speeds and stability during high-speed cornering. The chassis feels remarkably composed despite the car’s size and weight. The standard adaptive air suspension allows drivers to switch between comfortable cruising and firmer performance settings, although opting for the larger 22-inch wheels can make the ride slightly harsher over rough pavement. In testing, models equipped with optional carbon-ceramic brakes stopped from 70 mph in just 143 feet, while the RS7 generated an impressive 1.06 g of lateral grip on the skidpad.

With launch control engaged, the RS7 Performance delivers explosive acceleration that rivals many dedicated sports cars. Testing has shown a 0-to-60 mph time of just 2.9 seconds, an astonishing figure for a luxury sedan weighing well over two tons. For comparison, the high-performance Cadillac CT5‑V Blackwing requires roughly 3.7 seconds to reach 60 mph in testing, while the all-wheel-drive BMW M5 achieves the sprint in approximately 3.0 seconds. These numbers highlight just how brutally quick the RS7 remains within the premium sports-sedan segment.

Performance of this magnitude inevitably comes with a fuel-consumption trade-off.
EPA Fuel Economy Estimates
- City: 14 mpg
- Highway: 21 mpg
- Combined: 16 mpg
Despite these modest figures, real-world highway testing has returned approximately 23 mpg under steady cruising conditions. Still, the RS7’s powerful V-8 means it remains significantly thirstier than smaller luxury sedans, especially when driven aggressively.
interior:
The RS7’s cabin is a showcase of Audi’s signature blend of minimalist design and premium craftsmanship. High-quality materials such as fine leather upholstery, brushed aluminum trim, and optional carbon-fiber accents create a sophisticated yet sporty atmosphere throughout the interior. The driver is greeted by a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster known as Audi’s Virtual Cockpit, which can display navigation maps, performance data, and customizable gauges. The front sport seats offer excellent support during spirited driving and come standard with heating and ventilation, though some drivers may find their firm cushioning slightly tiring on extended journeys.

In the rear, the RS7 officially seats five passengers, though the back seat is most comfortable for two adults due to the large center tunnel. The 40/20/40 split-folding rear seats add versatility for transporting longer cargo while still carrying passengers. One of the RS7’s key advantages over traditional sport sedans is its hatchback design. Behind the rear seats, the car offers 25 cubic feet of cargo space, significantly more than many competitors. Folding the rear seats expands total capacity to 49 cubic feet, making the RS7 surprisingly practical for luggage, sports equipment, or road-trip gear. In testing, the cargo area accommodated seven carry-on suitcases with the seats up and 20 suitcases with the seats folded.
technology: The RS7 features Audi’s sophisticated dual-screen infotainment system, which integrates digital controls seamlessly into the center dashboard. A 10.1-inch touchscreen handles navigation, multimedia, and smartphone integration, while a secondary 8.6-inch touchscreen below it controls climate functions and additional vehicle settings. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, enabling seamless smartphone connectivity for apps, messaging, and navigation. The system also includes built-in navigation, wireless device charging, and a subscription-based Wi-Fi hotspot, ensuring passengers remain connected on the road. Audi offers a premium audio experience through a Bang & Olufsen sound system that produces an impressive 1820 watts of output through 19 speakers, delivering exceptional sound clarity throughout the cabin. Although the dual-screen interface looks modern and responsive, some drivers may find the lower touchscreen slightly distracting to operate while driving, particularly when adjusting climate settings.
safety:

A 10.1-inch touchscreen handles navigation, multimedia, and smartphone integration, while a secondary 8.6-inch touchscreen below it controls climate functions and additional vehicle settings. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, enabling seamless smartphone connectivity for apps, messaging, and navigation. Although the dual-screen interface looks modern and responsive, some drivers may find the lower touchscreen slightly distracting to operate while driving, particularly when adjusting climate settings.
warranty:
Warranty coverage for the RS7 aligns with other vehicles from Audi, providing solid protection for the first several years of ownership.
- Limited Warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years or 36,000 miles
For 2026, Audi also includes the Audi Signature Care program, which covers scheduled maintenance such as oil changes, inspections, and service visits during the first three years of ownership. While this coverage is competitive within the luxury segment, some mainstream brands offer longer powertrain warranties.
pros: Explosive 621-hp twin-turbo V-8 performance, stunning fastback design, luxurious interior technology, and surprisingly generous cargo space for a high-performance sedan.
cons: Fuel economy remains poor at 16 mpg combined, ride quality can become firm with large wheels, and the current generation is approaching the end of its lifecycle.
mn_take: The 2026 Audi RS7 remains one of the most exciting luxury sport sedans available, combining near-supercar acceleration, elegant design, and everyday usability into a remarkably well-rounded performance machine.

car_name: 2026 Audi RS6 Avant Review: A 621-HP Super Wagon That Blends Supercar Speed with Everyday Practicality
overview: The 2026 RS6 Avant proves that practicality and outrageous performance can coexist in the same machine. Built on the refined luxury underpinnings of the A6 wagon but infused with the aggressive engineering of Audi Sport, the RS6 Avant transforms the humble family hauler into a genuine performance monster. Its wide stance, flared fenders, large air intakes, and signature oval exhaust outlets instantly signal that this is no ordinary station wagon. At its heart lies a thunderous twin-turbocharged V-8 that delivers supercar-level acceleration, yet the RS6 still retains the everyday usability expected from a wagon—ample rear passenger space and generous cargo capacity. That unusual mix makes the RS6 Avant one of the most desirable enthusiast cars on sale today. It’s capable of thrilling back-road drives in the morning and hauling groceries, sports gear, or luggage later in the day without compromise.
pricing:
For the 2026 model year, the RS6 Avant lineup remains simple, with a single high-performance trim available.

RS6 Avant Performance: Starting at $131,995

Because the Performance trim already comes loaded with premium materials and advanced technology, most buyers will focus on optional packages rather than additional trims. The Sport Suspension Plus package, which replaces the standard adaptive air suspension with a more track-focused setup featuring Dynamic Ride Control, is a worthwhile upgrade for enthusiasts seeking sharper handling. Audi also offers an RS Sport Exhaust system that enhances the V-8 soundtrack, along with optional carbon-ceramic brakes that improve stopping performance and raise the car’s electronically limited top speed to 190 mph.
drivetrain:
The RS6 Avant Performance is powered by a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 paired with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system, producing a staggering 621 horsepower. Power is routed through a smooth yet responsive eight-speed automatic transmission and Audi’s legendary quattro all-wheel-drive system, which provides excellent traction in nearly all driving conditions. Beyond raw power, the RS6 Avant benefits from sophisticated chassis technology designed to balance comfort and precision. Four-wheel steering improves agility at low speeds and stability at highway speeds, while a torque-vectoring rear differential helps distribute power between the rear wheels to enhance cornering grip. Even though the RS6 weighs more than many sports cars, these systems make it feel surprisingly nimble on winding roads. During testing, models equipped with carbon-ceramic brakes managed to stop from 70 mph in just 140 feet, demonstrating the wagon’s impressive braking capability. Combined with sharp steering response and firm body control, the RS6 delivers a driving experience that rivals dedicated performance sedans and coupes.

With launch control engaged, the RS6 Avant Performance rockets from 0 to 60 mph in just 3.2 seconds, placing it firmly in supercar territory. For context, the recently introduced BMW M5 Touring achieved a nearly identical 3.1-second sprint in testing, showing just how competitive this segment of high-performance wagons has become. The RS6’s explosive acceleration is accompanied by a deep, muscular exhaust note that grows more aggressive under heavy throttle, further reinforcing the car’s performance credentials.

Given its enormous power output, fuel efficiency is understandably not the RS6 Avant’s strongest attribute.

EPA Estimates:
- City: 14 mpg
- Highway: 21 mpg
- Combined: 16 mpg
While these figures may appear modest, they are relatively reasonable considering the vehicle’s 621-hp twin-turbo V-8. By comparison, the more comfort-oriented Audi A6 Allroad achieves approximately 22 mpg in the city and 30 mpg on the highway, though it cannot match the RS6’s breathtaking performance.
interior:
Inside, the RS6 Avant blends luxury craftsmanship with sporty design cues that emphasize its performance nature. The cabin features extensive use of premium leather upholstery, contrast stitching, and optional carbon-fiber trim elements that give the interior a sophisticated yet athletic feel. Up front, the driver sits behind a 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster, part of Audi’s Virtual Cockpit system, which allows customizable display layouts for navigation, performance data, and driver information. The 10-way power-adjustable front seats are wrapped in high-quality leather and come standard with heating, ventilation, and extendable lower cushions to improve long-distance comfort.

Rear passengers are treated to impressive comfort for a performance vehicle. The 40/20/40 split-folding rear bench provides flexible seating and cargo arrangements, while available rear seat heating and dedicated climate controls ensure comfort for passengers during longer journeys. Legroom and foot room in the second row are generous for the segment, and the rear seats are designed to easily accommodate child safety seats. Cargo space remains a major advantage of the wagon body style. The RS6 Avant offers 30 cubic feet of cargo capacity behind the rear seats, expanding significantly when the seats are folded flat. In real-world testing, the cargo area was able to accommodate nine carry-on suitcases with the rear seats up and 23 suitcases when folded, making it one of the most practical high-performance vehicles available.
technology: Audi equips the RS6 Avant with a sophisticated dual-screen infotainment layout that integrates entertainment, navigation, and vehicle settings into a sleek digital interface. The primary 10.1-inch touchscreen handles multimedia functions, navigation, and smartphone connectivity, while a secondary 8.6-inch touchscreen below it controls climate settings and additional vehicle functions. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, allowing seamless smartphone integration for music streaming, navigation apps, and messaging. Built-in navigation, wireless device charging, and a Wi-Fi hotspot are also included, ensuring the RS6 remains fully connected for modern drivers. warranty:

pros: Explosive 621-hp twin-turbo V-8 performance, exceptional handling with quattro AWD, luxurious interior, and genuine wagon practicality with 30 cubic feet of cargo space.

car_name: 2026 Audi RS3 Review — 401-HP Five-Cylinder Sports Sedan with Explosive Performance
overview: The Audi RS3 may be the smallest performance sedan in Audi’s lineup, but it delivers performance that rivals much larger and more expensive sports cars. This compact four-door packs a charismatic turbocharged five-cylinder engine, aggressive styling, and a highly capable all-wheel-drive system into a surprisingly small footprint. Audi’s RS division has built a reputation for blending everyday usability with serious performance, and the RS3 is a perfect example of that philosophy. It shares its basic platform with the Audi A3 and Audi S3, but the RS3 adds significantly more power, a stiffer suspension setup, upgraded brakes, and a torque-vectoring all-wheel-drive system designed for enthusiastic driving. Despite its compact dimensions, the RS3 manages to deliver big thrills. Its distinctive five-cylinder soundtrack, rapid acceleration, and playful chassis make it one of the most entertaining compact sports sedans currently available. For 2026, the RS3 continues largely unchanged after receiving updates the previous year, meaning buyers still get the same formula of strong performance and modern Audi luxury.
pricing:
The 2026 Audi RS3 is offered as a single, fully equipped trim.

Trim pricing:
- RS3 – $67,395
Audi keeps the options list relatively short, but buyers can add a few performance upgrades. For example, enthusiasts who plan to take their RS3 to track days may want to opt for Pirelli P Zero Trofeo R performance tires, which dramatically increase grip and cornering capability. For everyday driving, however, the standard tires provide better longevity and ride comfort.
drivetrain:
Powering the RS3 is one of the most unique engines in the modern performance-car world: a turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-five engine. This distinctive powerplant produces 401 horsepower and delivers a characterful exhaust note that stands out from the more common four- and six-cylinder engines used by many competitors. The engine is paired with a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission that delivers lightning-fast shifts and responds quickly to throttle inputs. Power is sent to all four wheels through Audi’s quattro all-wheel-drive system, ensuring excellent traction during hard launches and spirited cornering.

One of the highlights of the RS3 is its advanced torque-vectoring rear differential, which can distribute power between the rear wheels to improve cornering agility. Audi also includes a special RS Torque Rear driving mode, often referred to as “drift mode,” which allows the rear end to rotate more freely for playful handling characteristics. Compared with the regular A3 and S3 models, the RS3 also benefits from larger brakes, a stiffer suspension, and stickier performance tires. These upgrades transform the compact sedan into a serious performance machine that feels equally comfortable on twisty back roads or racetracks.

Thanks to its powerful engine and all-wheel-drive traction, the RS3 delivers truly impressive acceleration for a compact sedan. Independent testing shows the RS3 can sprint from 0–60 mph in just 3.2 seconds, placing it firmly in sports-car territory. That figure is roughly a full second quicker than the Audi S3, highlighting the significant performance upgrade offered by the RS model. Despite this explosive acceleration, the car remains relatively easy to drive in everyday situations, with smooth power delivery and predictable handling.

Performance cars rarely prioritize fuel efficiency, but the RS3 still manages respectable numbers for its segment. The EPA estimates fuel economy at 20 mpg in the city and 29 mpg on the highway, with a combined rating of 23 mpg. In real-world highway testing at 75 mph, the RS3 performed even better than expected, achieving 34 mpg, which is impressive for a high-performance sports sedan.
interior: Inside, the RS3 shares much of its design with the standard A3 lineup but includes several upgrades that emphasize its sporty nature. The cabin features aggressively bolstered sport seats, premium materials, and distinctive RS-specific design elements that create a high-performance atmosphere. The dashboard layout is clean and driver-focused, with digital gauges positioned directly in front of the driver and large air vents placed high on the dashboard. Audi also offers a head-up display that projects key driving information onto the windshield. Despite the premium feel, interior space remains limited due to the car’s compact dimensions. The rear seat can accommodate passengers for short trips, but taller adults may find the space cramped. Cargo space is also modest. The trunk provides about 11 cubic feet of storage, which is smaller than many rivals. However, the 40/20/40 split-folding rear seats allow owners to expand cargo capacity when needed.
technology: The RS3 comes equipped with a 10.1-inch infotainment touchscreen positioned at the center of the dashboard. The system can be controlled through touch inputs, steering-wheel buttons, or voice commands. The interface supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, making it easy for drivers to integrate their smartphones. Built-in navigation, wireless charging, and a Wi-Fi hotspot are also available. Audi includes a 15-speaker Sonos premium audio system as standard equipment, delivering impressive sound quality throughout the cabin. The infotainment platform also allows users to download third-party apps such as Spotify and YouTube directly to the system.
safety: Although the RS3 focuses heavily on performance, Audi still equips it with a solid set of driver-assistance technologies. Standard safety features include automatic emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, and automatic high-beam headlights. These systems help improve safety and convenience during everyday driving.
warranty: Audi provides competitive warranty coverage for the RS3. The sedan includes a four-year or 50,000-mile limited warranty as well as the same coverage period for the powertrain. Audi also includes three years or 30,000 miles of complimentary scheduled maintenance, which helps reduce early ownership costs
pros: Unique five-cylinder engine, explosive acceleration, playful handling, and aggressive styling.
cons: Tight rear seating, limited trunk space, and a stiff ride on rough roads.
mn_take: The 2026 Audi RS3 delivers thrilling performance and a unique engine character in a compact package, making it one of the most exciting small sports sedans on the market.

car_name: 2027 Audi A6 e-tron Review — Nearly 400 Miles of Range in Audi’s New Electric Luxury Sedan
overview:
The Audi A6 e‑tron marks a major shift for Audi’s midsize luxury sedan lineup. While it shares a name with the traditional Audi A6, the electric version is essentially an entirely new vehicle with very little mechanical overlap. Instead of a conventional combustion engine and classic three-box sedan shape, the A6 e-tron adopts a sleek Sportback fastback design and runs purely on electric power. Built on Audi’s advanced Premium Platform Electric (PPE) architecture, the A6 e-tron focuses on delivering long range, modern technology, and everyday usability rather than outright performance. It sits in the rapidly growing luxury EV segment, competing with cars like the Tesla Model S, Lucid Air, and BMW i5.

For 2027, the A6 e-tron returns after skipping the 2026 model year. Audi has redesigned the steering wheel controls, bringing back its popular scroll-wheel interface, and has also updated the infotainment system to improve usability. Additionally, all 2027 Audi models now include three years of complimentary scheduled maintenance. Overall, the A6 e-tron is designed as a practical daily-driver EV that delivers impressive range, advanced digital technology, and comfortable interior space in a refined package.
pricing:
The 2027 Audi A6 e-tron starts at $67,995 and goes up to $75,895, depending on the trim level and options.

Trim-wise pricing:
- Premium – $67,995
- Premium Plus – $71,295
- Prestige – $75,895
Among these, the Premium Plus trim offers the best balance of features and price. It adds upgrades such as LED headlamps, a 360-degree camera system, augmented-reality head-up display, and enhanced ambient lighting, making it a compelling middle-ground option. Audi also offers a Quattro dual-motor setup that adds all-wheel drive and more power, which many buyers may find worth the additional cost.
drivetrain:
The A6 e-tron is available with two powertrain configurations.

The base setup uses a single electric motor producing 375 horsepower that drives the rear wheels. Buyers can also choose a dual-motor Quattro all-wheel-drive system that increases output to 456 horsepower. Although these numbers are respectable for a luxury sedan, they fall short of the extreme power figures seen in rivals such as the Lucid Air or higher-performance versions of the Porsche Taycan. Audi clearly positions the A6 e-tron as a balanced daily EV rather than a performance-focused machine. The sedan offers an optional adaptive air suspension system that adjusts ride height and stiffness depending on the driving mode. When cruising at higher speeds, the suspension can lower the vehicle to improve aerodynamic efficiency and increase range. In real-world driving, the A6 e-tron delivers good body control and stable handling, but the steering feels somewhat light and lacks the sporty engagement that enthusiasts might expect from an Audi sedan.

Despite its comfort-focused nature, the A6 e-tron still offers respectable acceleration. The rear-wheel-drive version can accelerate from 0–60 mph in about 4.9 seconds. Audi estimates the more powerful Quattro all-wheel-drive model will reach the same speed in roughly 4.3 seconds. For comparison, the rear-wheel-drive BMW i5 takes about 5.1 seconds to reach 60 mph, meaning the Audi still offers competitive performance within its segment.

One of the strongest aspects of the A6 e-tron is its impressive electric range.The sedan uses a 94.4-kWh lithium-ion battery pack, and Audi claims a driving range between 377 and 392 miles depending on configuration. The single-motor rear-drive model can reach up to 392 miles, while the dual-motor Quattro version delivers approximately 377 miles. This places the A6 e-tron among the longest-range electric sedans currently available. Charging performance is equally strong. The A6 e-tron supports DC fast charging at up to 270 kW, allowing the battery to recharge from 10 percent to 80 percent in about 21 minutes under ideal conditions.

Audi estimates efficiency figures of up to 132 MPGe in the city and 120 MPGe on the highway for the rear-wheel-drive version. The all-wheel-drive model is slightly less efficient, with estimates of 125 MPGe city and 116 MPGe highway.

These numbers make the A6 e-tron one of the more efficient luxury EV sedans in its class.
interior: Inside the cabin, the A6 e-tron emphasizes digital technology and modern design. The dashboard layout is dominated by large digital displays and clean surfaces that create a futuristic atmosphere. One of the standout features is the panoramic glass roof that can switch from transparent to opaque at the press of a button using polymer-dispersed liquid crystal technology. This allows passengers to control sunlight without using a physical sunshade. Higher trims also feature a full-width interior light bar beneath the windshield that visually communicates vehicle status. It can display different lighting signals for functions such as charging, locking, or turn signals. The second row offers reasonable space for adults despite the sloping roofline, although the raised floor means rear passengers may sit with slightly elevated knees. Cargo capacity is generous thanks to the liftback-style rear hatch, making the A6 e-tron more practical than many traditional sedans. The car also includes a small front trunk (frunk) for extra storage.
technology: Technology plays a major role in the A6 e-tron experience. The driver-oriented dashboard features a large OLED display system combining an 11.9-inch digital instrument cluster with a 14.5-inch infotainment touchscreen. Higher-end trims add a 10.9-inch passenger display, allowing the front passenger to control media or navigation independently. The infotainment system runs on Android Automotive OS, providing integrated apps, voice control, and wireless smartphone connectivity. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are included as standard features. Audi also offers a premium Bang & Olufsen sound system with 20 speakers, including speakers integrated into the front seat headrests, delivering an immersive audio experience.
safety: The A6 e-tron comes equipped with several modern driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance safety and convenience. Standard features include automatic emergency braking, lane-departure warning, adaptive cruise control, and a driver-drowsiness monitor. Optional systems add lane-centering assist, a 360-degree surround-view camera system, and additional parking assistance technologies.
warranty: Audi backs the A6 e-tron with warranty coverage similar to its other electric vehicles. The sedan includes a four-year or 50,000-mile limited warranty, along with an eight-year or 100,000-mile battery warranty for the electric components. For the 2027 model year, Audi also includes three years or 30,000 miles of complimentary scheduled maintenance, helping reduce early ownership costs.
pros: Excellent electric range, advanced digital cabin technology, fast charging capability, and comfortable everyday usability.
cons: Conservative exterior design, uninspiring steering feel, and rivals offer more power and luxury.
mn_take: The 2027 Audi A6 e-tron focuses on range, technology, and daily usability rather than excitement, making it a strong long-distance luxury EV even if it lacks the sporty character some competitors offer.

car_name: 2027 Audi e-tron GT Review — 912 HP Electric Super Sedan with Near-Taycan Performance
overview: The Audi e‑tron GT remains one of the most exciting electric performance sedans on sale. When Audi first launched the car, it was essentially the brand’s “moonshot” EV—designed to prove that electric vehicles could deliver not only efficiency but also breathtaking speed and serious driving engagement. Even several years after its debut, the e-tron GT still stands as one of Audi’s most formidable electric machines. Built on the same architecture as the Porsche Taycan, the e-tron GT combines Porsche-grade performance with Audi’s clean design language and refined interior. The result is a sleek four-door coupe that blends supercar acceleration, grand-touring comfort, and everyday usability. For 2027, the model carries forward the extensive updates introduced in 2025 and minor feature adjustments from 2026. That means the latest e-tron GT continues to deliver massive power, sharp handling, and impressive electric range while undercutting many rivals—especially the Porsche Taycan—on price.
pricing:
The 2027 Audi e-tron GT is expected to start at around $130,000 and climb to roughly $172,000 depending on the trim and options.

The lineup begins with the S e-tron GT Premium Plus, which offers strong performance and a generous list of luxury features. Moving up to the S e-tron GT Prestige adds more technology and comfort upgrades, while the range-topping RS e-tron GT Performance focuses on extreme performance with a massive boost in power. While the RS Performance variant delivers staggering performance numbers, the S trim arguably offers the best value in the lineup. It still produces supercar-level acceleration but comes at a significantly lower price.
drivetrain:
The 2027 Audi e-tron GT is expected to start at around $130,000 and climb to roughly $172,000 depending on the trim and options. The lineup begins with the S e-tron GT Premium Plus, which offers strong performance and a generous list of luxury features. Moving up to the S e-tron GT Prestige adds more technology and comfort upgrades, while the range-topping RS e-tron GT Performance focuses on extreme performance with a massive boost in power. While the RS Performance variant delivers staggering performance numbers, the S trim arguably offers the best value in the lineup. It still produces supercar-level acceleration but comes at a significantly lower price.

Performance is one of the e-tron GT’s biggest highlights. In independent testing, the RS e-tron GT Performance can sprint from 0–60 mph in just 2.1 seconds, placing it firmly in supercar territory. For comparison, the Porsche Taycan Turbo Cross Turismo reaches 60 mph in around 2.5 seconds, while the extreme Porsche Taycan Turbo GT does the run in roughly 1.9 seconds. Despite the brutal acceleration, the Audi still maintains excellent ride comfort and composure, making it suitable for both spirited driving and relaxed long-distance travel.

The e-tron GT is powered by a 97.0-kWh lithium-ion battery pack. Depending on the trim and wheel size, the EPA estimates driving range between 278 and 300 miles on a full charge. The S e-tron GT with 20-inch wheels delivers the best range, reaching up to 300 miles, while larger 21-inch wheels slightly reduce the range to around 294 miles. In real-world highway testing, the RS e-tron GT Performance achieved 280 miles, actually exceeding its official EPA estimate of 278 miles. Charging performance is equally impressive. Using a 320-kW DC fast charger, the battery can recharge from 10 to 80 percent in about 18 minutes, making long road trips far more practical.

Despite its extreme performance, the e-tron GT remains relatively efficient for an electric performance car. The S e-tron GT delivers up to 91 MPGe city and 88 MPGe highway, while the RS e-tron GT Performance is rated at 85 MPGe city and 82 MPGe highway.

These numbers place the car competitively within the high-performance EV segment.
interior:
Inside, the e-tron GT blends futuristic technology with traditional Audi craftsmanship. The cabin features an angular dashboard design, high-quality materials, and multiple digital displays that create a modern yet functional environment. Front-seat occupants sit in a low, sporty driving position that reinforces the car’s performance-focused character. Audi offers a variety of interior materials, including traditional leather upholstery as well as a leather-free interior option made from recycled materials, reflecting the brand’s sustainability efforts.

Luxury features include ambient interior lighting, a head-up display, heated and ventilated seats, and optional massage functions. The cabin is quiet and comfortable even at highway speeds, giving the car a grand-touring feel. Rear-seat legroom is respectable for a coupe-style sedan, but the sloping roofline slightly limits rear headroom, making the back seat less comfortable for taller passengers. Cargo capacity includes 9 cubic feet in the rear trunk and an additional 2 cubic feet in the front trunk (frunk), which is typical for performance EVs.
technology: The e-tron GT uses a 10.1-inch central touchscreen for its infotainment system. Unlike some newer Audi models that rely heavily on multiple touchscreens, this setup combines the touchscreen with physical controls and steering-wheel buttons for easier operation. Standard technology features include wireless Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth connectivity, wireless smartphone charging, and a Wi-Fi hotspot. Audi also includes a 16-speaker Bang & Olufsen premium sound system, delivering excellent audio quality that complements the car’s refined interior atmosphere.
safety: The e-tron GT comes equipped with a comprehensive set of driver-assistance technologies designed to improve safety and convenience. Standard features include adaptive cruise control with lane-centering assistance, forward-collision warning with automatic emergency braking, and a surround-view camera system. Optional upgrades add blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, lane-keeping assist, and remote self-parking, which allows the car to park itself via a smartphone app.
warranty: The e-tron GT comes equipped with a comprehensive set of driver-assistance technologies designed to improve safety and convenience. Standard features include adaptive cruise control with lane-centering assistance, forward-collision warning with automatic emergency braking, and a surround-view camera system. Optional upgrades add blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, lane-keeping assist, and remote self-parking, which allows the car to park itself via a smartphone app.
pros: Explosive acceleration, impressive electric range, striking design, and near-Porsche-level performance for less money.
cons: Tight rear headroom, limited cargo space, and a high starting price despite being cheaper than its Porsche counterpart.
mn_take: The 2027 Audi e-tron GT delivers supercar-level acceleration and Taycan-like driving dynamics in a sleek, luxurious package that feels every bit like a futuristic performance flagship.

car_name: 2026 Audi A8 Review — Understated Luxury with Flagship Comfort
overview: The Audi A8 represents the pinnacle of Audi’s sedan lineup, delivering a refined blend of advanced technology, serene ride comfort, and understated elegance. Unlike flashier rivals in the flagship luxury sedan segment, the A8 focuses on quiet sophistication and high-quality craftsmanship rather than dramatic styling. Buyers considering the A8 often cross-shop it with competitors such as the Mercedes-Benz S-Class, BMW 7 Series, and Genesis G90. While those models may offer more powerful engines or bolder design language, the Audi stands out for its balanced driving dynamics, whisper-quiet cabin, and premium materials. For 2026, the A8 remains largely unchanged, continuing with a single well-equipped trim and a focus on comfort-oriented luxury. The sedan features a turbocharged V-6 engine paired with a mild-hybrid system and Audi’s Quattro all-wheel drive, providing smooth performance and confident traction in all weather conditions.
pricing:
The 2026 A8 starts at $96,395, and Audi simplifies the buying process by offering the sedan in a single primary trim level. Instead of multiple trims, the company allows buyers to customize the car through optional equipment packages that add additional luxury and technology.

One of the most desirable upgrades is the Luxury package, which adds features designed to enhance comfort and cabin refinement. This package includes four-wheel steering for improved maneuverability, front seats with massage functions, heated armrests, and special acoustic glass that further reduces outside noise entering the cabin. To obtain the Luxury package, buyers must also select the Executive package, which adds heated rear seats, upgraded leather upholstery, enhanced lighting technology, and a suite of advanced driver-assistance features.

With these packages equipped, the A8 transforms into a true executive sedan that rivals the most luxurious offerings in the segment.
drivetrain:
Powering the A8 is a turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 engine producing 335 horsepower and 331 lb-ft of torque. The engine is paired with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system, which improves efficiency and smooths the operation of the automatic start-stop function during city driving. Power is delivered to all four wheels through Audi’s renowned Quattro all-wheel-drive system and an eight-speed automatic transmission. The powertrain emphasizes smoothness and refinement rather than outright aggression, but the A8 is still capable of impressive performance. The sedan accelerates from 0 to 60 mph in approximately 5.3 seconds, making it quick enough for confident highway merging and effortless overtaking.

On the road, the A8 excels at providing a serene driving experience. The adaptive air suspension glides over road imperfections, maintaining exceptional ride comfort even on rough surfaces. Extensive sound insulation and acoustic materials keep the cabin remarkably quiet, creating an atmosphere that feels more like a luxury lounge than a typical automobile. Despite its large size, the A8 remains surprisingly composed through corners. Its balanced chassis and optional four-wheel steering system help improve agility and make the car feel more manageable in tight city environments.

For buyers seeking significantly more performance, Audi offers the high-performance Audi S8, which features a powerful twin-turbocharged V-8 engine and sport-focused tuning. The A8’s mild-hybrid powertrain helps deliver respectable efficiency for a large luxury sedan. According to EPA estimates, it achieves 19 mpg in the city and 26 mpg on the highway, placing it competitively within its class. While fuel economy is not the primary focus for buyers in this segment, the A8 manages to balance performance and efficiency reasonably well.
interior: Step inside the A8 and the emphasis on luxury becomes immediately apparent. The cabin is spacious, elegantly designed, and filled with high-quality materials. Audi uses premium leather, soft-touch surfaces, aluminum trim, and carefully integrated ambient lighting to create an atmosphere that feels both modern and relaxing. Thanks to the sedan’s long wheelbase, both front and rear passengers enjoy generous legroom and headroom. The seating position is comfortable and supportive, making the A8 well suited for long journeys. The rear seats, in particular, offer an exceptionally comfortable environment. Buyers who opt for the Luxury Rear Seat package can replace the standard rear bench with two individual rear captain’s chairs separated by a center console. These seats feature heating, ventilation, massage functions, and even a heated foot-massage feature, transforming the back seat into an executive-class lounge. Cargo space measures 13 cubic feet, which is typical for vehicles in this class. While it may not be enormous, the trunk is large enough for several suitcases and everyday travel needs.
technology:
Audi equips the A8 with an impressive array of digital technology designed to enhance both convenience and connectivity. The dashboard features the brand’s 12.3-inch Virtual Cockpit digital instrument cluster, which displays navigation, vehicle data, and driving information in crisp, customizable graphics.
The center stack houses Audi’s dual-screen MMI infotainment system, consisting of a 10.1-inch upper touchscreen for media and navigation controls and an 8.6-inch lower touchscreen dedicated to climate and comfort settings. While the two-screen layout can appear complex at first glance, it becomes intuitive with regular use and provides a clean, modern interface. Smartphone connectivity comes standard with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, allowing drivers to integrate their mobile devices seamlessly with the vehicle’s infotainment system. Audi also offers premium audio systems developed by Bang & Olufsen. The standard system features 17 speakers, while the optional 23-speaker advanced system delivers an immersive surround-sound experience throughout the cabin.
safety: The A8 includes a variety of advanced driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance safety and reduce driver fatigue during long journeys. Standard equipment includes automated emergency braking with forward-collision warning, lane-departure warning, and front and rear parking sensors. Additional features such as adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keeping assist are available through optional packages, allowing the sedan to provide an even greater level of driving support on highways and in heavy traffic.
warranty:
The A8 includes a variety of advanced driver-assistance technologies designed to enhance safety and reduce driver fatigue during long journeys. Standard equipment includes automated emergency braking with forward-collision warning, lane-departure warning, and front and rear parking sensors.

Additional features such as adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, and lane-keeping assist are available through optional packages, allowing the sedan to provide an even greater level of driving support on highways and in heavy traffic.
pros: Exceptionally quiet cabin, spacious and luxurious interior, smooth ride quality, and advanced technology features.
cons: Conservative styling, less powerful than some flagship rivals, and several advanced features require optional packages.
mn_take: The 2026 Audi A8 is a refined executive sedan built for buyers who value subtle luxury, cutting-edge technology, and a serene driving experience rather than flashy design or outright performance.

car_name: 2026 Audi A6 Review — A Redesigned Executive Sedan Blending Luxury, Technology, and Performance
overview:
The newly redesigned Audi A6 continues Audi’s tradition of delivering understated luxury with a strong emphasis on comfort, technology, and refined performance. Long known as a sophisticated alternative to more flamboyant executive sedans, the A6 remains a favorite among buyers who prefer elegant styling and advanced engineering over flashy design. For 2026, Audi has given the A6 a complete redesign, introducing updated styling, improved technology, and a more powerful powertrain lineup. The new model retains its classic sedan silhouette but incorporates sharper design cues, a wider stance, and a more modern lighting signature that aligns with Audi’s latest design language.

Under the hood, the A6 now features a turbocharged V-6 engine as standard, paired with quattro all-wheel drive and a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. This combination delivers both smooth cruising and surprisingly quick acceleration. pros: Smooth ride quality, powerful V-6 engine, cutting-edge technology, and refined executive styling.

car_name: 2026 Audi A3 Review — A Compact Luxury Sedan with Premium Tech and Engaging Performance
overview:
The Audi A3 represents the entry point into Audi’s luxury sedan lineup in the United States, offering a refined blend of upscale styling, modern technology, and enjoyable driving dynamics. Despite being the smallest and most affordable sedan in Audi’s portfolio, the A3 manages to deliver the brand’s signature premium experience while maintaining impressive efficiency and everyday usability.

Designed with understated elegance, the A3 features sharp body lines, a bold front grille, and sleek LED lighting that give it a distinctly modern appearance. Inside, the sedan showcases a driver-focused cockpit with digital displays and thoughtful ergonomics, reflecting Audi’s reputation for advanced cabin design. While its compact dimensions limit rear passenger space and cargo capacity, the A3 remains an appealing choice for buyers seeking a stylish and tech-forward luxury sedan.

Power comes from a 201-horsepower turbocharged four-cylinder engine paired with a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive, delivering smooth acceleration and confident handling in a variety of driving conditions. The A3’s playful character and balanced ride make daily commuting more enjoyable, even if it stops short of being a full-fledged sports sedan. Competitors in this segment include the Acura Integra, Cadillac CT4, and Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class.
pricing:
MSRP Range: $41,395 – $44,295
Available Trims:
- Premium — $41,395
- Premium Plus — $44,295
The Premium trim offers the best value for most buyers, especially when equipped with the Convenience package. This option bundle adds several desirable features typically found on the higher Premium Plus trim, including adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitoring, memory seat and mirror settings, proximity keyless entry, and wireless smartphone charging, all while keeping the price relatively affordable. The Premium Plus trim builds upon the base model with additional technology and comfort upgrades, including the option for Audi’s Tech package, which introduces a larger digital instrument cluster and expanded connectivity features.
drivetrain:
Every A3 is powered by a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 201 horsepower and 236 lb-ft of torque. This engine works alongside a 48-volt mild-hybrid system, which improves efficiency and smooths out the start-stop operation during city driving. Power is sent to all four wheels through Audi’s Quattro all-wheel-drive system and a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, delivering quick shifts and responsive acceleration.

While the A3 isn’t designed to be a hardcore performance sedan, it remains lively and engaging on the road. The engine provides brisk acceleration, helping the car reach 0–60 mph in roughly 6.0 seconds, which is competitive for the segment. The chassis feels well balanced, and the suspension delivers a comfortable ride over most road surfaces while still maintaining enough agility to make cornering enjoyable. Steering feedback, however, is somewhat muted compared with sportier rivals, meaning the A3 leans more toward refined daily driving rather than pure driving excitement. Buyers seeking more aggressive performance may consider stepping up to the 328-horsepower Audi S3 or the high-performance Audi RS3.

Fuel efficiency is one of the A3’s strong points, particularly for a luxury sedan equipped with all-wheel drive.
EPA Estimates:
- 24 mpg city
- 34 mpg highway
- 28 mpg combined
In real-world highway testing at 75 mph, the A3 performed even better, returning an impressive 40 mpg, which exceeds its official EPA rating and makes it one of the more efficient vehicles in its class.
interior: Inside the cabin, the A3 delivers a modern and driver-focused environment. The dashboard design angles toward the driver, creating a cockpit-like feel that emphasizes control and accessibility. High-quality materials such as leather upholstery and metallic trim give the interior a premium appearance, although some lower sections of the cabin feature harder plastics that slightly diminish the overall luxury feel. The front seats are comfortable and supportive, offering a pleasant driving position that works well for both short commutes and longer highway journeys. The compact dimensions of the A3 become more noticeable in the rear, where space is somewhat limited.
