The back seat is best suited for children or shorter adults, as taller passengers may find legroom and headroom somewhat tight.  Cargo space is also modest. The A3 provides approximately 10.9 cubic feet of trunk space, enough for everyday errands or a few pieces of luggage. In practical testing, the trunk accommodated four carry-on suitcases, and folding the rear seats expanded capacity enough to hold up to 14 carry-ons.
technology: Technology plays a central role in the A3’s appeal. The sedan comes standard with a 10.1-inch touchscreen infotainment system paired with a 10.3-inch digital instrument cluster. The system features sharp graphics and an intuitive interface, making it easy to navigate menus and adjust settings. Connectivity features include wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, Bluetooth integration, and available wireless smartphone charging. Audi also offers a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster through the optional Tech package, allowing drivers to display navigation and vehicle information directly in front of them. Another highlight is the availability of a 15-speaker Sonos premium sound system, which provides clear and powerful audio for music lovers. The infotainment platform also supports downloadable third-party apps such as Spotify and YouTube, expanding its functionality beyond traditional in-car systems.
safety:
Standard Safety Features:
- Automated emergency braking with forward-collision warning
- Lane-departure warning
- Automatic high-beam headlights
Available Safety Features:
- Adaptive cruise control
- Lane-keeping assist
- Blind-spot monitoring
- Rear cross-traffic alert
- Parking sensors and park assist
The A3 includes a solid range of driver-assistance features designed to enhance everyday safety and convenience.
warranty:
- Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 30,000 miles
Audi’s warranty coverage is typical for the luxury segment and comparable to rivals such as BMW and Mercedes-Benz.
pros: Stylish design, efficient turbo engine, engaging handling, and a tech-rich driver-focused cabin.
cons: Limited rear-seat and cargo space, steering lacks feedback, and interior uses some hard plastics.
mn_take: The 2026 Audi A3 is a refined entry-level luxury sedan that combines efficiency, modern technology, and enjoyable driving dynamics in a compact yet premium package.

car_name: 2026 Audi Q8 Review — A Stylish Luxury SUV That Blends Performance, Technology, and Comfort
overview: The Audi Q8 stands as Audi’s flagship two-row luxury SUV, blending bold coupe-like styling with premium comfort and engaging road manners. Even though it shares its platform with the larger Audi Q7, the Q8 focuses more on design and driving character rather than maximum practicality. Its sloping roofline and muscular stance give it a sportier presence, though that styling comes at the cost of some cargo space. Powering the Q8 is a 335-horsepower turbocharged V-6 engine paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission and Audi’s renowned Quattro all-wheel-drive system. This combination delivers strong performance along with confident traction in all conditions. The SUV also offers impressive agility for its size, especially when equipped with adaptive air suspension and rear-wheel steering, which enhance both ride comfort and cornering capability. Inside, the Q8 features one of the most sophisticated cabins in the segment, combining premium materials, high-end technology, and thoughtful design. While rivals such as the BMW X6, Genesis GV80, and Porsche Cayenne offer similar luxury and performance, the Q8 distinguishes itself with its sleek styling, smooth ride quality, and strong balance between comfort and sportiness.
pricing:
MSRP Range: $76,895 – $87,495
Available Trims:
- Premium — $76,895
- Premium Plus — $82,095
- Prestige — $87,495
The base Premium trim is already well equipped with luxury features and advanced driver-assistance technology, making it a compelling starting point. Many buyers may find it worthwhile to add the Convenience Plus package, which introduces desirable upgrades such as a Bang & Olufsen sound system, LED ambient lighting, a heated steering wheel, black exterior trim, and a 360-degree camera system.  Moving up to the Premium Plus trim adds additional comfort-focused features, including ventilated front seats, four-zone automatic climate control, acoustic glass, heated rear seats, and soft-closing doors. The top-tier Prestige trim enhances the driving experience further with rear-wheel steering and OLED taillights, while the optional Sport Plus package introduces firmer suspension tuning, larger 23-inch wheels, and distinctive interior and exterior styling details.
drivetrain:
Under the hood, every Q8 is powered by a turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 engine producing 335 horsepower and 369 lb-ft of torque. The engine works alongside a 48-volt mild-hybrid system that smooths the automatic start-stop operation and improves efficiency in everyday driving. Power is delivered through an eight-speed automatic transmission and Audi’s Quattro all-wheel-drive system, ensuring strong traction and stability in various road conditions.

On the road, the Q8 feels confident and composed, striking an appealing balance between luxury comfort and athletic handling. The steering is light yet precise, making long highway drives relaxing, while the SUV’s well-controlled chassis allows it to tackle corners with surprising agility for a vehicle of its size. During testing, the Q8 accelerated from 0 to 60 mph in approximately 5.3 seconds, putting it close to rivals like the Genesis GV80 Coupe while remaining slightly behind the quicker six-cylinder versions of the BMW X6.

The optional adaptive air suspension significantly enhances ride quality by allowing the vehicle to adjust its ride height and damping characteristics. When paired with rear-wheel steering, available exclusively on the Prestige trim, the Q8 becomes easier to maneuver in tight spaces while also feeling more stable at higher speeds.

Despite its sporty design, the Q8 remains a capable SUV when it comes to towing duties. When properly equipped with the factory-installed trailer hitch, it can tow up to 7,700 pounds, making it suitable for pulling boats, campers, or small trailers.

Fuel economy is respectable but not class-leading for the segment.
EPA Estimates:
- 17 mpg city
- 23 mpg highway
- 19 mpg combined
In real-world highway testing at 75 mph, the Q8 performed better than expected, returning 28 mpg, significantly exceeding its official EPA highway rating.
interior:
Inside the Q8, Audi has created a cabin that feels both modern and luxurious. High-quality materials such as leather upholstery, brushed aluminum trim, and soft-touch surfaces are used throughout the interior, and the build quality is exemplary with tightly aligned panels and a solid, premium feel.

The front seats are heated and power-adjustable as standard, offering excellent comfort and support for long journeys. A large panoramic sunroof floods the cabin with natural light, enhancing the sense of space and openness. Higher trims add even more luxury features such as ventilated seats, additional leather upholstery options, and advanced climate control systems. Passenger space is generous for a two-row SUV. The second row provides ample legroom and headroom for adults, and the seats can both slide and recline, allowing passengers to adjust their seating position for greater comfort during longer trips.

Cargo capacity is somewhat affected by the Q8’s sloping roofline. Even so, it remains practical enough for everyday use. In testing, the Q8 accommodated eight carry-on suitcases behind the second row and 23 carry-on bags with the rear seats folded, slightly less than what the boxier Q7 can manage. Small-item storage inside the cabin is somewhat limited, however, with a shallow center-console bin and narrow door pockets.
technology: The Q8 features Audi’s advanced dual-screen infotainment system, which gives the dashboard a sleek and futuristic appearance. A 10.1-inch upper touchscreen handles navigation, media, and vehicle settings, while a second lower touchscreen controls climate functions and additional comfort features. Both displays provide haptic feedback to simulate the feel of physical buttons. The infotainment system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with Bluetooth connectivity and an integrated Wi-Fi hotspot. The interface is visually impressive and logically arranged, though the reliance on touch controls can take some time to get used to compared with traditional physical buttons. For audio enthusiasts, Audi offers two optional Bang & Olufsen premium sound systems, with either 17 or 19 speakers, delivering powerful and immersive sound quality throughout the cabin. Wireless smartphone charging and voice-command functionality further enhance the overall connectivity experience
safety:
Standard Safety Features:
- Blind-spot monitoring
- Adaptive cruise control
- Lane-keeping assist
Available Safety Features:
- 360-degree surround-view camera system
- Night vision system
The Q8 has received strong crash-test ratings from safety organizations and comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies.
warranty:
- Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 30,000 miles
Audi’s warranty coverage matches most German luxury rivals such as BMW and Mercedes-Benz.
pros: Stylish coupe-like design, engaging handling, powerful turbocharged V-6 performance, and a beautifully crafted tech-rich interior.
cons: Sloping roof reduces cargo practicality, fuel economy trails some rivals, and advanced suspension tech is limited to the top trim.
mn_take: The 2026 Audi Q8 successfully blends striking design, luxury comfort, and sporty dynamics into a refined two-row SUV that prioritizes style and driving enjoyment.

car_name: 2026 Audi Q7 Review — A Sophisticated Three-Row Luxury SUV That Still Feels Sporty
overview: The Audi Q7 continues to prove that a large luxury SUV doesn’t have to sacrifice driving enjoyment. Even though the current generation has been around for several years, the 2026 model still stands out in the midsize luxury SUV segment thanks to its refined driving dynamics, upscale cabin, and generous list of standard technology features. Unlike many three-row SUVs that prioritize size and practicality above everything else, the Q7 blends everyday family usability with the road manners of a smaller vehicle. Its handling is surprisingly composed, especially when equipped with optional features like rear-wheel steering and air suspension. That balance of comfort, agility, and premium design keeps it competitive against rivals such as the Volvo XC90, Lexus GX, and Acura MDX. While the third row is best reserved for children and cargo space isn’t the largest in the segment, the Q7 still offers a well-rounded blend of luxury, technology, and performance that keeps it near the top of its class.
pricing:
MSRP Range: $63,890 – $83,790
Available Trims:
- Premium 45 — $63,890
- Premium Plus 45 — $67,690
- Premium 55 — $69,990
- Premium Plus 55 — $75,290
- Prestige 55 — $78,990
- Prestige Sport Plus 55 — $83,790
The base Premium 45 model already includes strong standard equipment, and adding the Convenience Plus package is a smart move. This package bundles desirable features such as a Bang & Olufsen audio system, 360-degree camera system, ambient lighting, and larger 20-inch wheels without jumping to the more expensive trim levels.
drivetrain:
The 2026 Q7 offers two turbocharged engine options, both paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission and standard Quattro all-wheel drive.

The Q7 45 models use a 261-horsepower turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine supported by a 12-volt mild-hybrid system. This setup provides respectable acceleration and improved efficiency, making it a sensible choice for buyers who prioritize economy without sacrificing luxury. For stronger performance, the Q7 55 models upgrade to a 335-horsepower turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 engine paired with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system. This engine delivers noticeably stronger acceleration and a more effortless driving experience, particularly when merging onto highways or carrying a full load of passengers. Despite its size, the Q7 feels surprisingly nimble on the road. When equipped with adaptive air suspension and rear-wheel steering, the SUV corners with a level of agility rarely seen in vehicles of this size. At the same time, the suspension remains composed and comfortable over long highway drives. In testing, the V-6 powered Q7 accelerated from 0 to 60 mph in about 5.9 seconds, which is quick for a luxury three-row SUV.

Towing Capacity:
The Q7 is also capable when it comes to towing duties:
- 4,400 pounds with the turbocharged four-cylinder
- 7,700 pounds with the turbocharged V-6
This makes the V-6 model a practical option for towing small boats, campers, or utility trailers.

Fuel Economy:
Fuel economy varies depending on the engine choice:
Four-Cylinder (Q7 45):
- 20 mpg city
- 26 mpg highway

V-6 (Q7 55):
- 18 mpg city
- 23 mpg highway
In real-world highway testing, a four-cylinder Q7 achieved 26 mpg at 75 mph, matching its EPA highway estimate.
interior:
Inside, the Q7 delivers the type of refined environment expected from a modern Audi. The cabin feels contemporary and well crafted, combining soft-touch materials, aluminum trim, and leather surfaces to create a sophisticated atmosphere. Build quality is excellent throughout, and the design remains clean and minimalist despite the large amount of technology integrated into the dashboard. The front seats are exceptionally comfortable, offering generous cushioning and support for long drives. Higher trims add premium touches such as ventilation, massage functions, and extended leather upholstery. These features help elevate the Q7 closer to flagship luxury SUVs in terms of comfort.

The second row uses a unique 35/30/35 seat split, allowing greater flexibility when installing child seats or transporting passengers and cargo at the same time. While this design is practical, it slightly reduces the outboard seating width compared to traditional configurations. The third row is usable but tight, particularly for adults. Headroom and legroom are limited, making it better suited for children or occasional use. Fortunately, the third row can be folded electronically to create additional cargo space when it’s not needed. Cargo capacity starts at 14 cubic feet with all three rows in use, expanding to 36 cubic feet when the third row is folded, and up to 70 cubic feet with both rear rows down, providing ample room for luggage, sports equipment, or large grocery runs.
technology: Audi equips the Q7 with a technology-focused cockpit built around a dual-screen infotainment setup. The main 10.1-inch touchscreen handles navigation, media, and vehicle functions, while a lower 8.6-inch touchscreen controls climate settings and additional vehicle features. Above the steering wheel sits Audi’s 12.3-inch Virtual Cockpit digital gauge cluster, which provides customizable driving information and navigation displays. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with built-in Bluetooth connectivity and a Wi-Fi hotspot for passengers. While the dual-screen interface looks futuristic, it can require a bit of acclimation because many functions rely on touch controls rather than physical buttons. Audio performance is excellent. A 10-speaker system comes standard, while optional Bang & Olufsen sound systems with either 19 or 23 speakers deliver a much richer and more immersive listening experience.
safety:
Standard Safety Features:
- Adaptive cruise control
- Lane-keeping assist
- Blind-spot monitoring
Available Safety Technology:
- 360-degree surround-view camera system
- Remote park assist
- Advanced parking assistance systems
The Q7 has also received strong crash-test scores from safety agencies.
warranty:
- Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 30,000 miles
Coverage is competitive with German rivals, though some competitors offer longer powertrain warranties.
pros: Agile handling for a three-row SUV, luxurious and tech-rich interior, strong engine choices, and generous standard equipment.
cons: Third row is cramped for adults, cargo space trails some rivals, and advanced performance features can become expensive options.
mn_take: The 2026 Audi Q7 blends luxury, technology, and surprisingly sharp driving dynamics into one of the most refined three-row SUVs in its class.

car_name: 2026 Audi Q5 / Q5 Sportback Review — Tech-Rich Luxury Meets Everyday Refinement
overview: The 2026 Audi Q5 and its sleeker coupe-styled sibling, the Audi Q5 Sportback, continue to embody Audi’s philosophy of understated luxury blended with advanced technology. Following a full redesign last year, the Q5 enters 2026 with sharper styling, a more digitized cabin, and incremental performance improvements that keep it competitive in the compact luxury SUV segment. Positioned between comfort-focused cruisers and sportier driver’s SUVs, the Q5 rivals heavyweights like the BMW X3 and Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class. While it may not be the most playful option dynamically, the Q5 counters with refined road manners, sophisticated design, and one of the most tech-dense interiors in its class.
pricing:
MSRP Range: $54,095 – $61,995
Available Trims:
- Premium — $54,095
- Premium Plus — $56,995
- Prestige — $61,995
The mid-range Premium Plus trim represents the best value, adding premium features such as a Bang & Olufsen audio system, adaptive cruise control, head-up display, and a heated steering wheel—balancing luxury and price effectively.
drivetrain:
Every 2026 Q5 is powered by a 268-horsepower turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine paired with a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission and standard Quattro all-wheel drive. Power delivery is smooth and linear, with the dual-clutch gearbox offering quick yet seamless shifts both in city traffic and at highway speeds. Acceleration is brisk for the segment, with a tested 0–60 mph time of 5.8 seconds, making it competitive, though slightly slower than the outgoing generation’s 5.5-second run. Steering revisions have improved directional accuracy, but feedback remains muted, giving the Q5 a more comfort-oriented driving character rather than a sporty edge. Ride quality is a highlight. The standard suspension absorbs road imperfections with composure, delivering a quiet and stable highway experience. An optional air-ride suspension further enhances comfort while adding mild dynamic sharpness when driving on smoother pavement.

EPA fuel economy estimates for the gasoline Q5 stand at:
- 22 mpg — City
- 30 mpg — Highway
- 25 mpg — Combined
While respectable, these figures trail some rivals, including the BMW X3 and Mercedes-Benz GLC-Class, which offer slightly better efficiency in comparable configurations.
interior:
Inside, the Q5 showcases Audi’s signature Bauhaus-inspired design philosophy—minimalist, elegant, and technology-forward. The cabin feels airy and meticulously assembled, with premium materials such as leather upholstery, brushed metal accents, and soft-touch surfaces dominating key touchpoints. Front-seat comfort is generally strong, though the seats could benefit from additional cushioning for long-distance touring. A flat-bottom, flat-top steering wheel adds a subtle sporty flair, complementing the otherwise restrained layout.

Second-row space is adequate rather than class-leading. Adults around six feet tall can sit comfortably, though rivals offer slightly more legroom. Rear passengers benefit from modern conveniences like USB-C charging ports and available heated seats. Cargo practicality remains competitive despite a slight reduction versus the previous model. The Q5 offers 27.6 cubic feet of cargo space behind the second row, expanding to 56.9 cubic feet with the rear seats folded—sufficient for weekend travel or airport duties.
technology:
Technology is one of the Q5’s strongest selling points, anchored by a striking three-screen digital cockpit layout. An 11.9-inch digital instrument cluster flows seamlessly into a large 14.5-inch central touchscreen, forming the centerpiece of the dashboard. The interface is visually impressive, though its layered menus may require a learning curve for less tech-savvy users. An optional 10.9-inch passenger display adds another layer of functionality, allowing the co-driver to stream content or browse navigation data. A built-in privacy filter ensures the driver remains distraction-free while the screen is in use.

The system runs on Google’s Android Automotive software, supporting integrated apps alongside wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity. Audi’s optional 16-speaker Bang & Olufsen sound system delivers exceptional clarity and depth, transforming the cabin into a premium listening environment. A head-up display further enhances the high-tech driving experience.
safety:
Standard Safety Tech Includes:
- Automated emergency braking with forward-collision warning
- Lane-departure warning
Available Upgrades Include:
- Adaptive cruise control
- Traffic-sign recognition
- Expanded driver-assistance packages
While well-equipped, many advanced features remain optional rather than standard.
warranty:
- Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 30,000 miles
Coverage aligns with German luxury rivals but doesn’t lead the segment.
pros: Sophisticated styling, tech-laden triple-screen cabin, refined ride quality, and smooth 268-hp turbo performance enhance everyday luxury appeal.
cons: Rear space trails key rivals, steering lacks engagement, and performance feels competent rather than thrilling.
mn_take: The 2026 Audi Q5 prioritizes comfort, design, and cutting-edge tech over sportiness, making it a polished all-rounder in the compact luxury SUV space.

car_name: 2026 Audi Q3 Review — Redesigned Luxury, More Power, and Smarter Tech in a Compact Package
overview: The 2026 Audi Q3 marks a significant step forward for Audi’s smallest SUV, bringing sharper styling, a more premium cabin, and a noticeably stronger powertrain to the subcompact luxury segment. Positioned as a downsized alternative to the larger Audi Q5, the new Q3 continues to appeal to urban buyers seeking luxury, practicality, and everyday usability in a compact footprint. Competing directly with rivals such as the BMW X1 and Mercedes‑Benz GLA‑Class, the updated Q3 addresses one of its long-standing weaknesses—performance—while also introducing a more technology-rich interior and improved ride refinement. With standard all-wheel drive, refreshed suspension tuning, and a more premium feature set, the 2026 model feels far more competitive than before.
pricing:
For 2026, the Q3 lineup has been simplified into a single, well-equipped configuration:
- Starting MSRP: $44,995
- Trim: S Line Quattro (only trim)
The S Line package brings sportier design elements, including a more aggressive black grille, body-colored performance bumpers, and Selenite Silver accents around the diffuser and intake surrounds. New 18-inch alloy wheels come standard, while larger 19- and 20-inch options are available for buyers wanting a more assertive road presence.
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the 2026 Q3 receives a meaningful upgrade. Power comes from a revised 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine producing 255 horsepower and 273 lb-ft of torque, a noticeable bump over the outgoing model. The engine is paired with a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, delivering quicker, more responsive gear changes than the previous setup. Standard Quattro all-wheel drive ensures confident traction in varied weather conditions, reinforcing the Q3’s all-season usability. Audi estimates a 0–60 mph time of 5.5 seconds, placing it among the quicker options in the subcompact luxury SUV class.

Ride quality benefits from updated suspension tuning, offering a composed balance between comfort and agility. While adaptive dampers were tested in European models, U.S. versions focus on fixed suspension setups that still deliver confident cornering and a refined highway demeanor. Towing capacity is rated at 1,500 pounds, suitable for light recreational use.

Official EPA fuel economy figures haven’t been finalized at the time of writing, but expectations are that the revised turbo engine will deliver efficiency similar to or slightly better than the outgoing model, which averaged in the mid-20-mpg range combined. The dual-clutch gearbox and updated engine management system should contribute to improved real-world efficiency without sacrificing performance.
interior:
Step inside the 2026 Q3 and the improvements are immediately noticeable. Audi has reworked the cabin layout to create a more open, modern environment while also enhancing day-to-day usability. One of the biggest changes is the relocation of the gear selector to a steering-column stalk, freeing up valuable storage space in the center console and giving the cockpit a cleaner, less cluttered appearance. Material quality remains a strong suit, with available sustainably sourced wood trims, recycled upholstery fabrics, and premium soft-touch surfaces throughout the cabin. Buyers can also opt for acoustically laminated glass, which significantly reduces road and wind noise, contributing to the Q3’s impressively quiet interior at highway speeds.

Ambient lighting customization has expanded as well, offering multiple illumination themes that elevate the cabin’s upscale feel after dark. Passenger space remains comfortable for a subcompact SUV, and cargo practicality has improved. Rear cargo capacity now measures 29 cubic feet with the seats up—an increase from the previous 24 cubic feet—and expands to 48 cubic feet with the rear seats folded flat.
technology:
The 2026 Q3 introduces one of the most advanced infotainment layouts in its class, built around a striking panoramic digital display that blends an 11.9-inch digital instrument cluster with a 12.8-inch curved infotainment touchscreen. The driver-focused curvature enhances visibility and ergonomics, reinforcing Audi’s cockpit-centric design philosophy.

Running on an Android Automotive–based operating system, the system supports built-in third-party applications, allowing services such as YouTube streaming without requiring a connected smartphone. The interface is faster and more intuitive than before, complemented by AI-enhanced voice recognition that understands natural speech commands for navigation, media, and climate functions. Audi also offers a premium Sonos 12-speaker sound system delivering 420 watts, providing crisp audio clarity and deep bass response, making it one of the standout entertainment systems in the segment.
safety:
The Q3 comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies. Standard features include:
- Automatic emergency braking
- Lane-keep warning
- Front cross-traffic alert with collision mitigation
- Parking assistance
Available upgrades include adaptive cruise control with lane-change assist and an innovative “trainable” parking assist system that can memorize frequent parking maneuvers and execute them automatically.
warranty:
Warranty coverage remains in line with German luxury rivals:
- Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 30,000 miles
While competitive, some rivals still offer longer powertrain coverage.
pros: Stronger 255-hp turbo performance, refined ride quality, high-tech panoramic cockpit, and improved cargo practicality elevate overall luxury appeal.
cons: Brake pedal can feel overly sensitive, unconventional control layout needs acclimatization, and warranty coverage is merely average.
mn_take: The 2026 Audi Q3 evolves into a more complete luxury subcompact SUV, blending sharper performance, richer tech, and everyday versatility in a compact premium package.

car_name: 2026 Audi A5 — A Smarter, More Practical Evolution of Audi’s Compact Luxury Formula
overview: The 2026 Audi A5 steps into a newly consolidated role within Audi’s lineup, replacing both the outgoing A4 sedan and A5 Sportback with a single, more versatile offering. Now available exclusively as a four-door liftback, the A5 blends sleek coupe-like styling with everyday sedan usability and hatchback practicality. Larger exterior proportions translate into improved interior room and cargo versatility, making it one of the most well-rounded entries in the compact luxury segment. On the road, the A5 leans toward comfort but retains a subtle athletic edge. Its suspension tuning prioritizes ride composure over outright sportiness, yet it remains poised and confident through corners. The result is a balanced driving character—less aggressive than a BMW 3-series but more engaging than purely comfort-focused rivals.
pricing: Pricing for the 2026 A5 starts at $51,495 for the Premium trim and climbs to $57,995 for the fully loaded Prestige. The mid-range Premium Plus trim, priced at $53,995, represents the sweet spot, adding desirable features such as upgraded ambient lighting, a heated steering wheel, lane-centering adaptive cruise control, parking sensors, a panoramic glass roof, and a Bang & Olufsen audio system.
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the A5 features a single but well-rounded powertrain: a 268-horsepower turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder paired with a 48-volt mild-hybrid system. Power is delivered to all four wheels through Audi’s quattro all-wheel-drive system and a quick-shifting seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Performance is brisk rather than explosive. In testing, the A5 accelerated from 0–60 mph in 5.2 seconds, putting it right in line with base versions of rivals like the BMW 3-Series and Genesis G70. Throttle response is sharp, gear changes are crisp, and the mild-hybrid assist helps smooth power delivery in stop-and-go driving.

While the chassis feels slightly sportier than the previous generation, steering feedback remains muted, reinforcing the A5’s comfort-first personality. It’s a confident highway cruiser and a composed back-road companion rather than a hardcore driver’s sedan.

Efficiency is competitive for the class:
- 22 mpg city / 31 mpg highway / 26 mpg combined (EPA)
- Real-world highway testing returned an impressive 39 mpg at 75 mph, showcasing the benefits of the mild-hybrid system and aerodynamic liftback design.
interior: Inside, the A5 showcases Audi’s signature build quality, with premium materials, tight panel gaps, and a clean, contemporary design. Soft-touch surfaces, aluminum accents, and available ambient lighting create a refined environment, though the styling is more understated than flamboyant rivals. Front-seat comfort is excellent, with supportive cushioning and a wide range of power adjustments. Rear passengers benefit from generous legroom and good headroom, helped by the car’s larger footprint. The available panoramic glass roof enhances the cabin’s airy feel, especially for second-row occupants. Cargo practicality is where the A5 truly stands out. Thanks to its liftback rear design, it offers 23 cubic feet of cargo space with the rear seats up—significantly more usable than traditional sedan trunks in this class.
technology: Technology dominates the A5’s dashboard layout. A sweeping curved glass panel integrates an 11.9-inch digital instrument cluster with a large 14.5-inch central touchscreen, delivering sharp graphics and fast response times. The interface features intuitive menus, customizable layouts, and seamless smartphone integration via wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. An optional 10.9-inch passenger display adds functionality for navigation inputs and media control, designed to remain invisible to the driver while the vehicle is in motion. A head-up display projects speed, navigation prompts, and driver-assistance data directly into the driver’s line of sight. Audio quality is strong with the standard 10-speaker system, while the optional 19-speaker Bang & Olufsen 3D premium setup provides immersive, concert-like sound throughout the cabin.
safety: Audi equips the A5 with a comprehensive suite of safety technologies. Standard features include automated emergency braking with forward-collision warning, lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control. Higher trims add lane-centering, enhanced parking assistance, and additional highway-driving aids.
warranty:
Coverage is competitive but not class-leading:
- 4-year / 50,000-mile limited warranty
- 4-year / 50,000-mile powertrain warranty
- 3 years / 30,000 miles complimentary maintenance
pros: Comfortable ride, liftback practicality with 23 cu-ft cargo space, strong tech suite, and efficient mild-hybrid performance.
cons: Steering lacks feedback, screen-heavy dash may not suit all buyers, and interior design feels conservative.
mn_take: The 2026 A5 is Audi’s most practical compact luxury sedan yet—blending comfort, technology, and everyday usability into one sleek liftback package.

car_name: 2026 Aston Martin DBX — Supercar Pace Meets Ultra-Luxury SUV Practicality
overview: The 2026 Aston Martin DBX continues to redefine what an ultra-luxury performance SUV should feel like. Rather than diluting the brand’s sports-car DNA, the DBX translates it into a five-seat, family-friendly form factor without sacrificing drama or driver engagement. Sculpted bodywork, a commanding stance, and unmistakable Aston Martin design cues ensure it looks every bit as exotic as the marque’s two-door grand tourers. Beneath that elegance lies genuine supercar pace—making the DBX one of the quickest and most athletic SUVs on sale today, yet one that can just as easily handle long-distance touring or daily luxury duties.
pricing: For 2026, the DBX lineup centers around two high-performance variants. Pricing starts at $276,500 for the DBX 707 and rises to $282,000 for the new range-topping DBX S. Both trims arrive lavishly equipped, but buyers can elevate exclusivity further through Aston Martin’s extensive Q personalization program, which offers bespoke paint finishes, interior materials, and trim detailing tailored to individual tastes.
drivetrain:
Powering the DBX is a Mercedes-AMG-sourced 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V-8, extensively tuned by Aston Martin to deliver explosive performance. In the DBX 707, the engine produces 697 horsepower, while the newly introduced DBX S raises output to 717 horsepower. Both variants channel power through a nine-speed automatic transmission and a performance-biased all-wheel-drive system that primarily drives the rear wheels but can redirect torque forward when needed.

Acceleration is nothing short of staggering for a full-size luxury SUV. The DBX 707 reaches 0–60 mph in 3.1 seconds, putting it squarely in supercar territory and matching benchmarks set by rivals like the Lamborghini Urus. The DBX S, despite its extra power, delivers similar sprint times, with its gains focused more on high-speed performance and responsiveness.

Chassis sophistication is a major highlight. Standard adaptive dampers and height-adjustable air suspension allow the DBX to switch personalities seamlessly—from supple highway cruiser to sharply focused canyon carver. The S model further enhances agility with over 100 pounds of weight reduction, a carbon-fiber roof that lowers the center of gravity, and recalibrated steering for sharper turn-in. Braking performance is strong, with a 151-foot stop from 70 mph, though pedal feel can be softer than expected in aggressive driving.

Beyond performance, the DBX retains genuine SUV utility. It offers a maximum towing capacity of 5,940 pounds, making it capable of hauling boats, trailers, or recreational gear—an unusual but valuable trait in this segment.

Given its output, efficiency remains respectable for the class:
- DBX 707: 15 mpg city / 20 mpg highway / 17 mpg combined
- DBX S: 14 mpg city / 19 mpg highway / 16 mpg combined
Real-world highway testing of the 707 returned 20 mpg, matching its EPA estimate.
interior: Inside, the DBX delivers the handcrafted opulence expected from Aston Martin. The cabin is swathed in finely stitched leather, soft-touch materials, and a microsuede headliner, creating a warm yet performance-focused ambiance. Standard features include a digital instrument cluster, three-zone climate control, customizable ambient lighting, and heated front and rear seats. Passenger space is generous for the segment. Rear occupants benefit from ample legroom and headroom, making the DBX genuinely usable as a family luxury SUV. Cargo capacity is equally practical, offering 22 cubic feet behind the rear seats and expanding to 54 cubic feet with them folded—enough for long trips or lifestyle gear.
technology: Technology integration is modern and intuitive. A 10.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system pairs with a 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster, both supporting wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Standard equipment includes navigation, SiriusXM satellite radio, USB-C connectivity, and active noise cancellation. Audio performance is strong even in base form with a 14-speaker sound system, while audiophiles can opt for a 23-speaker Bowers & Wilkins setup delivering 1,600 watts of immersive output.
safety: The DBX comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of advanced driver-assistance technologies. Standard systems include automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, and additional highway-driving aids designed to make long journeys safer and less fatiguing.
warranty:
Warranty coverage is typical for the segment but not exceptional:
- 3-year / unlimited-mile limited warranty
- 3-year / unlimited-mile powertrain warranty
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance (available via paid extended plans)
pros: Supercar-level acceleration, striking Aston Martin design, and a rare blend of performance and real SUV practicality.
cons: Extremely high entry price, some rivals offer plusher cabins, and brake pedal feel could be sharper.
mn_take: The 2026 DBX proves Aston Martin can build a family SUV without losing its soul—ferociously quick, exquisitely styled, and thrillingly driver-focused.

car_name: 2026 Aston Martin Vanquish — 823-HP V-12 Grand Touring Royalty at Its Absolute Peak
overview: The 2026 Aston Martin Vanquish stands at the summit of the brand’s front-engine grand-touring lineage, delivering an intoxicating blend of hand-built luxury, dramatic styling, and ferocious V-12 performance. Conceived as the ultimate expression of Aston Martin’s road-going flagship, the Vanquish merges long-distance comfort with supercar-level straight-line speed. Its sculpted bodywork, impossibly long hood, and wide rear haunches give it an unmistakably aristocratic road presence—one that feels equally at home outside a Monte Carlo casino or carving through alpine passes. Offered in both Coupe and Volante convertible form, the Vanquish is designed to deliver sensory indulgence at every level, from the thunderous engine note to the opulence of its two-seat cabin.
pricing: Pricing for the 2026 Vanquish reflects its ultra-exclusive positioning in the luxury sports-car hierarchy. The Coupe starts at $436,500, while the open-top Volante commands a premium at $489,700. Both are offered as comprehensively equipped halo models rather than multi-trim lineups, though Aston Martin’s bespoke Q personalization program allows owners to commission highly individualized color palettes, materials, and interior finishes—often pushing final prices well beyond the half-million-dollar mark.
drivetrain:
Dominating the Vanquish’s character is its magnificent 5.2-liter twin-turbocharged V-12, a powerplant engineered to deliver both relentless acceleration and operatic acoustics. Producing an immense 823 horsepower and 738 lb-ft of torque, the engine channels its output exclusively to the rear wheels via an eight-speed automatic transmission. Performance is predictably staggering. Aston Martin estimates a 0–60 mph time of around 3.0 seconds, placing the Vanquish firmly within modern supercar territory despite its grand-touring mission. The rear-drive layout, paired with an electronically controlled differential, delivers engaging dynamics but also demands respect—full-throttle launches can easily overwhelm traction given the sheer torque on tap.

Chassis and performance highlights include:
- Standard carbon-ceramic brakes for fade-free stopping power
- 21-inch wheels wrapped in bespoke Pirelli P Zero tires
- Eight-stage traction control system
- Optional titanium exhaust system for an even more visceral soundtrack
The Volante convertible introduces just over 200 pounds of additional weight due to structural reinforcements and roof hardware, yet Aston Martin’s bespoke suspension tuning preserves handling composure remarkably well.

Efficiency is naturally secondary to performance in a twin-turbo V-12 flagship. EPA estimates are:
- 13 mpg city
- 21 mpg highway
These figures align with expectations for a high-displacement, ultra-high-output grand tourer.
interior: Inside, the Vanquish delivers a cabin experience befitting its flagship billing—lavish, intimate, and meticulously handcrafted. The strictly two-seat layout prioritizes indulgence over practicality, enveloping occupants in semi-aniline leather, faux-suede accents, and optional touches like a cashmere headliner. The standard 16-way power sport seats combine long-distance comfort with lateral support suited to spirited driving. Despite its performance focus, the Vanquish remains a true grand tourer. The trunk offers 8–9 cubic feet of cargo capacity—enough for weekend luggage—while buyers can commission bespoke fitted luggage sets tailored to their interior specification. In the Volante, the fabric soft top operates with elegant precision, opening in 14 seconds and closing in 16 seconds at speeds up to 31 mph, with remote operation available via the key fob.
technology: Technology integration is handled through a pair of seamlessly embedded 10.3-inch digital displays—one serving as the infotainment hub and the other as the configurable driver instrument cluster. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as standard, while built-in navigation incorporates What3Words functionality, enabling hyper-accurate destination input down to three-square-meter map sectors. Audio quality matches the car’s flagship status. Every Vanquish comes equipped with a 15-speaker Bowers & Wilkins surround-sound system powered by dual amplifiers, delivering concert-hall clarity even at highway speeds with the convertible roof lowered.
safety: While driver engagement remains central, the Vanquish integrates a comprehensive suite of modern safety technologies. Standard systems include adaptive cruise control, automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, traffic-sign recognition, and automatic high-beam headlamps—ensuring long-distance touring is as relaxing as it is exhilarating.
warranty:
Warranty coverage is relatively modest given the car’s price tier:
- 3-year / unlimited-mile limited warranty
- 3-year / unlimited-mile powertrain warranty
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance
Extended coverage packages are available through Aston Martin at additional cost.
pros: Monumental 823-hp twin-turbo V-12 performance, breathtaking grand-touring design, and an ultra-luxurious handcrafted flagship cabin.
cons: Rear-drive traction limits full power deployment, extremely high acquisition cost, and limited practicality beyond two passengers.
mn_take: The 2026 Vanquish is Aston Martin’s V-12 masterpiece—an opulent, thunderously powerful grand tourer built to deliver ultimate exclusivity and drama.

car_name: 2026 Aston Martin Vantage Roadster — Open-Top British Fury with 656-HP V-8 Thrill
overview: The 2026 Aston Martin Vantage Roadster arrives as the open-air extension of the comprehensively updated coupe, blending traditional British grand-touring character with sharper modern performance credentials. Built around Aston Martin’s classic front-engine, rear-wheel-drive layout, the Roadster amplifies the emotional appeal of the Vantage formula by pairing its thunderous twin-turbo V-8 with the sensory drama of top-down motoring. Despite the added complexity of its soft-top mechanism, the Roadster maintains the coupe’s aggressive proportions and athletic stance, preserving its identity as one of the most visually arresting luxury sports cars on sale today. With blistering acceleration, a richly vocal exhaust note, and a chassis tuned for both precision and playfulness, the Vantage Roadster positions itself as a more exclusive, more visceral alternative to rivals like the Porsche 911 Turbo and Mercedes‑AMG GT63.
pricing:
The Vantage range spans coupe and convertible body styles, each available in standard and higher-output S configurations:
- Coupe — $194,500
- Vantage S Coupe — $199,500
- Roadster — $209,400
- Vantage S Roadster — $214,500
While pricing places it firmly in six-figure territory, customization through Aston Martin’s bespoke “Q” division can dramatically elevate final cost via unique paints, exposed carbon, interior quilting, and performance options.
drivetrain:
At the heart of every 2026 Vantage sits a heavily reworked 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V-8 sourced from Mercedes-AMG but extensively tuned by Aston Martin. Output for standard models now stands at a formidable 656 horsepower, marking a substantial 128-hp increase over the previous Vantage F1 Edition. The more extreme Vantage S pushes output further to 670 horsepower, sharpening its track-leaning intent. Power is routed exclusively to the rear wheels through an eight-speed automatic transmission, as Aston Martin has discontinued the manual option. Performance is ferocious: the coupe has recorded 0–60 mph in 3.2 seconds in testing, while Aston claims 3.5 seconds for the Roadster—though real-world runs may prove quicker.

Chassis enhancements include:
- 7% greater structural stiffness
- Revised adaptive dampers
- Retuned suspension geometry
- New Michelin Pilot Sport 5S performance tires
Even with the convertible hardware, weight gain is limited to just 132 pounds, preserving the car’s balance. Steering precision, strong braking feel, and neutral cornering behavior make the Vantage equally capable on winding roads and high-speed touring routes.

Given its performance focus, efficiency remains secondary. EPA estimates stand at:
- 15 mpg city
- 22 mpg highway
- 18 mpg combined
These figures are typical for a high-output twin-turbo V-8 sports car in this segment.
interior:
Inside, the Vantage Roadster reflects Aston Martin’s push toward greater modernity without abandoning handcrafted luxury. The cabin is intimate and driver-centric, with seating strictly for two, but the redesign introduced with the latest generation brings improved layout coherence and material consistency. Rich leather upholstery, contrast stitching, embroidered headrests, and optional carbon-fiber trim create a cockpit that feels both bespoke and performance-oriented.

The new center console architecture is more intuitive, blending physical switchgear with digital interfaces, while heated and ventilated sport seats provide long-distance comfort despite the car’s aggressive character. Storage space remains limited—there’s a shallow center bin and slim door pockets—but the Roadster’s clever Z-fold roof design minimizes cargo compromise. Trunk capacity sits at 7 cubic feet, still sufficient to accommodate a full-size golf bag, reinforcing its grand-touring usability credentials.
technology:
Aston Martin has made a significant leap forward in in-car technology. The Vantage now features a crisp 12.5-inch touchscreen infotainment system, replacing the older 8.0-inch unit with faster software and sharper graphics. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, finally aligning the brand with modern connectivity expectations, while integrated navigation includes What3Words destination functionality for ultra-precise location input.

The digital ecosystem extends beyond the cabin through the new Aston Martin connected-services app, which syncs with the vehicle via onboard cellular connectivity to provide remote vehicle monitoring and ownership services. Audio performance is equally impressive, with a 390-watt 11-speaker system as standard, while audiophiles can opt for a 1,170-watt 15-speaker Bowers & Wilkins surround system that transforms the compact cabin into a concert-like soundstage.
safety: While performance remains the priority, the updated Vantage integrates a broader suite of driver-assistance technologies than before. Standard features include forward-collision warning with autonomous emergency braking, lane-departure warning with lane-keep assist, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert—bringing a layer of modern safety to an otherwise analog-feeling sports car experience.
warranty:
Warranty coverage is relatively modest for the segment:
- 3-year / unlimited-mile limited warranty
- 3-year / unlimited-mile powertrain warranty
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance
Extended coverage plans are available at additional cost.
pros: Explosive 656-hp twin-turbo V-8 performance, razor-sharp rear-drive dynamics, exotic roadster design, and a richly handcrafted luxury cabin.
cons: No manual transmission, limited cargo practicality, modest warranty coverage, and a price tag exceeding $200K in higher trims.
mn_take: The 2026 Vantage Roadster is a visceral, open-air grand tourer that fuses brutal AMG-derived power with unmistakable Aston Martin elegance and exclusivity.

car_name: 2026 Aston Martin DB12 S Review: 680-HP Super GT With Sharper Dynamics and Ultra-Luxury Tech
overview: The 2026 Aston Martin DB12 represents a defining moment for Aston Martin’s modern performance era. Marketed not simply as a grand tourer but as a “Super Tourer,” the DB12 blends traditional British craftsmanship with cutting-edge performance engineering. It replaces the DB11 while pushing the formula further—more power, sharper dynamics, and a significantly upgraded cabin technology suite. Visually, the DB12 retains Aston Martin’s timeless design DNA but evolves it with a wider track, enlarged front grille for improved cooling, slimmer LED matrix headlamps, and more aggressive aerodynamic surfacing. The proportions remain classic—long bonnet, low roofline, muscular rear haunches—but the detailing now leans more toward high-performance exotica than relaxed GT. For 2026, the biggest headline is the arrival of the DB12 S, a harder-edged halo variant focused on sharper driver engagement without sacrificing long-distance comfort.
pricing:
The DB12 sits deep in ultra-luxury territory, with pricing varying widely based on body style and bespoke commissioning:
- Coupe — $265,500
- Volante Convertible — $285,500
- DB12 S Coupe — ~$285,000 (est.)
- DB12 S Volante — ~$300,000 (est.)
- Goldfinger Edition — $380,507
Through Aston Martin’s Q personalization program, buyers can commission exclusive paints, exposed carbon packages, unique leather palettes, embroidery, jewelry-grade switchgear, and even one-off trim materials—often adding tens of thousands to MSRP.
drivetrain:
At the heart of the DB12 lies a hand-assembled 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V-8, extensively reworked by Aston Martin engineers.
Output figures are formidable:
- 671 hp (standard DB12)
- 690 hp (DB12 S)
- 590 lb-ft torque (approx.)
- 8-speed automatic transmission
- Rear-wheel drive with electronic limited-slip differential
Acceleration is explosive for a front-engine GT:
- 0–60 mph — ~3.5 sec
- 0–60 mph (S) — ~3.4 sec
- Top speed — 202 mph

Chassis sophistication is equally impressive. The DB12 rides on adaptive dampers with multiple drive modes, an advanced e-differential, and torque-vectoring Brake Slip Control. The S variant sharpens responses further via revised suspension geometry, recalibrated steering mapping, stiffer anti-roll bars, and standard carbon-ceramic brakes that reduce unsprung mass while delivering relentless stopping power. Despite its performance ceiling, ride compliance remains exceptional. Even on large wheels, the DB12 isolates road harshness with the composure expected of a long-distance GT. The only dynamic critique lies in its hyper-responsive throttle calibration, which can feel abrupt in low-speed driving.

Efficiency understandably takes a secondary role:
- 15 mpg city
- 22 mpg highway
- 17 mpg combined
Given the displacement, turbocharging, and output levels, these figures align with segment expectations.
interior: Inside, the DB12 delivers one of the most opulent cabins in the modern GT segment. Nearly every surface is wrapped in hand-stitched Bridge of Weir leather, complemented by open-pore wood, satin metal, or carbon fiber trim depending on configuration. Seat design balances performance bolstering with touring comfort. Multiple seat designs are offered, including heated sport seats in the S trimmed in Alcantara and semi-aniline leather. Driving position is low and cockpit-like, enhancing the sense of connection without sacrificing visibility. The 2+2 layout technically allows four occupants, but rear seating is symbolic—best suited for luggage or small bags. Trunk space measures roughly 7–9 cubic feet, adequate for weekend travel but modest versus traditional grand tourers. Cabin insulation is excellent, allowing the V-8’s soundtrack to remain present without overwhelming long-distance refinement.
technology: The DB12 marks the debut of Aston Martin’s first fully in-house infotainment ecosystem—an enormous leap over prior Mercedes-derived systems. At its center sits a 10.3-inch high-resolution touchscreen with faster processing, improved UI design, and integrated connected services. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with cloud-based navigation and OTA update capability. Importantly, Aston retains physical switchgear for climate, drive modes, exhaust settings, and chassis controls—preserving tactile usability absent in many screen-dominated rivals. Audio performance is equally premium. The standard 11-speaker system delivers rich clarity, while the optional 15-speaker Bowers & Wilkins surround system introduces aluminum double-dome tweeters, Continuum midrange drivers, and a powerful subwoofer engineered specifically for the DB12’s cabin acoustics.
safety: While performance remains central, the DB12 integrates modern driver-assistance tech including adaptive cruise control, autonomous emergency braking, lane-keeping assist, traffic sign recognition, and automatic high-beam control—enhancing usability on long continental drives.
warranty:
- Limited Warranty — 3 years / unlimited miles
- Powertrain — 3 years / unlimited miles
- Complimentary Maintenance — Not included
Coverage is competitive for the exotic segment, though some rivals include scheduled servicing.
pros: Explosive twin-turbo V-8 performance, breathtaking design presence, and a richly handcrafted ultra-luxury cabin.
cons: Overly sharp throttle tuning, minimal rear-seat usability, and absence of a flagship V-12 option.
mn_take: The DB12 elevates the grand-tourer formula into supercar territory—delivering dramatic performance wrapped in unmistakable Aston Martin elegance.

car_name: 2026 Alfa Romeo Stelvio Review — Specs, Performance, Interior, Features, MPG & Pricing
overview: The 2026 Alfa Romeo Stelvio continues to embody the brand’s driver-first philosophy in a segment increasingly dominated by comfort-biased crossovers. Styled with sculpted Italian flair and powered by a spirited turbocharged engine, the Stelvio feels far more like a raised sports sedan than a conventional luxury SUV. Even several years into its lifecycle, its design still turns heads, while its chassis tuning prioritizes agility and engagement over outright plushness. However, rivals have surged ahead in interior tech, fuel efficiency, and cargo practicality, making the Stelvio more of an enthusiast’s choice than a segment all-rounder.
pricing:
- Base: $53,245
- Veloce: $55,270
The Veloce trim remains the enthusiast pick, adding sport seats, aluminum paddle shifters, red Brembo brake calipers, a limited-slip rear differential, and a front strut-tower brace—hardware that enhances both aesthetics and dynamic capability.
drivetrain:
Under the hood sits a 2.0-liter turbocharged inline-four producing 280 horsepower and 306 lb-ft of torque, paired with an 8-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive.
Performance figures remain competitive:
- 0–60 mph: ~5.4 seconds
- Top speed: ~144 mph (electronically limited)
On the road, the Stelvio feels quicker than its numbers suggest. Throttle response is immediate, and the transmission delivers crisp upshifts during spirited driving. The exhaust note carries a raspy, sporty tone that reinforces its performance intent.

Handling is where the Stelvio truly distinguishes itself. Quick steering ratios, balanced weight distribution, and well-controlled body roll give it one of the most athletic driving characters in the compact luxury SUV class. Even on 20-inch wheels, ride compliance remains respectable, absorbing most road imperfections without harshness.

Fuel Economy
- EPA City: 22 mpg
- EPA Highway: 28 mpg
- Combined: ~24 mpg
- Real-world highway test: ~26 mpg
While respectable for a performance-leaning SUV, these figures trail more efficiency-focused competitors like hybridized rivals.
interior:
Step inside, and the Stelvio presents a driver-centric cockpit inspired by its sedan sibling, the Alfa Romeo Giulia. The seating position is sporty yet comfortable, with supportive leather-wrapped seats designed for long drives and enthusiastic cornering alike. Aluminum trim accents across the dashboard, doors, and center console add a premium visual touch, though some lower-dash and door materials don’t feel as rich as German competitors. Ergonomically, the layout is intuitive, placing key controls within easy reach of the driver. Front occupants benefit from generous headroom and shoulder space, while the rear bench accommodates three passengers, albeit with just adequate legroom for taller adults. Rear air vents and USB ports improve second-row usability.

Cargo capacity measures:
- 19 cubic feet behind rear seats
- Up to ~56 cubic feet with seats folded
- Fits 8 carry-on suitcases (19 with seats folded in testing)
Storage solutions include a removable center-console tray, a smartphone slot between cupholders, and door pockets sized for daily items.
technology: The Stelvio’s infotainment system centers around an 8.8-inch touchscreen, which now feels modest compared with the widescreen displays dominating the segment. The interface supports touch inputs as well as a rotary controller on the center console, offering multiple interaction methods. Graphics are clean and functional, but menu logic takes time to master, and response times lag behind newer competitors. Still, essential features are well covered: built-in navigation, Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth connectivity, and voice controls all come standard. A customizable digital instrument cluster adds a modern touch, allowing drivers to adjust information layouts based on preference. Audio duties are handled by an 8-speaker system as standard, while a 14-speaker Harman/Kardon setup is available for richer sound staging and deeper bass response.
safety:
Standard driver-assistance tech includes:
- Automated emergency braking
- Blind-spot monitoring
- Adaptive cruise control
Optional upgrades add lane-keeping assist and lane-centering functionality, enhancing highway driving convenience.
warranty:
- Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 1 year / 10,000 miles
Coverage is competitive but not class-leading, aligning closely with most European rivals.
pros: Thrilling handling, strong turbo performance, standout Italian styling.
cons: Aging infotainment, limited cargo space, below-average fuel economy.
mn_take: A driver-focused luxury SUV that prioritizes emotion and agility over tech and practicality.

car_name: 2026 Alfa Romeo Giulia Review — Italian Sports Sedan That Still Thrills
overview: The 2026 Alfa Romeo Giulia continues to embody everything enthusiasts love about Italian performance sedans—striking design, razor-sharp handling, and an emotional driving experience. Even when parked beside its German rivals, the Giulia’s sculpted bodywork, signature triangular grille, and aggressive stance make it instantly recognizable. For 2026, the Giulia carries over largely unchanged as an all-gasoline sports sedan while a next-generation model looms on the horizon. Beneath its stylish skin lies a finely tuned chassis and a spirited turbocharged engine that prioritizes driver engagement above all else. While its interior tech and outright luxury may trail class leaders, the Giulia remains one of the most entertaining compact luxury sedans to drive daily.
pricing:
- Base: $48,245
- Veloce: $49,870
Upgrading to the Veloce trim is worthwhile for enthusiasts, adding a limited-slip differential, sport seats with adjustable bolsters, gloss-red brake calipers, and available premium interior upgrades including leather-wrapped surfaces and a 14-speaker Harman/Kardon audio system.
drivetrain:
Under the hood sits a 280-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine paired with an 8-speed automatic transmission. Buyers can choose between rear-wheel drive for purist handling or all-wheel drive for added traction.
Acceleration is brisk:
- 0–60 mph: 4.6 seconds (RWD)
- 0–60 mph: 5.4 seconds (AWD)
The Giulia’s engine is lively and vocal, delivering a sporty exhaust note that enhances its character under hard acceleration. Alfa Romeo’s signature DNA drive-mode selector—Dynamic, Natural, and Advanced Efficiency—adjusts throttle response, steering weight, and transmission behavior, allowing the sedan to shift from relaxed commuter to back-road performer instantly. Handling is where the Giulia truly shines. Steering is sharp and communicative, body roll is tightly controlled, and the chassis feels light and balanced through corners. It’s a sedan that invites spirited driving yet remains comfortable enough for everyday use.

Fuel Economy:
- 23–24 mpg city
- 31–33 mpg highway
- 26–27 mpg combined
Real-world highway testing has returned up to 32 mpg, making the Giulia relatively efficient for a performance-focused luxury sedan.
interior: Inside, the Giulia blends sportiness with understated Italian elegance. The dashboard flows in a wide, driver-oriented sweep, with integrated infotainment neatly shaded beneath the upper dash brow. Soft-touch materials and leather surfaces create a premium ambiance, though the overall richness falls slightly short of rivals from Germany. Front seats are supportive and well-bolstered, especially with the optional sport seats that hold occupants firmly during aggressive cornering. Driving position is excellent, with clear outward visibility and a cockpit-like feel that enhances driver connection. Rear seating is snug but usable for adults on shorter journeys. Trunk practicality is decent, accommodating five carry-on suitcases, expanding to 14 with the rear seats folded—slightly behind segment leaders but still functional for daily needs.
technology: The Giulia features an 8.8-inch touchscreen infotainment system integrated into the dashboard, paired with a 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster offering multiple display themes such as Evolved, Relax, and Heritage. While the interface is relatively intuitive and supports navigation, Bluetooth, and smartphone integration, the system shows its age compared to newer competitors. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard but require a wired connection, and the screen graphics and response times aren’t as modern as rivals. Users can interact via touchscreen or a rotary controller on the center console. Standard audio comes through an 8-speaker setup, while audiophiles can upgrade to a 14-speaker Harman/Kardon premium system for richer sound quality.
safety:
Standard driver-assistance technologies include:
- Automated emergency braking
- Lane-keeping assist
- Adaptive cruise control
Optional packages add more advanced adaptive cruise with lane-centering capability for enhanced highway driving support.
warranty:
- Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 1 year / 10,000 miles
Coverage is competitive, though some rivals offer longer complimentary service periods.
pros: Sharp handling, thrilling driving dynamics, standout Italian styling, and strong turbo performance make it a true enthusiast’s luxury sedan.
cons: Outdated infotainment, wired smartphone connectivity, and cabin luxury that trails German competitors.
mn_take: The 2026 Giulia remains one of the most engaging driver’s sedans in the luxury segment, blending Italian passion with everyday usability despite aging tech.

car_name: 2026 Alfa Romeo Tonale Review — Italian Style Meets Compact Luxury Performance
overview:
The 2026 Alfa Romeo Tonale represents Alfa Romeo’s smallest SUV offering in the U.S. market, but it carries the brand’s unmistakable Italian character in both design and driving dynamics. Styled with sharp creases, a signature triangular grille, and athletic proportions, the Tonale stands out visually in a segment often dominated by conservative German styling.

For 2026, the Tonale receives a mild facelift inspired by the exotic 33 Stradale supercar, bringing subtle revisions to the front fascia along with new color options and a Sport Speciale trim. While compact in footprint, the Tonale prioritizes driver engagement and road feel over outright practicality, positioning itself as a sporty alternative to more comfort-focused subcompact luxury SUVs.
pricing:
The 2026 Tonale is competitively priced within the subcompact luxury segment:
- Sprint: $40,745
- Veloce: $45,245
- Sport Speciale: $45,245
The Veloce trim is the enthusiast’s choice, adding adaptive dampers, paddle shifters, ambient lighting, a power liftgate, red Brembo brake calipers, and larger alloy wheels that enhance both performance and visual appeal.
drivetrain:
Powering the Tonale is a turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 268 horsepower, paired with a 9-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive. The engine delivers brisk acceleration, propelling the SUV from 0–60 mph in 5.6 seconds, placing it right alongside performance-oriented rivals in the class. On the road, the Tonale feels light on its feet, with communicative steering and tight body control that make twisty roads genuinely enjoyable. Adaptive dampers on higher trims further sharpen handling responses while maintaining acceptable ride comfort. However, the transmission can feel slightly hesitant and jerky at low speeds, particularly in stop-and-go urban driving.
Towing capacity stands at 3,307 pounds, which is impressive for a vehicle in this size category.

Efficiency is respectable for a performance-leaning AWD luxury SUV:
- 21 mpg city
- 29 mpg highway
- 24 mpg combined
While not class-leading, these figures strike a fair balance between performance and everyday usability.
interior: Step inside, and the Tonale’s cabin reflects Alfa Romeo’s sporty heritage with a driver-centric layout inspired by the Giulia sedan and Stelvio SUV. The dashboard features sculpted surfaces, circular air vents, and a twin-hump instrument binnacle that adds visual drama to the cockpit. A thick-rimmed three-spoke steering wheel integrates the ignition button, reinforcing the performance-oriented theme, while large aluminum paddle shifters (on Veloce and above) enhance driver involvement. Material quality is solid, with soft-touch panels and contrast stitching, though overall plushness doesn’t quite reach the benchmark set by some German rivals. Front-seat comfort is good for long drives, but rear-seat space is tighter than competitors like the Volvo XC40 or Mini Countryman. Cargo practicality is adequate, accommodating five carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats and up to 17 with the second row folded.
technology: At the center of the dashboard sits a 10.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system running Uconnect 5 software, offering a crisp interface with customizable menus and responsive inputs. The system supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with Bluetooth connectivity and wireless smartphone charging, ensuring seamless device integration without cable clutter. Built-in navigation and onboard Wi-Fi expand the Tonale’s connected capabilities, while the standard six-speaker audio system provides decent clarity. Audiophiles can opt for the available 14-speaker Harman/Kardon premium sound system, which significantly enhances cabin acoustics with richer bass and clearer highs. The overall infotainment experience feels modern, intuitive, and well-integrated into the driver-focused cockpit design.
safety:
The Tonale comes equipped with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies, including:
- Automated emergency braking
- Lane-keeping assist
- Blind-spot monitoring
- Adaptive cruise control
Optional upgrades add parking sensors and advanced lane-centering functionality for enhanced highway driving support.
warranty:
- Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 1 year / 10,000 miles
Coverage is average for the segment, though the inclusion of scheduled maintenance is a welcome bonus.
pros: Striking Italian design, agile handling, strong turbo performance, and standard AWD make it one of the most fun-to-drive subcompact luxury SUVs.
cons: Snug rear space, transmission hesitation at low speeds, and cabin luxury that trails top German rivals.
mn_take: The 2026 Tonale delivers authentic Alfa Romeo driving flair in a compact luxury SUV, prioritizing style and sportiness over outright practicality.

car_name: 2026 Acura MDX Review — Performance-Focused Luxury Meets Three-Row Practicality
overview:
The 2026 Acura MDX continues to serve as the flagship SUV in Acura’s lineup, blending sharp styling, engaging road manners, and family-friendly three-row practicality into one well-rounded luxury package. Unlike many rivals that lean heavily into plush isolation, the MDX takes a more driver-centric approach, delivering handling composure and steering precision that feel unusually athletic for a midsize three-row SUV.

Under the hood, buyers get a choice between a naturally aspirated V-6 and a performance-oriented twin-turbo V-6 in the Type S, both paired with a refined 10-speed automatic transmission. While interior design is modern and tech-forward, the overall material richness doesn’t quite match the opulence seen in some European competitors. Still, the MDX strikes a compelling balance between sportiness, usability, and value in the luxury three-row segment.
pricing:
The 2026 MDX spans a broad pricing range depending on trim level and performance upgrades:
- Base: $53,250
- Technology: $58,650
- A-Spec: $63,850
- Advance: $68,350
- A-Spec Advance: $70,350
- Type S: $77,300
The Technology trim remains the sweet spot, adding premium leather upholstery, ambient lighting, a 19-speaker Bang & Olufsen audio system, and expanded driver-assistance tech without pushing into the Type S price territory.
drivetrain:
Powering the standard MDX is a 3.5-liter naturally aspirated V-6 producing 290 horsepower, paired with a smooth-shifting 10-speed automatic transmission. Front-wheel drive comes standard, while Acura’s torque-vectoring SH-AWD system is optional and significantly enhances cornering stability and traction. For enthusiasts, the Type S introduces a turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 delivering 355 horsepower and standard all-wheel drive. Acceleration is notably stronger, with 0–60 mph arriving in 5.5 seconds, compared to 6.4 seconds for the standard engine. Despite its size, the MDX feels composed through corners, with well-weighted steering and controlled body motions. Towing capacity reaches 3,500 pounds (FWD) and 5,000 pounds (AWD), making it capable for light trailer duties.

Fuel efficiency is mid-pack for the segment:
- 19 mpg city
- 26 mpg highway
- 22 mpg combined
Real-world highway testing has returned around 22–23 mpg, depending on trim and drivetrain. Performance models like the Type S trade a bit of efficiency for added power.
interior:
Inside, the MDX presents a modern, driver-focused cabin that blends premium design with everyday usability. Higher trims elevate the ambiance with stitched leather dashboards, open-pore wood, metallic accents, and piano-black detailing that give the SUV a sophisticated visual presence without feeling overly flashy.

Front seats are supportive and built for long-distance comfort, available with 16-way power adjustment, heating, ventilation, and even massage functions on upper trims. The second row offers generous legroom and cushioning, making it well-suited for adult passengers on extended trips. The third row, however, is better reserved for children or shorter journeys, as space is tighter compared to class leaders. Cargo capacity is practical: with all seats up, there’s room for about three carry-on suitcases, expanding to 27 cases with both rear rows folded.
technology: The MDX’s tech suite is one of its strongest highlights, anchored by a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment display paired with a 12.3-inch fully digital instrument cluster. The interface is crisp, responsive, and designed to keep key vehicle data and navigation visuals easily accessible to the driver. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with built-in navigation, a Wi-Fi hotspot, and wireless smartphone charging. Audio performance scales with trim: base models feature an 11-speaker system, while Technology and above trims upgrade to a 19-speaker Bang & Olufsen setup. The Type S pushes this further with an immersive 31-speaker premium audio system, delivering concert-like clarity throughout the cabin.
safety:
Acura equips every MDX with a comprehensive driver-assistance suite, including:
- Automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Lane-departure warning and lane-keeping assist
- Adaptive cruise control
- Blind-spot monitoring with lane-change assist
These systems work seamlessly in the background, enhancing driver confidence without feeling intrusive.
warranty:
- Limited Warranty: 4 years / 50,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 6 years / 70,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 2 years / 24,000 miles
Coverage is competitive for the luxury segment, with the added benefit of scheduled maintenance included early in ownership.
pros: Athletic handling, powerful V-6 options, premium tech features, and strong three-row versatility make it a driver’s luxury SUV.
cons: Fuel economy trails rivals, third row is tight for adults, and interior plushness falls short of top European competitors.
mn_take: The 2026 MDX stands out as a performance-leaning luxury three-row SUV that prioritizes driving engagement and technology over outright cabin opulence.

car_name: 2026 Acura RDX Review: Price, Specs, Performance, Fuel Economy, Interior & Features Explained
overview:
The 2026 Acura RDX continues to carve its space in the compact luxury SUV segment by blending sporty dynamics with strong value. Acura’s design language keeps the RDX looking sharp and athletic, highlighted by its diamond pentagon grille, sculpted body lines, and aggressive lighting signature. While it may not chase the ultra-plush experience of some European rivals, the RDX focuses on delivering an engaging drive paired with everyday practicality.

Built on a performance-oriented platform and equipped with standard all-wheel drive, the RDX appeals to buyers who want a premium SUV that feels lively behind the wheel. Its cabin is spacious, technology-packed, and driver-focused, though material richness doesn’t quite reach class leaders. Still, when viewed as a complete package—performance, features, and pricing—the RDX presents itself as a compelling alternative in the luxury crossover landscape.
pricing:
The 2026 Acura RDX is priced from $46,550 and goes up to $56,300 depending on trim selection and optional equipment.

The lineup includes Base, Technology, A-Spec, Advance, and A-Spec Advance trims. The Technology trim strikes the best balance for most buyers, adding premium leather upholstery, navigation, and a high-end audio system without pushing the price too close to European competitors. Higher trims introduce adaptive suspension, head-up display, and sportier visual enhancements, though they come at a noticeable premium.
drivetrain:
Every 2026 RDX is powered by a 272-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine paired with a 10-speed automatic transmission. Acura’s signature Super Handling All-Wheel Drive (SH-AWD) system is standard across the range, enhancing traction and cornering agility. Performance is one of the RDX’s strongest attributes. Throttle response is crisp, acceleration feels energetic in city driving, and the torque-vectoring AWD system helps the SUV rotate confidently through corners. Steering feedback is precise, giving the RDX a sportier personality than many comfort-focused rivals.

However, the transmission isn’t always quick to downshift during spirited driving, and the brake pedal feel can come across as soft under hard braking.
0–60 mph: ~6.2 seconds — competitive for the segment.

Fuel Economy:
EPA fuel-economy ratings for the 2026 RDX are:
- 21 mpg city
- 27 mpg highway
- 23 mpg combined
Real-world highway testing has produced results close to official estimates, making the RDX reasonably efficient for a turbocharged AWD luxury SUV, though hybrids in the class do better.
interior:
The RDX offers a roomy two-row cabin with ample headroom and legroom for adults in both rows. The seating position balances SUV visibility with a sporty, car-like feel for the driver.
Standard features include dual-zone climate control, power-adjustable heated front seats, and ambient lighting. Build quality is solid, but the overall ambiance leans more sporty than opulent. Rivals like the Mercedes-Benz GLC or BMW X3 deliver richer materials and a more luxurious atmosphere. Cargo practicality is strong, with space for 8 carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats and up to 22 with the second row folded, making it well suited for family duties and long trips.
technology: The RDX comes equipped with a 10.2-inch infotainment display positioned high on the dashboard for clear visibility. It supports touchscreen functionality along with Acura’s touchpad controller on the center console. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with a built-in Wi-Fi hotspot for seamless connectivity. Upgrading to the Technology package adds integrated navigation, additional USB ports for rear passengers, and a premium 12-speaker ELS Studio audio system.
