In real-world highway testing, it has returned around 36 mpg at 75 mph, still comfortably ahead of most gasoline-powered rivals. For commuters and long-distance drivers, the savings at the pump add up quickly.
interior: Inside, the Corolla Cross Hybrid mirrors the straightforward design of the Corolla sedan. Materials are functional rather than luxurious, but build quality feels solid. Higher trims improve the ambiance with faux-leather upholstery, heated front seats, ambient lighting, and a power-adjustable driver’s seat. Cargo space is a clear advantage over the Corolla car lineup, offering 22 cubic feet behind the rear seats—more than the sedan and hatchback. Rear-seat comfort is adequate for adults, though competitors offer slightly more legroom.
technology: For 2026, Toyota upgrades the Corolla Cross Hybrid with improved tech. A 10.5-inch touchscreen is now standard, running Toyota’s latest infotainment software. Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, and SiriusXM are included across the lineup. Optional features include a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster, wireless charging, rear-seat USB ports, and a JBL premium audio system, helping the Corolla Cross Hybrid feel more modern than earlier models.
safety:
Toyota continues its strong safety focus by making advanced driver assistance standard on every trim. The Corolla Cross Hybrid includes:
- Automatic emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Lane-departure warning with steering assist
- Adaptive cruise control
- Automatic high-beam headlights

These features make the Corolla Cross Hybrid one of the safer choices in the subcompact hybrid SUV segment.
warranty:
Toyota’s warranty coverage is competitive, with excellent protection for hybrid components.
- 3 years / 36,000 miles limited vehicle warranty
- 5 years / 60,000 miles powertrain warranty
- 10 years / 150,000 miles hybrid component coverage
- 2 years / 25,000 miles complimentary scheduled maintenance

This coverage enhances long-term ownership confidence.
pros: Excellent fuel economy, standard all-wheel drive, smooth hybrid performance, and strong safety tech.
cons: Uninspiring driving dynamics, basic interior materials on lower trims, and limited towing capacity.
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota Corolla Cross Hybrid is a smart, efficient, and practical compact SUV that prioritizes real-world usability and low ownership costs over excitement—making it an easy recommendation for efficiency-focused buyers.

car_name: 2026 Toyota Tundra Review: Price, Trims, V6 Performance, Towing, Safety & Verdict
overview:
The 2026 Toyota Tundra sticks to the traditional full-size pickup formula while carving out a personality of its own. Unlike many of its American rivals, the Tundra skips a V8 entirely, relying instead on a modern twin-turbocharged V6 engine offered in two output levels. Toyota also takes a slightly different engineering approach with a coil-spring rear suspension, which gives the Tundra a noticeably smoother and more controlled ride than many leaf-spring competitors in daily driving.

Available in Double Cab and CrewMax body styles, the Tundra delivers solid comfort, technology, and capability, though it doesn’t quite match the outright interior space, towing numbers, or luxury flourishes of the Ford F-150, Ram 1500, or GMC Sierra. Still, for buyers who prioritize refinement, long-term reliability, and real-world usability over spec-sheet bragging rights, the Tundra remains a dependable and well-rounded half-ton pickup.
pricing:
The 2026 Toyota Tundra lineup spans a wide price range, catering to both work-focused buyers and those seeking premium appointments.

SR – $43,355
Entry-level workhorse aimed at fleets and contractors.

SR5 – $48,605 (Recommended)
Adds more power, better tech, and towing-focused features.

Limited – $56,955
Focuses on comfort with leather upholstery and more standard tech.

Platinum – $65,790
Luxury-oriented trim with premium materials and advanced features.

1794 Edition – $66,475
Western-inspired styling with upscale interior finishes.

MotorNation Pick: The SR5 offers the best mix of price, power, and features, while higher trims make sense for buyers prioritizing comfort over capability.
drivetrain:
Every non-hybrid 2026 Tundra is powered by Toyota’s 3.4-liter twin-turbo V6, paired with a 10-speed automatic transmission. The base SR trim produces 348 horsepower, while all higher trims benefit from an upgraded tune delivering 389 horsepower. Power delivery is smooth and confident, with strong mid-range torque that makes highway merging and towing feel effortless.

Rear-wheel drive is standard, while four-wheel drive is optional via a part-time system. While it lacks the full-time 4WD setups offered by some rivals, the Tundra’s coil-spring rear suspension stands out by providing a more composed ride over broken pavement and uneven surfaces. Acceleration is respectable for the segment, with a tested 0–60 mph time of 6.1 seconds, though it trails quicker rivals like the Ford F-150.

The Tundra delivers enough muscle for most real-world needs, even if it doesn’t lead the class. When properly equipped, it can tow up to 12,000 pounds, which is lower than key competitors but still sufficient for boats, campers, and work trailers. Maximum payload stands at 1,940 pounds, again trailing the segment leaders but remaining usable for everyday hauling duties.

Toyota has improved usability for 2026 by making a tow hitch and 7/4-pin trailer wiring harness standard across the lineup, along with a larger 32.2-gallon fuel tank, improving long-distance towing range.

Fuel efficiency is competitive for a full-size pickup with a twin-turbo V6. While official EPA ratings for 2026 are pending, previous figures suggest 17–20 mpg city and 20–24 mpg highway, depending on configuration. Real-world testing has shown mixed results, with highway cruising returning around 19 mpg, though heavy use and towing can drop overall averages significantly
interior:
Inside, the 2026 Tundra feels sturdy and purposeful rather than flashy. The dashboard design is chunky and practical, with large controls and ample storage throughout the cabin. Base trims use harder plastics, while Limited and above bring leather upholstery, softer materials, and a more premium ambiance.

Front-seat space is generous, though rival trucks offer slightly more legroom. The CrewMax provides adequate rear-seat comfort, but again trails segment leaders in outright space. Cargo flexibility is strong, with 6.5-foot and 8-foot bed options, enough width for standard plywood sheets, and useful storage solutions including under-seat compartments and a large center console.
technology:
Technology is a strong point for the Tundra, especially in higher trims. An 8-inch touchscreen comes standard, while an impressive 14-inch infotainment display is available and dominates the dashboard with crisp graphics and quick responses. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with multiple USB ports and available Wi-Fi connectivity.

Premium trims add a 12-speaker JBL audio system, wireless charging, and even a 120-volt power outlet, enhancing the Tundra’s appeal as both a work truck and long-distance cruiser.
safety:
Toyota equips every 2026 Tundra with its Toyota Safety Sense 2.5 suite as standard.
- Adaptive cruise control
- Forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking
- Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Automatic high-beam headlights
- Available blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert and trailer detection
These features help the Tundra remain competitive in a segment where safety technology is increasingly important.
warranty:
Toyota’s warranty coverage is in line with segment norms, but its complimentary maintenance stands out.
- 3 years / 36,000 miles limited vehicle warranty
- 5 years / 60,000 miles powertrain warranty
- 2 years / 25,000 miles complimentary scheduled maintenance
This maintenance coverage provides added peace of mind for long-term ownership.
pros: Smooth twin-turbo V6 performance, comfortable ride quality, strong standard safety tech, and Toyota’s reputation for reliability.
cons: Lower towing and payload ratings, less interior space than rivals, and no V8 engine option.
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota Tundra may not top the spec sheets, but it delivers a refined, dependable, and comfortable full-size truck experience ideal for buyers who value usability over outright numbers.

car_name: 2026 Toyota Crown Review: Price, Hybrid Performance, Features, Safety & Verdict
overview: The 2026 Toyota Crown quietly redefines what a Toyota sedan can be. While the brand is traditionally associated with reliability and value, the Crown confidently steps into near-luxury territory with bold styling, a raised sedan stance, standard all-wheel drive, and exclusively hybrid powertrains. Its design is polarizing—tall, wide, and SUV-inspired—but that same unconventional approach gives it a commanding road presence unlike anything else in Toyota’s lineup. More importantly, the Crown’s interior quality, refinement, and technology bring it dangerously close to Lexus ES and Genesis G80 territory, while still wearing a Toyota badge and price tag.
pricing:
The 2026 Toyota Crown lineup is priced competitively for a premium hybrid sedan, with all trims offering AWD as standard.

XLE – $43,110
Entry point with strong standard equipment, hybrid AWD, and a comfort-focused setup.

Limited – $47,620
Adds more luxury touches including panoramic sunroof, leather upholstery, and upgraded tech.

Nightshade – $49,960
Focuses on darker exterior styling elements while retaining the standard hybrid powertrain.

Platinum (Hybrid Max) – $56,660
Top-spec trim with the powerful Hybrid Max system, adaptive dampers, and the most premium features.

MotorNation Pick: The Platinum stands out for buyers seeking performance and luxury in one package, while the Limited offers the best balance of price and premium feel.
drivetrain:
Every 2026 Toyota Crown is hybrid-powered, but the experience varies significantly by trim. The XLE, Limited, and Nightshade models use a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine paired with three electric motors, producing a combined 236 horsepower. This setup prioritizes smoothness and efficiency, delivering relaxed acceleration that suits daily commuting rather than spirited driving.

The Platinum trim is where things get interesting. It features Toyota’s Hybrid Max powertrain, combining a turbocharged 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine with dual electric motors for a robust 340 horsepower. Unlike the CVT used in lower trims, the Platinum gets a six-speed automatic transmission, which provides more natural gear shifts and a sportier driving feel. Adaptive dampers further sharpen its responses, making the Platinum noticeably more engaging on winding roads.

In performance testing, the standard hybrid Crown reaches 60 mph in about 7.2 seconds, while the Platinum does the sprint in a much quicker 5.1 seconds, firmly placing it among premium mid-size sedans.

Efficiency is one of the Crown’s strongest selling points. Although official EPA figures for 2026 are pending, they are expected to carry over unchanged.

Lower trims with the standard hybrid system are rated at approximately 42 mpg city and 41 mpg highway, which is exceptional for an AWD mid-size sedan. Real-world highway testing has shown results right on target, with some drivers achieving over 40 mpg consistently.

The more powerful Platinum Hybrid Max sacrifices some efficiency for performance, returning an estimated 29 mpg city and 32 mpg highway, which remains respectable given its output and standard AWD system.
interior:
Step inside the Crown and the transformation is immediate. The cabin feels far more upscale than most Toyotas, especially in Limited and Platinum trims. Soft-touch materials, clean dashboard design, and tasteful ambient lighting give it a premium atmosphere that rivals entry-luxury sedans. The raised seating position offers easier ingress and egress compared to traditional low-slung sedans, which many buyers will appreciate.

All trims come standard with heated, power-adjustable front seats, dual-zone automatic climate control, and generous legroom for both rows. Higher trims add ventilated front seats, leather upholstery, and a panoramic sunroof. Ride quality is tuned for comfort first, soaking up rough roads effortlessly, making the Crown a strong long-distance cruiser.
technology:
The 2026 Crown is well-equipped technologically, featuring a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system across all trims running Toyota’s latest software. The interface is responsive, easy to navigate, and finally feels competitive with premium rivals. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with wireless charging, multiple USB-C ports, onboard Wi-Fi, and a fully digital 12.3-inch instrument cluster.

Audio quality varies by trim, with the base XLE receiving a six-speaker system, while Limited and Platinum models upgrade to an 11-speaker JBL system, though it still falls slightly short of class-leading luxury audio setups.
safety:
Safety is a strong suit for the Crown, with a comprehensive suite of driver-assistance technologies standard across the lineup.
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Adaptive cruise control with lane centering
- Automatic high-beam headlights
- 5-star overall safety rating from NHTSA
These features make the Crown one of the most confidence-inspiring sedans in its segment.
warranty:
Toyota’s warranty coverage is solid and particularly strong for hybrid components.
- 3 years / 36,000 miles limited vehicle warranty
- 5 years / 60,000 miles powertrain warranty
- 10 years / 150,000 miles coverage for hybrid components
- 2 years / 25,000 miles complimentary scheduled maintenance
While rivals like Genesis offer longer overall coverage, Toyota’s hybrid warranty remains a major long-term ownership advantage.
pros: Premium interior quality, excellent fuel efficiency, standard AWD, and a powerful Hybrid Max option elevate the Crown beyond a typical Toyota sedan.
cons: Polarizing exterior design and average audio quality may not appeal to traditional luxury buyers.
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota Crown is a bold, near-luxury hybrid sedan that delivers comfort, efficiency, and surprising performance—perfect for buyers who want Lexus-level refinement without the Lexus price tag.

car_name: 2026 Toyota GR Supra – A Driver’s Sports Car in Its Final, Most Focused Form
overview:
The 2026 Toyota GR Supra remains one of the most emotionally engaging sports cars on sale, blending classic rear-wheel-drive balance with modern turbocharged performance. Its long hood, wide haunches, and unmistakable double-bubble roof immediately signal serious intent, while underneath the sculpted bodywork lies a mechanical package built squarely for driving enthusiasts.

Powered exclusively by a 382-horsepower turbocharged inline-six, the GR Supra delivers effortless acceleration and a deep, refined exhaust note that grows more addictive the harder it’s driven. Toyota offers both a six-speed manual transmission—a rarity in this segment—and a quick-shifting eight-speed automatic, allowing buyers to tailor the experience to their preferences. Though developed alongside the BMW Z4, the Supra feels distinct in character, prioritizing sharp reflexes and driver connection over outright comfort.

The cabin is compact and cockpit-like, emphasizing a low seating position and wraparound design. Entry and exit require a bit of commitment, especially for taller drivers, but once settled in, the GR Supra rewards with a driving experience that feels increasingly rare in the modern era—focused, mechanical, and deeply satisfying.

The big news for 2026 is the introduction of the GR Supra MkV Final Edition, a more hardcore and collectible version that sits at the top of the lineup. This special model benefits from revised differential tuning, larger Brembo brake discs, stiffer suspension bushings, and a unique adaptive damper calibration aimed at improving body control and cornering precision.

Visually, the MkV Final Edition stands apart with 19-inch matte black wheels, a carbon-fiber ducktail spoiler, carbon-fiber mirror caps, red seatbelts, and exclusive GR-branded interior details. Toyota also includes a fitted car cover, underlining the Final Edition’s special-status positioning and hinting that the GR Supra’s days may be numbered.
pricing:
The 2026 Toyota GR Supra lineup starts at $59,495 for the GR Supra 3.0, which already includes the full 382-hp engine, adaptive suspension, and a well-equipped interior. The 3.0 Premium, priced at $62,645, adds more comfort-focused features such as upgraded audio, a head-up display, and additional driver-assistance tech.

At the top sits the GR Supra MkV Final Edition, priced at $70,545. While it commands a noticeable premium, it also represents the most focused and best-handling Supra Toyota has ever offered from the factory.

If budget allows, the MkV Final Edition is the one to have—not only for its performance upgrades, but also for its long-term enthusiast appeal. Regardless of trim, the manual transmission remains the enthusiast’s pick.
drivetrain:
The GR Supra’s 3.0-liter turbocharged inline-six continues to be a standout in the segment, producing 382 horsepower and 368 lb-ft of torque. Power delivery is smooth yet forceful, with strong mid-range punch that makes overtaking effortless and corner exits exhilarating.

Buyers can choose between a six-speed manual that emphasizes engagement and control, or an eight-speed automatic that delivers quicker shift times and marginally faster acceleration. The Supra’s rear-wheel-drive layout, near-perfect weight distribution, and adaptive suspension allow it to feel both planted and playful, depending on how hard it’s driven.

Steering is precise and well-weighted, offering excellent feedback through fast corners. Importantly, the suspension remains compliant enough for daily use, making the Supra far more livable than its hardcore appearance suggests—though winter traction remains a challenge even with proper tires.

With the manual transmission, the GR Supra accelerates from 0–60 mph in 3.9 seconds, while the automatic can be even quicker under ideal conditions. In high-speed testing, the Supra has proven equally impressive, completing a 0–150–0 mph run in just over 31 seconds, highlighting both its strong acceleration and confidence-inspiring braking performance.

For a car focused so heavily on performance, efficiency is surprisingly reasonable:
- Automatic: 22 mpg city / 29 mpg highway
- Manual: 19 mpg city / 26 mpg highway
In real-world highway driving, previous long-term testing has shown the Supra capable of achieving mid-30 mpg figures, making it more efficient than many expect from a near-400-hp sports coupe.
interior:
The GR Supra’s interior is unapologetically driver-centric, with a low seating position, thick-rim steering wheel, and a minimalist dashboard layout. 14-way power-adjustable sport seats help maximize comfort in the tight cabin, though broader drivers may find space limited.

Cargo space is accessed through a hatchback opening and is usable for a weekend getaway. In testing, the Supra managed to accommodate four carry-on suitcases, which is respectable for a two-seat sports car. Interior quality feels solid, and BMW-sourced switchgear ensures familiar ergonomics and dependable functionality.
technology: The GR Supra uses an 8.8-inch infotainment display running a Toyota-skinned version of BMW’s iDrive system. Apple CarPlay and navigation are available, though Android Auto is notably absent. Higher trims add a 12-speaker JBL audio system, a head-up display, and wireless charging, enhancing daily usability without diluting the car’s focused nature.
safety:
Safety equipment is comprehensive for a sports coupe, with standard features including:
- Automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Lane-departure warning
- Automatic high-beam headlights
Optional packages add adaptive cruise control and blind-spot monitoring, providing extra reassurance for longer highway drives.
warranty:
Toyota backs the GR Supra with:
- Limited warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
While not class-leading, coverage is in line with competitors and supported by Toyota’s strong reliability reputation.
pros: Outstanding inline-six performance, manual transmission availability, precise handling, distinctive design, strong enthusiast appeal
cons: Tight cabin for larger drivers, limited outward visibility, rear-wheel drive limits winter usability
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota GR Supra is a rare modern sports car that prioritizes driver engagement above all else, and with the MkV Final Edition leading the lineup, it feels like a fitting and emotional high point for one of Toyota’s most iconic nameplates.

car_name: 2026 Toyota GR Corolla – A Rally-Bred Hot Hatch with Everyday Usability
overview:
The 2026 Toyota GR Corolla stands as one of the most authentic performance cars available today, blending motorsport engineering with real-world practicality in a way few modern hot hatches manage. Developed by Toyota’s Gazoo Racing division, this isn’t just a warmed-over Corolla—it’s a ground-up performance machine inspired by the brand’s rally program. While many rivals chase lap times through electronics and oversized engines, the GR Corolla focuses on mechanical grip, lightweight construction, and driver involvement.

Under the hood is a compact yet ferocious 1.6-liter turbocharged three-cylinder engine, derived from the globally celebrated GR Yaris. Despite its small displacement, it produces a robust 300 horsepower and 370 Nm (273 lb-ft) of torque, delivering explosive acceleration and a distinctive exhaust note. Power is sent to all four wheels via Toyota’s GR-Four all-wheel-drive system, giving the GR Corolla exceptional traction in all conditions. A six-speed manual transmission comes standard for purists, while an optional eight-speed automatic caters to drivers who want performance without sacrificing daily comfort.

Crucially, the GR Corolla retains the usability of a standard Corolla hatchback, offering four doors, a usable rear seat, and a practical cargo area. This dual personality—weekend track toy and weekday commuter—is what truly defines its appeal.
pricing:
The 2026 GR Corolla lineup remains refreshingly simple, keeping the focus firmly on performance rather than trim-level confusion.

The range starts with the GR Corolla Core, priced at $41,115, which already includes the full 300-hp powertrain, GR-Four AWD, performance suspension, limited-slip differentials, and a comprehensive safety suite. This trim delivers the purest expression of the GR Corolla’s mission and represents outstanding value in the hot-hatch segment.

At the top sits the GR Corolla Premium Plus, priced at $47,160. This version adds a carbon-fiber roof to lower the center of gravity, a more aggressive power bulge hood, a head-up display, upgraded interior materials, and a premium JBL sound system. While these features enhance the experience, the mechanical package remains identical.

For most enthusiasts, the Core trim remains the sweet spot, offering maximum performance per dollar without unnecessary weight or cost.
drivetrain:
At the heart of the GR Corolla lies one of the most technically impressive engines in the segment. The turbocharged 1.6-liter inline-three is small in size but immense in character, delivering strong mid-range punch and a willingness to rev that keeps the driving experience engaging at all speeds.

Power is routed through either a six-speed manual gearbox, praised for its short throws and mechanical feel, or an eight-speed automatic with paddle shifters that delivers quick, decisive shifts. The real highlight, however, is the GR-Four all-wheel-drive system, which allows the driver to actively adjust torque distribution:
- 60:40 front-to-rear for balanced daily driving
- 50:50 for maximum traction during spirited or track driving
- 30:70 rear-biased for aggressive cornering and playful handling

On a winding road, the GR Corolla feels exceptionally planted, with tenacious grip and minimal body roll. Steering is sharp and communicative, giving the driver confidence to push harder with every corner. The suspension is firm but well-controlled, striking a balance between track readiness and daily usability.

The GR Corolla’s performance figures back up its aggressive character:
- 0–60 mph: 4.9 seconds (manual)
- 0–60 mph: 5.0 seconds (automatic)
While slightly slower than some higher-powered rivals on paper, the GR Corolla feels more intense from behind the wheel thanks to its lighter feel, aggressive torque delivery, and mechanical engagement.

Considering its performance focus, efficiency remains respectable:
- EPA (Manual): ~21 mpg city / 28 mpg highway
- EPA (Automatic): ~19 mpg city / 27 mpg highway
- Real-world highway testing: Approximately 28 mpg at 75 mph
These figures make the GR Corolla far easier to live with daily than many traditional performance cars.
interior:
Inside, the GR Corolla combines familiar Corolla practicality with purposeful performance upgrades. The cabin features sport bucket seats with aggressive bolstering, GR-specific trim elements, aluminum pedals, and subtle red accents that reinforce its motorsport DNA. Build quality is solid, though the focus is clearly on function over luxury.

Rear-seat space is adequate for adults on shorter trips, though tighter than rivals such as the Volkswagen Golf R. Where the GR Corolla shines is cargo practicality: with the rear seats up, it comfortably holds three carry-on suitcases, expanding to 15 carry-on bags with the seats folded—making it one of the most usable performance hatchbacks on sale.
technology: Technology is straightforward and driver-focused. An 8.0-inch touchscreen comes standard, offering wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, Bluetooth connectivity, and an available Wi-Fi hotspot. Higher trims add a JBL premium audio system with Active Sound Control, enhancing cabin acoustics during spirited driving.
safety:
Despite its performance orientation, the GR Corolla doesn’t compromise on safety. Standard equipment includes:
- Automated emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist detection
- Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Adaptive cruise control
- Automatic high-beam headlights
These systems operate smoothly in the background, adding confidence without dulling the driving experience.
warranty:
Toyota backs the GR Corolla with a solid ownership package:
- Limited warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Complimentary maintenance: 2 years / 25,000 miles
A standout perk is the one-year National Auto Sport Association (NASA) membership, which includes a complimentary high-performance driving event—an ideal way for owners to safely explore the car’s capabilities.
pros: Explosive performance, adjustable all-wheel drive, standard manual transmission, genuine rally heritage, strong everyday practicality
cons: Firm ride quality, rear seat space is limited, interior prioritizes function over luxury
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota GR Corolla is a rare modern performance car that stays true to its motorsport roots—raw, engaging, and endlessly fun—while still being practical enough to live with every day, making it one of the most exciting hot hatches money can buy.

car_name: 2026 Toyota Corolla Review: Sensible, Efficient, and Still a Safe Bet
overview:
For decades, the Toyota Corolla has been the default choice for buyers who value reliability, safety, and low running costs, and the 2026 Corolla stays firmly true to that reputation. It may not be the most exciting compact car on sale, but it remains one of the most dependable daily drivers you can buy. Toyota continues to offer the Corolla in sedan and hatchback body styles, along with an extremely fuel-efficient hybrid option, ensuring there’s something for commuters, families, and budget-conscious buyers alike.

On the road, the Corolla prioritizes comfort and ease of use. The suspension is tuned for a smooth ride, visibility is excellent, and its compact dimensions make it stress-free to drive and park in tight urban spaces. That said, rivals like the Honda Civic and Mazda 3 feel more engaging to drive and offer sharper handling, which may matter to enthusiastic drivers. The Corolla instead focuses on being calm, predictable, and economical—qualities many buyers still value most.
pricing:
The 2026 Toyota Corolla starts at $24,120 and stretches to $30,335, depending on trim and powertrain choice. Toyota offers one of the widest trim spreads in the compact segment, including sporty and hybrid-focused variants.
- LE – $24,120: The most affordable entry point, aimed at comfort and efficiency.
- SE – $25,575 / $26,560: Sportier suspension tuning, larger wheels, and sharper styling.
- Hybrid LE – $25,970: Prioritizes maximum fuel efficiency at a modest premium.
- Nightshade Edition – ~$26,000 (est.): Adds dark exterior accents for a stealthy look.
- FX Edition – $28,175: Limited-run sporty hatchback with unique wheels and aero upgrades.
- Hybrid SE – $28,410: Blends sportier styling with hybrid efficiency.
- XSE / XLE – $28,570 to $29,835: Focus on premium features and technology.
- Hybrid XLE – $30,335: The most expensive Corolla, offering maximum efficiency with added luxury.
Best pick: The SE sedan strikes the best balance, offering improved driving dynamics, attractive styling, and solid standard features without pushing the price too high.
drivetrain:
Most Corolla models use a 2.0-liter naturally aspirated four-cylinder engine producing 169 horsepower, paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT) and front-wheel drive. Power delivery is smooth and predictable, but outright acceleration is modest, especially during highway overtakes, where the engine can sound strained under heavy throttle.

The hybrid Corolla pairs a gasoline engine with an electric motor for improved efficiency rather than performance. While it feels responsive in city driving thanks to electric assist, it is noticeably slower than the standard petrol version during hard acceleration.

Ride quality is a strong point. Both the sedan and hatchback absorb bumps well, making them comfortable for daily commuting. SE and XSE trims benefit from a sport-tuned suspension and larger 18-inch wheels, giving them slightly better cornering control, though they still fall short of the Civic or Mazda 3 in driving engagement.

0–60 mph and Driving Feel
- Hybrid AWD: ~9.0 seconds
- Hatchback (gas): ~8.3 seconds
Top speed is electronically limited to 107 mph (hybrid) and 111 mph (hatchback). Braking performance is adequate rather than impressive, but pedal feel remains consistent and confidence-inspiring.

Fuel efficiency remains one of the Corolla’s strongest selling points.
Non-hybrid (EPA):
-Up to 32 mpg city / 41 mpg highway / 35 mpg combined
Hybrid (EPA):
- Up to 53 mpg city / 46 mpg highway / 50 mpg combined

In real-world testing, hybrid models returned around 40 mpg at highway speeds, while petrol versions hovered near 40–41 mpg, depending on body style and trim—excellent figures for everyday use.
interior:
Inside, the 2026 Corolla feels modern and well-assembled, with soft-touch materials, a clean dashboard layout, and intuitive controls. Most trims come with keyless entry and push-button start, while higher variants add ambient lighting, heated front seats, and dual-zone climate control.

Rear-seat space is better in the sedan, making it the preferred option for families or frequent passengers. The hatchback, while more stylish, sacrifices legroom and practicality.

Cargo capacity varies significantly:
Hatchback:
- 18 cubic feet standard
- Up to 23 cubic feet with the Enhanced Cargo Space option
Sedan:
- 13 cubic feet, but impressively usable, fitting up to eight carry-on bags

Storage inside the cabin is adequate, though not class-leading, with useful center-console trays and door bins helping everyday usability.
technology:
Every Corolla comes standard with an 8.0-inch touchscreen supporting Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with a Wi-Fi hotspot (subscription-based). A larger 10.5-inch touchscreen is available on higher trims.

Digital instrumentation is now standard:
- 7.0-inch digital cluster: LE and SE
- 12.3-inch digital cluster: XSE and XLE

Additional highlights include four USB-C ports, wireless charging on select trims, and an optional JBL premium audio system.
safety:
Every Corolla comes standard with an 8.0-inch touchscreen supporting Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, along with a Wi-Fi hotspot (subscription-based). A larger 10.5-inch touchscreen is available on higher trims.

Digital instrumentation is now standard:
- 7.0-inch digital cluster: LE and SE
- 12.3-inch digital cluster: XSE and XLE

Additional highlights include four USB-C ports, wireless charging on select trims, and an optional JBL premium audio system.
warranty:
Toyota equips the 2026 Corolla with Safety Sense 3.0 as standard, reinforcing its reputation as one of the safest cars in its class. The system includes:
- Forward-collision warning with automated emergency braking and pedestrian detection
- Lane-departure warning with active lane-keeping assist
- Adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go functionality
- Automatic high-beam headlights and road sign assist

Strong expected crash-test performance from NHTSA and IIHS further boosts buyer confidence, especially for families and first-time car owners.
pros: Excellent fuel efficiency, strong reliability reputation, wide trim and body-style choices, comprehensive standard safety features
cons: Average performance, limited driving excitement, some rivals offer better interior space and handling
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota Corolla remains a smart, dependable choice for buyers who value efficiency, safety, and long-term peace of mind— even if it no longer leads the class in driving excitement.

car_name: 2026 Toyota Sequoia Review: Hybrid Muscle Meets Full-Size SUV Practicality
overview:
The 2026 Toyota Sequoia continues to chart a unique path in the full-size SUV segment by going hybrid-only, blending serious power with noticeably better fuel efficiency than traditional V-8 rivals. Built on the same body-on-frame TNGA-F platform as the Tundra pickup, the Sequoia feels every bit like a truck-based SUV—solid, capable, and confidence-inspiring—while its electrified powertrain helps soften the fuel-consumption blow that usually comes with this size.

With 437 horsepower, impressive towing capability, and trims ranging from family-friendly to hardcore off-road-focused, the Sequoia covers a wide spectrum of buyers. However, its biggest compromises show up in the rear: a tight third row and limited cargo space with all seats in use prevent it from matching the sheer practicality of rivals like the Chevrolet Tahoe or Ford Expedition.
pricing:
Toyota offers the 2026 Sequoia in a broad range of trims, each clearly positioned:

SR5 – $66,920
The entry-level Sequoia comes well equipped with the hybrid powertrain, standard safety tech, and solid interior quality, but its smaller infotainment screen and fewer luxury features make it feel basic for the price.

Limited – $72,690 (Best Value)
The sweet spot of the lineup, the Limited adds a 14.0-inch touchscreen, heated and ventilated front seats, power-folding third row, 20-inch wheels, and a power liftgate—features that most buyers expect in this class.

Platinum – $82,930
Focuses on comfort with upgraded materials, optional load-leveling rear suspension, and additional convenience features.

TRD Pro – $83,660
Designed for serious off-road use, it includes Fox dampers, skid plates, a locking rear differential, and aggressive 33-inch tires, plus the exclusive WaveMaker blue paint for 2026.

1794 Edition – $83,745
A Texas-inspired luxury trim with premium leather and western-themed design touches.

Capstone – $87,330
The flagship model, featuring textured premium leather, semi-aniline upholstery, and the most upscale cabin Toyota offers in the Sequoia lineup.
drivetrain:
Every 2026 Sequoia is powered by Toyota’s iForce MAX hybrid system, combining a twin-turbo 3.4-liter V-6 with an electric motor to deliver 437 hp and a massive 583 lb-ft of torque. Power is routed through a 10-speed automatic transmission, with rear-wheel drive standard and four-wheel drive available (and standard on TRD Pro).

Acceleration is strong for a vehicle this size, with a 0–60 mph time of around 5.6 seconds in four-wheel-drive form. The Sequoia feels quick in a straight line, but its wide stance, light steering, and sheer size make it less confidence-inspiring on tight roads. Ride quality is comfortable and well-damped, though the brake pedal can feel soft due to the hybrid system.

Towing is one of the Sequoia’s strongest suits:

Maximum towing capacity:
- Up to 9,520 pounds (RWD SR5)
- Around 8,980 pounds (4WD Capstone)
That beats many V-8 rivals and makes the Sequoia a legitimate option for towing boats, campers, or large trailers. Toyota’s Tow Technology package adds useful tools like Trailer Backup Guide and Straight Path Assist.

Thanks to its hybrid setup, the Sequoia is one of the most efficient full-size SUVs available:
- EPA estimates (RWD): 21 mpg city / 24 mpg highway / 22 mpg combined
- EPA estimates (4WD): 19 mpg city / 22 mpg highway / 20 mpg combined
Real-world highway testing returned around 19 mpg, still respectable given the Sequoia’s size and performance.
interior:
Inside, the Sequoia offers a commanding driving position and a wide range of interior styles depending on trim. Front-row comfort is excellent, and higher trims add heated and ventilated seats, premium leather, and a panoramic sunroof.

The third row, however, is a clear weak point. Legroom and headroom are tight, especially with the sunroof, and the high floor limits comfort for adults. Cargo space is also compromised, with just 12 cubic feet available behind the third row—far less than key competitors. Folding the third row helps, but the load floor isn’t flat.
technology:
Most trims come standard with a 14.0-inch touchscreen running Toyota’s latest infotainment software, offering wireless Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Wi-Fi hotspot capability, and cloud-based navigation. The base SR5 uses a smaller 8.0-inch display, though functionality remains largely the same.

Higher trims can be equipped with a premium audio system, digital rearview mirror, and additional camera views for towing and parking assistance.
safety:
Toyota equips every 2026 Sequoia with a full suite of driver-assistance tech as standard:
- Forward-collision warning with automated emergency braking
- Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Adaptive cruise control
- Automatic high-beam headlights
These systems work seamlessly and help offset the Sequoia’s large size in daily driving.
warranty:
Toyota’s coverage is competitive and strengthened by generous hybrid protection:
- Limited warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Hybrid components: 10 years / 150,000 miles
- Complimentary maintenance: 2 years / 25,000 miles
pros: Powerful and efficient hybrid powertrain, excellent towing capacity, wide trim variety, standard safety tech across the range
cons: Cramped third row, limited cargo space with all seats in use, expensive compared to some rivals
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota Sequoia is a bold, hybrid-powered alternative in the full-size SUV space—delivering big power and strong efficiency, but asking buyers to accept compromises in third-row comfort and cargo practicality.

car_name: 2026 Toyota Land Cruiser Review: A Modern Classic Rebuilt for Real-World Adventure
overview:
The 2026 Toyota Land Cruiser represents one of the most important shifts in the model’s long and storied history. Gone is the oversized, V-8-powered luxury bruiser; in its place is a leaner, more efficient, and more accessible Land Cruiser that still holds firmly onto the brand’s off-road DNA. By downsizing the body and introducing a hybrid powertrain as standard, Toyota has repositioned the Land Cruiser to better suit modern buyers who want genuine trail capability without sacrificing daily usability.

Sharing its rugged architecture with the Lexus GX, the new Land Cruiser adopts a body-on-frame platform, true four-wheel drive, and mechanical off-road hardware that many rivals have abandoned. At the same time, its smaller footprint, improved fuel efficiency, and quieter road manners make it far easier to live with day-to-day. While the loss of a third row and V-8 power may disappoint traditionalists, the new Land Cruiser feels more focused, more efficient, and arguably more authentic than before.
pricing:
Toyota keeps the 2026 Land Cruiser lineup intentionally simple, offering two clearly differentiated trims:

Land Cruiser 1958 – $59,095
This entry-level trim pays homage to the original Land Cruiser with round LED headlights and a deliberately utilitarian aesthetic. Standard equipment includes heated front seats, a heated steering wheel, cloth upholstery, skid plates, a locking center differential, crawl control, and an 8.0-inch infotainment screen. While mechanically identical to the higher trim, some interior materials feel basic, especially at this price point.

Land Cruiser – $63,940 (Recommended)
The standard Land Cruiser trim is the better all-around choice. It adds ventilated front seats, improved interior finishes, a 12.3-inch touchscreen, a 10-speaker premium audio system, and wider all-terrain tires for improved trail grip. These upgrades significantly enhance comfort and justify the price increase.

Best Buy Verdict: The higher Land Cruiser trim delivers the best balance of ruggedness and refinement, making it the smarter long-term ownership choice.
drivetrain:
Every 2026 Land Cruiser is powered by a 2.4-liter turbocharged four-cylinder hybrid system, producing a combined 326 horsepower. The setup pairs the gas engine with dual electric motors and sends power through an 8-speed automatic transmission to a full-time four-wheel-drive system.

Off-road hardware includes low-range gearing, a locking center differential, crawl control, and hill-descent assist—features that confirm this is no soft-roader. On pavement, the hybrid powertrain delivers strong low-end torque and smoother acceleration than expected, while remaining noticeably quieter than traditional off-road SUVs like the Wrangler or Bronco.

Acceleration is respectable rather than thrilling, with a 0–60 mph time of around 7.7 seconds, but the Land Cruiser’s strength lies in its torque delivery and composure rather than outright speed.

Towing Capability
Despite its reduced size, the Land Cruiser remains highly capable when it comes to hauling:
- Maximum towing capacity: 6,000 pounds
This comfortably exceeds most off-road-focused rivals and allows the Land Cruiser to double as a tow vehicle for boats, campers, or overlanding trailers.

Efficiency is one of the biggest improvements over previous generations:

EPA ratings:
- City: 22 mpg
- Highway: 25 mpg
- Combined: 23 mpg
In real-world highway testing, fuel economy dipped slightly to around 21 mpg, but that figure remains impressive for a body-on-frame SUV with full-time four-wheel drive.
interior:
The 2026 Land Cruiser is now strictly a two-row, five-seat SUV, a deliberate decision that prioritizes strength, weight reduction, and off-road performance. Front-seat comfort is excellent, with an upright driving position that provides strong outward visibility—especially useful on trails.

The 1958 trim leans rugged and minimal, while the higher trim introduces ventilated seats, optional leather upholstery, and a more premium overall ambiance. Rear-seat space is generous for adults, and cargo capacity is competitive, accommodating 17 carry-on suitcases behind the second row and 31 with the seats folded.
technology:
The 2026 Land Cruiser is now strictly a two-row, five-seat SUV, a deliberate decision that prioritizes strength, weight reduction, and off-road performance. Front-seat comfort is excellent, with an upright driving position that provides strong outward visibility—especially useful on trails.

The 1958 trim leans rugged and minimal, while the higher trim introduces ventilated seats, optional leather upholstery, and a more premium overall ambiance. Rear-seat space is generous for adults, and cargo capacity is competitive, accommodating 17 carry-on suitcases behind the second row and 31 with the seats folded.
safety:
The 2026 Land Cruiser comes standard with Toyota Safety Sense 3.0, providing a robust safety net without diluting its off-road focus.

Standard safety features include:
- Automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Adaptive cruise control with lane-centering capability
- Automatic high-beam headlights

Toyota’s safety systems are well-calibrated for highway driving and can be easily managed when venturing off-road.
warranty:
Toyota backs the Land Cruiser with solid ownership coverage and a strong hybrid warranty:
- Limited warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Hybrid system warranty: 10 years / 150,000 miles
- Complimentary maintenance: 2 years / 25,000 miles

The long hybrid coverage adds peace of mind for buyers new to electrified off-road vehicles.
pros: Authentic off-road hardware, strong hybrid torque, improved efficiency, refined ride quality, manageable size for trails
cons: No third-row seating, base trim interior feels underwhelming for the price, real-world fuel economy trails EPA estimates
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota Land Cruiser successfully redefines the nameplate for a new era—combining real off-road capability, improved efficiency, and everyday comfort into one of the most compelling adventure SUVs on sale today.

car_name: 2026 Toyota Highlander Review: Comfort-First Family SUV with Premium Pricing
overview:
The 2026 Toyota Highlander continues as a familiar, comfort-oriented midsize three-row SUV aimed squarely at families who value refinement, reliability, and ease of ownership over excitement. For 2026, Toyota simplifies the lineup by making all-wheel drive standard across all trims and discontinuing the base LE model, which also pushes the starting price higher than before.

Positioned below the larger and more modern Toyota Grand Highlander, the regular Highlander feels conservative but polished. Its strengths lie in a quiet cabin, smooth ride quality, and a long list of standard safety and convenience features. However, the cramped third row and rising prices make it a tougher sell in a segment filled with more spacious and visually striking competitors.
pricing:
The 2026 Toyota Highlander is offered in four well-equipped trims, all with standard AWD:

XLE – $47,540
The most accessible trim now starts at a premium price but includes heated front seats, leatherette upholstery, power-adjustable front seats, Toyota Safety Sense, and the option of seven- or eight-passenger seating.
XSE – $49,610
Adds a sportier exterior design with unique wheels, black accents, sport-tuned suspension, and interior trim upgrades, appealing to buyers who want a slightly more aggressive look without sacrificing comfort.
Limited – $51,995
Focuses on luxury with genuine leather upholstery, ventilated front seats, larger 12.3-inch infotainment screen, upgraded audio, and added driver-assistance features.
Platinum – $55,195
The flagship trim offers maximum comfort and tech, including a panoramic view monitor, head-up display, premium JBL audio system, digital rearview mirror, and exclusive interior materials.

Best Value Pick: The XLE remains the sweet spot for most buyers, delivering core comfort and safety features without pushing too close to luxury-brand pricing.
drivetrain:
The 2026 Highlander is powered exclusively by a 265-hp turbocharged 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine, paired with an 8-speed automatic transmission and standard all-wheel drive.

Acceleration is adequate rather than exciting, with a 0–60 mph time of around 7.2 seconds, which is competitive but not class-leading. The Highlander prioritizes smooth, predictable responses over sharp handling, making it well-suited for relaxed highway cruising and daily commuting. Ride quality remains one of its strongest traits, soaking up rough roads with ease and maintaining a calm demeanor even at higher speeds.

While official EPA ratings for the 2026 model are pending, fuel economy is expected to mirror the previous AWD Highlander:

Estimated EPA Ratings:
- City: ~21 mpg
- Highway: ~28 mpg
These figures are average for the segment and may feel underwhelming compared to hybrid alternatives, including Toyota’s own Highlander Hybrid.
interior:
Inside, the Highlander delivers a clean, well-organized cabin that emphasizes usability over flair. Materials quality is solid throughout, with higher trims offering noticeably more premium touches.

The first and second rows are spacious and supportive, making long journeys comfortable for adults. Buyers can choose between captain’s chairs or a bench seat in the second row, allowing for either seven- or eight-passenger configurations.

The third row, however, remains a weak point. Legroom is tight, and it’s best reserved for children or short trips. Cargo space is also modest for the class, offering around 23 cubic feet behind the third row and expanding to 57 cubic feet with the third row folded.
technology:
Technology is modern but not cutting-edge. Lower trims feature an 8.0-inch touchscreen, while higher trims upgrade to a 12.3-inch display with sharper graphics and more functionality.
- Standard features include:
- Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
- Bluetooth connectivity
- Wireless charging pad
Upper trims add navigation, a premium 11-speaker JBL sound system, and a head-up display on the Platinum, enhancing the overall driving experience.
safety:
Safety remains a major highlight for the 2026 Highlander, with Toyota equipping every trim with an extensive suite of driver-assistance technologies.
- Standard Safety Features include:
- Automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Adaptive cruise control with lane-centering
- Lane-keeping assist and lane-departure warning
- Blind-spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert
- Traffic-sign recognition and automatic high beams

Available on higher trims:
- 360-degree surround-view camera
- Front and rear parking sensors

The Highlander is expected to continue earning strong safety scores from NHTSA and IIHS, reinforcing its family-friendly appeal.
warranty:
Toyota’s warranty coverage is competitive and backed by strong reliability credentials.

Warranty Coverage:
- Limited warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Complimentary maintenance: 2 years / 25,000 miles

While not class-leading, the included free maintenance adds tangible value during early ownership.
pros: Comfortable ride, quiet and well-built interior, strong safety tech as standard, proven Toyota reliability
cons: Cramped third row, conservative design, pricier than the larger Grand Highlander
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota Highlander is a safe, comfortable, and dependable family SUV, but with rising prices and limited third-row space, it makes the most sense for buyers who prioritize refinement and reliability over size, style, or driving excitement.

car_name: 2026 Toyota bZ Review: Improved Range, Stronger Performance, and a Fresh Start for Toyota’s Electric SUV
overview:
For 2026, Toyota gives its compact electric SUV a much-needed reset—starting with the name. The awkward bZ4X badge is gone, replaced simply by Toyota bZ, and the changes extend far beyond branding. With more power, longer range, faster charging, and a redesigned interior, the 2026 Toyota bZ finally feels competitive in the rapidly evolving electric SUV segment.

Toyota has significantly upgraded the bZ’s electric powertrain, addressing one of the biggest criticisms of the outgoing model. Front-wheel-drive versions now offer noticeably more power, while all-wheel-drive models gain a substantial boost that transforms straight-line performance. Charging capability also takes a big step forward, thanks to the switch to NACS (Tesla-style) charging, unlocking access to Tesla’s extensive Supercharger network.

While it still prioritizes comfort and efficiency over outright sportiness, the 2026 bZ is now a more complete and confidence-inspiring EV—one that better reflects Toyota’s reputation for engineering polish and long-term dependability.
pricing:
The 2026 Toyota bZ remains competitively priced among electric compact SUVs, undercutting several rivals while offering meaningful upgrades.

- XLE (FWD/AWD) – $36,350
- XLE Plus (FWD/AWD) – $39,350 (Recommended)
- Limited (FWD/AWD) – $44,750

The XLE Plus strikes the best balance of price, range, and features, offering the larger battery pack, stronger power output, and improved interior tech without venturing too close to premium-EV pricing. Buyers who prioritize performance may want to step up to AWD versions, which deliver a dramatic increase in horsepower and improved acceleration.
drivetrain:
Toyota has made major strides in performance for 2026. Depending on configuration, the bZ now offers three distinct output levels:

- FWD XLE: 168 hp
- FWD XLE Plus / Limited: 221 hp
- AWD XLE / Limited: 338 hp

The all-wheel-drive bZ is the standout here. With dual motors and 338 horsepower, it finally delivers the urgency expected in this segment and is estimated to reach 0–60 mph in around 4.8 seconds, placing it firmly among quicker compact electric SUVs. Front-wheel-drive models are more relaxed, with 0–60 mph times estimated at just over 7 seconds, but still feel smoother and more responsive than before.

Ride quality remains a strength. The bZ prioritizes comfort with a composed suspension setup that handles broken pavement well, while steering is light and predictable. It’s not a performance EV, but it’s now far more engaging than the previous iteration.

Range and charging improvements are among the bZ’s most important upgrades.

Battery Packs:
- 57.7 kWh (FWD XLE)
- 74.7 kWh (all other trims)
Estimated Driving Range:
- FWD XLE: ~236 miles
- FWD XLE Plus: up to 314 miles
- AWD XLE: ~288 miles
- AWD Limited: ~278 miles

Toyota claims overall range is up by as much as 25 percent compared to the previous model year. Just as important, the bZ now features a NACS charging port, allowing access to Tesla Superchargers—significantly improving charging convenience for North American buyers.

On a DC fast charger, Toyota says the bZ can charge from 10 to 80 percent in about 30 minutes, aided by a new battery preconditioning system. AC charging is also faster thanks to an upgraded 11-kW onboard charger, making overnight home charging more efficient.

Official EPA MPGe ratings for the 2026 bZ are not yet available, but Toyota estimates efficiency figures similar to or slightly improved over the outgoing model.
- Estimated Combined Efficiency: ~93–115 MPGe (depending on trim and drivetrain)
Real-world testing is expected to confirm competitive efficiency, especially for front-wheel-drive versions focused on maximizing range.
interior:
Inside, the 2026 bZ benefits from a redesigned dashboard that improves visibility and usability. The layout feels more conventional and user-friendly than before, while still maintaining a modern, minimalist EV aesthetic.

Key interior highlights include:
- 14.0-inch central touchscreen
- Digital gauge cluster with improved sightlines
- Dual wireless smartphone charging pads
- Open center-console storage (though still no glovebox)

Passenger space is generous, especially up front, giving the cabin an airy feel. Cargo capacity remains unchanged at 26–28 cubic feet depending on configuration—adequate for daily use, though smaller than the RAV4 and some key rivals. There’s also no front trunk (frunk), which slightly limits storage flexibility.
technology:
Technology is one of the bZ’s strongest areas. The large 14.0-inch infotainment display runs Toyota’s latest software and supports wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as standard. Controls are a mix of touch-sensitive and physical buttons, helping reduce driver distraction.

Audio options include a standard six-speaker system and an available nine-speaker premium setup, while multiple USB ports and wireless chargers cater to modern connectivity needs.
safety:
Toyota equips every 2026 bZ with a comprehensive safety suite as standard. Key features include:
- Automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Adaptive cruise control

Higher trims add advanced driver-assistance technologies such as lane-change assist and Traffic Jam Assist, which allows hands-free driving in limited, low-speed conditions. The bZ is expected to maintain strong crash-test ratings from both NHTSA and IIHS, consistent with Toyota’s safety reputation.
warranty:
Toyota offers solid, confidence-inspiring coverage for the bZ, particularly for EV-specific components.
- Limited Warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Electric Components Warranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 2 years / 25,000 miles

The inclusion of complimentary maintenance gives the bZ an edge over many EV competitors, helping to reduce early ownership costs.
pros: Strong performance in AWD form, significantly improved range and charging, access to Tesla Superchargers, comfortable ride, generous standard safety features
cons: Cargo space trails some rivals, no frunk, base FWD model still feels underpowered
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota bZ finally delivers on its promise, pairing Toyota reliability with real-world EV performance, competitive range, and vastly improved charging—making it a smart, well-rounded electric SUV choice for everyday buyers.

car_name: 2026 Toyota Corolla Cross Review: Sensible, Spacious, and Efficient for Everyday SUV Buyers
overview:
The 2026 Toyota Corolla Cross is exactly what its name suggests: a Corolla reimagined for an SUV-focused world. Sitting below the RAV4 in Toyota’s lineup, the Corolla Cross targets buyers who value affordability, fuel efficiency, and long-term reliability, but want the higher seating position and added cargo flexibility of a compact SUV. While it may not excite enthusiasts, the Corolla Cross succeeds by being easy to live with, practical, and reassuringly familiar.

Styling is clean and inoffensive rather than bold, which aligns with the Corolla brand’s no-nonsense appeal. For 2026, Toyota gives the Cross a slightly tougher look with a redesigned grille and subtle exterior tweaks, helping it feel a bit more contemporary. Inside, the cabin mirrors the regular Corolla’s layout, prioritizing usability and durability over flair. Importantly, the Corolla Cross delivers more interior and cargo space than its sedan and hatchback siblings, making it a logical upgrade for small families or urban buyers who need flexibility without stepping up to a larger SUV.

The standard gasoline-powered Corolla Cross focuses on efficiency and comfort rather than speed. Acceleration is modest at best, but the payoff comes in the form of smooth ride quality, predictable handling, and low ownership costs. Buyers seeking stronger performance can opt for the Corolla Cross Hybrid, reviewed separately, but for many, the standard model’s relaxed demeanor will be more than sufficient for daily duties.
pricing:
The 2026 Toyota Corolla Cross remains competitively priced in the subcompact SUV segment, starting at $26,485 and topping out at $31,410.

- L – $26,485
- LE – $28,815
- XLE – $31,410 (Recommended)

While the L and LE trims cover the basics, the XLE is the most compelling choice. It adds features that many SUV buyers now expect, including heated front seats, a 10-way power-adjustable driver’s seat, dual-zone automatic climate control, blind-spot monitoring, front and rear parking sensors, and stylish 18-inch alloy wheels. For buyers planning to keep the vehicle long-term, the XLE’s added comfort and safety features justify the higher upfront cost.
drivetrain:
The standard Corolla Cross is powered by a 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine producing 169 horsepower and 150 lb-ft of torque, paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT). Front-wheel drive comes standard, while all-wheel drive is available for buyers who want extra confidence in poor weather.

In everyday driving, the powertrain feels adequate but unenthusiastic. Acceleration is slow, especially when merging onto highways or passing at speed, and the engine can sound coarse when pushed hard. In testing, an all-wheel-drive Corolla Cross reached 0–60 mph in about 9.2 seconds, which places it near the back of the segment. That said, most competitors are not significantly quicker, and the Corolla Cross prioritizes smoothness and efficiency over outright pace.

Where the Corolla Cross shines is ride comfort. The suspension is tuned to absorb bumps and rough pavement well, making it a comfortable companion for commuting and longer trips. Steering is light and predictable, reinforcing the vehicle’s easygoing, stress-free character.

Fuel efficiency is one of the Corolla Cross’s strongest selling points. While official EPA ratings for 2026 are not yet published, Toyota is expected to carry over figures similar to the 2025 model.

- Estimated EPA (FWD): 31 mpg city / 33 mpg highway / 32 mpg combined
- Estimated EPA (AWD): Approximately 2 mpg lower across the board
In real-world testing, an all-wheel-drive Corolla Cross returned around 30 mpg at a steady 75 mph, which is respectable for a gasoline-powered subcompact SUV. Buyers prioritizing maximum efficiency may want to consider the hybrid version, but the standard Corolla Cross still delivers solid fuel economy for its class.
interior:
Inside, the Corolla Cross feels immediately familiar to anyone who has spent time in a modern Corolla. Materials are durable rather than luxurious, and the design emphasizes simplicity and ergonomics. Lower trims are fairly basic, but the XLE adds faux-leather upholstery, heated front seats, and upgraded trim details, giving the cabin a more upscale feel.

Rear-seat space is slightly improved compared with the Corolla hatchback and roughly on par with the sedan, making it usable for adults on shorter trips. The real advantage comes in cargo capacity. With 24 cubic feet of space behind the rear seats, the Corolla Cross offers significantly more room than the Corolla sedan or hatchback. Folding the rear seats expands the load area further, making it well suited for groceries, luggage, or weekend gear.
technology:
Technology is straightforward and user-friendly. An 8.0-inch touchscreen with Toyota’s latest infotainment software is standard across the lineup, while the XLE gains a larger 10.5-inch display. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto come standard, along with a six-speaker audio system.

For 2026, Toyota improves everyday usability by making wireless charging and rear-seat USB-C ports standard on LE and XLE trims. Buyers who value audio quality can opt for a JBL premium sound system with a subwoofer on higher trims. Overall, the tech experience is modern enough without feeling overwhelming.
safety:
Toyota equips every 2026 Corolla Cross with an impressive suite of standard safety and driver-assistance features under its Toyota Safety Sense package. This includes automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, lane-departure warning with steering assist, adaptive cruise control, road-sign assist, and automatic high beams.

These systems work seamlessly in daily driving and add meaningful confidence, particularly for highway use and urban traffic. Higher trims enhance safety further with features such as blind-spot monitoring, rear cross-traffic alert, and parking sensors. The Corolla Cross also earns solid crash-test ratings from both the NHTSA and IIHS, reinforcing Toyota’s reputation for safety.
warranty:
Warranty coverage for the Corolla Cross is competitive, though not class-leading. Toyota provides a three-year/36,000-mile limited warranty and a five-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty, which matches most mainstream rivals.

Where Toyota stands out is maintenance. The Corolla Cross includes two years or 25,000 miles of complimentary scheduled maintenance, covering routine services such as oil changes and inspections. For buyers focused on predictable ownership costs, this added coverage is a meaningful advantage, even if rivals like Hyundai and Kia offer longer warranty terms overall.
pros: Excellent fuel efficiency, generous cargo space for the class, strong standard safety features, comfortable ride, Toyota reliability
cons: Sluggish acceleration, engine sounds strained under load, interior feels basic in lower trims
mn_take: The 2026 Toyota Corolla Cross isn’t exciting, but it nails the fundamentals with efficiency, space, safety, and long-term dependability—making it a smart, sensible choice for buyers who value practicality above all else.

car_name: 2026 Honda Accord Review: A Benchmark Midsize Sedan That Still Sets the Standard
overview:
The 2026 Honda Accord continues to define what a modern midsize sedan should be, earning yet another place on Car and Driver’s 10Best Cars list and reinforcing its reputation as a segment leader. In an era where sedans are increasingly overshadowed by SUVs, the Accord stands tall by offering a rare combination of engaging driving dynamics, excellent efficiency, generous space, and everyday usability.

One of the Accord’s greatest strengths is how polished it feels on the road. Steering response is accurate, body control is well managed, and the ride remains comfortable even on longer journeys. Honda has also paid close attention to practicality: the interior is spacious for both rows of passengers, the materials feel upscale for the class, and the layout prioritizes ease of use rather than flashy gimmicks. Controls for infotainment and climate are logical and intuitive, which makes daily driving effortless.

For 2026, Honda continues to offer two powertrains, but the spotlight clearly shines on the hybrid setup, which is available on all but the two base trims. It delivers stronger performance than the standard turbo engine while also posting impressive fuel-economy figures that rival smaller compact cars. While longtime fans may miss the older turbo engine paired with a manual gearbox, the current Accord remains refined, confident, and rewarding enough to stay at the top of the midsize-sedan class.
pricing:
The 2026 Honda Accord is competitively priced, starting at $29,590 and extending to $40,690 for the fully loaded hybrid model.

- LX – $29,590
- SE – $31,890
- Sport Hybrid – $34,990 (Recommended)
- EX-L Hybrid – $36,290
- Sport-L Hybrid – $36,690
- Touring Hybrid – $40,690

Among these, the Sport Hybrid stands out as the sweet spot. It’s the most affordable way to access Honda’s excellent hybrid powertrain while also adding features such as a larger infotainment screen, heated front seats, a power sunroof, and upgraded interior finishes. Buyers looking for a more premium, near-luxury experience will find the Touring Hybrid appealing thanks to its Bose audio system, head-up display, and additional comfort features.
drivetrain:
Honda offers two front-wheel-drive powertrains for the Accord, both paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT).

The LX and SE trims are powered by a 1.5-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine producing 192 horsepower. While not particularly quick, this engine delivers smooth, predictable acceleration and feels well suited to commuting and highway driving.

Most of the lineup uses Honda’s highly refined hybrid system, which combines a 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine with two electric motors for a total of 204 horsepower. This setup provides stronger low-end torque, quicker throttle response, and a more relaxed driving character overall. In testing, the hybrid Accord reaches 0–60 mph in 6.7 seconds, compared with 7.3 seconds for the non-hybrid model.

Beyond straight-line numbers, the Accord continues to impress with its balance. Steering is light yet precise, the suspension absorbs road imperfections gracefully, and the chassis feels stable and composed even at higher speeds. It’s not a sports sedan, but it remains one of the most satisfying family sedans to drive.

Efficiency is a major selling point, particularly for the hybrid trims.

- Non-hybrid (estimated): 29 mpg city / 37 mpg highway
- Hybrid (estimated): up to 51 mpg city / 44 mpg highway

In real-world highway testing, a non-hybrid Accord returned around 40 mpg, while the hybrid achieved roughly 39 mpg at a steady 75 mph. These numbers put the Accord Hybrid among the most fuel-efficient midsize sedans on the market, even when compared with rivals like the Toyota Camry.
interior:
The Accord’s interior strikes a balance between modern design and everyday usability. A full-width honeycomb trim element conceals the air vents and gives the dashboard a clean, cohesive look that’s shared with other recent Honda models.

Up front, the seats are supportive and comfortable for long drives, with ample headroom and legroom. In the rear, passengers benefit from generous legroom and knee clearance, making the Accord an excellent choice for families or frequent rear-seat occupants. Headroom is slightly reduced due to the sloping roofline, but overall comfort remains strong.

Cargo capacity is another highlight. The Accord’s 16.7-cubic-foot trunk easily accommodates seven carry-on suitcases, expanding to around 20 suitcases with the rear seats folded—competitive even by class-leading standards.
technology:
Technology in the 2026 Accord is modern, responsive, and thoughtfully integrated.

Standard equipment includes a 9.0-inch touchscreen, while higher trims upgrade to a 12.3-inch display. All models feature a 10.2-inch digital instrument cluster, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and a wireless charging pad.

Audio options range from a basic four-speaker system in the LX to an excellent 12-speaker Bose premium system in the Touring Hybrid. Higher trims also add a head-up display, reinforcing the Accord’s move toward near-luxury territory.
safety:
Safety remains one of the Accord’s strongest pillars, with Honda equipping every model with its comprehensive Honda Sensing suite as standard.

Key standard features include automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, lane-keeping assist, lane-departure warning, adaptive cruise control, traffic-sign recognition, and forward-collision warning. These systems work smoothly in real-world driving and add a layer of confidence during highway cruising and city commutes alike.

Higher trims further enhance safety with features such as front and rear parking sensors and a multi-angle rearview camera. The Accord also earns strong crash-test ratings from both the NHTSA and the IIHS, reinforcing its reputation as one of the safest choices in the midsize-sedan segment.
warranty:
Honda’s warranty coverage is competitive, though not class-leading, but the inclusion of complimentary maintenance adds value.

The Accord comes with a three-year/36,000-mile limited warranty and a five-year/60,000-mile powertrain warranty, which aligns with most mainstream rivals. Hybrid models benefit from additional coverage for key electrified components, providing extra peace of mind for long-term ownership.

Notably, Honda includes one year or 12,000 miles of complimentary scheduled maintenance, covering basic services such as oil changes and inspections. While brands like Hyundai offer longer warranties overall, Honda’s reputation for reliability helps offset the shorter coverage period.
pros: Refined and engaging driving experience, excellent hybrid efficiency, spacious interior, intuitive technology, strong safety credentials
cons: No all-wheel drive option, base engine feels underpowered, warranty coverage trails some competitors
mn_take: The 2026 Honda Accord, especially in hybrid form, remains the benchmark midsize sedan by combining efficiency, comfort, safety, and driving enjoyment in a way that few rivals consistently manage.

car_name: 2026 Honda Civic & Civic Hybrid Review: Still the Benchmark in the Compact Sedan Segment
overview:
The 2026 Honda Civic and Civic Hybrid continue to set the gold standard in the compact car segment by blending efficiency, everyday usability, and an engaging driving experience into a well-rounded package. Positioned as one of the most sensible yet desirable choices in its class, the Civic balances affordability with refinement in a way few rivals can match.

Honda offers two distinct powertrains to suit different buyers. The standard 2.0-liter naturally aspirated four-cylinder produces 150 horsepower, delivering smooth and predictable performance ideal for daily commuting. For buyers seeking stronger acceleration and class-leading efficiency, the Civic Hybrid’s 200-horsepower setup combines a gasoline engine with dual electric motors, resulting in quicker responses and noticeably better fuel economy without sacrificing comfort.

Both sedan and hatchback body styles return for 2026, offering flexibility for different lifestyles. The sedan emphasizes a traditional, clean profile, while the hatchback provides added cargo versatility without compromising rear-seat space. Inside, the Civic offers a surprisingly roomy cabin, intuitive controls, and thoughtful storage solutions throughout. Standard driver-assistance features further strengthen its appeal, and the Civic’s placement on the 2026 10Best Cars list marks its 12th appearance, underscoring its long-standing excellence.
pricing:
The 2026 Honda Civic lineup starts at $25,890 and climbs to $34,790, depending on configuration and equipment.
- LX Sedan – $25,890
- Sport Sedan – $27,890
- Sport Hatchback – $29,090
- Sport Hybrid Sedan – $30,590
- Sport Hybrid Hatchback – $31,790 (Recommended)
- Sport Touring Hybrid Sedan – $33,590
- Sport Touring Hybrid Hatchback – $34,790

The Sport Hybrid trims represent the sweet spot, combining strong performance, excellent fuel efficiency, and a generous feature list. The Sport Touring Hybrid adds premium conveniences such as a larger touchscreen, wireless smartphone connectivity, and upgraded interior materials for buyers seeking a near-luxury feel in a compact package.
drivetrain:
The standard Civic’s 150-hp 2.0-liter engine is paired with a CVT and front-wheel drive. While outright acceleration is modest, the engine is smooth and reliable, and the car’s well-tuned suspension and light steering make it easy to maneuver in urban environments and stable at highway speeds.

The Civic Hybrid elevates the driving experience significantly. Its 200-hp combined output delivers brisk acceleration and instant torque, making it feel far more responsive than the non-hybrid version. In testing, the hybrid sedan achieved 0–60 mph in just 6.2 seconds, outperforming many competitors and even approaching the performance of sportier variants like the Civic Si. The non-hybrid, by comparison, takes 8.9 seconds to reach 60 mph.

Ride quality remains composed across all trims, with the hybrid models offering especially smooth power delivery and reduced engine noise during low-speed driving.

Fuel efficiency is a key strength of the Civic lineup, particularly in hybrid form.
- Hybrid models deliver up to 50 mpg city and 47 mpg highway, with real-world highway testing confirming 47 mpg at 75 mph.
- Non-hybrid models remain competitive, returning approximately 32 mpg city and 41 mpg highway.

This combination of strong performance and low fuel consumption makes the Civic Hybrid one of the most efficient non-plug-in vehicles in its class.
interior:
The Civic’s interior emphasizes simplicity, ergonomics, and space efficiency. Both body styles seat five passengers, with generous front-seat legroom and a rear bench capable of comfortably accommodating two adults. Materials quality is solid throughout, improving further in higher trims with soft-touch surfaces and available leather upholstery.

Front seats provide good all-day comfort, though the absence of adjustable lumbar support is noticeable on longer drives. Storage options are plentiful, with large door pockets, a deep center console, and intelligently placed cupholders.

Cargo capacity is impressive for a compact car. The sedan fits six carry-on suitcases in the trunk, while the hatchback offers even more versatility, accommodating up to 17 carry-ons with the rear seats folded flat.
technology:
A 7.0-inch touchscreen comes standard, while higher trims feature a 9.0-inch infotainment display with faster response times and wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Select hybrid trims also include a 10.2-inch fully digital instrument cluster, adding a more modern, upscale touch.

Optional features include built-in navigation, a wireless charging pad, and a 12-speaker Bose premium audio system, which delivers strong clarity and bass. While the base screen feels small compared to newer competitors, overall usability remains excellent.
safety:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Lane-keeping assist and lane-departure warning
- Adaptive cruise control with low-speed follow capability
- Five-star overall safety rating from NHTSA
- Available blind-spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert
- Optional front and rear parking sensors on higher trims
warranty:
- Limited vehicle warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Hybrid battery and component warranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles
- Complimentary scheduled maintenance: 1 year / 12,000 miles
pros: Excellent fuel efficiency, refined ride quality, strong hybrid performance, spacious and practical interior
cons: Base infotainment screen feels undersized, no manual option on standard trims, warranty coverage is average for the segment
mn_take: The 2026 Honda Civic—especially in hybrid form—remains one of the most complete compact cars on sale, delivering a rare blend of efficiency, performance, comfort, and long-term value that continues to make it a benchmark in its class.

car_name: 2026 Honda Prelude Review: Hybrid Power, Pricing, Performance, Features & Verdict
overview:
The 2026 Honda Prelude marks the return of one of Honda’s most iconic nameplates, reimagined for a new era defined by electrification and efficiency. Instead of a high-revving naturally aspirated engine and a manual gearbox—hallmarks of past Preludes—the new model embraces a 200-horsepower hybrid powertrain derived from the modern Civic lineup.
