While purists may initially balk at the absence of a manual transmission, Honda’s intent is clear: the Prelude is positioned as a stylish, accessible, and efficient sport coupe rather than a hardcore performance machine.

Built on the same fundamental architecture as the Civic and closely related to the sporty Honda Civic Si, the Prelude benefits from meaningful chassis and suspension upgrades. Honda has also borrowed components from the range-topping Honda Civic Type R, raising expectations for handling precision and driver engagement. The result is a sleek two-door hybrid coupe with a liftback design, modest rear seating, and a clear focus on everyday usability blended with sporty character.

What’s New for 2026

Everything. The Prelude is an all-new addition to Honda’s current lineup, reviving a name last seen decades ago. While the badge carries significant heritage from the 1980s and 1990s, the 2026 model represents a complete reset—introducing a hybrid-only drivetrain, modern digital tech, and a single, fully loaded trim strategy. In effect, it also fills the gap left by the discontinued Civic Coupe.
pricing:
Honda is keeping things simple with the Prelude. There is one fully loaded trim, and pricing reflects its niche positioning as a premium compact sport coupe.
- Prelude (single trim): $43,195

With no additional trims or factory options beyond accessories and exterior colors, buyers get a comprehensive standard feature set without navigating complex packages.
drivetrain:
Under the hood, the 2026 Prelude uses a 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine paired with an electric motor, producing a combined 200 horsepower. Power is sent to the front wheels through a CVT, but Honda has introduced a new S+ Shift system that uses paddle shifters, simulated gear steps, and faux rev-matching to mimic the feel of a traditional automatic or manual transmission.

While this setup lacks the raw engagement of older Preludes, it delivers smooth, linear acceleration and competitive performance for the segment. Honda estimates a 0–60 mph time of around 6.0 seconds, placing it close to enthusiast favorites like the Mazda MX-5 Miata and Toyota GR86, though those rivals remain lighter and more performance-focused.

Early prototype drives suggest the Prelude excels in cornering stability and steering balance, benefiting from its widened track, retuned suspension, and lower center of gravity compared to the Civic Hybrid. It may not be the fastest, but it promises to be confidence-inspiring and engaging on twisty roads.

Official EPA ratings have not yet been released, but expectations are high. Given its shared hardware with the Civic Hybrid, the Prelude is projected to return approximately:
~52 mpg city
~49 mpg highway

If these figures hold, the Prelude would be one of the most fuel-efficient sport-oriented coupes on the market, blending performance aesthetics with commuter-friendly running costs.
interior:
Inside, the Prelude closely mirrors the Civic’s modern, driver-focused cabin but adds unique trim details to elevate its sporty appeal. The front seats are heated as standard and feature contrast stitching, while material quality is expected to be solid rather than luxurious.

The rear seat is present but compact, best suited for short trips or occasional use. Thanks to its liftback hatch design, cargo practicality is better than most coupes, with folding rear seats allowing the Prelude to carry more than just weekend bags.

Overall, the interior prioritizes ergonomics, visibility, and ease of use over extravagance—very much in line with Honda’s design philosophy.
technology:
The Prelude comes well equipped with modern tech, all standard due to its single-trim strategy:
- 9.0-inch touchscreen infotainment system
- 10.2-inch digital instrument cluster
- Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
- Built-in Google-based software
- 8-speaker Bose premium audio system

The interface is familiar to Civic owners, offering quick responses, clean graphics, and strong voice-command functionality.
safety:
With only one trim level, the Prelude includes Honda’s full safety suite as standard, ensuring no compromises in this area. Key features include:
- Adaptive cruise control
- Lane-keeping assist
- Automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Road-departure mitigation

Crash-test ratings from NHTSA and IIHS are pending, but expectations are strong given Honda’s track record and the Prelude’s shared platform with highly rated Civic models.
warranty:
The Prelude follows Honda’s standard warranty structure, which is competitive but not class-leading:
- Limited warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Hybrid system warranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles
- Complimentary maintenance: 1 year / 12,000 miles

While shorter than some rivals, Honda’s reliability reputation helps offset the modest coverage terms.
pros: Iconic nameplate revival, excellent fuel efficiency, sharp handling, modern tech, distinctive coupe-hatch design.
cons: No manual transmission, modest power output for enthusiasts, limited rear-seat space.
mn_take: The 2026 Honda Prelude isn’t a throwback sports car—it’s a forward-looking hybrid coupe that blends style, efficiency, and everyday usability, making it an appealing choice for drivers who want something sporty without sacrificing practicality or fuel economy.

car_name: 2026 Honda CR-V Hybrid Review: Price, Mileage, Performance, Safety & Warranty
overview:
The 2026 Honda CR-V Hybrid is an exceptionally versatile compact SUV that pairs Honda’s well-loved CR-V practicality with a fuel-sipping, more powerful electrified powertrain. Where the non-hybrid CR-V leans on conventional efficiency and refinement, the hybrid version elevates the formula with better fuel economy, quicker acceleration in many conditions, and the versatility of front- or all-wheel drive.

Front-wheel drive models are EPA-rated at 40 mpg combined, while AWD variants post a still impressive 37 mpg combined—figures that place the CR-V Hybrid among the most efficient vehicles in its class. The driving experience is smooth and composed; it won’t thrill like a sport compact, but it rewards with quiet cruising, predictable handling, and confidence-inspiring manners in a variety of road conditions.

Inside, the CR-V Hybrid strikes a balance between comfort and user-friendly ergonomics. Cabin space remains generous for both passengers and cargo, with ample headroom, legroom, and a thoughtful layout of controls and storage. The overall package leans into practicality and long-term usability, supported by the latest infotainment and safety tech.

For the 2026 model year, the CR-V Hybrid adds a new TrailSport trim—Honda’s more rugged-looking variant with distinctive 18-inch wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires, a unique body design including faux skid plates, and TrailSport logos embroidered into headrests and floor mats.
- Across the lineup, Honda also updates the tech suite with these enhancements:
- Standard 9.0-inch touchscreen with wireless connectivity
- Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto standard on all trims
- Wireless phone charging included
- Enhanced AWD traction management that actively distributes torque at low speeds (below 9 mph) for better grip

A few small exterior styling tweaks and larger alloy wheels on the Sport Touring help differentiate trims visually, completing a modest but meaningful set of 2026 changes.
pricing:
The 2026 Honda CR-V Hybrid’s pricing is competitive, starting at $37,080 and stretching to $44,000 for the top-tier Sport Touring trim with all the bells and whistles.
- Sport – $37,080
- Sport-L – $40,175 (Recommended)
- TrailSport – $40,250
- Sport Touring – $44,000

If you don’t need all-weather capability right away, the front-wheel-drive Sport-L is the best blend of features and value, with a larger digital gauge cluster and available upgraded audio without the price jump into Sport Touring. For buyers who want a slightly more adventurous look and mild off-road capability, the TrailSport adds unique exterior trim and traction-oriented features—albeit with a slight efficiency penalty.
drivetrain:
Under the hood is a 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine paired with two electric motors, delivering 204 total horsepower—14 hp more than the non-hybrid CR-V. The integration between electric and gasoline propulsion is seamless; transitions are nearly imperceptible, and the overall experience is quieter than the conventional CR-V.

While the CR-V Hybrid isn’t a performance SUV, its output is well suited for daily driving and highway merging. The Sport Touring achieved 0–60 mph in about 7.1 seconds in testing, quicker than many naturally aspirated compact SUVs, while the TrailSport came in around 7.3 seconds—still brisk for a family SUV with all-terrain tires.

The addition of an enhanced AWD traction-management system improves grip and confidence in low-traction conditions by actively splitting torque between the axles at low speeds. Comfort is prioritized over handling drama, but the ride remains composed and predictable throughout a wide range of road surfaces.

Efficiency is a hallmark of the CR-V Hybrid:

EPA Estimated Fuel Economy
- Sport (FWD): 43 mpg city / 36 mpg highway / 40 mpg combined
- AWD models: 40 mpg city / 34 mpg highway / 37 mpg combined
- TrailSport: 38 mpg city / 33 mpg highway / 35 mpg combined

Real-World Testing
- On a 75-mph highway route, an AWD Sport Touring Hybrid returned 35 mpg, slightly above its EPA highway estimate and reflective of real-world efficiency.

These numbers position the CR-V Hybrid as a strong choice for both daily commuting and longer road trips, with savings that quickly add up compared to traditional gasoline models.
interior:
The CR-V Hybrid’s cabin is spacious and well organized. Design cues emphasize passenger comfort and practicality, with logically placed controls and plenty of storage solutions throughout the cabin. Higher trims introduce soft-touch materials, contrast stitching, and an appealing honeycomb-textured dashboard panel that adds visual interest without distraction.

Passenger Comfort
- Generous second-row legroom that accommodates adults comfortably
- Supportive front seats with available heating and ventilation
- Large windows and thoughtfully positioned HVAC vents for consistent airflow

Cargo Space
- Holds 11 carry-on suitcases behind the rear seats
- Expands to 29 carry-on suitcases with the rear seats folded flat, offering excellent usability for weekend gear or luggage
technology:
Honda’s updated tech package enhances usability across the lineup:
- Standard 9.0-inch touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto
- Wireless phone charging on all trims
- 10.2-inch digital instrument cluster on Sport-L and higher trims
- Sport Touring includes built-in Google navigation and a premium Bose audio system

The system’s responsiveness and clarity have improved over previous years, making the tech experience feel modern and intuitive.
safety:
The 2026 Honda CR-V Hybrid delivers a comprehensive set of standard and available safety technologies, contributing to its strong safety profile:

Standard Safety Tech
- Automated emergency braking with forward-collision warning
- Lane-keeping assist
- Blind-spot monitoring
- Adaptive cruise control with traffic-jam assist
- Rear cross-traffic alert

Available Safety Enhancements
- Front and rear parking sensors (Sport-L and Touring)
- Enhanced AWD traction-management system for low-speed grip
- Lane-centering assist

The CR-V Hybrid maintains a 5-star overall rating from NHTSA and earns top defense ratings in IIHS testing, affirming its ability to protect occupants in a variety of scenarios.
warranty:
Honda offers a competitive ownership package, though it’s more conservative than some rivals:
- Limited warranty: 3 years or 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles
- Complimentary scheduled maintenance: 1 year or 12,000 miles

While not class-leading, these coverage terms are solid and align with many competitors. The inclusion of complimentary maintenance for the first year adds value, especially compared with rivals that offer none.
pros: Excellent fuel economy, smooth and refined hybrid propulsion, spacious interior and cargo area, advanced safety tech.
cons: Conservative styling, non-sporty driving dynamics, warranty coverage is shorter than some rivals.
mn_take: The 2026 Honda CR-V Hybrid is the benchmark hybrid compact SUV, delivering a compelling mix of efficiency, comfort, space, and safety that makes it an easy recommendation for families and daily drivers alike.

car_name: 2026 Honda Prologue Price, Trims, Range, Features, Safety & Warranty – Full Review
overview:
Honda’s first mainstream electric SUV, the 2026 Prologue, takes a slightly unconventional route into the EV space. Developed alongside General Motors and sharing its underpinnings with the Chevrolet Blazer EV, the Prologue focuses more on comfort, space, and everyday usability than outright performance or cutting-edge tech theatrics.

From a design standpoint, it looks clean and modern without being flashy, aligning well with Honda’s conservative design philosophy. Inside, the cabin is spacious and practical, making the Prologue feel like a natural transition for buyers moving from a CR-V or Passport into an electric vehicle. While it lacks the trademark sporty edge Honda is known for, it compensates with a calm driving experience, competitive range figures, and an easy-to-live-with personality.
pricing:
The 2026 Honda Prologue is offered in three familiar trims, with prices reflecting its position in the mid-size electric SUV segment:
- EX – $48,895
- Touring (Recommended) – $53,195
- Elite – $59,395

The EX trim is well equipped for the price, but the Touring trim strikes the best balance by adding premium features without pushing the Prologue into luxury-brand pricing territory. The Elite trim focuses on maximum equipment and all-wheel drive, though it comes with a noticeable range penalty.
drivetrain:
The Prologue is available with two electric drivetrain configurations:
- Single-motor, front-wheel drive: 220 hp
- Dual-motor, all-wheel drive: 300 hp
Acceleration is adequate rather than thrilling. The AWD Elite model manages a 0–60 mph time of around 5.9 seconds, which is respectable for a family-oriented EV but falls short of sportier rivals like the Hyundai Ioniq 5 or Kia EV6. Ride quality is smooth and composed, prioritizing comfort over aggressive cornering, and the steering feels light but somewhat detached compared to traditional Hondas.

All Prologue variants use an 85.0-kWh battery pack sourced from GM.
- FWD EX & Touring: up to 308 miles (EPA-estimated)
- AWD EX & Touring: 294 miles
- Elite AWD: 283 miles

In real-world testing, the Elite AWD delivered around 240 miles, which is lower than its EPA estimate but still acceptable for daily use. DC fast charging peaks at 155 kW, allowing reasonably quick top-ups on long journeys. Honda also offers a home charging solution for convenient overnight charging.
interior:
The Prologue’s interior focuses on space and simplicity. While some GM-sourced switchgear is noticeable, Honda has toned down the design with muted colors and a clean dashboard layout.

Passenger space is a strong point. The long wheelbase translates into excellent rear-seat legroom, making the Prologue a comfortable option for families. Cargo capacity is also competitive, offering 25.2 cubic feet in FWD models and 23.7 cubic feet in AWD versions.
technology:
An 11.3-inch touchscreen dominates the dashboard and comes standard across all trims, paired with an 11.0-inch digital instrument cluster. Unlike its GM sibling, the Prologue includes wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, which is a major usability advantage over the Chevrolet Blazer EV.

Higher trims add a 12-speaker Bose audio system, head-up display (Elite only), wireless phone charging, and built-in Google-based navigation.
safety:
The 2026 Honda Prologue comes standard with Honda Sensing, delivering a comprehensive safety suite across all trims.
Standard safety highlights include:
- Automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Lane-keeping assist and lane-departure warning
- Adaptive cruise control with traffic-following capability
- Traffic sign recognition

Available safety upgrades include:
- Front and rear parking sensors
- 360-degree surround-view camera system (Elite)

The Prologue has earned a 5-star overall safety rating from NHTSA, reinforcing its family-friendly credentials.
warranty:
Honda offers solid but not class-leading coverage for the Prologue, aligned with most mainstream EV rivals.

Warranty coverage includes:
- Limited vehicle warranty: 3 years / 36,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- EV battery and electric components: 8 years / 100,000 miles
- Complimentary scheduled maintenance: 2 years / 24,000 miles

While not as generous as Hyundai’s coverage, it remains competitive within the segment.
pros: Spacious cabin, competitive driving range, wireless smartphone connectivity, comfortable ride.
cons: Lacks sporty character, visible GM switchgear, charging speed trails some rivals.
mn_take: The 2026 Honda Prologue is a sensible, comfortable, and easy-to-own electric SUV that prioritizes space and range over excitement—ideal for buyers seeking a familiar Honda experience in an EV form.

car_name: 2026 Hyundai Elantra Review: Price, Trims, Mileage, Performance, Safety & Features
overview:
The 2026 Hyundai Elantra continues to play the role of a well-rounded compact sedan that tries to satisfy a wide spectrum of buyers. At its core, the Elantra remains an affordable and practical four-door with generous interior space, user-friendly technology, and a broad powertrain lineup. While the standard gasoline model won’t excite keen drivers, it delivers solid everyday usability at a very approachable price point. Buyers seeking better efficiency can opt for the refined hybrid variant, while those wanting sharper performance have the turbocharged N Line to consider.

Despite its sharply creased exterior and coupe-like profile, the Elantra makes smart use of its footprint. The cabin feels noticeably roomy for a compact sedan, with ample legroom in both rows and a dashboard layout that keeps controls intuitive and within easy reach. Against rivals such as the Honda Civic, Toyota Prius, and Volkswagen Jetta, the Elantra stands out by offering one of the widest spreads of pricing, powertrains, and features in the segment.

Expert Tip: Enthusiasts with a higher budget should look at the 286-hp Elantra N, which is reviewed separately and remains the performance halo of the lineup.

Changes for 2026 are modest. Hyundai has streamlined the lineup by replacing the SEL Convenience with a new SEL Sport Premium trim, which bundles popular comfort and technology features into a more clearly defined mid-range option. Otherwise, the Elantra carries forward largely unchanged, which isn’t a bad thing given its competitive positioning.
pricing:
Pricing remains one of the Elantra’s biggest strengths, with a low entry point and logical step-ups across the range.

- SE – $23,870: Base model with solid standard safety tech and infotainment, aimed at budget-focused buyers.
- SEL Sport – $24,995: Adds sportier exterior cues and extra convenience features.
- SEL Sport Premium – $26,320 (Recommended): Introduces adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go, heated front seats, a split-folding rear seat, and a dual-screen setup, making it the best-balanced non-hybrid choice.
- Hybrid Blue – $26,695: Focuses on maximum fuel efficiency with fewer luxury add-ons.
- Limited – $28,420: Emphasizes comfort and tech with upgraded materials and features.
- Hybrid SEL Sport – $28,670: Combines hybrid efficiency with sportier styling.
- N Line – $30,645: Adds a turbo engine, sport suspension tuning, and visual upgrades.
- Hybrid Limited – $31,045: The most efficient and feature-rich Elantra in the lineup.
drivetrain:
Hyundai offers the Elantra with three distinct powertrain philosophies. The standard 2.0-liter naturally aspirated four-cylinder produces 147 hp and is paired with a CVT, prioritizing smoothness and economy over excitement. Performance is adequate for daily commuting, though ride composure and handling feel less polished when pushed.

The Elantra Hybrid pairs a 1.6-liter engine with an electric motor for a combined 139 hp, using a six-speed dual-clutch automatic rather than a CVT. This setup gives the hybrid a more natural driving feel than many competitors, with reduced engine droning and smooth low-speed response.

For drivers wanting punch, the Elantra N Line uses a 201-hp turbocharged 1.6-liter four-cylinder with a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission. It offers noticeably stronger acceleration, better steering feel, and more controlled body motions, making it the most engaging Elantra short of the full N model.

0–60 mph times:
- Non-hybrid: 8.1 seconds
- Hybrid: 8.4 seconds
- N Line (est.): ~6.5 seconds

Efficiency is a major Elantra selling point. EPA figures are expected to carry over from 2025.
- Hybrid: Up to 51 mpg city / 58 mpg highway (Blue trim); real-world highway testing returned 48 mpg.
- 2.0L Gas: Around 30–32 mpg city / 39–41 mpg highway, depending on trim and wheels; real-world highway result was 38 mpg.
- N Line: Rated at 28 mpg city / 35 mpg highway, respectable given its performance focus.
interior:
Inside, the Elantra emphasizes functionality over luxury, but the layout is clean and thoughtfully designed. The driver-oriented dashboard angles controls toward the driver, while materials are durable, if not premium. Both front and rear seats offer adult-friendly space, a notable advantage in the compact class.

Cargo capacity is also competitive. In testing, the trunk accommodated six carry-on suitcases, making it practical for airport runs and weekend trips.
technology: Lower trims feature an 8.0-inch touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, while higher trims upgrade to dual 10.3-inch displays for the instrument cluster and infotainment. While the larger system requires wired smartphone connectivity, it adds satellite radio and a more upscale presentation. Audio options range from a standard six-speaker setup to an available eight-speaker Bose system on Limited and N Line trims.
safety:
The Elantra earns a five-star overall rating from NHTSA, reinforcing its strong safety credentials.
Standard features include: automated emergency braking, lane-departure warning, and lane-keeping assist.
Available features: adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go and lane-centering assist, which require stepping up to mid or higher trims.
warranty:
Hyundai continues to lead the segment in ownership coverage.
- Limited warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty: 10 years / 100,000 miles
- Complimentary maintenance: 3 years / 36,000 miles

This coverage remains a key differentiator versus most compact sedan rivals.
pros: Wide trim and powertrain choices, roomy interior, excellent fuel economy, class-leading warranty.
cons: Base engine lacks refinement, interior materials feel basic, wired CarPlay on higher trims.
mn_take: The 2026 Hyundai Elantra isn’t the most exciting compact sedan, but its blend of value, efficiency, space, and warranty coverage makes it one of the smartest all-round choices in the segment.

car_name: 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 Review: Price, Range, Specs, Interior, Safety & Real-World Appeal
overview:
The 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 marks a major step forward for Hyundai’s electric ambitions, entering the market as a fully electric, three-row family SUV designed to rival both premium and mainstream competitors. Inspired heavily by the futuristic Seven concept, the Ioniq 9 translates concept-car drama into a practical, road-ready form with bold proportions, clean surfacing, and a commanding stance. In size and road presence, it closely mirrors the Hyundai Palisade, while sharing its electric underpinnings with the Kia EV9.

Underneath the sculpted bodywork is Hyundai-Kia’s advanced E-GMP platform, engineered specifically for electric vehicles. This architecture allows for a flat floor, expansive interior space, ultra-fast charging, and long driving range. With seating for up to seven, multiple powertrain choices, and a maximum range of up to 335 miles, the Ioniq 9 positions itself as a genuinely usable electric SUV for large families, long road trips, and daily commuting alike.

Everything about the Ioniq 9 is new. This model represents Hyundai’s first three-row EV SUV and the flagship of its Ioniq lineup. Compared to earlier Ioniq models, it introduces a larger battery, more powerful dual-motor options, new comfort-focused interior features such as massage seats, and next-generation EV software with intelligent route planning. Hyundai has confirmed U.S. availability beginning in early 2025 for the 2026 model year.
pricing:
Pricing for the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 reflects its flagship positioning, starting at $60,555 and extending to $79,090 for fully loaded performance trims.

- S (RWD): $60,555
- SE (AWD): $64,365
- SEL (AWD): $67,920
- Performance Limited (AWD): $72,850
- Performance Calligraphy (AWD): $76,590
- Performance Calligraphy Design: $79,090

The S RWD trim delivers the longest range and will appeal to efficiency-focused buyers. However, the SE AWD emerges as the most balanced choice, adding all-wheel drive, enhanced traction in poor weather, and a higher towing capacity of 5,000 pounds, making it better suited to family road trips and outdoor use.
drivetrain:
The Ioniq 9 is offered with three distinct electric powertrain configurations, all paired with a large 110.3-kWh lithium-ion battery, one of the biggest in the segment.

The rear-wheel-drive version uses a single motor producing 215 horsepower, delivering smooth and quiet performance ideal for relaxed cruising. Stepping up to the dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup increases total output to 303 horsepower, improving acceleration and all-weather confidence. At the top of the range, the Performance AWD model produces a substantial 422 horsepower, transforming the Ioniq 9 into one of the quickest three-row electric SUVs available.

Despite its size, the Ioniq 9 feels composed on the road. Self-leveling suspension dampers help maintain ride quality regardless of passenger or cargo load, while torque vectoring improves stability through corners. In testing, the Performance AWD model reached 0–60 mph in 4.4 seconds, with a claimed top speed of 124 mph, figures that rival many performance-oriented SUVs.

Practicality extends to towing as well. The rear-wheel-drive Ioniq 9 is rated to tow 3,500 pounds, sufficient for small trailers or boats. All-wheel-drive models increase that figure to 5,000 pounds, placing the Ioniq 9 among the most capable electric SUVs for towing. A dedicated trailer mode automatically adjusts range calculations based on trailer weight, helping drivers plan longer journeys more accurately.

Range is a key strength of the Ioniq 9. Hyundai estimates up to 335 miles of range for the S RWD model with 19-inch wheels. The SE and SEL AWD trims are rated at 320 miles, while the more powerful Performance AWD versions deliver 311 miles per charge.

Charging performance is equally impressive. Thanks to its 800-volt electrical architecture, the Ioniq 9 supports 350-kW DC fast charging, allowing the battery to recharge from 10 to 80 percent in approximately 24 minutes under ideal conditions. This makes the Ioniq 9 well-suited for long-distance travel, reducing charging downtime compared to older EVs.

According to EPA estimates, the Ioniq 9 S RWD achieves 92 MPGe combined, while SE and SEL AWD trims return 88 MPGe. Performance AWD variants are rated at 85 MPGe combined, reflecting their higher power output and performance-oriented tuning. These figures are competitive for a three-row electric SUV of this size and weight.
interior:
Inside, the Ioniq 9 adopts a lounge-inspired design philosophy focused on space, light, and relaxation. The flat floor and long wheelbase translate into generous legroom across all three rows. Front occupants benefit from Relaxation Seats with dynamic massage, while second-row seating can be configured for six or seven passengers.

Hyundai has also emphasized sustainability, using recycled PET plastics, wool fabrics, synthetic leather, and suede-like materials throughout the cabin. Cargo space measures 22 cubic feet behind the third row, expanding to 46 cubic feet when the rear seats are folded. A front trunk adds extra storage, offering 3 cubic feet in RWD models and 2 cubic feet in AWD versions.
technology: Technology is a major highlight. A wide, curved display integrates a 12.0-inch digital instrument cluster with a large infotainment touchscreen. EV-specific navigation includes intelligent route planning with charging stops. The cabin is equipped with seven USB-C ports, wireless charging, digital key functionality, Hyundai Bluelink connected services, and an 8-speaker audio system, with a 14-speaker Bose premium setup available on higher trims.
safety:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist detection, designed to reduce the severity of frontal collisions in both city and highway driving.
- Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, which actively helps guide the vehicle back into its lane when unintended drift is detected.
- Adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go functionality, capable of maintaining a set distance from the vehicle ahead even in heavy traffic conditions.
- Blind-spot monitoring and rear cross-traffic alert, assisting drivers during lane changes and while reversing out of parking spaces.
- Surround-view camera system (available), offering a 360-degree view to improve visibility in tight urban environments.
Crash-test ratings from NHTSA and IIHS are expected to place the Ioniq 9 among the safest electric SUVs in its class, continuing Hyundai’s strong safety track record.
warranty:
- 5-year / 60,000-mile limited vehicle warranty, covering most components and electronics.
- 10-year / 100,000-mile powertrain warranty, one of the longest in the industry and a major ownership advantage.
- 10-year / 100,000-mile battery warranty, providing long-term confidence for EV buyers concerned about battery degradation and replacement costs.

No complimentary scheduled maintenance for 2026 models, meaning routine servicing costs are borne by the owner, though EV maintenance requirements remain lower than those of combustion-engine SUVs.
pros: Long driving range, ultra-fast charging, spacious three-row interior, strong performance options, premium cabin feel.
cons: High entry price, large footprint for city use, no complimentary maintenance.
mn_take: The 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 stands out as a future-ready family EV, combining long range, fast charging, and a refined cabin to set a new benchmark for three-row electric SUVs.

car_name: 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid Review: Price, Trims, Specs, Mileage & Features
overview:
The 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid marks a major milestone for Hyundai’s flagship three-row SUV, introducing electrification to a nameplate already known for comfort, space, and premium appeal. This first-ever hybrid Palisade blends the bold, upright styling of the all-new second-generation model with a powerful and efficient gas-electric powertrain, producing a combined 329 horsepower—a healthy 42-hp advantage over the outgoing V-6.

Compared to the previous Palisade, the 2026 model is slightly longer and wider, enhancing cabin room and road presence. Design highlights such as forward-angled D-pillars, expansive glass areas, and a more architectural profile give it a modern, upscale character while also improving outward visibility and cabin airiness. Positioned directly against rivals like the Toyota Grand Highlander Hybrid and the Mazda CX-90 Hybrid, the Palisade Hybrid combines space, efficiency, and features so effectively that it earned a place on the 2026 10Best Trucks and SUVs list.

For 2026, the Palisade enters its second generation, and the biggest news is the introduction of the hybrid variant. The platform has been stretched slightly for better interior packaging, while exterior styling adopts Hyundai’s newer boxy design language seen on models like the Santa Fe and Ioniq family. Inside, a redesigned horizontal dashboard, upgraded seat cushioning, increased recline angles, and improved thigh support elevate long-distance comfort, especially for second-row passengers.
pricing:
The 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid is priced from $45,760 to $58,380, placing it competitively within the midsize hybrid SUV segment.

Blue SEL – $45,760: Entry trim with hybrid powertrain, three-row seating, large digital displays, and full safety suite

SEL 7P – $47,760: Captain’s chairs for improved second-row comfort, seating for seven

SEL 8P – $47,760: Second-row bench, maximum seating capacity of eight

Blue SEL Premium – $49,120 (Recommended): Adds ventilated seats, heated steering wheel, and 360-degree camera

SEL Premium – $51,120: Further comfort and convenience upgrades

Limited – $53,590: Luxury-focused trim with premium materials and advanced tech

Calligraphy – $58,380: Fully loaded flagship with exclusive styling, high-end leather, and top-tier features

The Blue SEL Premium stands out as the sweet spot, offering near-luxury features without the steep price of upper trims.
drivetrain:
Powering the Palisade Hybrid is a turbocharged 2.5-liter gasoline engine paired with two electric motors, integrated into a six-speed automatic transmission. The system delivers a combined 329 hp and 399 lb-ft of torque, with all-wheel drive standard across the range.

Performance is surprisingly strong for a three-row hybrid SUV. In testing, the Palisade Hybrid accelerated from 0–60 mph in 6.6 seconds, noticeably quicker than the non-hybrid V-6 Palisade. Power delivery is smooth and immediate, while ride quality remains plush and composed, clearly tuned for comfort rather than aggressive driving.

The 2026 Palisade Hybrid is rated to tow up to 4,000 pounds, making it capable enough for small boats, campers, or utility trailers, though it falls short of the 5,000-pound rating offered by the non-hybrid Palisade.

Efficiency is where the hybrid truly shines. EPA ratings reach up to 33 mpg city and 35 mpg highway for front-wheel-drive models, with AWD trims rated slightly lower. In real-world highway testing at 75 mph, an AWD Palisade Hybrid returned 28 mpg, a respectable figure given its size, power, and standard AWD system.
interior:
Inside, the Palisade Hybrid mirrors the standard model’s premium, family-friendly layout. Three rows come standard, with seating for eight passengers via a second-row bench or seven with optional captain’s chairs. Every row benefits from cupholders, USB-C charging ports, and thoughtful storage solutions.

Available features such as a UV-C sanitizing tray, wireless charging pad, digital rearview mirror, and ventilated first- and second-row seats reinforce the Palisade’s upscale positioning. Cargo space remains generous, making it well-suited for long road trips and daily family use.
technology: A curved panoramic display integrates dual 12.3-inch screens for the instrument cluster and infotainment system. Standard features include wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, onboard Wi-Fi, navigation, Amazon Alexa integration, Hyundai Pay, and an optional 14-speaker Bose premium audio system for higher trims.
safety:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Standard lane-departure warning and lane-keeping assist
- Standard adaptive cruise control with lane centering
- Available surround-view camera system and advanced parking aids
warranty:
- 5-year / 60,000-mile limited vehicle warranty
- 10-year / 100,000-mile powertrain warranty (first owner)
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance for 2026 models
pros: Powerful hybrid system, excellent fuel efficiency, spacious and premium interior, standard AWD.
cons: No free maintenance, towing capacity lower than non-hybrid, top trims get expensive.
mn_take: The 2026 Hyundai Palisade Hybrid delivers the perfect blend of power, efficiency, and luxury, making it one of the most well-rounded three-row hybrid SUVs you can buy.

car_name: 2026 Hyundai Santa Fe Review: Price, Trims, Features, Performance & Specs
overview:
The 2026 Hyundai Santa Fe blurs the line between mainstream and premium, combining rugged, almost luxury-SUV styling with family-friendly pricing. At a glance, its boxy proportions, upright stance, and squared-off LED lighting give it a presence more commonly associated with high-end adventure SUVs. Yet beneath that upscale exterior lies a practical and approachable three-row crossover designed to comfortably move up to seven passengers.

Beyond aesthetics, the Santa Fe’s shape pays real dividends in everyday use. A wide tailgate and tall roofline translate into excellent cargo access, while the interior delivers a modern, tech-forward environment filled with thoughtful storage solutions and high-quality materials—especially in upper trims. Positioned below larger alternatives like the Hyundai Palisade, the Santa Fe focuses on efficiency, maneuverability, and value, making it an ideal choice for families who don’t need a full-size three-row SUV.

For 2026, Hyundai addresses one of the Santa Fe’s biggest criticisms by replacing the previous eight-speed dual-clutch transmission with a traditional eight-speed torque-converter automatic. The change improves low-speed smoothness, durability, and overall refinement—particularly in stop-and-go traffic.

Additional updates focus on equipment enhancements:
- Limited trims now come standard with second-row captain’s chairs (bench optional)
- Limited and XRT trims gain dual wireless phone chargers
- XRT trim adds a new Terrain Mode system with Mud, Snow, and Sand settings
- Calligraphy trim introduces a rich Pecan Brown Nappa leather interior, reinforcing the Santa Fe’s near-luxury appeal
pricing:
The 2026 Hyundai Santa Fe starts at $36,650 and tops out at $49,200, undercutting several key rivals such as the Honda Pilot and Toyota Grand Highlander.

SE – $36,650
Strong value entry point with modern safety tech and three-row seating.

SEL – $39,190 (Best Value)
Adds heated front seats, power-adjustable driver seat, faux-leather upholstery, wireless charging, roof rails, and dual-zone climate control with rear vents.

XRT – $43,640
A more rugged-looking option with standard AWD, unique styling elements, increased towing capability, and terrain-select modes.

Limited – $46,200
Focuses on comfort and convenience with captain’s chairs, upgraded materials, and more advanced technology.

Calligraphy – $49,200
The luxury-oriented flagship featuring Nappa leather, premium trim materials, and the most advanced tech features available.

All-wheel drive costs $1,715 on most trims but comes standard on the XRT.
drivetrain:
Every non-hybrid Santa Fe is powered by a 277-hp turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-four paired with the new eight-speed automatic transmission. Front-wheel drive is standard, while all-wheel drive is optional.

The powertrain delivers confident acceleration and smooth power delivery, prioritizing relaxed cruising over aggressive driving. In testing, the Santa Fe recorded a 0–60 mph time of 6.3 seconds, making it quicker than several competitors despite its comfort-oriented tuning. Steering feel is light but predictable, and while body roll is present in corners, the suspension does an excellent job of isolating passengers from rough road surfaces—particularly on long highway drives.

The Santa Fe is more capable than its crossover styling suggests:
- Standard towing capacity: 3,500 pounds (with trailer brakes)
- XRT trim: Up to 4,500 pounds, making it one of the more capable options in its class

This makes it suitable for small campers, boats, or utility trailers without stepping up to a larger SUV.

EPA estimates for the 2026 model are pending, but based on prior data:
- FWD models: up to 20 mpg city / 29 mpg highway
- AWD models: slightly lower, around 28 mpg highway
- XRT trim: drops to approximately 19 mpg city / 26 mpg highway

In real-world testing, an AWD Calligraphy returned 24 mpg at a steady 75 mph, reflecting the Santa Fe’s focus on refinement rather than outright efficiency.
interior:
The Santa Fe’s interior design draws inspiration from premium brands, emphasizing horizontal lines, soft-touch materials, and an open, airy layout.
- First Row: Spacious and upscale, especially in Limited and Calligraphy trims with features like Nappa leather, wood trim, and even an extendable driver footrest.
- Second Row: Captain’s chairs or bench seating depending on trim, with ample adult legroom.
- Third Row: Best suited for children or shorter trips, but usable when needed.

Cargo Capacity
- 14.6 cu ft behind the third row
- 16 carry-on bags with third row folded
- 34 carry-on bags with both rear rows folded
technology:
Dominating the dashboard are dual 12.3-inch displays, one for digital gauges and the other for infotainment. Despite the screen-heavy design, Hyundai smartly retains physical knobs for volume and climate control.

Key tech highlights include:
- Wireless Apple CarPlay & Android Auto (standard)
- Dual wireless phone charging (upper trims)
- Bose premium audio system (available)
- UV-C sterilization compartment for small personal items
safety:
The Santa Fe comes well-equipped with advanced safety technology, much of it standard:

Standard Safety Features
- Forward-collision warning with automated emergency braking
- Adaptive cruise control with stop-and-go
- Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Driver-attention monitoring

Crash-test ratings can be found through NHTSA and IIHS, where the Santa Fe historically performs strongly.
warranty:
Hyundai continues to lead the segment in ownership coverage:
- Limited Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 10 years / 100,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 36,000 miles
pros: Bold design, spacious and upscale interior, strong warranty, excellent value for a three-row SUV.
cons: Third row isn’t class-leading, fuel economy trails hybrid rivals, handling favors comfort over sportiness.
mn_take: The 2026 Hyundai Santa Fe is a stylish, practical, and highly refined family SUV that delivers premium looks and real-world usability at a mainstream price.

car_name: 2026 Hyundai Tucson Hybrid Price, Trims, Mileage, Features & Performance Review
overview:
The 2026 Hyundai Tucson Hybrid takes the already well-rounded Tucson formula and elevates it with electrified efficiency and improved performance. While the standard gasoline Tucson remains a competent compact SUV, the hybrid and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) variants offer tangible advantages that go beyond fuel savings. With quicker acceleration, quieter operation in city driving, and reduced fuel consumption, the Tucson Hybrid feels more refined and better suited to modern commuting.

Hyundai has also ensured that choosing the hybrid doesn’t mean sacrificing practicality or comfort. Interior space, cargo capacity, and overall usability closely mirror the regular Tucson, while the cabin design leans heavily into a clean, tech-forward aesthetic. Positioned against rivals such as the Honda CR-V Hybrid and Toyota RAV4 Hybrid, the Tucson Hybrid stands out with competitive pricing, generous standard features, and one of the best warranty packages in the segment.
pricing:
The 2026 Hyundai Tucson Hybrid starts at $34,050, undercutting several key competitors while offering standard all-wheel drive across most trims.

Blue SE Hybrid – $34,050
The most affordable entry into the lineup, offering standard AWD, a comprehensive safety suite, and excellent fuel economy. Ideal for buyers prioritizing efficiency and value.

SEL Hybrid – $35,500
Builds on the SE with added convenience features and interior upgrades, making it better suited for daily family use.

SEL Convenience Hybrid – $36,500 (Recommended)
Widely considered the best-balanced trim, adding heated front and rear seats, a digital instrument cluster, wireless smartphone charging, a power tailgate, and upgraded upholstery.

SEL Plug-In Hybrid – $41,925
Introduces plug-in capability with meaningful electric-only driving range, appealing to buyers who can charge regularly.

Limited Hybrid – $43,675
Focuses on premium touches such as enhanced interior materials, larger displays, and advanced driver-assistance technologies.

Limited Plug-In Hybrid – $50,150
The flagship trim combines maximum luxury with electrification, but at a price that edges into near-luxury territory.
drivetrain:
The Tucson Hybrid pairs a 1.6-liter turbocharged four-cylinder engine with an electric motor, delivering a combined 231 horsepower and 258 lb-ft of torque. Power is sent through a six-speed automatic transmission, and all-wheel drive comes standard, giving the Tucson confident traction in varied weather conditions.

The Plug-In Hybrid ups the output to 268 horsepower, providing noticeably stronger mid-range acceleration. While neither version is intended to be sporty, both feel significantly quicker and more responsive than the gas-only Tucson, especially during highway merging and urban stop-and-go driving.

Earlier testing shows the Tucson Hybrid achieving 0–60 mph in approximately 7.1 seconds, which is quicker than many compact SUV rivals and clearly ahead of the non-hybrid model.

Efficiency is a core strength of the Tucson Hybrid lineup:
- Hybrid: EPA-rated at up to 38 mpg city and 38 mpg highway
- Plug-In Hybrid: 77 MPGe combined, with 32 miles of electric-only range

In real-world highway driving at sustained speeds, observed fuel economy can dip into the high 20s, but mixed driving consistently delivers strong results. The PHEV version is especially appealing for short daily commutes, where many trips can be completed without using gasoline at all.
interior: Inside, the Tucson Hybrid benefits from Hyundai’s latest interior design philosophy, blending minimalism with technology. The cabin feels airy and well-finished, with soft-touch materials on frequently used surfaces and a logical control layout. Seating comfort is a strong point, with supportive cushions and ample legroom in both rows. Cargo space remains competitive for the compact SUV class, accommodating everyday errands with ease and expanding sufficiently for weekend trips when the rear seats are folded.
technology: Every Tucson Hybrid features a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system, offering crisp graphics and quick response times. Higher trims add a second 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster, creating a seamless dual-screen setup that enhances the premium feel. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, while available features include a wireless charging pad, Bose premium audio, and Hyundai’s Digital Key, allowing owners to lock, unlock, and start the vehicle using a smartphone.
safety:
Safety remains a priority, with the Tucson Hybrid earning a 5-star overall rating from NHTSA.

Standard Safety Equipment
- Automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist
- Forward collision warning
- Blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert

Available Advanced Driver Assistance
- Adaptive cruise control with lane-centering
- Highway driving assist on upper trims
- Surround-view camera system
warranty:
Hyundai continues to set the benchmark for warranty coverage in the mainstream SUV market.
- Limited Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles
- Powertrain Warranty: 10 years / 100,000 miles
- Complimentary Maintenance: 3 years / 36,000 miles

This coverage, combined with the inherent reliability and lower servicing needs of a hybrid powertrain, makes long-term ownership particularly appealing.
pros: Strong fuel efficiency, smooth hybrid power delivery, spacious and tech-rich interior, class-leading warranty.
cons: Real-world highway mpg can trail EPA figures, upper trims become expensive, PHEV pricing climbs quickly.
mn_take: The 2026 Hyundai Tucson Hybrid strikes an excellent balance between efficiency, comfort, and technology, making it one of the smartest compact hybrid SUVs for value-focused buyers.

car_name: 2026 Hyundai Santa Cruz Price, Trims, Features & Performance Review
overview:
The 2026 Hyundai Santa Cruz continues to carve out a unique space between compact SUVs and traditional pickup trucks. Based on the Tucson platform, it blends car-like comfort with genuine utility thanks to its integrated cargo bed. While it won’t replace a midsize or full-size pickup for heavy-duty work, the Santa Cruz is purpose-built for urban buyers who want flexibility without sacrificing ride quality, refinement, or efficiency. For 2026, Hyundai carries forward the refreshed design introduced last year, keeping the Santa Cruz visually bold and mechanically familiar.

What sets the Santa Cruz apart is its everyday usability. It feels more like a crossover on the road, offers a noticeably premium cabin for the segment, and remains easy to live with in tight city environments. Compared to rivals like the Ford Maverick, it leans more toward comfort and technology rather than outright value or hybrid efficiency.
pricing:
The 2026 Hyundai Santa Cruz price starts at $31,350, with multiple trims catering to different buyer priorities:

SE – $31,350
Entry-level trim with the 191-hp naturally aspirated engine, front-wheel drive as standard, and a strong list of safety and infotainment features.

SEL – $33,000
Adds convenience upgrades and more interior refinement, making it a balanced daily-driver choice.

SEL Activity – $36,050
Focuses on lifestyle usability with features like wireless charging, a more versatile bed setup, and added tech.

XRT – $42,950 (Recommended)
The most affordable way into the powerful turbocharged engine. Comes standard with all-wheel drive, rugged exterior accents, a 360-degree camera, and Blind-Spot View Monitor.

Limited – $45,300
Fully loaded trim with the most premium interior materials, advanced tech, and the smoothest overall driving experience.
drivetrain:
Hyundai offers two distinct powertrains, depending on the trim:

Lower trims (SE, SEL, SEL Activity) use a 2.5-liter naturally aspirated four-cylinder producing 191 horsepower and 181 lb-ft of torque, paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission. This setup prioritizes smoothness and efficiency but feels relaxed rather than quick, especially under load.

Higher trims (XRT and Limited) upgrade to a turbocharged 2.5-liter four-cylinder delivering 281 horsepower and 311 lb-ft of torque, mated to an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. This version transforms the Santa Cruz, offering strong acceleration and confident highway performance. In real-world testing, the turbo Santa Cruz achieves 0–60 mph in around 6.0 seconds, making it one of the quickest vehicles in its class.

All-wheel drive is optional on lower trims and standard with the turbo engine, enhancing traction and towing confidence.

While official EPA figures for 2026 are yet to be released, expectations remain in line with the outgoing model:

City: up to 22 mpg

Highway: up to 30 mpg

Combined: around 25 mpg

Real-world highway testing of the turbo model has returned 30 mpg at 75 mph, which is impressive given its performance and AWD capability. Although it can’t match the Ford Maverick Hybrid for efficiency, the Santa Cruz balances power and economy well.
interior:
Inside, the Santa Cruz punches above its weight. Hyundai’s interior design philosophy shines through with clean lines, high-quality materials, and a layout that feels more premium than most compact trucks.

The front seats are supportive and comfortable for long drives, while the driving position feels natural and SUV-like. Rear-seat space is competitive for a crew-cab layout, making it usable for adults on shorter trips. Road and wind noise are well controlled, reinforcing the Santa Cruz’s crossover roots.
technology:
Technology is one of the Santa Cruz’s strongest suits. Most trims feature a 12.3-inch touchscreen, while higher trims add dual 12.3-inch displays integrated into a single curved panel for a modern, upscale look.

Standard features include:

Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto

Bluetooth connectivity

Hyundai BlueLink connected services (free for three years)

Higher trims add wireless charging, enhanced camera systems, and digital conveniences that make daily use seamless.
safety:
The 2026 Hyundai Santa Cruz offers a comprehensive safety package, with strong crash-test performance and modern driver assistance tech.

Standard Safety Features

Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist

Blind-spot monitoring with rear cross-traffic alert

Driver attention warning

Forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking

Available / Higher-Trim Safety Tech

Adaptive cruise control

360-degree surround-view camera

Blind-Spot View Monitor (camera-based display in gauge cluster)

With these systems, the Santa Cruz delivers reassuring safety credentials for families and daily commuters alike.
warranty:
Hyundai continues to lead the segment with one of the most generous ownership packages available:

Warranty Coverage

Limited Warranty: 5 years / 60,000 miles

Powertrain Warranty: 10 years / 100,000 miles

Maintenance

Complimentary scheduled maintenance: 3 years / 36,000 miles

This coverage significantly reduces long-term ownership costs and adds peace of mind compared to most rivals.
pros: Refined ride, powerful turbo option, premium interior, strong tech and warranty coverage.
cons: Higher trims get expensive, no hybrid option, short cargo bed limits heavy-duty use.
mn_take: The 2026 Hyundai Santa Cruz is ideal for buyers who want pickup utility wrapped in a comfortable, tech-rich, SUV-like package without sacrificing everyday drivability.

car_name: 2026 Hyundai Kona Electric Review
overview:
The 2026 Hyundai Kona Electric focuses on value rather than outright performance, positioning itself as one of the most affordable electric subcompact SUVs on sale. With its sharp, futuristic styling and a thoughtfully designed interior, the Kona Electric manages to feel modern and practical despite its entry-level electric hardware. For 2026, Hyundai has simplified the lineup dramatically, offering the Kona Electric only in SE trim, paired with a smaller battery and a modest single-motor setup.

This streamlined approach means the Kona Electric no longer chases class-leading acceleration or range figures. Instead, it targets budget-conscious EV buyers who want a stylish, easy-to-live-with electric SUV for daily commuting and urban use. Rivals such as the Kia Niro EV and Volvo EX30 offer stronger performance and longer range, but at a noticeably higher price. For buyers prioritizing affordability and everyday usability, the Kona Electric still makes a strong case.
pricing:
For 2026, the Kona Electric is available exclusively in SE trim, with pricing expected to start around $35,000. While this may seem limiting on paper, the SE is far from barebones. Standard equipment includes dual-zone automatic climate control, navigation-based cruise control, a Wi-Fi hotspot, and Hyundai’s latest digital cockpit layout.

With higher trims like SEL, N Line, and Limited discontinued, the buying process is refreshingly simple. Buyers no longer need to balance range-versus-price trade-offs across trims—what you see is what you get.
drivetrain:
The 2026 Kona Electric is powered by a single 133-horsepower electric motor, driving the front wheels. This setup prioritizes smoothness and efficiency over speed. Around town, the instant torque typical of EVs makes the Kona feel responsive enough for city driving, but acceleration tapers off quickly at higher speeds.

Hyundai’s tuning clearly favors comfort. Steering is light, suspension tuning is forgiving, and road noise is well suppressed, making the Kona Electric a relaxed daily commuter. Estimated 0–60 mph acceleration of around 8.6 seconds places it among the slower EVs in the segment, especially compared to earlier Kona Electric versions and competitors like the Kia Niro EV.

Power comes from a 48.6-kWh battery pack, delivering an EPA-estimated range of 200 miles. While this isn’t class-leading, it’s sufficient for most daily commutes and short road trips with planning. Buyers who regularly travel longer distances may find alternatives like the Kia Niro EV more appealing due to their extended range.

When connected to a DC fast charger, the Kona Electric can recharge from 10 to 80 percent in approximately 45 minutes, which is acceptable but not particularly fast by modern EV standards. For home charging, overnight Level 2 charging remains the most practical solution.

Efficiency is one area where the Kona Electric shines. Based on previous EPA figures, it achieves an estimated 131 MPGe in the city and 105 MPGe on the highway. In real-world testing at a steady 75 mph, the Kona Electric returned around 110 MPGe, outperforming several larger and heavier electric SUVs. These numbers make it a cost-effective EV to run, especially for urban drivers.
interior:
Hyundai has given the Kona Electric a genuinely modern cabin that feels more upscale than its price suggests. The dashboard is dominated by a wide digital display that integrates the instrument cluster and infotainment system seamlessly. A floating center console and horizontal control layout help create a sense of openness, while ambient lighting adds a touch of flair.

Rear-seat space is generous for a subcompact EV, offering 36.4 inches of rear legroom, which is more accommodating than many rivals, including the Volvo EX30. Cargo capacity is another strong point, with 26 cubic feet available behind the rear seats and up to 64 cubic feet when they’re folded down. A small front trunk adds minor extra storage for charging cables.
technology: The Kona Electric features dual 12.3-inch displays, one serving as the digital instrument cluster and the other handling infotainment duties. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, along with Bluetooth connectivity and a Wi-Fi hotspot. The system is intuitive, visually crisp, and quick to respond, reinforcing the Kona Electric’s tech-forward feel.
safety:
Standard automated emergency braking, designed to detect vehicles ahead and reduce collision severity.

Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, helping maintain lane discipline during daily driving.

Standard blind-spot monitoring, improving awareness in city traffic and on highways.

Available adaptive cruise control, adding convenience during longer drives.

Optional surround-view camera system and parking assistance, enhancing ease of maneuvering in tight spaces.
warranty:
Limited warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles.

Powertrain warranty: 10 years or 100,000 miles.

Battery warranty: 10 years or 100,000 miles, providing long-term peace of mind for EV ownership.

Complimentary maintenance: 3 years or 36,000 miles, covering inspections, tire rotations, and cabin air-filter changes.

Hyundai’s warranty package remains one of the strongest advantages in the EV market, particularly for first-time electric vehicle buyers.
pros: Affordable entry into EV ownership, efficient powertrain, spacious and modern interior.
cons: Limited range, slow acceleration, single-trim availability.
mn_take: The 2026 Hyundai Kona Electric is a sensible, value-focused EV that trades performance and range for affordability, efficiency, and everyday comfort—making it an ideal urban electric SUV for budget-conscious buyers.

car_name: 2026 Hyundai Venue Review: Pricing, Features, Mileage & MotorNation’s Take
overview:
The 2026 Hyundai Venue is one of the smallest and most affordable SUVs you can buy today, yet it manages to feel thoughtfully designed rather than bare-bones. Measuring noticeably shorter than most subcompact SUVs, the Venue is clearly aimed at urban buyers who prioritize easy maneuverability, low running costs, and straightforward technology. Despite its compact footprint and budget-friendly price, the cabin doesn’t feel cramped or cheaply executed. Hyundai’s clean dashboard layout, solid build quality, and intuitive infotainment system give the Venue a mature, well-rounded feel for its class.

In city environments, the Venue’s light steering, tight turning radius, and compact dimensions make it an easy companion for traffic-heavy commutes and narrow parking spaces. On the flip side, its light weight and modest engine output mean highway driving requires more attention, especially in windy conditions or during overtaking maneuvers. Rivals such as the Kia Soul and Chevrolet Trax offer more space and power, but the Venue undercuts many of them on price, which remains its strongest selling point.
pricing:
The 2026 Hyundai Venue lineup has been simplified, making buying decisions easier than before. Prices start at $22,150 and top out at $24,200, positioning the Venue among the most affordable SUVs in the U.S. market.

Venue SE – $22,150: The base trim comes well-equipped for the price, offering an 8.0-inch touchscreen, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and essential safety features.

Venue SEL – $24,200 (Recommended): The range-topping SEL adds meaningful upgrades such as heated front seats, wireless phone charging, automatic climate control, heated side mirrors, and two-tone exterior paint options.

For most buyers, the SEL is worth the small premium, as it significantly improves daily comfort without pushing the Venue out of budget territory.
drivetrain:
The Venue is powered by a 121-horsepower four-cylinder engine paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT), driving the front wheels exclusively. There’s no all-wheel-drive option, which reinforces the Venue’s city-first focus. Around town, the engine feels responsive enough, and throttle response is well-suited to stop-and-go traffic.

On highways, however, the Venue’s limitations become apparent. Acceleration is leisurely, and merging or passing requires planning. In instrumented testing, the Venue reached 0–60 mph in about 8.5 seconds, which is slower than many competitors but still marginally quicker than the Nissan Kicks. This is not an enthusiast’s SUV, but it delivers predictable, easy-going performance for everyday use.

Efficiency is one of the Venue’s highlights. While official EPA figures for 2026 are expected to mirror the previous year, estimates stand at 29 mpg city and 32 mpg highway. In real-world highway testing at 75 mph, the Venue returned 31 mpg, which is respectable for a gasoline-powered subcompact SUV. Some rivals, including the Nissan Kicks, offer slightly better mileage, but the difference is unlikely to be a deal-breaker for most buyers.
interior:
Inside, the Venue punches above its weight. The front seats are comfortable, visibility is excellent, and the cabin layout prioritizes usability over flash. Controls are logically placed, materials feel durable, and storage spaces are cleverly integrated throughout the cabin. The SEL trim adds heated front seats and automatic climate control, enhancing comfort in colder climates.

Rear-seat space is adequate for the class, though taller passengers may feel constrained on longer trips. Cargo capacity measures 19 cubic feet with the rear seats up, expanding to 32 cubic feet when folded flat—enough for grocery runs, weekend luggage, or small furniture items.
technology: Every 2026 Hyundai Venue comes standard with an 8.0-inch touchscreen infotainment system featuring wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. The system is quick to respond, easy to navigate, and refreshingly simple, with physical knobs for volume and tuning. A six-speaker audio system is standard across all trims, and higher trims add wireless phone charging for added convenience.
safety:
Standard automated emergency braking, designed to detect vehicles ahead and reduce the risk or severity of frontal collisions.

Lane-keeping assist and lane-departure warning, helping the driver stay centered in the lane during routine driving.

Automatic high-beam headlights, improving nighttime visibility without driver intervention.

Available blind-spot monitoring, alerting drivers to vehicles in adjacent lanes.

Available rear cross-traffic alert, especially useful when backing out of tight parking spaces.

Five-star overall safety rating from NHTSA, reinforcing the Venue’s credentials as a safe, city-friendly SUV.

While advanced features like adaptive cruise control are absent, the Venue covers the essentials well for its price point.
warranty:
Limited warranty: 5 years or 60,000 miles, exceeding coverage offered by most competitors.

Powertrain warranty: 10 years or 100,000 miles, one of the longest in the industry.

Complimentary maintenance: 3 years or 36,000 miles, adding tangible value during early ownership.

Hyundai’s warranty package remains one of the Venue’s biggest advantages, particularly for first-time buyers or long-term owners.
pros: Affordable pricing, excellent warranty, city-friendly size.
cons: Weak highway performance, no all-wheel drive.
mn_take: The 2026 Hyundai Venue is a smart, budget-conscious urban SUV that delivers solid features, strong warranty coverage, and easy drivability—ideal for city dwellers who value practicality over performance.

car_name: 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing Review: Pricing, Performance, Safety & MotorNation’s Take
overview:
The 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing stands as a defiant statement in an era moving rapidly toward electrification and downsized powertrains. At its core is a supercharged V-8, rear-wheel drive, and a standard six-speed manual transmission—ingredients that feel increasingly rare in today’s performance-sedan market. While rivals such as the BMW M5 and the Audi RS7 lean heavily on technology and luxury, the Blackwing prioritizes mechanical engagement and driver involvement. It may not deliver the most opulent cabin in the segment, but from behind the wheel, few sedans can match its intensity, balance, and emotional appeal.

For 2026, Cadillac introduces the Curated by Cadillac program for the CT5-V Blackwing. These limited-production models are hand-built and hand-painted at Cadillac’s Artisan Center, offering exclusive customization options far beyond the standard production car. Blind Zone Steering Assist is now standard across the lineup, while certain interior color schemes and the Le Monstre Special Edition have been discontinued, subtly simplifying the configuration choices.
pricing:
The 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing lineup starts at $102,795 and extends well into bespoke territory.

CT5-V Blackwing – $102,795: The standard model already includes the full 668-hp V-8, adaptive suspension, performance brakes, and a six-speed manual transmission.

CT5-V Blackwing Curated by Cadillac – approx. $158,000: Hand-crafted and highly personalized, this version targets collectors and enthusiasts seeking exclusivity and factory-approved customization.

While the automatic transmission is marginally quicker, the manual remains the purist’s choice and the one that best defines the Blackwing’s character.
drivetrain:
Under the hood sits a 6.2-liter supercharged V-8 producing 668 horsepower, making this one of the most powerful sedans on sale today. Power is sent to the rear wheels through either a standard six-speed manual or an optional 10-speed automatic. Advanced hardware such as a limited-slip differential, launch control with line lock, and Cadillac’s Performance Traction Management system allow drivers to explore the car’s limits with confidence. Magnetorheological dampers provide an impressive dual personality—composed and comfortable during daily driving, yet razor-sharp when pushed hard.

Performance numbers are nothing short of staggering. The manual CT5-V Blackwing reaches 0–60 mph in 3.6 seconds, while the automatic trims that to 3.5 seconds. In extended testing, its braking and high-speed stability rival far more exotic machinery, placing it surprisingly close to track-focused sports cars. Optional Precision and Carbon packages further sharpen handling with stiffer suspension tuning and wider performance tires.

Efficiency is understandably not the Blackwing’s primary focus. EPA estimates stand at 13 mpg city and 22 mpg highway for the automatic, with the manual slightly lower on the highway. Real-world highway testing has shown figures as high as 24 mpg, which is respectable given the car’s output and performance envelope.
interior: Inside, the CT5-V Blackwing blends performance cues with everyday usability. Leather upholstery, massaging and ventilated front seats, a digital gauge cluster, and ambient lighting come standard. While material quality does not fully match some European rivals at this price point, the cabin remains functional and driver-focused. The trunk offers practical space, accommodating five carry-on suitcases, making the Blackwing surprisingly usable as a daily driver.
technology: Dominating the dashboard is a 33.0-inch curved display with ultra-high resolution, running a Google-based operating system. Built-in navigation, performance telemetry, tire-temperature monitoring, and optional performance data recording transform the CT5-V Blackwing into a serious track-analysis tool. Wireless Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Wi-Fi connectivity, and a 16-speaker AKG audio system are all standard.
safety:
Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, capable of detecting vehicles and people at urban and highway speeds to help reduce frontal collision severity.

Forward collision alert provides visual and audible warnings when rapid closing speeds are detected, especially useful during spirited driving or highway cruising.

Lane-departure warning with lane-keeping assist, gently steering the car back into its lane when unintentional drift is detected.

Blind-spot monitoring with Blind Zone Steering Assist, which actively nudges the steering wheel away from adjacent vehicles during lane-change maneuvers.

Rear cross-traffic alert and rear automatic emergency braking, assisting drivers when reversing out of tight parking spaces.

Available adaptive cruise control with hands-free Super Cruise capability on automatic-equipped models, allowing hands-free driving on compatible highways with driver attention monitoring.

Despite its extreme performance focus, the CT5-V Blackwing delivers a well-rounded safety suite that balances daily usability with high-speed confidence.
warranty:
Limited vehicle warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles, covering most components and electronics.

Powertrain warranty: 6 years or 70,000 miles, significantly longer than coverage offered by rivals like the BMW M5 and Audi RS7, adding peace of mind for long-term ownership.

Corrosion protection warranty included as part of Cadillac’s standard coverage.

Complimentary maintenance: First scheduled service visit is covered, though Cadillac does not offer extended free maintenance programs like some European competitors.

While not class-leading in complimentary servicing, Cadillac’s long powertrain coverage is a strong advantage for buyers planning to keep the car beyond the lease period.
pros: Explosive V-8 performance, manual transmission, track-ready dynamics.
cons: Interior luxury trails rivals, limited complimentary maintenance.
mn_take: The 2026 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing is a future classic—an unapologetic, V-8-powered sports sedan that prioritizes driver thrill over trends, making it one of the most memorable performance cars you can still buy new.

car_name: 2026 Cadillac CT5 Review: Pricing, Trims, Performance, Safety & MotorNation’s Take
overview:
The 2026 Cadillac CT5 clearly shows how far Cadillac has evolved from its traditional, comfort-first sedan roots. Instead of soft suspensions and sofa-like seats, the CT5 focuses on sharper handling, confident road manners, and a more driver-centric feel. It competes directly with compact luxury sedans such as the BMW 3 Series, Mercedes-Benz C-Class, and Genesis G70. While it may not deliver the same level of interior richness as some German rivals, the CT5 counters with strong engine options, advanced technology, and pricing that undercuts much of the competition.

Following its facelift last year, the CT5 carries forward into 2026 with minimal changes. Cadillac has refreshed the exterior color palette, introducing Vibrant White Tricoat in place of Crystal White Tricoat and adding new shades such as Coastal Blue Metallic and Cyber Yellow Metallic. Mechanically and technologically, the sedan remains unchanged, which is not a drawback given how modern the current package already feels.
pricing:
The 2026 Cadillac CT5 is priced from $50,995 to $60,095, depending on the trim level.

Premium Luxury – $50,995: Designed for buyers prioritizing comfort and features, this trim includes upscale interior appointments, advanced driver assistance options, and a more relaxed suspension tune.

Sport – $51,995: Adds a more aggressive visual package and sportier chassis tuning, appealing to drivers who want a sharper, more engaging feel without moving to a full performance model.

CT5-V – $60,095: The enthusiast-focused variant offering significantly upgraded performance hardware, adaptive suspension, and a more track-capable setup.

For most buyers, the Premium Luxury trim offers the best blend of price, comfort, and technology, while the CT5-V is the obvious choice for driving enthusiasts.
drivetrain:
The standard powertrain is a 237-hp 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder, which delivers smooth performance but feels underpowered for a luxury sports sedan in this segment. Upgrading to the 3.0-liter twin-turbo V-6 with 335 horsepower is strongly recommended, as it dramatically improves acceleration and overall driving enjoyment.
The CT5-V raises the bar with a 360-hp version of the V-6, paired with adaptive dampers and an electronically controlled limited-slip differential. All engines are mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission, with rear-wheel drive standard and all-wheel drive available.

In testing, the four-cylinder CT5 reaches 60 mph in about 6.6 seconds, which is slower than most rivals. The CT5-V, however, completes the same sprint in approximately 4.8 seconds, placing it firmly in sports-sedan territory and allowing it to compete with benchmarks like the BMW 330i and the Alfa Romeo Giulia. Steering precision, chassis balance, and ride control are standout traits, especially in the V trim.

Fuel economy remains respectable across the range. The four-cylinder model is rated at 23 mpg city and 32 mpg highway, making it the most efficient option. The 335-hp V-6 returns 19 mpg city and 28 mpg highway, while the CT5-V dips slightly to 18 mpg city and 27 mpg highway. These figures are competitive but not class-leading.
interior: The CT5’s cabin emphasizes space and technology more than traditional luxury flair. Rear-seat legroom is generous, outperforming several European competitors, making it a strong choice for daily commuting and occasional rear passengers. Material quality is mixed, with premium trim elements contrasted by harder plastics in some areas. Cargo space is practical, accommodating five carry-on suitcases, though rivals offer slightly larger trunks.
technology: A major highlight is Cadillac’s 33.0-inch curved digital display, integrating the instrument cluster and infotainment system into one seamless panel. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, wireless charging, onboard Wi-Fi hotspot capability, and an available AKG premium sound system reinforce the CT5’s tech-forward positioning.
safety:
Standard forward collision alert with automated emergency braking and pedestrian detection

Standard lane-departure warning and lane-keeping assist to help reduce highway fatigue

Standard rear park assist and rear cross-traffic alert for improved urban maneuverability

Available adaptive cruise control with Super Cruise, enabling true hands-free driving on compatible highways

Optional enhanced driver assistance package adding lane-change assistance and improved highway automation
warranty:
Limited warranty: 4 years or 50,000 miles, covering most components

Powertrain warranty: 6 years or 70,000 miles, exceeding coverage offered by many German rivals

Complimentary maintenance: First scheduled service included at no cost

Overall ownership costs remain competitive, though brands like Genesis still offer more comprehensive free maintenance plans
pros: Strong V-6 performance, engaging handling, advanced tech for the price.
cons: Base engine feels weak, interior materials don’t fully match luxury rivals
mn_take: Cadillac CT5 delivers excellent performance value and modern features, making it a smart alternative to European luxury sedans if driving dynamics matter more than ultimate interior opulence.

car_name: 2026 Cadillac CT4-V Blackwing Review, Pricing, Specs & Features — A True Sports Sedan With Performance DNA
overview: In a market steadily abandoning combustion engines and manual gearboxes, the 2026 Cadillac CT4-V Blackwing feels like a defiant final stand for driving enthusiasts. It is not just fast on paper; it is engineered to engage the driver at every level, from steering feel to throttle response. Under the hood sits a 472-horsepower twin-turbocharged V6, driving the rear wheels and paired with a standard six-speed manual transmission, a rarity that instantly sets it apart from nearly every modern rival. Cadillac has resisted the temptation to chase outright lap times with all-wheel drive and instead focused on balance, feedback, and precision. While the interior design shows its age and rear-seat space is limited, the experience from behind the wheel is so rewarding that these compromises feel almost intentional.
pricing:
Cadillac simplifies the buying process by offering the CT4-V Blackwing as a single, fully focused model rather than multiple trims.

The starting price is $65,395, positioning it well below many European rivals while offering comparable—or in some cases superior—driver engagement. Buyers mainly choose between the manual or automatic transmission and then personalize the car through performance-oriented packages such as carbon-fiber aero upgrades, track-focused seats, and advanced telemetry systems.
drivetrain:
Powering the CT4-V Blackwing is a 3.6-liter twin-turbo V6 producing 472 horsepower and 445 lb-ft of torque, sent exclusively to the rear wheels. The engine delivers strong mid-range punch, aggressive top-end pull, and a mechanical soundtrack that feels authentic rather than artificially enhanced.

The six-speed manual is standard and offers crisp engagement with well-judged ratios, while the optional 10-speed automatic delivers lightning-quick shifts for those prioritizing outright speed.
